Updates to the Retirement Adjustment Register form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024%2003Mar%20QR/BA-129%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024 03Mar QR/BA-129 (Epic).htm

Updates to the Retirement Adjustment Register form

Previously, the Retirement Register Adjustment form only had an option to enter Successor Retirement Deferral amounts. This functionality did not allow you to specify what portion of the amount entered (if any) should be allocated to Successor Catch-up Deferral bucket. With the new addition of the 3 Successor fields (Successor Catch-up Deferral, Successor ROTH Deferral and Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral) you will be able to correct any previous retirement register adjustment entry amounts that caused the employee to exceed the retirement deferral tax year limit. A negative amount for the overage can be entered in the Successor Retirement Deferral field and a positive amount can be entered into the Successor Catch-up Deferral field. Now that the amounts are in the correct buckets, the desired tax year limits will be looked at and applied.

The following three fields will now also display under the Successor Deferrals section of this form:

  • Successor Catch-Up Deferral

  • Successor ROTH Deferral

  • Successor ROTH Catch-Up Deferral

  • These fields are for successor deferrals corresponding to similar fields under the Contributions section for the employee.

  • All the above fields are optional.

  • By default, these fields will be blank.

  • You can only enter numeric values in here up to 2 decimal places. If a number is entered without that format, it will automatically be converted to that format. Negative numeric values are allowed.

  • The Employee Tax Deferral Register form and the chart on the form is also updated to include the following successor values.

  • Successor Retirement Deferral

  • Successor Catch-up Deferral

  • Successor ROTH Deferral

  • Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral

  • Since successor deferrals for the year is a part of the YTD retirement contributions, it will not exceed the annual IRS limits set at the:

  • System level at either on the:

  • System Parameters>Actions>Tax Year Limits form OR

  • Plan Year Deferral Limits section under Retirement Plans form OR at the

  • Employee level on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form

  • The system from now on will calculate the:

Catchup Limit = Catch-up Contributions + Roth Catch-up Contributions + Successor -Catch-up Deferral + Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral

  • If limits exist for the year in question at the employee level, they will override (used in place of) the plan level and system level tax year limits.

  • If no limits exist for the year in question at the employee level but exist at the plan level, the plan level will override (used in place of) the system level tax year limits.

  • If no limits exist for the year in question at the employee level or plan level, the system level tax year limits will be used.

  • If the value entered in any of the four fields above renders the successor deferrals for the year to be over-limit, then you will receive a error message stating The amount entered is over the catch-up limit. A maximum amount of $X,XXX.XX can be entered.

  • The Retirement Match P-T-D Register Report generated by the PYTD Retirement Contribution Summary form is also updated to display the following two additional columns:

  • Successor Retirement Deferral - This the total of Successor Retirement Deferral and Successor Catch-up Deferral as per the 401k Register from the Employee Retirement Plan Register

  • Successor ROTH Deferral - This is the total of Successor ROTH Deferral + Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral as per 401k Register from the Employee Retirement Plan Register.

  • The Payroll Retirement Contributions Report is also updated to display the following additional columns between the Employer Non-Elect Match and the Employee Loan Payment columns:

  • Successor Retirement Deferral

  • Successor Catch-up Deferral

  • Successor ROTH Deferral

  • Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral

  • The Retirement Contributions Register Report is also updated to display the following additional columns after the Safe Harbor (2) Match column:

  • Successor Retirement Deferral

  • Successor Catch-up Deferral

  • Successor ROTH Deferral

  • Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral

  • The Retirement Adjustment Transaction Audit Report is also updated to display the following additional columns after the Safe Harbor Type 2 Match column:

  • Successor Retirement Deferral

  • Successor Catch-up Deferral

  • Successor ROTH Deferral

  • Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral

  • The Employee Retirement Plan Register form and the chart on the form is also updated to include the following successor values.

  • Successor Retirement Deferral

  • Successor Catch-up Deferral

  • Successor ROTH Deferral

  • Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral

  • When you make an adjustment to any of the four successor deferrals noted above either in the Retirement Adjustment Register form, or using the Retirement Adjustments Import form, it will get updated in the Employee 401K Register.

JIRA # 2600, 2601, 2602, 2604, 2605, 2606, 2607, 2608, , 2631 2671

Updates to the Retirement Export form

On the Retirement Export form, when you select 401K Extended Download as the Vendor/Template, you will now see a new checkbox called Include Successor Deferrals.

  • By default, this box will be unchecked.

  • If you check this box, then the export file generated will contain the following columns between SH-NONELECT AMOUNT and EMPLOYEE TOTAL columns:

  • Successor Retirement Deferral

  • Successor Catch-up Deferral

  • Successor ROTH Deferral

  • Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral

  • The value in the EMPLOYEE TOTAL column will include the values in the above fields.

Enhancements to the ACA Eligibility Calculation Process

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024%2003Mar%20QR/BA-2488%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024 03Mar QR/BA-2488 (Epic).htm

Enhancements to the ACA Eligibility Determination Process

Background

There is an automatic PrismHR process which checks an employee’s eligibility for health insurance coverage under the Affordable Care Act (ACA). This process is triggered by different events in the system, such as new hires, rehires, imports, and employment type changes.

Under the Affordable Care Act, employees with part-time hours that exceed a certain threshold can become eligible for offers of coverage under certain plans. When this occurs, the employee enters a “Stability Period”. During the Stability Period, their hours are measured to determine whether they still qualify for coverage.

Typically, when an employee enters a Stability Period, a manual or automatic process then adds them to the ACA Offered Employees form. The employee remains part-time, but their placement on this form indicates that the system should treat them as full-time employees for ACA reporting purposes. This means that any listed employees who were eligible for at least one month of coverage under the ACA will receive a copy of Form 1095-C at the end of the year.

[Image: ACA Offered Employees with Stability start and end dates highlighted]

However, the automatic eligibility check process did not account for part-time employees listed on this form. Due to their part-time status, they were considered ineligible for an offer of coverage. The following enhancements address this issue.

Enhancement to the Eligibility Check

Note: Note: To use these new features, you must enable the STATUS.CHG.ELIG custom feature code on the System Parameters form.

[Image: Custom Feature Codes grid, showing STATUS.CHG.ELIG]

The enhanced process treats employees on the ACA Offered Employees form as though they are full-time employees. If they meet the other requirements for ACA plan eligibility (outlined below) the system offers them coverage.

With these enhancements, the system determines eligibility as follows:

  1. Eligibility calculation is triggered for a specific employee and benefit plan.

  2. Is the employee part-time but otherwise eligible for coverage, based on the benefit rule? If yes, continue.

  3. Is the plan eligible under the ACA? (Insurance Class is “Medical” and Do NOT Include in ACA Reporting is not selected). If yes, continue.

  4. Does the employee have an ACA Stability Start and End Date? (Listed on the ACA Offered Employees form). If yes, continue.

  5. Does the Coverage Start Date fall within their stability period? If yes, the employee is eligible for an ACA coverage offer under this plan.

Enhancements to the Employee Benefits Enrollment Form

Whenever you select an employee and a benefit plan on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, the system runs the eligibility check process to determine if the employee is eligible for that plan.

With these new enhancements, if the employee fails the eligibility check but a future-dated Stability Period is listed on the ACA Offered Employees form, the system displays a message:

Employee not eligible for this benefit until [Stability Period Start Date, MM/DD/YYYY] based on the ACA Offered Employees grid.

If the employee is automatically determined to be eligible under this plan, the Coverage Details panel displays the message “There is an ACA Eligibility Override”.

[Image: There is an ACA Override]

Disabling the Enhancements

You can use a new System Parameters option, called Suppress ACA Eligibility Check, to disable these enhancements.

Note: Note: If you select this option, part-time employees on the ACA Offered Employees form will be considered ineligible for coverage.

[Image: System Param to suppress ACA Eligibility]

For more information about ACA and benefits features in PrismHR, see the ACA User Guide, the Benefits Enrollment User Guide, and the Benefits Administration User Guide.

JIRA # BA-2488, 2646, 2577, 2580

Changes to the Group Benefit Plans form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024%2003Mar%20QR/BA-2489%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024 03Mar QR/BA-2489 (Epic).htm

Changes to the Group Benefit Plans form

From now on, the Offer Type field will only show the list of compatible options based on the selection made for the Insurance Class field on this form.

There are seven insurance classes that can be assigned to a Group Benefit Plan. The corresponding Offer Types are as follows:

Insurance Class: Medical

  • Medical (MED)

  • Accident Benefits (ACC)

  • Cancer Benefits (CAN)

  • Critical Illness (CRI)

  • Domestic Partner Medical (MDP)

  • Gap Insurance (GAP)

  • Identity Theft (IDT)

  • Telehealth (TEL)

  • Voluntary Benefits (VOL)

  • Voluntary Hospitalization (HOS)

Insurance Class: Dental

  • Dental (DEN)

  • Domestic Partner Dental (DDP)

  • Voluntary Benefits (VOL)

Insurance Class: Vision

  • Vision (VIS)

  • Domestic Partner Vision (VDP)

  • Voluntary Benefits (VOL)

Insurance Class: Life Insurance

  • Accidental Death and Dismemberment (ADD)

  • Basic Life Extra (BLX)

  • Critical Illness as Life (CRL)

  • Group Term Life (GTL)

  • Life Insurance - Basic (LIF)

  • Life Insurance - Basic - Child Only (LIC)

  • Life Insurance - Basic - Spouse Only (LIS)

  • Whole Life (WLI)

Insurance Class: Short-Term Disability

  • Additional STD (SDA)

  • Short Term Disability (STD)

  • Voluntary Benefits (VOL)

Insurance Class: Long-Term Disability

  • Additional LTD (LDA)

  • Long Term Disability (LTD)

  • Voluntary Benefits (VOL)

Insurance Class: Other

  • Ancillary (ANC)

  • Legal (LGL)

  • Pet Benefits (PET)

  • Voluntary Benefits (VOL)

Insurance Class: Bond

  • –Select One–

Note:

When no Insurance Class is available, the Offer Type dropdown lists –Select One– as the only option.

For an existing Offer Type in PrismHR which is not compatible with the Insurance Class selected, PrismHR will now display the words (Not Valid) next to the Offer Type name. If you try to save a Group Benefit Plan record which has a non-compatible Offer Type, the following message displays:

Offer Type “XXXX” is not compatible with the current Insurance Class.

Select a compatible Offer Type from the dropdown or set this field to the default value of “–Select–”. Once you select a compatible Offer Type, the invalid Offer Type is removed from the dropdown list.

JIRA # BA-2511, 2513

Benefit Rates Import

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024%2003Mar%20QR/BA-314%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024 03Mar QR/BA-314 (Epic).htm

Benefit Rates Import

Use this Benefit Rates Import form to initiate a new import or complete an existing import in progress of benefit rates (premium or billing) into PrismHR using a predefined benefit rates import template. You can also view completed benefit rates imports on this form. This benefit rates import process cannot be used to change or overwrite existing benefit rates.

Note: Note: Client Access Group security is not enabled on this form.

To access the form, on the Work Centers panel, under Onboarding & Benefits, click Benefit Imports & Reporting. Under Benefit Imports, click Benefit Rates Import.

[Image: screenshot]

You can also search for this form on the search box in the main navigation search bar.

[Image: screenshot]

This form has the following two sections:

  • Imports in Progress

  • Past Imports

Imports in Progress

When you access this form for the first time, all the tables will be blank and you should select the New Import button to proceed to the Benefit Rates Import Setup & File Import form to define and begin a new benefit rate import.

[Image: screenshot]

User - This field is a dropdown. By default, the user id of the user who has logged in will display here. You can also select a different user from the drop-down.

This section displays all benefit rate imports that are not completed successfully for the selected user. This section will display the last 7 imports in progress at a glance on-screen for the selected user. In case there are more than 7 imports in progress for the selected user, you will see a scroll bar on the right. Scroll to view all the imports in progress for the selected user. The information is displayed in a table that has the following columns:

  1. Name - This is the import name that was provided for that benefit rate import. If you click one of the names, it will take you to the Benefit Rates Import Setup & File Import form for further action to complete the import.

  2. Type - This is the benefit rate type that you are importing for the import. This will be:

a. Premium Rates OR
b. Billing Rates
— —

  1. Plan Used for Template - This is the Benefit Plan ID used for the import template.

  2. Last Modified Date - This shows when this import was last worked upon.

  3. Last Modified User - This shows the user id of the user who worked on the import last.

  4. Status - This shows the status of the import in progress and can be any one of the following:

a. Template Defined – When an import has been defined but no import file is uploaded.
b. Ready for Import - When an import has been defined AND an import file is uploaded.
— —
  1. — Import Errors - When an import attempt has failed. This will produce a Benefit Rate Import Error Report
  1. Error Report - When the Status above is either Template Defined or Ready for Import, this column will display a ‘-’ [dash]. When the Status above is Import Errors, then this column will display a link to open and view the error report for the corresponding import that was not successful. It provides a list of all the errors that this import encountered. You can correct these errors and try again to complete the import. Following is a sample Benefit Rate Import Error Report.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Actions - If you want to delete an existing import in progress, you can click the Recycle Bin icon. If you select delete, you will receive a verification message stating Are you sure you want to delete this import? This cannot be undone.

  • If you click Yes, then the line item will be removed from the form.

  • If you click No you will remain in the form without any action.

New Import - If you want to initiate a new Benefit Rates Import using a predefined benefit rates import template, click this button which will take you to the Benefit Rates Import Setup & File Import screen. All the fields will be blank on that screen. You will need to fill up the necessary fields to set up and complete the import.

Past Imports

This section lists all the benefit rate imports completed successfully for the selected date range. By default the date range is a calendar month ending on the current date. You can manually change the date range. This section will display the last 7 completed imports at a glance on-screen for the selected date range. In case there are more than 7 completed imports for the selected date range, you will see a scroll bar on the right. Scroll to view all the completed imports for the selected date range.

Past Imports that are older than one year (since completion date) are automatically deleted and no longer display in the table.

The completed imports are sorted first by Date Completed and then by Name. The latest imports are listed at the top.

[Image: screenshot]

The information is displayed in a table that has the following columns:

  1. Name - This is the import name that you had provided for that benefit rate import.

  2. Type - This is the benefit rate type that you imported. This will be:

  • Premium Rates OR

  • Billing Rates

  1. Plan Used for Template - This is the Benefit Plan ID used for the import template.

  2. Date Completed - This is the date when the benefit rate was imported into PrismHR.

  3. Processed by User - This is the user ID of the user who completed the benefit rate import.

  4. Import File - This is the benefit rates import file that was used for the import. Following is a sample import file used for Billing Rates plan type:

[Image: screenshot]

The headers will vary depending on the plan type you are importing.

  1. Import Report - This link will provide you with the Benefit Rates Import Success Report for the import which shows a summary of Plans, records and line items imported that correlate with the total number of successful record imported as reported in the toast message.

[Image: screenshot]

The following is a sample Benefit Rates Import Success Report using the Import File above.

Benefit Rates Import Setup & File Import

Use this Benefit Rates Import Setup & File Import form to set up and import new benefit rates (premium or billing) into PrismHR using a predefined benefit rates import template. You also need to use this form to complete existing Imports in Progress.

Note:

  • You can only access this form from the Benefit Rates Import form.

  • You can click the New Import button on the Benefit Rates Import form to come to this form, OR,

  • You can click the Name link of an existing Import in Progress on the Benefit Rates Import form to come to this form.

Using the New Import button

When you click the New Import button on the Benefit Rates Import form, you come to this form. All fields on this form will be blank.

  1. Complete the following fields:

  • Import Name - Give the import a unique name that does not already exist in PrismHR to identify it.

  • If you try to provide an import name for a new benefit rate import which already exists in PrismHR, you will get an error message stating The Import Name entered has already been used. Import name must be unique.

  • The name can have alpha-numeric characters but cannot contain special characters. If you include special characters in the import name, you will get an error message stating The Import name cannot contain special characters.

  • The import name cannot contain spaces. If you enter an import name with spaces, you will get an error message stating Import Names cannot contain spaces.

  • Import names must contain at least 3 characters. If you enter an import name with less than three characters, you will get an error message stating Import Names must contain at least 3 characters.

  • Which Rate are you Importing? - Select one of the following benefit rate types from the following:

  • Premium Rates OR

  • Billing Rates

  • Plan ID - This link will only become active after you select a benefit rate type above. This will define the import template going forward.

  • You can either enter the Plan ID manually or click the Plan ID link and select a plan as your template builder based on pre-defined defaults and selectable filters.

  • If you click the Plan ID link you will see the Select Benefit Plan selector based on your selected benefit rate type.

Note: You cannot manually enter a Plan ID if for that Plan ID the Manual Calculation field is set to Coverage Entered Manually in the Group Benefit Plans form. Since these plans do not have rate tables, there are no rates that can be imported in Group Benefit Plans, and they cannot be supported in the Benefit Rate Import. If try to do it, you will get an error message stating Plan ID has Coverage & Premiums Entered Manually. Not supported for Import. These plans, however, will not show up when you are using the Select Benefit Plan selector.

Please note that:

  • If you manually enter a Plan ID and try to save the form without entering a benefit rate type, then you will get an error message stating Rate type selection is required.

  • You can only select an active plan for the import. If you select a plan that is terminated, you will get an error message stating Plan ID is Terminated. Not valid for Import.

  • If the Family Rate Premiums field under the Other Processing Parameters section on the Group Benefit Plans form is checked, then exclude family rates plans from the import. If not, you will get an error message stating Plan ID has Family Rated Premiums. Not supported for Import.

  • Medical, Dental and Vision plans are currently supported. If you select any other insurance class plans, you will get an error message stating Plan ID is [NAME] Insurance Class. Not supported for Import.

  • Plans for which the Manual Calculation field is set to Coverage & Premiums Entered Manually in the Group Benefits Plan form are excluded.

For Premium Rates import, the following is a sample selector which you can customize according to your needs:

[Image: screenshot]

For Billing Rates import, the following is a sample selector which you can customize according to your needs:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. You can click Cancel at this point to remove all the data in this form and return to the Benefit Rates Import form.

  2. Click Save to save your import template once you have provided a valid input for all the three required fields noted above. A line item is listed in the Imports in Progress section on the Benefit Rates Import form. Upon save, the Import Name field and the rate type become read only. However, you can still edit the Plan ID field. If you do so, you will receive a warning message stating Are you sure you want to change the plan this import is based on? It may affect the plans that can be included in this import. If an import file has been uploaded, it will be removed. You either click Yes or No accordingly.

  • If the Import Name field is blank, you will get an error message stating Import Names must contain at least 3 characters.

  • If a rate type is not selected, you will an error message stating Rate type selection is required.

  • If the Plan ID field is blank, you will get an error message stating Plan ID is required.

What is an Import Template Builder?

Based on the benefit plan that you enter in the Plan ID field, you can import numerous benefit plans that have the same setup.

For example, if the Plan ID used to define the template is a plan with Age Banded Medical Rates and Rate Groups for Premium Rates, then a plan with only Age Banded Medical Rates WOULD NOT be included in a Premium Rate Table but WOULD be included in a Billing Rate Table since Rate Groups for Premium Rates is not used for Billing Rates. If BOTH plans do not have any values checked, then these are considered to match.

For example, if you put in a medical Plan that is age banded, any medical, dental and vision plan that is age banded can be imported together. Please note, the benefit plans need to be an exact match. Using the prior example, it cannot be age banded and tobacco banded.

Once you save your import template, the following section shows up on screen where you will see a list of all plans that match the setup as the selected Plan ID. This table is a reference for all the different setups that can be. In our example above, we have selected a medical plan that is age banded, so that column is populated below.

Note: If you now try to change the Plan ID, you will receive a warning message stating Are you sure you want to change the plan this import is based on? It may affect the plans that can be included in this import. If an import file has been uploaded, it will be removed.

  • If you select No, then the Plan ID remains unaltered, and you can continue with the import process.

  • If you select Yes, then the Plan ID changes and the table of available plans that can be imported based on the plan selection also changes. This would affect what can be included in the import file.

  • The updated Plan ID will be saved to the import definition template.

  • The table of available plans will be updated based on the newly selected Plan ID.

  • The Premium and Billing Rate Template available via the links in the Import Template Builder will update based on the new Plan ID.

  • If there is an import file already uploaded, the file is removed from the import.

  • Since this is a change to the import, the Imports in Progress table on the Benefit Rate Import form is updated with Last Modified User and Last Modified Date.

  1. The file name will display in the Upload Billing Rates section.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click the Import Rates button to import the benefit rates into PrismHR. This button will not be visible until the import file has been uploaded. A job progress window opens showing the processing steps.
  1. — If the processing completes without errors, click Close to close the job progress window. When the import is successful, you will be returned to the Benefit Rates Import form and receive a confirmation message. The said import will be listed under the Past Imports section on the Benefit Rates Import form.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. — If the processing completes with errors, click Close to close the job progress window. The Benefit Rate Import Error Report opens up for the import showing all the errors preventing a successful import. You can correct all the listed errors in your import file, delete the existing import file on the system, upload the corrected import file and continue.
  1. Click Close to close this form at any time. If you close this form before successfully completing an import, then the import will be listed under the Imports in Progress section on the Benefit Rates Import form with the appropriate Status. You can click that import anytime to resume your import from where you left off.

Using the Name link under Imports in Progress

If the Status of the Import is:

  • Template Defined – Continue from Step 4 above.

  • Ready for Import - Continue from Step 8 above.

  • Import Errors - Make necessary corrections to your import file and continue from Step 4 above.

To validate what was imported, go to the Group Benefit Plans form. Enter the Benefit Plan ID for which you have imported the rates. Select Actions and then select Premium Rates or Billing Rates whichever is applicable. Then complete the information on the form that matches what you imported.

Data Import Tool

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024%2003Mar%20QR/BA_Data_Import_Tool_Enhancements_QR202403.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024 03Mar QR/BA_Data_Import_Tool_Enhancements_QR202403.htm

Data Import Tool

The following enhancements now reside in the Data Import Tool, which is available on the Operations|Import Processing menu.

New Import Template

A new import template, Eligible ZIP Codes, is now available. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use this import template to import eligible ZIP codes for the client to reduce the amount of manual work required.

Note: The Eligible ZIP Codes import template is only available for service providers.

To import this data and display an on-screen report:

  1. Select Eligible ZIP Codes from the Import Template menu.

  2. Enter or select a Plan ID.

  3. Click Find File to upload the file.

  4. After importing the file a message displays, “File content successfully uploaded and ready to be imported.” Click OK. The imported ZIP codes display and an Import button. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Import. After the import finishes a message displays, “File content successfully imported. View report for details.” Click OK. A Report button displays.

  2. Click Report. An on-screen report displays the imported ZIP codes and their location. (You can also download this report.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. As part of this import process, the imported ZIP codes now display in the Eligible Zip Codes form, which you can access by selecting Eligible Zip Codes on the Actions menu in the Group Benefit Plans form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following when using the Eligible ZIP Codes import template:

  • When you select a Plan ID, benefits plans that use networks do not display in the Select Benefit Plans list. In addition, benefit plans with a termination date equal to or less than the current date do not display in this list.

  • If you enter a Plan ID that already has eligible ZIP codes on record a warning displays, “Warning! Eligible ZIP codes are already on file for this plan. If you import, you will overwrite them. Do you want to continue?” Click Yes to continue.

  • If you import a ZIP code that does not exist a warning displays for each ZIP code that the system cannot validate, “Warning - Key <ZIP code> is not valid for ZIP codes.”

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Group Benefit Plans form cannot import data using the Eligible ZIP Codes import template.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Group Benefit Plans form can view the Eligible ZIP Codes import template, but cannot import data.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

Support for FSA/HSA/COM Offer Types

Previously, the system only supported offer types available on the Group Benefit Plans form when using the Plan Comparison Data import template. (This import template allows you to import benefit plan comparison information.)

The system now provides additional support for the FSA, HSA, and Commuter offer types available on the Flex Spend Account Types form.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration Guide.

Enhancement to Benefit Plan Setup Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024%2006Jun%20QR/BA-1316.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024 06Jun QR/BA-1316.htm

Enhancement to Benefit Plan Setup Form

A new field, Only apply to S-Corp Principal Employees, now displays in the Fringe Benefit Pay Codes panel on the Benefit Plan Setup form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

The Only apply to S-Corp Principal Employees field defines whether only S-Corp Principal employees will have the client benefit portion treated as a fringe benefit for the Fringe Benefit Pay Code. Otherwise, this portion is treated as a normal deduction.

Note: Note the following:

  • If you enable this field, on the Benefit Plan setup only employees who the system designates as an S-Corp Principal employee will have the client-paid portion of the benefit treated as a fringe benefit through the payroll process. (If they are not an S-Corp Principal employee then the employer portion is not treated as a fringe benefit.)

  • If you do not enable this field, on the Benefit Plan setup the system performs as usual and treats the client-paid portion of that benefit as a fringe benefit, assigning it to the defined fringe benefit Pay Code through the payroll process.

  • The system performs an additional validation during payroll calculation, which checks each employee who is enrolled in the benefit plan to determine if they are an S-Corp Principal. Employees enrolled in the benefit plan who the system designates as an S-Corp Principal must have the client paid portion of that benefit assigned to the defined fringe benefit pay code and listed in the Other Payments on their payroll voucher.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Benefits Administration User Guide.

Tab Order Updated in Benefit Forms

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024%2006Jun%20QR/BA-2773%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024 06Jun QR/BA-2773 (Epic).htm

Tab Order Updated in Benefit Forms

The tab order has been updated in the Benefit forms described below, so you can tab through all the fields in a logical order for data entry and avoid using the mouse.

The tab order now flows through each section in the correct sequence in their entirety before moving on to the next section. Also, within each section, you can now tab all the fields in the left column and then proceed to the next column on the right. If any field that has an associated field to the right of it comes next, before you move on to the next line and keep moving down. Once you have completed the button panel, you will be directed to the main navigation bar.

This enhancement affects the following forms:

  • Benefit Group Change: Tab order is from top to bottom of form.

Note: To tab in order through the entire form, you must enter or select an existing Employee ID.

  • Employee Dependents: Tab order is from top of section to bottom of section in the left column, then in the same order in the right column. For example, tabbing from the Middle Initial field in the bottom of the left column advances to the Birth Date field at the top of the right column.

Note: To tab in order through the entire form, you must enter or select an existing Employee ID, then select a Dependent ID or click New.

  • Employee Flexible Spending Accounts: Tab order is from top to bottom of form. If you enter or select an existing Employee ID and Plan Year and tab to the last line in the Elections grid, a new line displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  • Group Benefit Plans: Tab order is from top of section to bottom of section in the left column, then in the same order in the right column. For example, tabbing from the Rate Groups for Premium Rates field in the bottom of the left column advances to the Deduction Code field at the top of the right column.

  • Relationships: Tab order is from top to bottom of form. If you enter or select an existing Relationship Code and tab to the last line in the Plan Types grid, a new line displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  • Wellness Status Change: Tab order is from top to bottom of form.

Note: To tab in order through the entire form, you must enter or select an existing Employee ID.

New Rate Group Selector on the Benefit Plan Setup form

Now on the Benefit Plan Setup form, under the Group Benefits Setup section, when you click the link named:

  • The new selector will only display the active billing rate groups assigned to the Plan on the Benefit Plan Setup form which have an Effective Date tied to the Billing Rate Group.

  • Premium Rate Group:

  • The new selector will only display the active premium rate groups assigned to the Plan on the Benefit Plan Setup form which have an Effective Date tied to the Premium Rate Group.

  • Pending Rate Group:

Changes to Benefit Group History

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024%2006Jun%20QR/BA-2946%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024 06Jun QR/BA-2946 (Epic).htm

Changes to Benefit Group History

Previously, the Benefit Group History form did not keep a full history causing administrative challenges with future dated changes when manually updating the Benefit Group on the Employee Details form. PrismHR has implemented the following changes to mitigate this from this release:

  • With this release, a new utility called UTL.FIX.CURRENT.BENEFIT.GROUP, has been created that will write a Benefit Group History record for ALL employees and update the Benefit Group assigned to each employee on the date the utility runs. In addition, a utility script named UPDATE.ALL.HRPY.DBRUN.BA3299 was also created to run UTL.FIX.CURRENT.BENEFIT.GROUP on each UniData account. This utility will automatically run and update all employee benefit group history records in each account. This utility will however skip certain ‘non-critical’ accounts namely .TEMPL, .DEMO, .TEST in order to optimize processing time. If you have any questions or concerns please contact your customer service representative.

  • On the Employee Details form, under the Work tab, under the Assignments section, the hyperlink named Future Date has been removed. A new hyperlink named Change has been added beside the Beneft Group hyperlink. When you click Change, the Benefit Group Change form opens up in a modal. On the Benefit Group Change form, now you can change the date in the Benefit Group Start Date field. Click Save to update the information. This information will immediately update the Benefit Group History form as a result of the utility mentioned above. You can close the Benefit Group Change form and return to the Employee Details form.

For entering a past date in the Benefit Group Start Datefield:

  • If a Benefit Group History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the past date entered in the Benefit Group Start Date field, you will get a warning message stating A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. Do you wish to continue? On the warning message, when you click:

  • Yes - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form. When you click Save on the Benefit Group Change form, the prior benefit group history record will be replaced with the current data.

  • No - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form EXCEPT for the Benefit Group Start Date field which will remain blank. No benefit group history record will be written.

  • If a Benefit Group History record currently exists with an Effective Date greater than the past date entered in the Benefit Group Start Date field, you will get a warning message stating A future dated change record with an effective date equal to currently exists. Are you sure you want to continue? On the warning message, when you click:

  • Yes - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form. When you click Save on the Benefit Group Change form, the prior benefit group history record will be replaced with the current data.

  • No - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form EXCEPT for the Benefit Group Start Date field which will remain blank. No benefit group history record will be written.

  • If a Benefit Group History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the past date AND a Benefit Group History record exists with an Effective Date greater than the past date entered in the Benefit Group Start Date field, you will get a warning message stating A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. There is also a future dated change record with an effective date equal to . Do you wish to continue? On the warning message, when you click:

  • Yes - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form. When you click Save on the Benefit Group Change form, the prior benefit group history record will be replaced with the current data.

  • No - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form EXCEPT for the Benefit Group Start Date field which will remain blank. No benefit group history record will be written.

For entering a current date in the Benefit Group Start Datefield:

  • If a Benefit Group History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the current date entered in the Benefit Group Start Date field, you will get a warning message stating A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. Do you wish to continue? On the warning message, when you click:

  • Yes - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form. When you click Save on the Benefit Group Change form, the prior benefit group history record will be replaced with the current data. When you exit the Benefit Group Change form, the new Benefit Group will display immediately in the Benefit Group field on the Employee Details form, under the Work tab, under the Assignments section.

  • No - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form EXCEPT for the Benefit Group Start Date field which will remain blank. No benefit group history record will be written.

  • If a Benefit Group History record currently exists with an Effective Date greater than the current date entered in the Benefit Group Start Date field, you will get a warning message stating A future dated change record with an effective date equal to currently exists. Are you sure you want to continue? On the warning message, when you click:

  • Yes - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form. When you click Save on the Benefit Group Change form, the prior benefit group history record will be replaced with the current data.

  • No - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form EXCEPT for the Benefit Group Start Date field which will remain blank. No benefit group history record will be written.

  • If a Benefit Group History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the future date entered in the Benefit Group Start Date field, you will get a warning message stating A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. Do you wish to continue? On the warning message, when you click:

  • Yes - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form. When you click Save on the Benefit Group Change form, the prior benefit group history record will be replaced with the current data.

  • No - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form EXCEPT for the Benefit Group Start Date field which will remain blank. No benefit group history record will be written.

Are you sure you want to continue? On the warning message, when you click:

  • Yes - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form. When you click Save on the Benefit Group Change form, the prior benefit group history record will be replaced with the current data.

  • No - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form EXCEPT for the Benefit Group Start Date field which will remain blank. No benefit group history record will be written.

  • If a Benefit Group History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the future date AND a Benefit Group History record exists with an Effective Date greater than the future date entered in the Benefit Group Start Date field, you will get a warning message stating A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. There is also a future dated change record with an effective date equal to . Do you wish to continue? On the warning message, when you click:

  • Yes - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form. When you click Save on the Benefit Group Change form, the prior benefit group history record will be replaced with the current data.

  • No - The warning message will close. All previously entered information will be displayed on the Benefit Group Change form EXCEPT for the Benefit Group Start Date field which will remain blank. No benefit group history record will be written.

  • When an Import is used, the Benefit Group will now be written to the employee’s record using today’s date and a benefit group history record will be created immediately

  • When an API is used, the Benefit Group will be written to the employee’s record using today’s date and a benefit group history record will be created immediately.

  • When using the Bulk Change utility, the existing functionality will not change but a benefit group history record will be created immediately.

  • All New Hire processes (manual entry, Onboarding, Import, API) will trigger a Benefit Group History record creation using the Original Hire Date as the Effective Date assigned to the benefit history record.

  • When using the rehire process, the Benefit Group will be written to the employees record using the current system date as the Effective Date. If the Benefit Group was not changed when using the rehire process, the Benefit Group will still be updated to the employee’s record using the current system date as the Effective Date.

  • Note: Any changes made in the Employment Details panel and the Pay Details panel take effect immediately and do not abide by the date entered in the Rehire Date field in the Rehire panel. (Future dated changes are not supported. If you enter a future date, the system uses the current date.)

Other Enhancements

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024%2006Jun%20QR/Other%20Enhancements%20BA202406.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024 06Jun QR/Other Enhancements BA202406.htm

Other Enhancements

Benefit Adjustments Warning Range

You can now configure a system-level range of acceptable benefit adjustment amounts. If a range is specified, the system displays a warning when manual or imported benefit adjustment amounts fall outside the range.

Enter the values in the Benefit Adjustment Warning Range, located on the System Parameters form. The warning displays if the following fields contain a value outside the range:

  • Bill Amount

  • Employee Contribution

  • Insurance Cost

For more information, see the System Administration User Guide and the Payroll Administration User Guide.

JIRA # WSP-12, 13, 14

Enhancements to the Benefit Plan Setup Form

Most PrismHR forms support navigating from field to field with the Tab key. However, on this form, pressing Tab caused the cursor to jump around the page unexpectedly. The tabbing pattern was improved for this form so the cursor now advances in a logical order from field to field.

JIRA # WSP-16

Enhancements to the Group Benefit Plans Form

In the Carrier Code Maintenance panel of the Group Benefit Plans form, you can now include the Carrier Policy ID.

Note: Note: The Carrier Policy ID and Carrier Group Number are distinct identifiers.

JIRA # WSP-25

Enhancements to the Retirement Adjustments Import

The Retirement Adjustments Import now applies the same validations as the Retirement Register Adjustment form, and generates the same kind of errors. This process creates a new voucher for each valid entry on the import, and updates the appropriate retirement registers and reports.

In addition, the import Preview and Sample Header File were updated to reflect the new optional import columns.

[Image: Updated preview panel for the Retirement Adjustments Import, with new and renamed columns.]

The table summarizes the changes to the columns.

Column Title Details

Employee Changed from: SSN/EE ID
Employer ID New
Plan Changed from: Retirement Plan ID
Adjustment Date (MM/DD/YYYY) Changed from: Trans Date (MM/DD/YYYY)

ROTH Catch-up Contribution (Optional) New

Successor Catch-up Deferral (Optional) New
Successor ROTH Deferral (Optional) New
Successor ROTH Catch-up Deferral (Optional) New
Loan (Optional) New
Loan Payment (Optional) New

JIRA # WSP-15, 18

New Wash Rule Option “End of Month”

On the Benefit Plan Setup form, the Wash Rule Date On/Before now supports an option called “End of Month”. If selected and an employee is enrolled in a group benefit plan mid-month, the system creates benefits charges for the entire month.

Note: Note: During terminations, if the client benefit plan’s Coverage Ends On option is set to “End of Month Following Termination Date”, the new wash rule setting has no impact. However, any other Coverage Ends On option will cause the system to generate a full month’s charge upon termination.

JIRA # WSP-313

Bug Fixes

Jira # Issue Resolution
WSP-27 For group benefit plans with Insurance Class set to “Bond”, an issue with two different forms in the Actions menu (Billing Rates and Premium Rates) prevented deleting the Effective Date value on those forms. This is fixed and the Effective Date now deletes successfully.
WSP-340 The Retirement Adjustments Import did not respect user-level client access security, allowing data imports to prohibited clients. This is fixed. Now, users can only import adjustments for clients allowed by their client access setup.

  • Employment Status - This filter has the following drop-down options:

Changes to the Client Benefit Plan Defaults form

The layout of this form has been completely changed. The purpose of this form is to allow you to set up benefit plans in bulk for multiple clients at once. You can create templates for repeated use or set up a template for one time use. This makes it convenient for customers who bring in new clients and have standard plans for them. You will not have to go to the Benefit Plan Setup form for each client to set up those standard benefit plans but can do that in bulk instead using the Client Benefit Plan Defaults form.

Following is a sample of the Client Benefit Plan Defaults form.

[Image: screenshot]

Once a default plan is selected here the Last Updated date and time for the default plan template will display.
Plan ID If you are using the Saved Plan Defaults field above, then this field will be pre-populated with the selected plans. You can make changes like add plans or delete them. Alternative Contribution Rate Group field validations added to the Benefit Rules form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024%2009Sep%20QR/BA-3104%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024 09Sep QR/BA-3104 (Epic).htm

Alternative Contribution Rate Group field validations added to the Benefit Rules form

We have now added the following validations to the Alternative Contribution Rate Group field on the Benefit Rules form:

  • An Alternate Contribution Plan is required before selecting an Alternative Contribution Rate Group. This information is also provided as a tooltip for this field on the form.

  • If you try to enter a value in the Alternative Contribution Rate Group field when the Alternate Contribution Plan is blank, then you will get an error message stating An Alternate Contribution Plan has not been defined. The Alternative Contribution Rate Group will be cleared out. Click OK to acknowledge the message and you will be returned to the Benefit Rules form with all previously entered data populated except for the value in the Alternative Contribution Rate Group field which is cleared out.

  • When selecting the Alternative Contribution Rate Group hyperlink, the selector will only populate Rate Groups based on the Alternate Contribution Plan defined.

  • Any existing value in the Alternative Contribution Rate Group field will remain visible regardless of whether an Alternate Contribution Plan had been defined earlier or not. You can delete the existing Alternative Contribution Rate Group value.

  • If an Alternate Contribution Plan has been defined but you have not entered any value in the Alternative Contribution Rate Group field, upon Save, a message will display stating An Alternate Contribution Plan has been defined which requires an Alternative Contribution Rate Group to be selected. Click OK to acknowledge the message and you will be returned to the Benefit Rules form to enter a value in the Alternative Contribution Rate Group field.

Changes to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024%2009Sep%20QR/BA-3107%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024 09Sep QR/BA-3107 (Epic).htm

Changes to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form

The following changes were made to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form which you can access from the

[Image: screenshot]

menu on the System Parameters form.

  • A new hyperlink named Copy Rates has been added to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form. This allows you the convenience of copying existing rates from one tax year to another instead of manually completing the table. Only users with Full Access to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form will be able to see the Copy Rates option.

  • Once you enter a Tax Year (say 2023) on the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form, the Copy Rates option becomes visible. You can also click the Tax Year hyperlink to select a tax year. If you manually enter a non-existing tax year then the Copy Rates option will not display. Click the Copy Rates hyperlink. A new selector named Copy Tax Rates opens as shown below.

  • On the Copy Tax Rates selector, the From field is already pre-populated with the tax year (2023) entered above. On the To field, select the tax year from the drop-down to which you want to copy the tax rates. You will see the current tax year and subsequent two tax years in the drop-down. Select 2024 if you want to copy the 2023 tax rates to 2024. Once you select a value for To field from the drop-down, the Copy button becomes selectable.

  • Click Copy. A warning message opens stating Warning! Overwrite existing tax rates for 2024?

  • Click Yes - The 2023 tax rates are copied for the 2024 tax year in the system. You will receive a confirmation message stating Tax rates successfully copied. Do you want to view the tax rates for 2024?

  • Click Yes - The 2023 tax rates are copied to 2024. The Copy Tax Rates selector closes and you return to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form. The tax year now reflects 2024 instead of 2023.

  • Click No - The 2023 tax rates are copied to 2024. The Copy Tax Rates selector closes and you return to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form. The tax year now reflects 2023.

  • Click No - The 2023 tax rates are not copied to 2024. You return to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form. The tax year reflects 2023.

  • Click Close - The 2023 tax rates are not copied to 2024. You return to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form. The tax year reflects 2023.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note:

If you pull up an existing tax year record (say 2023), make changes but do not save the record and click the Copy Rates hyperlink, you will receive a warning message stating There are unsaved changes that will not be copied. Do you wish to continue?

  • Click Yes - The last saved record for the From Tax Year selected will be used when coping rates to the To Tax Year. Unsaved changes on the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form will be ignored.

  • Click No - You return to the Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form with all the unsaved changes.

The Tax Rates for Taxable Life Coverage form now also has the following buttons:

Cancel - Click Cancel to clear the form at any time. All unsaved changes will be lost.

Close - This button is displayed when this form is opened in a modal. Click Close to close the form. All unsaved changes will be lost.

========================================================================

Calculate Safe Harbor 2 Match automatically during New Hire

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024%2009Sep%20QR/BA-3127%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024 09Sep QR/BA-3127 (Epic).htm

Calculate Safe Harbor 2 Match automatically during New Hire

Given that an employee is hired into a Client which has a Retirement Plan that is not setup to auto enroll but has a Safe Harbor 2 Match or a non-elective match defined, during the new hire process, an eligibility calculation will be triggered which then creates an Eligible Unenrolled Retirement Plan enrollment record for the applicable employees with an effective date that coincides with their calculated eligibility date. Once the first payroll processes that coincides with their eligibility date, the record will be flipped to an Active Enrollment and the match taken.

The setups that will trigger the auto enroll of the Safe Harbor 2 / Non Elective matches are:

  • Match Logic Type = Safe Harbor 2

  • Match Logic Type = Traditional, Layered, Safe Harbor 1 AND if Calculate Safe Harbor 2 Non-Elective Contribution in addition is flagged

  • Match logic Type = Traditional, Layered, Safe Harbor 1 AND if ‘Non-Elective Rate’ has a value input

========================================================================

60-63 Catch Up

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024%2009Sep%20QR/BA-3398%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024 09Sep QR/BA-3398 (Epic).htm

60-63 Catch Up

The Secure 2.0 Act includes a new provision taking effect from January 1, 2025 where employees turning between 60 and 63 during the tax year are provided a higher catchup contribution limit. PrismHR now supports this feature.

On the Tax Year Limits Maintenance form (System Parameters>Actions>Tax Year Limits) AND on the Retirement Plans form, under the Plan Year Deferral Limits section a new column named 60-63 Catch Up is introduced after the Catch Up Limit column.

You will be able to enter and save value in this field if you have full access to the forms.

This field is optional.

This field will only accept numerical values.

  • The 60-63 Catch Up amount must be equal to or greater than the value entered in the corresponding Catch Up Limit field. If not, you will receive an error message stating Amount must be equal to or greater than Catch Up Limit.

  • The Catch Up Limit amount must be equal to or less than the value entered in the corresponding 60-63 Catch Up field. If not, you will receive an error message stating Amount must be equal to or less than 60-63 Catch Up.

  • If the Catch Up Limit field is empty, any value in the 60-63 Catch-Up field will present an error stating 60-63 Catch-Up limits must be defined.

========================================================================

Changes to the Employee Benefit History form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024%2009Sep%20QR/WSP-344.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024 09Sep QR/WSP-344.htm

Changes to the Employee Benefit History form

Previously, the Employee Benefit History form did not capture the complete benefit coverage history sequence. For example, when an employee waived coverage, then elected Employee Only Coverage, and then changed to Employee and Spouse coverage, then terminated coverage, then elected Family coverage, then terminated employment etc. Besides, if an active employee was terminated and then rehired to become active again, the Employee Benefit History form did not demonstrate the gap in coverage. It appeared as if the employee was having continuous coverage from the original Coverage Starts date.

PrismHR has now implemented a common utility program to generate the employee benefit history records that will solve the above issues.

Note: Note: You must DELETE the terminated record and create a new active, eligible, or waived record for the history to display. This will allow the record to reflect the accurate start date for the latest active record.

On the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, after you have selected an Employee and a Benefit Plan, under the

[Image: screenshot]

menu, click History to open the Employee Benefit History form.

[Image: screenshot]

From the above example, every blank status denotes an enrollment. The other statuses like Terminated, Waived etc. are self explanatory which show different Coverage Starts date.

As earlier, you can click on the different Sequences to view the status in detail on the Employee Benefit History Detail form.

Note: Note: Currently, COBRA enrollments & deletions are not being captured by this utility.

JIRA # BA-3822

Now you cannot delete a benefit plan using the Benefit Plan Setup form if there are associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records for the client for the selected Plan ID that have a status of Active, Terminated, or COBRA as this will orphan the associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records and can cause payroll errors along with other issues.

  • If you try to delete a benefit plan from the Benefit Plan Setup form and if there are associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records for the client for the selected Plan ID that have a status of Active, Terminated, or COBRA, you will receive an error stating This plan cannot be deleted. There are employees assigned to this benefit plan with enrollment history. Example: Employee Enrollment for Employee ID [XXXXX] and Effective Date [XX/XX/XXXX].

  • If you try to delete a benefit plan from the Benefit Plan Setup form and if there are associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records for the client for the selected Plan ID that have a status of Pending, Waived, or Eligible, you will receive a warning stating There are employees assigned to this benefit plan with an enrollment status of pending, waived and/or eligible. Do you wish to continue?

  • Click Yes to delete the selected Plan ID.

  • Click No to return to the Benefit Plan Setup form with the selected Plan ID and associated data populated.

You can only delete a benefit plan from the Benefit Plan Setup form if there are no associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records for the client for the selected Plan ID that have a status of Active, Terminated, or COBRA.

JIRA # BA-3823

Changes to the Benefit Rules form

  • Now you cannot delete the sole Benefit Rule Effective Date for a Benefit Group having a specified Benefit Plan if there associated Employee Benefit Enrollment records for the Benefit Group and that specified Benefit Plan with a status of Active or COBRA. This action will orphan the associated records and can cause payroll errors along with other issues. If you try to delete it, you will receive an error message stating This benefit rule cannot be deleted. There are employees using this benefit rule with active enrollments. Example: Employee Enrollment for Employee ID [XXXXX] and Effective Date [XX/XX/XXXX].

  • If it is not the sole Benefit Rule Effective Date for that Benefit Group having that Benefit Plan, OR there are no active enrollments associated with the benefit rule, then you can delete it.

JIRA # BA-3932

Changes to the Benefit Plan Setup form

New fields added

As part of the SECURE 2.0 Act, a new auto-enrollment requirement goes into effect on January 1, 2025, giving employers time to prepare and update their plans to comply with new regulations. New 401(k) and 403(b) plans established after the passing of SECURE 2.0 (December 29, 2022) must automatically enroll all eligible employees at a default contribution rate between 3 and 10%. In addition to auto-enrollment at a default contribution rate, plans must also automatically escalate contributions by 1% each year until they reach a predetermined rate by the employer (between 10 and 15%).

Note: Note: Though we put in the fields, but there is not yet any logic tied to these. No auto escalation will occur at this time. This is prep work to allow Service Providers to begin entry of these provisions prior to the effective date.

[Image: screenshot]

On the Benefit Plan Setup form, after you select the Plan Class as Retirement, and after you have checked the Auto Enrollment field, the following additional fields will display:

Field Name Description
Auto Escalator This field will only display if the Auto Enrollment field is checked for a Retirement Plan. - Unchecked - (Default) Plans will not automatically escalate contributions annually. - Checked - In addition to auto-enrollment at a default contribution rate, plans will automatically escalate contributions by 1% each year until they reach a predetermined rate by the employer (between 10 and 15%).
  • Unchecked - (Default) Plans will not automatically escalate contributions annually.
  • Checked - In addition to auto-enrollment at a default contribution rate, plans will automatically escalate contributions by 1% each year until they reach a predetermined rate by the employer (between 10 and 15%). | Auto Escalator Max Percent | This field becomes visible only after the Auto Enrollment field is checked. However, this field becomes editable only after the Auto Escalator field is checked. Enter any value between 10-15 (including up to 2 decimal places), which is the maximum predetermined benefit rate percentage decided by the employer for that client. - If the Auto Escalator field is checked, then this field is mandatory. if you do enter a value, you will receive an error stating Auto Escalator Max Percent is required when using Auto Escalator. - If the value entered is outside the permitted range, you will receive a warning message stating Auto Escalator Max Percent must be between 10%-15% when using Auto Escalator. |
  • If the Auto Escalator field is checked, then this field is mandatory. if you do enter a value, you will receive an error stating Auto Escalator Max Percent is required when using Auto Escalator.
  • If the value entered is outside the permitted range, you will receive a warning message stating Auto Escalator Max Percent must be between 10%-15% when using Auto Escalator. JIRA # BA-3811

JIRA # BA-3812

Changes to the Client Details form

The Secure 2.0 Act includes a new provision taking effect January 1, 2025, where employees turning between 60 and 63 during the tax year are provided with a higher catchup contribution limit. Like “normal” catchup, this is expected to be a standard, but not a guaranteed plan feature. This means that you need the capacity to “turn off” this functionality at the client level.

PrismHR now supports this requirement.

[Image: screenshot]

On the Client Details form, under the Benefits tab, under the Group Benefits section, a new field named Disable Accelerated Catchup? has been added.

  • Unchecked - (Default) Catchup 60-63 option is available at the client level

  • Checked - Catchup 60-63 option is disabled at the client level

Changes to the Benefit Adjustments form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024%2011Nov%20QR/BA-3645%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/2024 11Nov QR/BA-3645 (Epic).htm

Changes to the Benefit Adjustments form

[Image: screenshot]

  • A new filter named Filter By Status is added to the Benefit Adjustments form to assist you with the usability of the form and provide a higher level of ‘point of need’ data. Using this filter, you can filter the list of benefit adjustments for the employee displayed on screen. You can choose one of the following dropdown options:

  • All - To list all benefit adjustments for the employee.

  • Outstanding - To list all benefit adjustments for the employee where Cycles Billed is less than Cycles.

  • Complete - To list all benefit adjustments for the employee where Cycles Billed is equal to Cycles.

  • A checkbox has been added to the left of the header named Benefit Plan. You now have the option to select this checkbox to select all benefit adjustments for the employee in bulk which have zero Cycles Billed.

  • A checkbox has been added to the left of each benefit adjustment for the employee which have zero Cycles Billed. You now have the option to select one or more to delete the selected benefit adjustment/s only.

  • The Delete button will by default remain disabled. It will get enabled only if you try to either delete in bulk or delete selected benefit adjustments for the employee which have zero Cycles Billed. Once you click Delete, you will receive a confirmation stating Adjustments will be deleted. Are you sure?

  • Click Yes to delete the selected adjustments and return to the Benefit Adjustments form with the updated adjustment list.

  • Click No to return to the Benefit Adjustments form without any changes. The selections remain.

JIRA # BA-3724, BA-3893

Changes to the Adjustment Details form

[Image: screenshot]

  • When a benefit adjustment is pulled via the payroll process and the Cycles Billed value is updated to the next number in the sequence, the following corresponding information is now listed in the new table on the right of the form:

  • Voucher # - You can click this hyperlink to open the Employee Voucher in a modal. You can navigate to the Benefits tab to view the adjustment details.

  • Pay Date - The Pay Date of the Employee Voucher.

  • Batch # - The Payroll Number of the Employee Voucher.

  • New tooltips are provided for the following fields:

  • Cycles - This is the number of future payroll cycles to apply this adjustment.

  • Cycles Billed - This is the number of times this adjustment has been applied to the employee’s paycheck so far. It is not recommended that this value be changed.

  • The following fields have been renamed:

  • The earlier Comments field has been changed to Comment with no change in functionality.

  • The earlier B/R Adj Amount field has been changed to B/R Adjustment with no change in functionality.

  • The following two fields are also now available on the Adjustment Details form:

  • Net Inv Effect

  • Ref. Number

  • When an adjustment record already has cycles billed, the Cycles Billed field for this adjustment will be read only. The Delete button will also remain disabled for such adjustments. This is because manually modifying the value in the Cycles Billed field will impact the number of adjustment runs, and therefore the total billed. The Delete button will remain active only if the Cycles Billed field for this adjustment is zero.

menu. On the User Roles form, the Loans Details / EMPLOYEE.401K.PLANS.LOANS*INQUIRY is no longer an available option for Service Provider or Worksite Manager user role types.

New Quicklink added

A new Quicklink to the Employee Retirement Plan Register form is added on the top right of the Retirement Plan Enrollment form, which will display only after the Employee and the Retirement Plan fields are selected on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form. This provides ease of access to the Employee Retirement Plan Register form for the selected employee directly from the Retirement Plan Enrollment form.

[Image: screenshot]

When you click the Quicklink to the Employee Retirement Plan Register form from the Retirement Plan Enrollment form, the Employee Retirement Plan Register form opens in a modal where:

  • The Employee ID field is auto-populated from the Retirement Plan Enrollment form.

  • The Plan ID dropdown will have all the retirement plans for the employee selected on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form. You can select one of them.

  • The Employee Retirement Plan Register modal form behaves the same way as the regular Employee Retirement Plan Register form. You can select the other fields as necessary to view the relevant information.

  • Click Cancel to clear this modal form. The Employee ID field will not be cleared.

  • Click Close to close this modal.

Note: Note: This Quicklink will not be visible if you do not have access to the Employee Retirement Plan Register form.

JIRA # BA-3749, BA-3867

New Sections added

After the Employee Overrides/Deferral section, the following two new sections are added to the Retirement Plan Enrollment form.

  • Employee Retirement Loans

  • Retirement Register Adjustments

[Image: screenshot]

Employee Retirement Loans section

Now you can directly access existing employee retirement loan information for the selected Employee, for the Retirement Plan field selected on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form and processed for the selected client using this form. If an employee has been in more than one retirement plan, only those Employee Retirement Loans that were processed for the selected Retirement Plan field will display. This section lists the employee retirement loans for the selected employee in an ascending order by Loan No. by default. This grid has the following columns:

  • Loan No.

  • Loan Amount

  • Loan Date

  • Deduction Start Date

  • Payment Amount

  • Pay Back Amount

  • Override Payment Amount

  • Override From Pay Date

  • Override To Pay Date

  • Paid Back To Date

  • Balance Due

You can click on any of the column headers in the grid to sort the retirement loans as you choose.

  • Click a Loan No. hyperlink from the list to open the loan details on the Employee Retirement Loans modal form with all corresponding data prepopulated that is tied to the Loan No. selected.

  • The Loan Number, Employee and the Retirement Plan fields are read only and auto-populated from the Retirement Plan Enrollment form.

  • You can edit the other fields for this retirement loan.

  • Click Save to save the changes to this retirement loan.

  • Click Delete to delete this retirement loan. After deleting the retirement loan, it will not appear in the list under the Employee Retirement Loans section on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form.

  • Click Close to close the Employee Retirement Loans modal form and return to the Retirement Plan Enrollment form. Any unsaved changes will be lost.

  • Click the Set up new loan hyperlink to set up a new retirement loan for the selected employee on the Employee Retirement Loans modal form.

  • The Loan Number is prepopulated with a system generated number. You cannot edit this.

  • The Employee and the Retirement Plan fields are read only and auto-populated from the Retirement Plan Enrollment form You cannot edit this.

  • Enter the other required fields for this new retirement loan for this employee.

  • Click Save to save the new retirement loan for the employee. After saving the new retirement loan, it will appear in the list under the Employee Retirement Loans section on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form.

  • Click Delete to delete this new retirement loan.

  • Click Close to close the Employee Retirement Loans modal form Retirement Plan Enrollment form. Any unsaved changes will be lost.

JIRA # BA-3746, BA-3857, BA-3948, BA-3880

Retirement Register Adjustments section

Now you can access existing employee retirement register adjustment information for the selected Employee, for the Retirement Plan field selected on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form and processed for the selected client using this form. If an employee has been in more than one retirement plan, only those Retirement Register Adjustments that were processed for the selected Retirement Plan field will display. This section lists the existing employee retirement register adjustments in an ascending order by Transaction No. by default. This grid has the following columns:

  • Transaction No.

  • Transaction Date

  • Voucher Number

  • Annotation

You can click on any of the column headers in the grid to sort the retirement register adjustments as you choose.

  • Click a Transaction No. hyperlink from the list to open the retirement register adjustment details on the Retirement Register Adjustment modal form with all corresponding data prepopulated that is tied to the Transaction No. selected.

  • The Transaction, Employee, Employer ID and the Plan fields are read only and auto-populated from the Retirement Plan Enrollment form.

  • You can edit the other fields for this retirement register adjustment.

  • Click Save to save the changes to this retirement register adjustment.

  • Click Close to close the Retirement Register Adjustment modal form and return to the Retirement Plan Enrollment form. Any unsaved changes will be lost.

  • Click the New transaction hyperlink to set up a new retirement register adjustment for the selected employee on the Retirement Register Adjustment modal form.

  • The Transaction is prepopulated with a system generated number. You cannot edit this.

  • The Employee, Employer ID and the Plan fields are read only and auto-populated from the Retirement Plan Enrollment form You cannot edit this.

  • Enter the other required fields for this new retirement register adjustment for this employee.

  • Click Save to save the new retirement register adjustment for the employee. After saving the new retirement register adjustment, it will appear in the list under the Retirement Register Adjustments section on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form.

  • Click Close to close the Retirement Register Adjustment modal form and return to the Retirement Plan Enrollment form. Any unsaved changes will be lost.
