Changes to the Data Import Tool form

A new Import Template named Offer Types is added to the Data Import Tool form as shown below. Use this option to update only the Offer Types field for existing Benefit Plan IDs on the Group Benefit Plans form. If you try to modify any other field using this process, you will receive an error.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. To access this form, click [Image: screenshot] (Back Office). Under Operations|Import, click Data Import Tool.

  2. Select Offer Types from the Import Template dropdown.

  3. Click the Download Data File hyperlink to download the sample header file. The header file will have the four columns under the File Format tab as shown in the picture above. Fill up the necessary data for all the Benefit Plan IDs for which you want to update the Offer Type to build your Import file. If you want to update the Offer Type for all such Benefit Plan IDs in bulk that do not have an associated offer type, then select the checkbox named Prepopulate file (all plans with BLANK Offer Type). A csv file will get downloaded to your system prepopulated with all the Benefit Plan IDs that do not have an Offer Type.

  4. Click Find File to open the File Upload dialog box.

  5. Click Add Files in the File Upload dialog box.

  6. Select the specified Import File from your system that you have created. Once selected the Import File will display in the File Upload dialog box.

  7. Click Start Upload to upload the file.

  8. Click Close on the File Upload dialog box.

  9. The uploaded Import File name will display under the File Name field on the form. The content of the file will display under File Content tab. Errors if any will display in the Messages tab. Correct the errors and redo the process.

  10. Click Import to import the content into PrismHR.

  11. Click Report to display the Imported Offer Types Report. The Import Status field will tell you if that Offer Type for that Plan ID was imported or not. If not, then the Comments field will tell you the reason.

Once the import is successful, the Offer Type field on the Group Benefit Plans form will be updated for the plans contained in the Import File.

  • Vision (VIS)

New Benefit Salary Maintenance form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025%2003Mar%20QR/BA-3590%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025 03Mar QR/BA-3590 (Epic).htm

New Benefit Salary Maintenance form

A new form named Benefit Salary Maintenance has been introduced. Use this form to add an effective date to change employee Benefit Salary and track historical Benefit Salary changes. Thus managing changes to Benefits Salary can be done proactively without real-time changes being necessary for Benefit calculation accuracy.

To access this form, click HR. Under HR|Action, click Benefit Salary Maintenance.

The form contains the fields listed below:

  • Employee- Hyperlink to select the employee.

  • Current Annual Pay Rate- The current annual pay rate of the selected employee.

  • Current Rate Effective Date- The date from which the current rate for annual pay applies to the selected employee.

  • Current Benefit Salary- The current Benefit Salary of the selected employee.

  • New Benefit Salary- New Benefit Salary that you want to add for the selected employee.

  • Benefit Salary Start Date- The start date from when you want to apply the updated employee benefit salary.

You can save or modify the benefit salary and effective date.

  • Click Save to update the Benefit Salary and its effective date. It also updates the current data under the Pay tab on the Employee Details form.

  • Click Cancel to clear this form at any time.

[Image: screenshot]

JIRA # BA-4290, BA-4371

New Benefit Salary History Section

A new section named Benefit Salary History section has been added to streamline the process of viewing employee’s benefit salary information.

The current and future dates under the Date Effective column are hyperlinks. Click any link to edit the selected Benefit Salary record and add a new effective date.

  • Click Save to save the selected benefit salary record with the updated changes.

  • Click Cancel to clear the selected New Effective Date.

  • Click Close to close the modal form and return to the Benefit Salary Maintenance form without making changes to the selected benefit salary record.

JIRA # BA-4285, BA-4286

On the New Hire form, under the Pay Details section, if you enter a value in the Benefits Calculation Salary field, then that value populates the Benefit Salary field under the Pay tab of the Employee Details form, which creates a new history record for that Benefit Salary in the Benefit Salary History section.

JIRA # BA-4399

Changes to the Rehire form

On the Rehire form, when you select an employee to rehire and save the form, then if the employee had a historical benefit salary record, the rehire process will create a new Benefit Salary History record to match the previous Benefit Salary amount with the current date’s effective date. Also, if a new Benefit Salary History record is created in the rehire process, an alert notification stating The employee’s benefit salary was reinstated as part of the rehire process. Review benefit salary history for accuracy. is displayed.

JIRA # BA-4310

Validations for the Effective Dates

The following validations have been added while selecting Past/Current/Future effective dates for a Benefit Salary History record:

  • When you enter Past date as the effective date:
  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the past date entered in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. Do you wish to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to save the date selected for the Benefit Salary Start Date field.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date greater than the past date entered in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A future dated change record with an effective date equal to currently exists. Are you sure you want to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to save the new history record with the new effective data.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the past date and a Benefit Salary History record exists with an Effective Date greater than the past date entered in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. There is also a future dated change record with an effective date equal to . Do you wish to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to replace the prior history record with the same effective date with the current data.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  • When you enter Current date as the effective date:

  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the current date in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. Do you wish to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to save the date selected for the Benefit Salary Start Date field. The newly added Benefit Salary will display immediately in the Benefit Salary field under the Pay tab of the Employee Details form.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date greater than the current date entered in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A future dated change record with an effective date equal to currently exists. Are you sure you want to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to create the new history record with the new effective data. The newly added Benefit Salary will display immediately in the Benefit Salary field under the Pay tab of the Employee Details form.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the current date and a Benefit Salary History record exists with an Effective Date greater than the current date entered in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. There is also a future dated change record with an effective date equal to . Do you wish to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to replace the prior history record with the same effective date with the current data. The newly added Benefit Salary will display immediately in the Benefit Salary field under the Pay tab of the Employee Details form.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  • When you enter Future date as the effective date:

  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the future date in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. Do you wish to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to replace the prior history record with the current data once you save the form.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date greater than the future date entered in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A future dated change record with an effective date equal to currently exists. Are you sure you want to continue? is displayed.

Note: If there are multiple future dates, the warning message uses the next available pending future date.

  • Click Yes to save the effective date and create the new history with the new effective data once you save the form.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

  1. — If a Benefit Salary History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the future date and a Benefit Salary History record exists with an Effective Date greater than the future date entered in the Benefit Salary Start Date field, then an alert message stating, A change record with an effective date equal to already exists. If you continue the existing record will be replaced. There is also a future dated change record with an effective date equal to . Do you wish to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to replace the prior history record with the current data once you save the form.

  • Click No to leave the Benefit Salary Start Date field blank.

New Benefit Utilities form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025%2003Mar%20QR/BA-3592%20&%20BA-3898%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025 03Mar QR/BA-3592 & BA-3898 (Epic).htm

New Benefit Utilities form

A new form named Benefit Utilities has been introduced to manage Benefit related utilities.

[Image: screenshot]

To access this form, click Back Office. Under Operations|Utility Processing, click Benefit Utilities.

The form has the following filter:

  • Utility- This filter has the following drop-down options:

  • Select - This is the default option.

  • Manage Orphaned Benefit Records - Select this filter to display the Orphaned Record Type filter, which has the following drop-down options:

  • Select - This is the default option.

  • Plan Types - The orphaned records due to missing Group Benefit Plan Types code.

  • SH2 Auto Enroll - Select this filter to identify the existing employees that are eligible for Safe Harbor 2 Match that do not have an active Retirement Plan Enrollment record.

  • Click Search to get the results based on your filter selection.

  • Click Cancel to clear this form at any time.

Manage Orphaned Benefit Records Filter

When you select the Manage Orphaned Benefit Records, based on the Orphaned Record Type filter that follows, you can choose the Client ID and the Benefit Plan ID from the respective tables that is displayed in the Report Filters section.

  • Client ID - This field is optional. Leave this field blank for this report to run for all clients. If you want to restrict this report to run for selected clients, enter their Client IDs here or click the Client ID link and select them from the Select Clients dialog box.

  • Benefit Plan ID - This field is optional. Leave this field blank for this report to run for all the benefit plans. If you want to restrict this report to run for selected benefit plans, enter the Benefit Plan IDs here or click the Benefit Plan ID link and select them from the Select Benefit Plan dialog box.

JIRA # BA-4354, BA-4355, BA-4518

Select Orphaned Record Type as Plan Types and then click Search. The list of orphaned records caused by deleting the Group Benefit Plan Type are displayed. The list of orphaned records displayed in the Results section helps you to reconcile the records.

The Results section displays the following columns:

  • File Name - Name of the file. In this scenario, it is BENEFIT.PLANS.

  • Employee ID - Unique ID of the employee.

  • Client ID - Unique ID of the client to which the employee is associated with.

  • Benefit Plan ID - The Benefit Plan ID in which the employee is enrolled.

  • Billing Rate Group - The Billing Rate Group of the employee.

  • Premium Rate Group - The Premium Rate Group that the employee is assigned to.

  • Network ID - The network ID.

  • Effective Date - The effective date from which the benefit plan was active.

  • Plan Type - The type of the plan.

  • Orphaned Reason - Indicates the reason the record was orphaned. In this scenario, it was due to the deletion of the Group Benefit Plan Type.

[Image: screenshot]

JIRA # BA-4404

SH2 Auto Enroll Filter

When you select the SH2 Auto Enroll filter, the Report Filters section is displayed. Here, you can choose the Client ID and the Retirement Plan ID selectors and select the clients, or the retirement plans the employees are enrolled in. You can also leave these selectors blank if you want the search results to appear for all clients and all retirement plans.

Now, click Search. A job control runs. Once the job control process is completed, click Close to view the list of eligible employees for Safe Harbor 2 Match that do not have an active Retirement Plan Enrollments records in the Results section.

[Image: screenshot]

The Results section displays the following columns:

  • Client ID - Unique ID of the client with which the employee is associated.

  • Employee Name - Name of the employee.

  • Retirement Plan ID - The retirement plans to which the employees are enrolled.

  • Status - Status of the retirement plan.

  • Status Date - The status date.

  • Eligible For Match - If the employee is eligible for Safe Harbor 2 Match.

  • Match Starts On - The date on which the eligibility for Safe Harbor 2 Match starts.

  • Loan Payment Cycles - The Loan payment cycles.

  • Retirement Benefit Group - The retirement benefit group in which the employee is enrolled in.

  • Catch-Up Starts At Limit - If the employee is eligible for catch-up.

  • Effective Date - The effective date from which the retirement plan was active.

Select the employees that you want to update the retirement plans for and click Update. Based on the number of records you have selected, a confirmation message stating, Retirement Plan Enrollments will be created. Are you sure? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to create an eligible retirement plan enrollment record. Once the retirement plan enrollment record is created, then the payroll process will update these records to Active.

  • Click No to remain on the form.

[Image: screenshot]

Under the Group Benefit Plans section, a new field, named PEO Master Plan, which is a checkbox has been introduced. This field is used as an indicator to identify a Group Benefit Plan as being one of the PEO’s Master Benefit Plans.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025%2003Mar%20QR/BA-3930%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025 03Mar QR/BA-3930 (Epic).htm

Validations added to the Group Benefit Plans form

The following validations are now added to the Group Benefit Plans form:

  • When saving the form, if states are defined in the States Offered column and at the same time if the ZIP Codes Exist column in the Plan Networks section is flagged as Yes, then a warning message stating Benefit Plan has States Offered defined along with Networks with Zip Codes assigned which may cause enrollment issues. Would you like to continue? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to save the record with the current values entered.

  • Click No to return back to the form.

[Image: screenshot]

  • Under the Special Options section, when you select and the Age/Rate Date Fixed by Rate Guaranty field and there are Employee Benefit Enrollments records tied to the Benefit Plan selected that have a status of Active, then a message stating There are active employees in this benefit plan. The Age/Rate Date Fixed by Rate Guaranty will not apply to employees enrolled prior to this flag being checked. The current coverage detail record for each employee will need to be saved or a new coverage detail record created in order to apply the Age/Rate Date Fixed by Rate Guaranty. is displayed.

[Image: screenshot]

  • On the Group Benefit Plans (Global) form, if you save the form with the Mid-Month Coverage Dates field selected, then at the client level, on the Benefit Rules form, under the Eligibility Rules section, the Eligibility Date Used drop-down will display all the three options available but will allow you to select only the Calculated Eligibility Date option. The other two options will be disabled with a tag, Not Valid next to the option names as shown in the image below.

[Image: screenshot]

Eligible Benefits Determinant field validations added to the Client Benefit form

On the Client Benefit form, under the Benefits tab, for the Eligible Benefits Determinant field, the following validations has been added for the following selections:

  • Departments Restrict Eligibility

  • Benefit Groups Restrict Eligibility

  • Divisions Restrict Eligibility

  • Locations Restrict Eligibility

[Image: screenshot]

  • Departments Restrict Eligibility: Select this option to be able to select one or more Benefit Plan IDs under the Eligible Benefits section on the Departments form. If this option is not selected, then you will not be able to select any Benefit Plan IDs under the Eligible Benefits section on the Departments form. A conditional message stating Access to this section requires the Eligible Benefits Determinant to be set to Departments Restrict Eligibility on the Client Details form. is also displayed under the Eligible Benefits section of the Departments form.

  • Benefit Groups Restrict Eligibility: Select this option to be able to select one or more Benefit Plan IDs under the Eligible Benefits - Group Benefit Plans section on the Benefit Groups form. If this option is not selected, then you will not be able to select any Benefit Plan IDs under the Eligible Benefits - Group Benefit Plans section on the Benefit Groups form. A conditional message stating Access to this section requires the Eligible Benefits Determinant to be set to Benefit Groups Restrict Eligibility on the Client Details form. is also displayed under the Eligible Benefits - Group Benefit Plans section of the Benefit Groups form.

  • Divisions Restrict Eligibility: Select this option to be able to select one or more Benefit Plan IDs under the Eligible Benefits section on the Divisions form. If this option is not selected, then you will not be able to select any Benefit Plan IDs under the Eligible Benefits section on the Divisions form. A conditional message stating Access to this section requires the Eligible Benefits Determinant to be set to Divisions Restrict Eligibility on the Client Details form. is also displayed under the Eligible Benefits section of the Divisions form.

  • Locations Restrict Eligibility: Select this option to be able to select one or more Benefit Plan IDs under the Eligible Benefits section on the Worksite Locations form. If this option is not selected, then you will not be able to select any Benefit Plan IDs under the Eligible Benefits section on the Worksite Locations form. A conditional message stating Access to this section requires the Eligible Benefits Determinant to be set to Locations Restrict Eligibility on the Client Details form is also displayed under the Eligible Benefits section of the Worksite Locations form.

Note: If you select any All Plans Eligible then on the Eligible Benefits section on the corresponding forms will be displayed as a read only section.

Changes to the Data Import Tool form

A new Import Template named Eligible Benefits is added to the Data Import Tool form as shown below. This option is available only for Service Providers. You can click the Download Data File to download the Eligible Benefits template in a csv format.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. To access this form, click [Image: screenshot] (Back Office). Under Operations|Import Processing, click Data Import Tool.

  2. Select Eligible Benefits from the Import Template drop-down.

  3. Click the Download Data File hyperlink to download the Eligible Benefits sample template. The template file will have the nine columns under the File Format tab as shown in the picture above. Fill up the necessary data for all the Eligible Benefits for which you to build your Import file.

  4. If you want a prepopulated data of the clients, then you will have to select the clients from the Client ID selector.

  5. Click the Client ID selector to open the Select Clients dialog box. Another way to enter client details is by providing the Client ID in the box.

  • You can select the clients by clicking the list of clients that you want to add. The added clients will be displayed in the Selected Clients section. Click Add All to add all the clients at once. Click Remove All to remove the clients from the Selected Clients section at once.

  • You can enter the Client ID or Name to narrow down the search.

  • You can filter the clients based on the Eligible Benefits Determinant for different restrict eligibility such as Benefit Groups, Locations, Divisions, and Departments.

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Done to add the selected clients. The added clients will be displayed on the Data Import Tool page.

  2. Now, click the Download Data File hyperlink to download the file of prepopulated data for all the clients selected.

  3. Check the Include Obsolete/Expired values checkbox based on your requirement. The default is unchecked.

  • Checked: The Locations / Departments / Divisions that are flagged as Obsolete will be displayed on the downloaded file.

  • Unchecked: The different types of eligible benefits determinants will not be displayed on the downloaded file.

  1. Click Find File to open the File Upload dialog box.

  2. Click Add Files in the File Upload dialog box.

  3. Select the specified Import File from your system that you have created. Once selected, the Import File will display in the File Upload dialog box.

  4. Click Start Upload to upload the file.

  5. Click Close on the File Upload dialog box.

  6. The content of the file will display under File Content tab. Errors, if any, will display in the Messages tab. Correct the errors and redo the process.

  7. Click Import to import the content into PrismHR.

  8. Click Report to display the Imported Eligible Benefits Report. The Import Status column will tell you if that Eligible Benefits for that Client was imported or not. If not, then the Comments column will tell you the reason.

On the Group Benefit Plans form, in the Offer Type field, if you select any Offer Type other than Voluntary, the system will automatically assign the Insurance Class field without the user having to assign it manually. The system will display the Insurance Class field as a read-only field. When you select Offer Type as Voluntary, the Insurance Class field becomes a required field, and you must manually select the corresponding insurance class.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The Offer Type field is mandatory. If you leave it blank, you will receive an error message stating Offer Type is mandatory.

Please note the following list of insurance class and their corresponding offer types:

  • Insurance Class: Medical

  • Medical (MED)

  • Accident Benefits (ACC)

  • Cancer Benefits (CAN)

  • Critical Illness (CRI)

  • Domestic Partner Medical (MDP)

  • Gap Insurance (GAP)

  • Identity Theft (IDT)

  • Telehealth (TEL)

  • Voluntary Hospitalization (HOS)

  • Insurance Class: Dental

  • Dental (DEN)

  • Domestic Partner Dental (DDP)

  • Insurance Class: Vision

  • Vision (VIS)

  • Domestic Partner Vision (VDP)

  • Insurance Class: Life Insurance

  • Accidental Death and Dismemberment (ADD)

  • Basic Life Extra (BLX)

  • Critical Illness as Life (CRL)

  • Group Term Life (GTL)

  • Life Insurance - Basic (LIF)

  • Life Insurance - Basic - Child Only (LIC)

  • Life Insurance - Basic - Spouse Only (LIS)

  • Whole Life (WLI)

  • Insurance Class: Short-Term Disability

  • Additional STD (SDA)

  • Short Term Disability (STD)

  • Insurance Class: Long-Term Disability

  • Additional LTD (LDA)

  • Long Term Disability (LTD)

  • Insurance Class: Other

  • Ancillary (ANC)

  • Legal (LGL)

  • Pet Benefits (PET)

  • Dependent Reduction Provision (Spanish) - Contents will display to employees in online Benefits Enrollment when dependents are selected to be covered in Spanish.

JIRA # WSP-1072, WSP-1192

New Brokers form

Under the Actions menu, a new form named Brokers has been added. To access this form, users must have FULL access to BROKERMAINT and BENEFIT.PLANSMAINT.

[Image: screenshot]

This modal form creates a repository of the Brokers information in the system. The form contains fields listed below:

  • Broker Id- Unique id assigned to each broker.

  • New Record- This hyperlink creates a new Broker ID by system-generated sequential numbers to ensure records are stored in a consistent manner. Users with INQUIRY access to the Broker Maintenance form cannot click the New Record hyperlink or manually key in value in the Broker ID textbox field.

  • Broker Name- Name of the broker

  • Address One- Address line one of the broker.

  • Address Two- Address line two of the broker.

  • ZIP Code- ZIP Code of the broker’s address.

  • City- Name of the city in which Broker resides.

  • State- State Code along with full name of the State.

  • Email Address- Email ID of the broker.

  • Phone- Contact number of the broker.

Users can add new brokers, delete or modify an existing broker information.

  • Click Save to save the broker information in the system.

  • Click Delete to remove the record of broker information from the system.

  • Click Cancel to clear out the information that you have filled out in the form.

  • Click Close to close the Brokers modal form without saving it.

[Image: screenshot]

On the Brokers form, you can search for a broker information by keying in the Broker ID in the respective field. If you enter a value that is not in the record, you will get a warning message that states, Record not on file, please click ‘New Record.’

JIRA # WSP-1222

New Coverage Ends On Field

Under the Other Processing Parameters section, a new field named Coverage Ends On has been introduced. This field defines the date on which you want the coverage to end.

[Image: screenshot]

  • The Coverage Ends On field is setup at the Global level and is similar to the Coverage Ends On field that is available on the Benefit Plan Setup form which is setup at the client level.

  • When you set the Coverage Ends On at the Global level on this form, then the Coverage Ends On field on the Benefit Plan Setup form becomes a non-mandatory field.

  • When you set the Coverage Ends On field at the global level on the Group Benefit Plans form, then that selected option is displayed as default on the Coverage Ends On field on the Benefit Plan Setup form. For example, if you set Coverage Ends On as Employee’s Date of Termination on the Group Benefit Plans form, then on the Benefit Plan Setup form, on the Coverage Ends On field, the option, Employee’s Date of Termination will be labeled as default for you to identify that the setting is being used on the system level.

[Image: screenshot]

JIRA # WSP-1397, WSP-1399, WSP-1403

New Use Billing Wash Rule? Field

Under the Other Processing Parameters section, a new field named Use Billing Wash Rule? has been introduced.

[Image: screenshot]

This field has two options:

  • Select No to disable the billing wash rule at the global system level. This is the default option.

  • Select Yes to enable the billing wash rule. When this is enabled a new field named Wash Rule Date On/Before displays which will allow you to apply the wash rule on or before the 10th Day of the Month through the 20th Day of the Month, or at End of Month.

The Pay Code selector has been enhanced across the following forms:

  • Retirement Plan Enrollment

  • Benefit Plan Setup

  • When you select Plan Class as:

  • Retirement, or

  • Employer Match

  • When you select Plan Class as Group Benefit, then:

  • Fringe Benefit Pay Code

  • HSA Plans

  • Group Benefit Plans > Actions Menu > Section 105 > Section 105 Pay Code

  • Section 125 Benefit Plans

[Image: screenshot]

  • You can enter a Pay Code or Pay Description to narrow down the search.

  • This selector has the following filters:

  • Pay Type- This filter has the following drop-down options:

  • All - This is the default option. The other options in this filter will display the pay types applicable for different forms and fields for pay code.

  • Pay Class- This filter has the following drop-down options:

  • All - This is the default option. The other options in this filter will display the pay class as applicable.

  • Calculation Method- This filter has the following drop-down options:

  • All - This is the default option. The other options in this filter will list down all the different calculation methods of pay types.

  • Obsolete - This filter has the following drop-down options:

  • All - Based on the date listed in the Obsolete Date field on the Pay Codes form, the search result is displayed. It displays all the available pay codes.

  • No - This is the default option. It displays the list of pay codes for which Obsolete Date field is blank.

  • Yes - It displays the list of pay codes for which Obsolete Date field is filled.

  • You can click on any column header in the list, for example, Pay Code or Pay Description and so on to sort the list accordingly.

New Gross Wage % Functionality

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025%2004Apr/BA-4046%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025 04Apr/BA-4046 (Epic).htm

New Gross Wage % Functionality

A new option has been added to define when a medical plan allows plan elections for employee and dependent with contributions up to a certain percent of gross wages for the employee portion.

Changes to the Group Benefit Plans form

Under the Group Benefit Plans section, a new checkbox named Allow Gross Wage % Contribution Method has been added to allow you to set the Percent of Gross Wages as the employee contribution towards a medical plan (employee premium only).

[Image: screenshot]

  • This checkbox is only valid for those benefit plans whose Insurance Class is set as Medical.

  • To select the Allow Gross Wage % Contribution Method checkbox please ensure that the following checkboxes have been unchecked:

  • Single Coverage Gross Wage %

  • Do NOT Include In ACA Reporting

  • Additionally, you can select this checkbox only if the Cost Basis field is set to either Monthly, Quarterly, or Yearly. If it is set to Weekly, then a message stating This feature is not compatible with a Cost Basis of Weekly is displayed.

  • If the Single Coverage Gross Wage % checkbox is selected and you select the Allow Gross Wage % Contribution Method checkbox, then a warning message stating The Single Coverage Gross Wages % Checkbox must be unselected is displayed.

  • Click this checkbox to display the multivalued grid where you can enter an Effective Date along with a Percent of Gross Wages which will be used as a default setting.

  • On the Group Benefit Plans form, if you select the Allow Gross Wage % Contribution Method checkbox then on the Benefit Plan Setup form, the following fields will be disabled:

  • One Month Prepay

  • Cafe Plan Eligible

  • Hawaii 1.5% Rule

JIRA # BA-4472, BA-4507, WSP-1762

Changes to the Benefit Rules form

Under the Contribution Rules section, a new field named Percent of Gross Wages has been added to override the Gross Wage % value assigned on the Group Benefit Plans form for medical plans.

[Image: screenshot]

  • This newly added field will only display if you have selected the Allow Gross Wage % Contribution Method checkbox and defined the Effective Date for that medical benefit plan on the Group Benefit Plans form. If this criteria is not met then a message stating Not applicable for this plan is displayed.

  • When the Percent of Gross Wages field is displayed, then the Max Contribution ($) column is disabled.

  • If the Benefit Plans are flagged with rule Effective Date that does not correlate to the Plan Setting effective date, then a message stating No Effective Date for Plan Setting as of is displayed.

JIRA # BA-4473

Changes to the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form

Under the Employee Contribution Rules section, a new field named Percent of Gross Wages has been added to override the Gross Wage % value assigned on the Group Benefit Plans form and the Benefit Rules form (if applicable) for Medical plans.

[Image: screenshot]

This newly added field will only display if you have selected the Allow Gross Wage % Contribution Method checkbox and defined the Effective Date for that medical benefit plan on the Group Benefit Plans form. If this criteria is not met then a message stating Not applicable for this plan is displayed.

JIRA # BA-4474

Changes to the Employee Benefits Enrollment form

Under the Coverage Details section, a new field named Percent of Gross Wages has been added to indicate if an employee is enrolled in a medical plan which uses the Gross % of Wages to calculate the employee’s portion of the premium which displays the Gross % of Wages value that is being used.

[Image: screenshot]

  • This newly added field will only display when an employee is enrolled in a medical plan which uses the Gross % of Wages to calculate the Employee portion of the premium.

  • The value in the Percent of Gross Wages field that you assign on the Employee Benefit Rules Overrides form is displayed here.

  • If no value is assigned on the Employee Benefit Rules Overrides form, then the value assigned on the Benefit Rules form is displayed.

  • If no value is assigned on either the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides or the Benefit Rules forms, then the value assigned on the Group Benefit Plans form is displayed.

Note: The Percent of Gross Wages field will not be displayed for the COBRA plans.

JIRA # BA-4476, WSP-1723

Changes to the Payroll Calculations

On the Process Payroll form, the payroll calculation process now includes the gross wages and calculates the employee contribution based on the Benefit Rules and value assigned to the Benefit Plan for Gross % of Wages.

  • If a benefit plan uses the Percent of Gross Wages value, then while calculating the contribution towards the Employee portion of premium, if Max Contribution has been defined for any Benefit Rule, then it will ignore the Max Contribution value. You must also set The Contribution rule amounts made by Company or Employee field to Employee for the payroll process to include gross wages.

The logic to determine the Percent of Gross Wages being used is as follows:

  • If the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form uses the Percent of Gross Wages value, then:

  • the value in the Percent of Gross Wages field on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form will be used to calculate the Percent of Gross Wages or else it will use the value assigned on the Group Benefit Plans form to calculate Percent of Gross Wages.

  • If the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form does not use the Percent of Gross Wages value, then:

  • the value in the Percent of Gross Wages field on the Benefit Rules form will be used to calculate the Percent of Gross Wages or else it will use the value assigned on the Group Benefit Plans form to calculate Percent of Gross Wages.

The payroll calculation is as below:

  • Once the Percent of Gross Wages value has been determined, this value is used to calculate the Contribution Amount for the Employee portion of the premium.

  • If the Percent of Gross Wages value is not being considered, then the Contribution Amount is calculated for the Employee portion of the premium based on the Benefit Rule grid.

  • If the Percent of Gross Wages value is less than the Calculated Contribution from the Benefit Rule grid, then the Percent of Gross Wages is used as the contribution towards the Employee portion of premium. The dependent premium is calculated in full by the benefit rule.

  • If the Percent of Gross Wages value is greater than the Calculated Contribution from the Benefit Rule grid, then the Calculated Contribution is used from the Benefit Rule grid as the contribution towards the Employee portion of premium.

  • Payee Type- This filter has the following drop-down options:

  • State Disbursement Unit - The unit which requires to send electronic payments to state government agencies.

This section is expandable and when expanded, it provides the following sub-sections:

Changes to the Employee Deduction Arrears form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025%2006June/WSP-120%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025 06June/WSP-120 (Epic).htm

Changes to the Employee Deduction Arrears form

Removing the Delete column and Introducing Convert to Adjustment Button

The earlier Delete column has now been removed from the Employee Deduction Arrears form. Enhancement to the Change Status button and a new button named Convert to Adjustment has been introduced for users to convert an arrears record into a Benefit Adjustment.

  • Enhancement to the Change Status button

  • The Change Status button is only visible if the USEWEEKLYBENEFITS Custom Feature Code is set on the System Parameters form. You can make a change using the Change Status button to save the change immediately without needing to click Save on the form.

  • Select an arrears record with Arrears Status as Automatic and click the Change Status button. A message is displayed stating, Arrears Status can only be changed from Optional to Automatic. Changing Automatic status to Optional must occur within the Employee Deduction Arrears Detail screen.

[Image: screenshot]

  • New Convert to Adjustment button

  • The Convert to Adjustment button is only available for users with Full access to the Benefit Adjustments form. If a user does not have access to the Benefits Adjustments form, then the Convert to Adjustment button is displayed but is disabled.

  • The Convert to Adjustment button is enabled only when one arrears record is selected. If you select multiple arrears records, then this button is disabled.

  • When you select an arrears record which has no Benefit Plan ID defined, then the Convert to Adjustment button is disabled.

  • Select an arrears record and click the Convert to Adjustment button. A modal form is displayed with Benefit Plan and Arrears Balance pre-populated. Additionally, a static text message is displayed stating, This action will divide the arrears balance by the number of cycles indicated below to create benefit adjustments. Please note that rounding may cause slight discrepancies and additional adjustments may be needed. The arrears balance will be removed.

  • On the modal form, enter a date in the Start Date field and provide a value in the Adjustment Cycles field. Click Create. A confirmation pop-up indicating that the adjustment has been created is displayed stating, Your change has caused the system to create billing adjustments. Would you like to review?

  • Click Yes to open the Benefit Adjustments modal form where you can review the newly created benefit adjustment and make changed if necessary.

  • Click No to close the confirmation pop-up window.

  • Click Cancel to clear this form at any time.

  • Click Close to close the modal form.

[Image: screenshot]

Please note the following:

  • The Adjustment Cycles field is a mandatory field and accepts only numeric characters with value 1 or greater than 1.

  • On entering the value in the Adjustment Cycles field, a calculated text is displayed which follows the calculation of dividing the arrears balance by the number of adjustment cycles entered. For example if the Arrears Balance is 40 and the Adjustment Cycles that you entered is 10, then the calculated text that is displayed would be, Adjustment to be created: 4.00 over 10 cycles.

JIRA # WSP-1627, WSP-1628, WSP-1642, WSP-1941, WSP-2005, WSP-2050

Changes to the Employee Deduction Arrears Detail form

On the Employee Deduction Arrears form, when you click an arrears record to open the Employee Deduction Arrears Detail modal form, the earlier Done and Cancel buttons have been replaced by Save, Delete, and Close buttons.

[Image: screenshot]

  • Click Save to save the record and close the modal form. The saved data is displayed on the main Employee Deduction Arrears form.

  • Click Delete to delete an arrears record. Clicking Delete displays a warning message stating, This arrears record will be deleted immediately. Do you want to continue?

  • Click Yes to delete the record and the data for that record will no longer display on the main Employee Deduction Arrears form.

  • Click No to close the warning message and return on the Employee Deduction Arrears Detail modal form with all the previously entered data.

  • Click Close to close the modal form and return on the main Employee Deduction Arrears form. Any unsaved changes will be lost.

The Delete button is enabled only when you select one or more arrears records.

  • Select the arrears records that you want to delete and click Delete. A warning message stating, arrears record(s) will be deleted. Do you want to continue? is displayed.

Changes to the Benefit Adjustments form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025%2006June/WSP-1238%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025 06June/WSP-1238 (Epic).htm

Changes to the Benefit Adjustments form

Under the Benefit Adjustments section, after you select an Employee and select the Benefit Plan record, then on the Adjustment Details modal form, that is displayed, two new read-only fields named Bill Code and Deduction Rebate Bill Code have been added to take the Bill Code and Rebate Bill Code available on the Deduction Codes form into account and accurately assess and calculate the value displayed in the Net Inv Effect field.

[Image: screenshot]

  • Bill Code- The value in this field is fetched from the corresponding Group Benefit Plan based on the following criteria from the fields on the System Parameters and the Benefit Plan Setup forms:
System Parameters form (Require Prepay Benefit Account No. field) Benefit Plan Setup form (One Month Prepay field) The Bill Code displayed on the Benefit Adjustments form
No Unchecked Bill Code
Setup Unchecked Bill Code
Yes Unchecked Bill Code
Yes Checked Prepay Bill Code

Note: If the identified Bill Code field is empty in any of the scenarios above, then the Bill Code field on the Adjustment Details modal form will display N/A as the value.

  • Deduction Rebate Bill Code- The applicable deduction code value in this field is fetched from the Deduction Code in use for the employee enrollment based on the following criteria from the fields on the System Parameters, Benefit Plan Setup, and Employee Benefits Enrollment forms:
System Parameters form (Require Prepay Benefit Account No. field) Benefit Plan Setup form (One Month Prepay field) Employee Benefits Enrollment (Section 125 field) The Deduction Code displayed on the Benefit Adjustments form
No Unchecked Unchecked Deduction Code
Setup Unchecked Unchecked Deduction Code
No Unchecked Checked 125 Deduction Code
Setup Unchecked Checked 125 Deduction Code
Yes Unchecked Unchecked Deduction Code
Yes Unchecked Checked 125 Deduction Code
Yes Checked Unchecked Deduction Code Prepay
Yes Checked Checked 125 Deduction Code Prepay

Note: If the identified Deduction Rebate Bill Code field is empty in any of the scenarios above, then the Deduction Rebate Bill Code field on the Adjustment Details modal form will display N/A as the value.

With the introduction of these two new fields, the calculation method for Net Inv Effect has also changed. The following table illustrates the calculation method based on the values fetched in the Bill Code and the Deduction Rebate Bill Code fields:

Bill Code found? Deduction Rebate Bill Code found? Net Inv Effect Calculation
Yes N/A Bill Amount - Employee Contribution
N/A Yes (- EE Contribution)
N/A N/A 0.00
Yes Yes (Bill Amount - Employee Contribution) - Employee Contribution

Please note the following:

  • On the Adjustment Details modal form, as and when you change the Benefit Plan ID input, the display of values in the Bill Code, Deduction Rebate Bill Code, and Net Inv Effect fields refreshes and displays the values associated with the changed Benefit Plan ID.

  • Similarly, the calculation of Net Inv Effect is also refreshed when you change the Adjust Cycles on the Adjust Cycles pop-up window. Additionally, the Net Inv Effect column for the Benefit Adjustment’s voucher summary table is also calculated appropriately based on the calculation scenario mentioned above.

  • On the Benefit Adjustments Report form, when you run a report, the Net Inv Effect column follows the updated calculating logic to match the configuration assessment and calculation logic from the Benefit Adjustments form.

JIRA # WSP-1833, WSP-2033, WSP-2034, WSP-2035

Under the Employee Benefits Enrollment section, after you have selected an Employee and the Benefit Plan, three new read-only fields named Bill Code, Deduction Rebate Bill Code, and Net Inv Effect have been added for users to easily and accurately view what impact the pay period premium will have on invoice billing.

The values in all these newly added fields are fetched as per the logic discussed in the See Changes to the Benefit Adjustments form release notes.

Changes to the Group Benefit Plans form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025%2006June/WSP-1239%20(Epic),%20WSP-1259%20(Epic)%20&%20WSP-1248%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025 06June/WSP-1239 (Epic), WSP-1259 (Epic) & WSP-1248 (Epic).htm

Changes to the Group Benefit Plans form

New Do Not Allow EE Contribution checkbox

Under the Group Benefit Plans section, a new checkbox named Do Not Allow EE Contribution has been added which ensures that clients are informed that the plans are client-paid while setting up benefit rules.

[Image: screenshot]

  • When you select this checkbox, the system checks for any clients to which this plan is currently assigned to and displays a warning message stating, Important Notice: You currently have active Clients associated with this plan. We strongly advise reviewing the Benefit Contribution Rules to ensure your plan aligns with the selected requirements. Would you like to go to Clients Assigned To to see the list of associated Clients?.

  • Click Yes to open the Clients Assigned To modal form to view the clients currently assigned to the benefit plan.

  • Click No to close the warning message.

  • When you select this checkbox, then on the Benefit Rules form, if the following validations are not met:

  • Under the Contribution Rules section, the Contribution Method field is set to Percentage as the only valid option.

  • If the Contribution rule amounts made by Company or Employee field is set to Employee, then the Contribution Amount and the DEP Contribution Amount field values should be 0.

  • If the Contribution rule amounts made by Company or Employee field is set to Company, then the Contribution Amount and the DEP Contribution Amount field values should be 100.

then, while saving the benefit rules, a warning message stating, This plan configuration prevents employee contributions, please review the Contribution Rules and verify the plan meets this requirement. is displayed.

Click OK to close the warning message and save the benefit rule.

  • Similarly, on the Benefit Rules Import form, the above mentioned validation is reviewed. If you select the Do Not Allow EE Contribution checkbox, then the system checks the import file data to ensure a valid setup is entered and a warning message stating The plan configuration for prevents employee contributions, please review the Contribution Rules and verify the plan meets this requirement. is displayed.

  • This warning message is not hard-stop error, which means you can bypass the warnings displayed and post the benefit rules.

  • When you select the Do Not Allow EE Contribution checkbox, then on the Benefit Rules form, under the Contribution Rules section, an informational text stating, This plan is set to not allow employee contributions, please ensure the contribution rules meet this requirement. is displayed to notify the user that the plan is set up to disallow employee contribution so that they are aware while adding or updating the contribution rules.

JIRA # WSP-1327, WSP-1328, WSP-1335, WSP-1389

New Override Dependent Age Limits By State field

On the Group Benefit Plans form, under the Other Processing Parameters section, below the Disabled Dependent Eligible field, a new checkbox field named Override Dependent Age Limits By State has been added to allow you to configure state level override(s) for Dependent Age Limits so that you can easily manage differences in plans at the state level.

[Image: screenshot]

  • Unchecked - (Default) The Dependent Age Limit State Overrides table remains hidden.

  • Checked - The Dependent Age Limit Override table is displayed with the following column headers:

  • States- Enter the state code or select from the Select States selector.

  • Dep Age Limit- Provide the dependent age limit.

  • Dep Age Calculation Method- Select how you want to calculate the dependent’s age from the drop-down options. The available options are:

  • On date of birth (DOB)

  • End of DOB year

  • End of DOB month

  • Disabled Dep?- Specify if the dependent is disabled.

  • Disabled Alt Age Limit- If the dependent is disabled, specify the age limit. This field is enabled only if you select Yes for the Disabled Dep? field.

If there are no states listed in this table, then upon saving the form an error message stating No state listed in the dependent age limit override table is displayed.

Also, if you do not input any value in any one of the row in the table, then upon saving the form an error message stating The [field name] for the state of [State value] is missing from the dependent age limit override table is displayed.

Note: The system uses the State’s Dependent Age limit and its related Calculation Method and Disabled Eligibility Limit as an override for determining when the Dependent Age Limit becomes effective. If there is no override configured for a given state in the Dependent Age Limit Override table, then the system uses the existing Dependent Age Limit (and related field’s) values as default.

New Billing History Section

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025%2006June/WSP-1273%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025 06June/WSP-1273 (Epic).htm

New Billing History Section

In order to allow you to view the billing history for a specific employee/plan along with the ability to select custom date range to review billing history, a new section named Billing History has been added to the following forms:

  • Employee Benefits Enrollment

  • Employee Benefit Overview

[Image: screenshot]

This section is expandable and when expanded, it provides the Selection Parameters section.

Under the Selection Parameters section, the Defined Ranges drop-down field is available for you to select from a list of pre-defined date ranges or enter your own date range to review billing history.

The Defined Ranges drop-down contains the following options:

  • Current Month (default)- The date range is displayed as the first day of current month and the last day of current month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 6/1/2024-6/30/2024.

  • Year-to-date- The date range is displayed as the first day of the current year till the current system date. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition displayed on this selection will be 1/1/2024-6/15/2024.

Note: This drop-down option is not available under the Billing History section on the Employee Benefit Overview form.

  • Prior Month- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous month and the last day of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 5/1/2024-5/31/2024.

  • Prior 2 Months- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous two months and the last day of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 4/1/2024-5/31/2024.

  • Prior 3 Months- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous three months and the last day of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 3/1/2024-5/31/2024.

  • Prior Year- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous year and the last day of the previous year. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 1/1/2023-12/31/2023.

Note: This drop-down option is not available under the Billing History section on the Employee Benefit Overview form.

  • Custom Date Range- You can choose dates in the Pay Date On Or After and the Pay Date On Or Before fields.

  • Select Batch ID- You can select the Payroll Number.

Please note the following:

  • When you select a pre-defined range from the drop-down other than Custom Date Range or Select Batch ID, then you can view the start and the end date values in a read-only format.

  • When you select Custom Date Range option from the drop-down, two fields, Pay Date On Or After and the Pay Date On Or Before appears where you can specify a date range other than the one listed above and successfully generate accurate report results.

Note: This Pay Date range for this drop-down option is limited to 6 months. If the date range entered is longer than 6 months, then a warning message stating, Pay Date range is limited to 6 months. Please select a Pay Date which is greater than or equal to . is displayed.

  • When you select Select Batch ID option from the drop-down, then a Payroll Voucher field, which is a hyperlink appears where you can select a payroll number from the Select Payroll Number selector that displays. You can also type in the payroll number in the Payroll Number field. If you enter a payroll number that does not match with the data set available on the Select Payroll Number selector, then an error is displayed stating, is not a valid payroll number for this action.

  • The data under this section includes detailed pay date information, ensuring totals are consistently displayed. The following headers are visible if any data is displayed:

  • Plan Description

  • Voucher #

  • Pay Date

  • From Arrears

  • Amount Billed

  • Employee Deduction

  • Net-Amount Billed

  • The Totals section is a fixed section which is displayed at the bottom of the screen, ensuring it is always visible without the need for scrolling on the screen.

  • As and when you change the Selection Parameters by defining the date ranges, the on-screen data is displayed accordingly.

  • You can also download a benefits billing history report for a specific employee/plan and review the billing history in an editable format. Click the Download Report button to open the report results window for the Benefit Billing Detail Report with existing parameters from the Billing History fields.

Note: The Download Report button is disabled when there are no results for a defined date range.

  • On the Employee Benefit Overview form, under the Billing History section, an additional Report Filter named Benefit Plan ID is added that allows users to select specific benefit plans for inclusion in the displayed data.

  • Click the Benefit Plan ID hyperlink to select eligible Benefit Plans from the Select Benefit Plan selector for each employee or client.

[Image: screenshot]

  • On the Employee Benefit Overview form, under the Employee Benefit Overview section, when you select a benefit plan, you can view and change selection parameters to the Billing History on the pop-up window that is displayed.

[Image: screenshot]

  • Year-to-date- The date range is displayed as the first day of the current year till the current system date. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition displayed on this selection will be 1/1/2024-6/15/2024.

  • Prior 2 Months- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous two months and the last day of the previous month. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 4/1/2024-5/31/2024.

  • Prior Year- The date range is displayed as the first day of the previous year and the last day of the previous year. For example, if the current system date is 6/15/2024, then the range definition for this selection will be 1/1/2023-12/31/2023.

  • Custom Date Range- You can choose dates in the Pay Date On Or After and the Pay Date On Or Before fields.

  • When you select a pre-defined range from the drop-down other than Custom Date Range or Select Batch ID, then you can view the start and the end date values in a read-only format.

  • When you select Custom Date Range option from the drop-down, two fields, Pay Date On Or After and the Pay Date On Or Before appears where you can specify a date range other than the one listed above and successfully generate accurate report results.

  • When you select Select Batch ID option from the drop-down, then a Payroll Voucher field, which is a hyperlink appears where you can select a payroll number from the Select Payroll Number selector that displays. You can also type in the payroll number in the Payroll Number field. JIRA # WSP-1434, WSP-1588, WSP-2007

Changes to the Sort Parameters Section

The earlier Sort Criteria drop-down is now removed and has been replaced by the following options:

  • Primary Sort- This selector indicates the top-level of sort organization for the report results. This drop-down has the following options:
a. Select
b. Employee
— —
c. Benefit Plan
— —
d. Location
— —
e. Department
— —

  • When you select Location or Department as the Primary Sort then the generated report contains one extra leading column (either location or department, as dictated by the Primary Sort selector).

  • When you select Employee or Benefit Plan as the Primary Sort, then the first column of the report will indicate the Primary Sort. Employee as Primary Sort will include Employee ID column first and Employee Name second, followed by the Secondary Sort column and subsequent columns.

  • Secondary Sort- This selector indicates the order of sort organization within the Primary Sort and the order of the column(s) following the Primary Sort column. For example, if you select Benefit Plan as the Primary Sort option and Employee as the Secondary Sort option, then the results displayed will be first by Plan ID and then by Employee ID within the respective Plan ID result segments. This drop-down has the following options:

a. Select
b. Employee
— —
c. Benefit Plan
— —
  • Report Type
  1. — Detail- When you select Report Type as Detail, then the report generated displays the results based on the payroll voucher/pay date level detail. Below are the following columns that are displayed in the report results:

  • Location or Department- Only if Primary Sort is selected as Location or Department.

  • Employee ID

  • Employee Name- Employee ID and Employee Name is always displayed next to each other depending on the sort criteria.

  • Plan ID

  • Plan Description- Plan ID and Plan Description is always displayed next to each other depending on the sort criteria.

  • Pay Date- If you have Inquiry or Full access to EMPLOYEE.PAYROLL.VOUCHERSINQ.VOUCHER, then the Pay Date* field will contain a hyperlink. Click the hyperlink to open the Employee Voucher modal form. You can view the Voucher Number in a read-only format. The hyperlink is unavailable if you have Deny access to EMPLOYEE.PAYROLL.VOUCHERS*INQ.VOUCHER.

  • From Arrears

  • Amount Billed

  • Employee Deduction

  • Net-Amount Billed

  1. — Summary (default)- If you select Report Type as Summary, then the report output aggregates the report results into segments dictated by sort parameters.

[Image: screenshot]

Please note the following validations:

  • If you try to select the Secondary Sort parameter when the Primary Sort is set to –Select–, then an error message is displayed stating, Primary Sort must be entered before Secondary Sort can be entered.

  • If you select Benefit Plan for Primary Sort, then the Secondary Sort field is defaulted to Employee as the only available option and the field becomes non-editable.

  • If you select Employee for Primary Sort, then the Secondary Sort is defaulted to Benefit Plan as the only available option and the field becomes non-editable.

  • If you select Primary Sort as Department or Location, then both the option for the Secondary Sort field will be available to select.

Benefit Plan Setup form

Under the Benefit Plan Setup section, after you have selected the Plan Class and the Plan ID, then under the

[Image: screenshot]

menu, a new option named Employee Assigned To has been added to display employees that are enrolled in the selected Benefit Plan.

Note: The Employee Assigned To option is available only if the Plan Class field is set to Group Benefit.

[Image: screenshot]

  • Click the Employee Assigned To to open the modal form. The Benefit Plan and the Plan Name will be listed on this form.

  • The Active employee count displays the number of active employees based on the active Enrollment Status count.

JIRA # WSP-2152

New Rate Groups Import Template on the Data Import Tool form

A new Import Template named Rate Groups is added to the Data Import Tool form as shown below. This option is available only for Service Providers. You can click the Download Data File to download the Rate Groups template in a .csv file.

[Image: screenshot]

You can use this import template to import new Rate Groups for the client.

To import rate groups and display an on-screen report:

  1. Select Rate Groups from the Import Template menu.

  2. Select the Prepopulate file checkbox if you want to download the data file that includes all the fields that are being imported from the list of Rate Groups configured with a full export of all existing Rate Group data in a .CSV file.

  3. Click Find File to upload the file.

  4. After importing the file a message displays, File content successfully uploaded and ready to be imported. Click OK. The imported rate groups display and an Import button.

  5. Click Import. After the import finishes a message displays, File content successfully imported. View report for details. Click OK. A Report button displays.

  6. Click Report. An on-screen report displays the imported Rate Groups. (You can also download this report.)

  7. As part of this import process, the imported Rate Groups now display in the Rate Groups form.

Note: Note the following when using the Rate Groups import template:

  • Users whose user role is set to FULL for the Data Import Tool form and only INQUIRY access to the Rate Groups form can download the sample data file but cannot upload data using the Find File button.

  • Users whose user role is set to FULL for the Data Import Tool form and only DENY access to the Rate Groups form cannot view the Rate Groups import template option.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool form cannot view the Download Data File or the Find File buttons.

Note: When you import the rate groups and generate a report, the heading of the report page displays an incorrect report title name. This issue will be fixed in the upcoming August release.

Changes to the Benefit Utilities form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025%2008Aug/WSP-2458%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025 08Aug/WSP-2458 (Epic).htm

Changes to the Benefit Utilities form

Under the Benefit Utilities section, when you select Utility as Manage Orphaned Benefit Records, then under the Orphaned Record Type, a new drop-down option named Relationships have been added which displays the orphaned records due to missing relationship code.

[Image: screenshot]

  • When you select the Manage Orphaned Benefit Records, based on the Orphaned Record Type filter that follows, you can choose the Client ID displayed in the Report Filters section.

  • Client ID - This field is optional. Leave this field blank for this report to run for all clients. If you want to restrict this report to run for selected clients, enter their Client IDs here or click the Client ID link and select them from the Select Clients dialog box.

  • Select Orphaned Record Type as Relationships and then click Search. The list of orphaned records caused by missing relationship codes are displayed. The list of orphaned records displayed in the Results section helps you to reconcile the records.

The Results section displays the following columns:

  • File Name - Name of the file. In this scenario, it is BENEFIT.PLANS.

  • Employee ID - Unique ID of the employee.

  • Employment Status Class - Indicates the status of employment.

  • Client ID - Unique ID of the client to which the employee is associated with.

  • Dependent ID - The dependent ID associated with the client.

  • Dependent Name - Name of the dependent.

  • Relationship Code - Unique code that indicates the relationship of the dependent.

  • Orphaned Reason - Indicates the reason the record was orphaned. In this scenario, it was due to missing relationship codes.

[Image: screenshot]

  • Under the Results section, click Report to export a report of the orphaned records.

JIRA # WSP-1703, WSP-2449

New Report button

When you select Utility as Manage Orphaned Benefit Records, then for the options under the Orphaned Record Type drop-down, when you click Search to run the report filters, then under the Results section that is displayed, a new button named Report has been added to allow you to export the report of orphaned records for the selected orphaned record types.

[Image: screenshot]

Additionally, the report header name that is displayed on clicking the Report button for each of the options under the Orphaned Record Type drop-down are as follows:

Orphaned Record Type Report Name Header
Benefit Plan Setup Orphaned Benefit Plan Setup Records
Group Benefit Plan Types Orphaned Group Benefit Plan Type Records
Plan Types Orphaned Plan Type Records

JIRA # WSP-2451, WSP-2452, WSP-2453

New Overage Enrollees Report form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025%2009Sep/WSP-2016%20(Epic)%20WSP-2206.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025 09Sep/WSP-2016 (Epic) WSP-2206.htm

New Overage Enrollees Report form

A new form named Overage Enrollees Report has been introduced to run a report of overage enrollees for benefit plans where Maximum Age has been defined in the Benefit Rules eligibility criteria.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: This form is for Employee enrolles only.

To access this form, click Reports. Under Benefits|Report, click Overage Enrollees Report.

The form has the following section:

  • Selection Criteria- This section has the following field:

  • Client ID - This field is optional. Leave this field blank for this report to run for all clients. If you want to restrict this report to run for selected clients, enter their Client IDs here or click the Client ID link and select them from the Select Clients dialog box.

  • Click Run to view the report where the enrolled employee’s calculated age is greater than the Maximum Age indicated for the plan’s Benefit Rules.

The report page displays the following columns:

  • Client ID

  • Employee ID

  • Employee Name

  • Birth Date

  • Age

  • Benefit Plan ID

  • Benefit Plan Name

  • Cutoff Age

Note: You can export the report results into XLS file format.

  • Click Clear to clear the form at any time.

  • Click Close to close this form.

JIRA # WSP-2206, WSP-2231

New Maximum Age field

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025%2009Sep/WSP-2016%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025 09Sep/WSP-2016 (Epic).htm

New Maximum Age field

In order to set a maximum age value for eligibility in a given plan while administering client Benefit Plan Rules, a new field named Maximum Age has been added under the Eligibility Rules section of the following form:

  • Benefit Rules

  • Employee Benefit Rule Overrides

[Image: screenshot]

  • The newly added field is non-mandatory. Additionally, it accepts only numeric values. If you enter a non-numeric value, an error message stating, A valid integer is required. is displayed.

  • The value in the Maximum Age field must be greater than the value in the Minimum Age field. In the Minimum Age field, if you enter a value greater than the value in the Maximum Age field, a warning message stating, Minimum age should be less than maximum age. is displayed.

  • If the Maximum Age is set for the employee on the Benefit Rule or the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form for a given Plan, then while enrolling the employee in a benefit plan on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, a warning message is displayed if the employee’s actual age is greater than the Maximum Age. Additionally, when a rule for Maximum Age is defined on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form for a given Employee ID and Plan ID, the override rule takes precedence over any existing client rule for the field.

  • On the Benefit Rules Import form, the sample file has been updated to accept the parameter of the newly added Maximum Age field. The file accepts only integer value and is non-mandatory field. If you upload a file for the import process with Minimum Age greater than or equal to the Maximum Age, an error message is displayed.

JIRA # WSP-2205, WSP-2481, WSP-2487

Changes to the Retirement Plan Enrollment form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025%2009Sep/WSP-2250%20(Epic)%20WSP-2544%20&%20WSP-2513.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025 09Sep/WSP-2250 (Epic) WSP-2544 & WSP-2513.htm

Changes to the Retirement Plan Enrollment form

On the Retirement Plan Enrollment form, under the Election Details section, the Auto Escalation? field is now available to indicate whether Auto Escalation applies to an Elective Percent. This field will display only if the Auto Escalator field is checked for this retirement plan on the Benefit Plan Setup form.

A new read-only field named Next Auto Escalation Date is also added to display the next escalation date. This field is displayed only if you have checked the Auto Escalation? field. Additionally, when an employee is auto enrolled in a retirement plan, the Auto Escalation? field is automatically checked.

[Image: screenshot]

  • When you flag the Auto Escalation? field then, the Payroll Calculation process triggers a retirement auto enrollment record to be created for eligible employees using the calculated date with the defined auto enrollment percent (between 3% - 10%) up to the maximum defined amount which is set on the Benefit Plan Setup form.

  • Also, when an existing retirement plan enrollment has the Auto Escalation? field flagged and has a Next Auto Escalation Date which is less than or equal to the calculated payroll, then a new Election Detail is automatically created with an Effective Date equal to the defined Next Auto Escalation Date. The value in the Amount column for Elective Percent field reflects the prior election amount in addition to the auto escalation percent.

Please note the following validations on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form:

  • For an existing Retirement Plan Enrollment record, when the Auto Escalation? field is checked and if you change value in any field which affects employee election amounts for contributions, then while saving the form a warning message stating Changes have been made to employee contributions. Do you wish to remove ‘Auto Escalation’? is displayed.

  • You cannot select the Auto Escalation? checkbox if you are using Dollar as the value for Elective contribution method. If you use the Dollar as the value and select the Auto Escalation? checkbox, then a warning message stating, Auto Escalation cannot be enabled when the Elective contribution method is set to ‘Dollar’ is displayed.

New Auto Escalate On field

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025%2009Sep/WSP-2250%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025 09Sep/WSP-2250 (Epic).htm

New Auto Escalate On field

On the Benefit Plan Setup form, after you have selected the Plan Class as Retirement, then under the Eligibility Criteria section, a new field named Auto Escalate On has been added to define when the auto escalation must occur at the client level.

[Image: screenshot]

  • The newly added field is a mandatory field and is displayed only when you select the Auto Escalator checkbox.

  • This field has the following drop-down options:

  • –Select–- (This option operates the same as Plan Anniversary After 12 Months (Default) option)

  • Plan Anniversary After 12 Months (Default)- When this option is selected, then the calculated date for auto escalation should be the next Plan Anniversary Date which is equal to or greater than the Status Date (considered as Plan Anniversary date) assigned to the enrollment record (found on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form) plus 12 months.

  • Plan Anniversary- This option is considered to be the Start Date assigned to the Retirement Plan on the Benefit Plan Setup form. The plan enrollment uses the next Plan Anniversary Date as the calculated date for auto escalation.

  • Employee Enrollment Anniversary- This option is considered to be the Start Date assigned to the Employee’s retirement enrollment plan.

  • If the Premium Rate Group field in unchecked, then on clicking Save, the system verifies that there are no Premium Rate records associated with the selected Rate Group.

Changes to the Benefit Utilities form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025%2010Oct/WSP-1432%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025 10Oct/WSP-1432 (Epic).htm

Changes to the Benefit Utilities form

Under the Benefit Utilities section, a new utility named Unarchive Enrollments has been added to unarchive employees web enrollment configurations so that the users can re-enable an online workflow that had previously been archived.

[Image: screenshot]

When you select the Unarchive Enrollments utility, the Report Filters section is displayed.

Under the Reports Filters section:

  • Choose the Starting Archive Date and the Ending Archive Date. These fields are mandatory.

  • Client ID - This field is optional. Leave this field blank for this report to run for all clients. If you want to restrict this report to run for selected clients, enter their Client IDs here or click the Client ID link and select them from the Select Clients dialog box.

Now, click Search. A job control runs. Once the job control process is completed, click Close to view the list of archived employees.

The Results section displays the following columns:

  • Confirmation # - The unique confirmation ID.

  • Client ID - Unique ID of the client with which the employee is associated.

  • Employee Name - Name of the employee. It is displayed as a hyperlink. Clicking this opens the Employee Details form with the information of the selected employee.

  • Employment Status Class - Current status of the employee’s employment.

  • Enrollment Type - The type of web enrollment in which the employee is enrolled in.

  • Archive Date - Date on which the employee was archived.

  • WEO Status - Status of the weekend option premium.

  • Batch Number - The batch number in which the employee is.

  • Batch Status - Status of the batch number

  • Completed Batch - If the batch number in which the employee is has been completed or not.

  • Updated - Status of the updation.

Select the employee(s) that you want to unarchive and click Unarchive. Based on the number of records you have selected, a confirmation message stating, Archived Enrollments will be unarchived. Are you sure? is displayed.

  • Click Yes to unarchive the selected eligible Web Enrollment records.

  • Click No to remain on the form.
