New Prohibit 401(k) Deductions functionality

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025%2010Oct/WSP-2060%20(Epic).htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/2025 10Oct/WSP-2060 (Epic).htm

New Prohibit 401(k) Deductions functionality

On the Retirement Plans form, under the Deduction/Bill Code Overrides grid, a new column named Prohibit Deductions and Prohibit Billing has been added to prevent employee Retirement Plan Enrollments from being created with deduction types indicated as Prohibited on this form.

[Image: screenshot]

  • When you select the Prohibit Deductions or Prohibit Billing checkbox for any of the Deduction or Billing Code, then that code row clears any existing Deduction Code/Billing Code value and the row is disabled.

Additionally, when you save the form with a Retirement Plan record, the system check for the following validation for each Deduction or Billing Code on the form:

  • If Prohibit Deductions/Billing is unchecked:

  • record cannot be saved when corresponding Plan-level code is null and Global Setting is null.

  • record can be saved when either corresponding Plan-level code is not null or Global Setting is not null or both values are not null.

  • If Prohibit Deductions/Billing is checked:

  • record can be saved regardless of whether corresponding Plan-level code is null and/or Global Setting is null.

JIRA # WSP-2655

Changes to the Retirement Plan Enrollment form

On the Retirement Plans form, under the Deduction/Bill Code Overrides grid, when the Prohibit Deductions is checked for a Retirement Plan Deduction Code then on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form, under the Election Details section, when you create a new Retirement Election detail, the corresponding Retirement Plan Enrollment Election Type field(s) gets disabled.

Additionally, if a previous election exists with values in the now prohibited Election Type, the new effective date does not populate data in to the prohibited (now disabled) field.

If an election amount already exists on the detail record for a prohibited deduction code type, and when you try to save the form, then a warning message stating, This retirement plan prohibits [deduction type] elections. Create a new enrollment detail record to update the employee elections. is displayed.

JIRA # WSP-2656

Changes to the Process Payroll form

  • When an employee is enrolled in a Retirement Plan that has one or more Deduction Types flagged as Prohibited and an employee’s existing elections in that plan reflect a deferral of the prohibited Deduction Type, then on the Process Payroll form, when you initialize a payroll for that employee, a warning message stating, has retirement elections in prohibited by the plan setup. Deductions will not be taken. is displayed.

[Image: screenshot]

Below is the table that shows the affected Retirement Plan Enrollment Deferrals for contributions due to prohibited Retirement Plan Deduction Code:

Prohibited Retirement Plan Deduction Code on the Retirement Plans form — Retirement Plan Enrollment Deferrals for contributions that shows calculation error/ payroll warning on the Process Payroll form

Employee Deferral Deduction Code — Pre-Tax Contribution

Employee Catch-Up Deduction Code — Catch-Up Contribution

Employee Post-Tax Deduction Code — Post-Tax Contribution

Roth Post-Tax Deduction Code — Roth Contribution

Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code — Roth Catch-Up Contribution

  • On the System Parameters form, under the Global Codes Setup section, if the Employer Match Billing Code is configured and at the same time a Retirement Plan is configured for the Employer Match Bill Code with the Prohibit Billing checkbox selected, then the payroll process ignores the global bill code and does not produce any employer match billing for the plan in the payroll.

JIRA # WSP-2657, WSP-2787

Changes to the Slavic 401K Import form

On the Slavic 401K Import form, while performing the Slavic 401K import process, the following validations has been added:

  • On the Retirement Plans form, if the Prohibit Deductions is checked for the Employee Deferral Deduction Code or the Employee Catch-up Deduction Code for the indicated retirement plan and the employee election reflects type D in column D of the import file, then on the Slavic 401K Import form, when you try the import process, an error message stating, Deferral type prohibited by plan setup, cannot import row . is displayed and the import process fails.

  • On the Retirement Plans form, if the Prohibit Deductions is checked for the Roth Post-tax Deduction Code or the Roth Catch-up Deduction Code for the indicated retirement plan and the employee election reflects type R in column D of the import file, then on the Slavic 401K Import form, when you try the import process, an error message stating, Deferral type prohibited by plan setup, cannot import row . is displayed and the import process fails.

[Image: screenshot]

JIRA # WSP-2664

Changes to the Benefit Plan Setup form

On the Retirement Plans form, if a retirement plan is configured with the Employee Deferral Deduction Code flagged to Prohibit Deductions, then on the Benefit Plan Setup form, when you set Plan Class as Retirement and select the retirement plan, then under the Eligibility Criteria section, the Auto Enrollment and the Auto Enrollment Percent fields are disabled.

For the prohibited retirement plan, if there is a value in the Auto Enrollment and Auto Enrollment Percent fields, then the existing values are displayed as it is but the fields remains disabled. When you save the form with existing values in these fields, then a warning message stating, This Retirement Plan has been updated to prohibit pre-tax contributions used for Auto-enrollment functionality. Saving this record will clear the values in the Auto-enrollment fields. Would you like to proceed? is displayed.

Deductions will not be taken. is displayed in the Payroll Validation Report output. This error message is displayed on the report shown on the screen as well as in the downloaded .csv output file.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/BA_Fixes_202401_MR.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/BA_Fixes_202401_MR.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we strive to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed.

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
BA-1705 Previously, if you added a Life Insurance Benefit Plan for an employee prior to adding a Medical Plan for the same employee on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form (Benefit Enrollment Maintenance > Benefit Enrollments > Employee Benefits Enrollment), an incorrect error message displayed which listed the previously selected Life Insurance Plan ID as a Medical Plan: “Warning! Employee is already active in another medical plan [Currently Selected Medical Plan ID]. Warning! Employee is already active in another medical plan [Previously Selected Life Insurance Plan ID].” You could then select the Life Insurance Plan in the Plan to Replace field (with a Medical Plan still selected in the Benefit Plan field) and complete the enrollment record. This resulted in the employee’s previously added Life Insurance Benefit Plan being updated to a Status of Terminated. This issue is fixed.
BA-1792 On the At a Glance panel of the Enhanced Dashboard in Employee Benefit Enrollments > Employees view (with an employee selected to view the employee details), if you selected Actions > Benefit Adjustments on a Plan ID line item, the Employee field was editable instead of Read Only as it had been in prior releases. This issue is fixed. Now, when you navigate from the At a Glance panel of the Enhanced Dashboard in Employee Benefit Enrollments > Employees view to access an employee’s Benefit Adjustments, the Employee field is Read Only.
BA-1801 On the At a Glance panel of the Enhanced Dashboard in Employee Benefit Enrollments > Employees view (with an employee selected to view the employee details), if you clicked a Plan ID link to view the Employee Benefit Enrollments form, the Employee field label was being overwritten by other text causing it to be illegible. Additionally, the Employee field was editable instead of Read Only as it had been in prior releases. This issue is fixed. Now, when you navigate from the At a Glance panel of the Enhanced Dashboard in Employee Benefit Enrollments > Employees to view the Employee Benefits Enrollments form by clicking the Plan ID link, the Employee field label is no longer being overwritten by other text and Employee field is Read Only.
BA-1816 Previously, the date formatting of the Birth Date column on the File Content tab of the Employee Dependents Data Import (Operations > Import Processing > Data Import Tool > Import Template = Employee Dependents) was inconsistent as it displayed date values as formatted in the import file. Examples: 2/5/20, 02/05/2020, 02/05/20. This issue is fixed. Now, the Birth Date column displays all date values in the same two-digit month, two-digit day, and four-digit year format which is the same format they will be in once imported into the system. Example: 02/05/2020.
BA-1960 Previously, on the Benefit Adjustments form (Benefit Enrollment Maintenance > Benefit Enrollments > Benefit Adjustments) the Filter by Plan dropdown selector field overlapped part of the Benefit Plan description (i.e., Plan Name) that displays to the right of the field. This issue occurred when the Plan Name was longer than approximately 17 characters. This issue is fixed.
BA-2111 Previously, you could not manually add a Benefit Plan ID that contained any lowercase letters to the Plan field of the Eligible Benefits - Group Benefits Plans section on the Benefit Groups form (Benefit Plan Maintenance > Group Benefit Plans (Client) > Benefit Groups). This issue is fixed. Now you can manually add a Benefit Plan ID containing lowercase letters to the Benefit Groups form.
BA-2126 Previously, you could not enter negative numbers in the Transaction Amount field with a Transaction Type of Service Fee or Adjustment on the COBRA Transaction Entry form (COBRA Processing > COBRA Processing > COBRA Transaction Entry). This issue is fixed. You can now enter negative amounts for Service Fee and Adjustment on the COBRA Transaction Entry form.
BA-2157 Previously, there was a form refresh issue when accessing an Employee Dependent record from the Employee Benefits Enrollment form using the specific scenario below: 1. Access the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, select an employee (using the Employee link), and select a Benefit Plan. 2. Select Dependents on the Actions menu and then select a Dependent ID on the Employee Dependents form. 3. Close the Employee Dependents form. 4. Select a different employee on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form (using the Employee link), and select a Benefit Plan. 5. Select Dependents on the Actions menu and then select a Dependent ID on the Employee Dependents form. 6. Close the Employee Dependents form. 7. Now, select the same employee originally selected in Step 1 (using the Employee link), and select a Benefit Plan. 8. Select Dependents on the Actions menu and then select a Dependent ID on the Employee Dependents form. Prior Result:The dependent record for the previously selected employee (Step 4) displayed. This issue is fixed.
BA-2158 Previously, enabling the PENDING-BILL-RATE-CLIENT or PENDING-BILL-RATE-GLOBAL custom feature codes created a field display issue on the Benefit Plan Setup form. When you changed the Plan Class on the Benefit Plan Setup form from Group Benefits to any other Plan Class, two fields related to the custom feature codes (Pend Prem Rate Group and Pend Prem Rate Group Effective Date) that were previously displaying in the Group Benefits Setup section of the Benefit Plan Setup form moved to the top of the form. The fields appeared to be “floating” as they were no longer anchored to a section of the form. This issue is fixed.
BA-2168 Previously, when you used the multi-select function to add additional plans to a Benefit Group (Benefit Plan Maintenance > Group Benefit Plans (Client) > Benefit Groups) and there were one or more previously selected plans already displayed in the “Eligible Benefits - Group Benefit Plans” section, the system attempted to add the existing selections to the list again while also the newly selected plans. This resulted in the following error: “Value [Plan ID] has already been entered here.” This issue is fixed.
BA-2194 Previously, COBRA Election Notice Monthly Premium calculation incorrectly used Premium Rates (i.e., Actual Cost) when the COBRA Premiums Based On field on the COBRA Processing Parameters form (COBRA Processing > COBRA Setup > COBRA Processing Parameters) was set to Standard Billing. This issue is fixed. Now, the COBRA Election Notice Monthly Premium calculations are derived as follows: - When the COBRA Premiums Based On field on the COBRA Processing Parameters form is set to Standard Billing, the Monthly Premium equals Billing Rate plus the percentage entered in the COBRA Insurance Premium Markup field. - When the COBRA Premiums Based On field on the COBRA Processing Parameters form is set to Actual Cost, the Monthly Premium equals Premium Rate plus the percentage entered in the COBRA Insurance Premium Markup field. > Note: Note: The default COBRA Premium Markup is 2%.
BA-2260 Previously, if you moved an employee to a new benefit group, any prior Life Insurance enrollment record could not be accessed (Benefit Enrollment Maintenance > Benefit Enrollments > Employee Benefits Enrollment) if there was no benefit rule on the new client or the new benefit group dating back to the original coverage start date of the enrollment. An error displayed and the record could not be opened. This issue is fixed. Now, the enrollment record displays with the following warning message: “No Benefit Rule date found for coverage date {coverage start date} BENEFIT RULE MISSING, Client# {client number} Group: {group ID}” Click OK on the warning message to proceed with opening the enrollment record.
BA-2490 Previously, if you cloned a client (Client > Action > Clone Client) and the Benefit Groups option was not selected under “What to Clone”, the system incorrectly created a Benefit Group association using the New Client ID value as the Benefit Group ID. The associated Benefit Group ID did not actually exist. Therefore, when you added benefit plans to the newly cloned client record, the following error displayed: “Warning: There are issues with this plan’s set-up. Please fix the items listed. Unable to find any Benefits Rules for Benefit Group [Associated Benefit Group ID].” This issue is fixed. Now, when you clone a client, only the default PRIMARY Benefit Group is associated with the cloned client if the Benefit Groups option is not selected as an item to clone in the “What to Clone” section of the Clone Client form. If the Benefit Groups option is selected as an item to clone in the “What to Clone” section of the Clone Client form, the benefit groups associations on the “cloned from” record are added to the cloned client record.
BA-2493 Previously, the validation of Gender on the Employee Dependents Import (Operations > Import Processing > Data Import Tool > Import Template = Employee Dependents) was incorrect. A correct Gender value of M or F resulted in the system erroneously displaying “Error uploading file content. See Messages tab for details.” during the import. The Messages tab displayed: “Error: Gender on line 2 must be M or F”. This issue is fixed. This system now properly evaluates and validates M or F Gender values and no longer displays the import errors.
BA-2499 Previously, when adding a new Employee Benefit Rule Override (Benefit Enrollment Maintenance > Benefit Enrollments > Employee Benefit Rule Overrides) for a Life Insurance Plan and selecting a Multiplier Pay Basis in the Coverage Rules section, upon Save, the Multiplier Pay Basis selection was not held. When you returned to the record the field was reset to –Select–. This issue is fixed. The Multiplier Pay Basis selection is now held upon Save.
BA-2503 Previously, the first occurrence of the word “maximum” was misspelled on the following error message that displays on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form (Benefit Enrollment Maintenance > Benefit Enrollments > Employee Benefits Enrollment) when you enter a life insurance plan with an age reduction schedule whereby the coverage amount entered causes the maximum coverage basis to be exceeded: “An age reduction schedule is being applied based on the group benefit plan setup. The coverage amount $X,XXX,XXX.XX entered results in a coverage basis, $X,XXX,XXX.XX that exceeds the maximum amount of $X,XXX,XXX.XX . The maximum coverage amount you can enter is $X,XXX,XXX.XX.” This issue is fixed.
BA-2509 Previously, when you used Copy Benefit Plan on the Group Benefit Plan Actions menu (Benefit Plan Maintenance > Group Benefit Plans (Global) > Group Benefit Plans > Actions) to copy to a new Plan ID containing lowercase letters in the Benefit Plan ID to Copy to field (Client > Change > Copy Benefit Plan), the copy function converted all lowercase letters to uppercase. The issue is fixed. Now, the new Plan ID is copied as entered.
BA-2526 Previously, the drop down selector for the Extra Voucher Types field located in the Extra Options section of the Retirement Plan Enrollment form (Benefit Enrollment Maintenance > Retirement Enrollments > Retirement Plan Enrollment) did not display for certain users due to a caching issue. This issue is fixed.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/BA_Fixes_202403_QR.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/BA_Fixes_202403_QR.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the March 2024 quarterly release.

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
BA-3163 Previously, life coverage amount was getting auto updated to salary multiplier and/or max coverage when previously enrolled in $0 coverage. When coverage is entered manually and when the employee coverage amount is zero or less than the minimum coverage defined, payroll should not alter the coverage amount and the coverage min/max should be ignored. However, when the employee coverage amount is zero, the payroll process in PrismHR was updating the employee coverage to the calculated coverage maximum based on the defined plan parameters. This is now resolved via hotfix CM-3858. Now, when coverage is entered manually and when the employee coverage amount is zero or less than the minimum coverage defined, payroll does not alter the coverage amount and the coverage min/max is ignored.
BA-2667 Previously, for a medical plan that was Tobacco Banded, Gender Banded, Spouse Gender Banded, Age Banded, and Premium Rates Vary by Network was set to Yes, on the Group Benefit Plans form, then on the Premium Rates form: - The value in the To Age field in the first line was getting cleared out AND - The value in the From Age field in the second line defaulted to 1. Now, for a medical plan that is Tobacco Banded, Gender Banded, Spouse Gender Banded, Age Banded, and Premium Rates Vary by Network is set to Yes, on the Group Benefit Plans form, then all the fields on the Premium Rates form behave as expected.
  • The value in the To Age field in the first line was getting cleared out AND
  • The value in the From Age field in the second line defaulted to 1. | BA-2479 | Previously, on the Client Benefit Plan Defaults form, the 4th option on the Coverage Ends On dropdown incorrectly stated, “When Employee’s Term Date is X day of a month then benefits end 15th of Month else End of Month”. | Now, on the Client Benefit Plan Defaults form, the 4th option on the Coverage Ends On dropdown correctly states “When Employee’s Term Date <= Xth of month benefits stop End of Previous Month else End of Current Month”. | | BA-2455 | Previously, if you manually added a new effective date or processed payroll for a fully automatic plan going through Benefit Enrollment, the system did not correctly calculate the coverage basis amount. | Now, if you manually add a new effective date or process payroll for a fully automatic plan going through Benefit Enrollment, the system correctly calculates the coverage basis amount. | | BA-2442 | Previously, age reduction was not occurring in electronic enrollment when a plan was set to Manual Calculation. | Now, age reduction correctly occurs in electronic enrollment when a plan is set to Manual Calculation. | | BA-2300 | Previously, in some scenarios, on the Benefit Rules form, when a user with inquiry access selected the Benefit Plan and the Effective Date that was not equal to or was less than the oldest billing rate date, irrespective of your response to the warning message, the Contribution Method dropdown displayed only for the top row (EE). | Now, on the Benefit Rules form, when a user with inquiry access selects the Benefit Plan and the Effective Date that is not equal to or is less than the oldest billing rate date, irrespective of your response to the warning message, the Contribution Method dropdown displays correctly for all rows. | | BA-2239 | Previously, when coverage was entered manually, employees who fell within the Age Reduction Schedule (i.e. 65 and older) were defaulting to 10,000 in Coverage in the online enrollment ONLY, when the End Coverage Amount on the Group Benefit Plan (Global) setup was 600,000 or greater. This would also happen if the Percent of Full Coverage was less than 60%. The system was only allowing the employee to elect 10K if they fell within an age which reduced more than 60% of coverage. | Now, under the same conditions, employees can elect more than 10K of coverage. | | BA-1915 | Previously, on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, if a plan displayed Underwriting Questions and if you selected the Cancel button or made changes to the Benefit Plan field, the questions on Underwriting Questions section would not clear. | Now, on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, if a plan displays ‘Underwriting Questions’, and if you select the Cancel button or make changes to the Benefit Plan field, the questions on Underwriting Questions section clears. | | BA-1901 | Previously, on the Group Benefit Plans form, under the Group Benefit Plans section when a Life Insurance plan was set up with Coverage Entered Manually selected for the Manual Calculation field, the system ignored the Employee Salary Multiplier setting under the Coverage Amounts section, and allowed employees to elect a maximum coverage amount that exceeded the maximum allowed by the multiplier. For example, if an employee earned 50K and the life insurance plan was set up with a multiplier to allow the employee to elect up to 3 times the salary, with a maximum coverage amount of $300,000, the maximum election should cap at 150K. However, the employee was able to elect 175K. | Now, the system is correctly using the salary multiplier as a limiter when determining maximum coverage. | ========================================================================

BA-2920 Previously, the system incorrectly allowed the Benefit Plan ID field to be editable for Billing Rates or Premium Rates for an Insurance Class other than Medical, Dental or Vision. Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/BA_Fixes_202405_MR.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/BA_Fixes_202405_MR.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following is a recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the May 2024 Monthly release.

Benefit Group History record created for every manual change

To ensure that the system always correctly captures any manual change made to the Benefit Group field, from now on, a Benefit Group History record will be created when a user manually changes the Benefit Group assigned to an employee on the Work tab of the Employee Details form. This change becomes effective immediately and the Benefit Group History record is stamped with an Effective Date which matches the date the change was made.

The Benefit Group field on the Employee Details form will remain enabled. When a user changes the value assigned to this field and selects “Save”, a Benefit Group History record will be created and stamped with the current date as the Effective Date. Benefit Group History records will be displayed on the Benefit Group History form and Benefit Group History Adjustment form.

Warning Scenario 1:

If a Benefit Group History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the current date (say if the current date is 04/24/2024), then the following warning message will display when the user enters a new value in the Benefit Group field:

[Image: screenshot]

  • Yes: If selected, the modal will close. The data on the form will be updated to the value the user entered and the prior history record will be replaced with the current data once “Save” is selected on the Employee Details form.

  • No: If selected, the modal should close and the previous value should be restored in the Benefit Group field. No record will be replaced or written when “Save” is selected on the Employee Details form.

Warning Scenario 2:

If a Benefit Group History record currently exists with an Effective Date greater than the current date (say Effective Date of 04/26/2024 if the current date is 04/24/2024), then the following warning message should display when the user enters a new value in the Benefit Group field:

[Image: screenshot]

  • Yes: If selected, the modal will close. The data on the form will be updated to the value the user entered and a new Benefit Group History record will be created with the current data once “Save” is selected on the Employee Details form.

  • No: If selected, the modal will close and the previous value will be restored in the Benefit Group field. No record will be replaced or written when “Save” is selected on the Employee Details form.

Warning Scenario 3:

If a Benefit Group History record currently exists with an Effective Date equal to the current date (say current date is 04/24/2024) AND a Benefit Group History record also exists with an Effective Date greater than the current date (say 05/01/2024), the following warning message should display when the user enters a value in the Benefit Group field:

[Image: screenshot]

  • Yes: If selected, the modal will close. The data on the form will be updated to the value the user entered and the prior Benefit Group History record will be replaced with the current data once “Save” is selected on the Employee Details form.

  • No: If selected, the modal will close and the previous value will be restored in the Benefit Group field. No record will be replaced or written when “Save” is selected on the Employee Details form.

JIRA # BA-3298

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/BA_Fixes_202409_QR.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/BA_Fixes_202409_QR.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the September 2024 quarterly release.

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
BA-3600 Previously, the Retirement Register Adjustment incorrectly showed an error stating This transaction has already been posted. You may not post it again for new transactions when clicking save after resizing browser window. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3560 Previously, on the Retirement Plan Years form, under the Plan Year Reporting Periods section, you could enter the same value multiple times for the Period column. Now, on the Retirement Plan Years form, under the Plan Year Reporting Periods section, you can only enter unique values for the Period column. No duplicate values will be allowed.
BA-3405 Previously, when a change was made to the Wellness Qualification Status and Assessment Completion Date fields on the Employee Details form, the Wellness Status History form did not keep a full history causing administrative challenges with future dated changes. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3334 Previously, when an employee was hired mid-month (say 06/08/2024) in an auto enrolled plan with a 30 day waiting period (where Coverage Starts on 07/08/2024), the system was incorrectly creating a negative Benefit Adjustment for the prior month (202406), which is before the Benefit Effective Date. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3329 Previously, from the Group Benefit Plans form, under Actions menu when you chose the Premium Rates form BENEFIT.FRMED.NETWORK.RG.RATES.MNT, after selecting an option from the drop-down for the Network ID field the Service Area did not display on the right of the field. Now, from the Group Benefit Plans form, under Actions menu when you choose the Premium Rates form BENEFIT.FRMED.NETWORK.RG.RATES.MNT, after selecting an option from the drop-down for the Network ID field the Service Area displays on the right of the field.
BA-3191 Previously, when a plan was set up on the Group Benefit Plans form with: Insurance Class = Medical, Dental, or Vision Gender Banded = Selected Spouse Gender Banded = Selected AND With a Plan Type that is for Employee + Spouse or Family Coverage AND At least one existing Effective Date, then the Existing Effective Dates dropdown list did not appear for certain scenarios. Now, this is fixed
BA-3096 Previously, regarding: Enrollment: Given that an employee has coverage in a GTL eligible Life plan where the Deduction Start Date is after the Coverage Start Date, the taxable fringe pay amount (GTL) is not triggered when payroll is calculated/processed for a pay date that falls between the Deduction Start Date and Coverage Start Date. This situation usually occurs when an enrollment record is created and the current date is after the Coverage Start Date on the enrollment. In most cases, Benefit Adjustments have been created for the premium owed for this period of time. AND Termination: Given that an employee has coverage in a GTL eligible Life plan where the Deduction End Date is before the Coverage End Date, the taxable fringe pay amount (GTL) is not triggered when payroll is calculated/processed for a pay date that falls between the Deduction End Date and Coverage End Date. In most cases, Benefit Adjustments have been created for the premium owed for this period of time. Now this issue is fixed. The GTL logic will be utilized during the payroll process so that Benefit Deductions (to include Benefit Adjustments) for applicable Benefit Plans are included. The current GTL rounding, age, and basic calculation logic will not be changed. Given that an employee has coverage in a GTL eligible Life plan as of their pay date, the GTL calculation will be triggered, specified by using the lesser of the Coverage Start vs Deduction Start and greater of the Coverage End vs Deduction End dates to determine if the GTL calculation should occur.
BA-3009 Previously, on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form, once you clicked the New Effective Date hyperlink and entered a new Effective Date, then the all the relevant fields were not clearing as expected. Now, this is fixed.
BA-2957 Previously, on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form, once you clicked the Alternate Contribution Plan hyperlink, the Description column on the selector was blank. Now, on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form, once you click the Alternate Contribution Plan hyperlink, all the columns on the selector display as expected.
BA-2736 Previously, when a Benefit Plan was flagged as One Month Prepay and Add One Month For Prepay, and a Pending Premium Rate Group was assigned, the Pending Premium Rate Group was not being applied to the prepay premium cost on the payroll. Now, this is fixed.
BA-1588 Previously, when setting up an Import Definition in Benefit Import Maintenance, the system did not allow more than one SKIP field. Now, when setting up an Import Definition in Benefit Import Maintenance, the system allows as many SKIP fields necessary.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/BA_Fixes_202410_MR.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/BA_Fixes_202410_MR.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the October 2024 monthly release.

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
BA-3784 Previously, for a medical, dental or vision benefit plan with networks, where premium rate groups vary by network, the premium rate group form did not display the Rate Group on form report after a Network is displayed. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3961 Previously, after completing a transaction on the Retirement Register Adjustments form, if you moved away to a different form and then came back to the Retirement Register Adjustments form and reopened the transaction mentioned above, then the Plan field displayed blank for that transaction which was incorrect. Now, after completing a transaction on the Retirement Register Adjustments form, if you move away to a different form and then come back to the Retirement Register Adjustments form and reopen the transaction mentioned above, then the Plan field displays the correct benefit plan for that transaction.
BA-3943 Previously, when a new Effective Date was entered on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form, the date immediately disappeared from the form. Now, when a new Effective Date is entered on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form, the new date does not disappear from the form.
BA-3916 Previously, on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form, after selecting an employee without an active retirement enrollment record if you selected a Retirement Plan, and then resized the window to a smaller window and then back to full size, then the Retirement Plan field cleared out. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3899 Previously, on the Benefit Rules form, when the Contribution rule amounts made by Company or Employee field was set to Company, and under the Contribution Rules section the Contribution Method was set to Percentage, then the Total Contribution and the Total Billed fields did not populate the correct values. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3884 Previously, the Employee ID field got cleared upon resizing the browser on the standalone Employee Retirement Loans form. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3829 Previously, on the Employee Retirement Plan Register form, for a selected Employee ID, the Plan ID dropdown displayed the current plan along with any other prior plans which the employee was enrolled in, all with the status of the current enrolled plan. Now, on the Employee Retirement Plan Register form, for a selected Employee ID, the Plan ID dropdown displays only the current plan as having an active status and any other prior plans which the employee was enrolled in with no status.
BA-3806 Previously, if there was an HSA and a Dependent care flex spend account type on a posted payroll voucher, both hyperlinks only opened one Deduction Carryover Trace. It wasn’t pulling up the correct applicable trace when there were more than one flex spend account type hyperlink on the posted payroll voucher. (This was only applicable to HSA and Dependent care flex spend account types that are mid-year plans) Now, this is fixed.
BA-3761 Previously, whenever you clicked Save on the Employee Details form for an employee, a new Benefit Group History record was being created for that employee even if the Benefit Group was not changed. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3686 Previously, on the Group Benefit Plans form, under the Web Enrollment Parameters section, you incorrectly received an error message stating That is not a defined attribute when tabbing through blank column under the Process Attribute field. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3655 Previously, on the Benefit Plan Setup form, when adding a Flexible Spending Plan Class, under some scenarios, upon Save the Employment Type(s) field options selected were not saved for the FSA plan. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3654 Previously, under some scenarios, the custom feature code FAILINITSCORPFLEX was not working. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3641 Previously, on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, in some scenarios, an additional blank dependent row was added to the Covered Dependents section after adding more than one covered dependent. Now, this is fixed.

Other Fixes

The following are some other issues that we’ve fixed in the October 2024 monthly release.

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
WSP-863 Previously, on the Enrollment Options form, the Spanish Header incorrectly read Life Events Documents Required (Spanish). Now, on the Enrollment Options form, the Spanish Header correctly reads Life Events - Documents Required (Spanish).
WSP-820 Previously, if an eligible record was created manually on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form for an employee having a dependent spouse, having Insurance Class selected as Life Insurance, Short Term Disability or Long Term Disability, and the Status is changed to Active, then a user was unable to enter a coverage amount in the Coverage field for the spouse. Now, if an eligible record is created manually on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form for an employee having a dependent spouse, having Insurance Class selected as Life Insurance, Short Term Disability or Long Term Disability, and the Status is changed to Active, then a user is able to enter a coverage amount in the Coverage field for the spouse.
WSP-821 Previously, even if a user did not have access to the Employee Details form but had full access to the any of the following forms, they were still able to access employee details on the Employee Details form by clicking the Employee ID hyperlink on the Employees Assigned To form listed under the [Image: screenshot] menu on that form. 1. Benefit Groups 2. Divisions 3. Departments 4. Positions 5. Projects 6. Worksite Locations 7. Shifts 8. Skills Now, this is fixed.

  2. Divisions
  3. Departments
  4. Positions
  5. Projects
  6. Worksite Locations
  7. Shifts

  8. Skills

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/BA_Fixes_202411_QR.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/BA_Fixes_202411_QR.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the November 2024 monthly release.

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
BA-4016 Previously, in some scenarios, while processing payrolls, the system incorrectly generated an error stating Retirement Plan match rules not setup for Group:0 for an employee even though Group 0 did not exist under the Benefit Groups form. You had to soft save the Employee Retirement Plan Register for the employee to process payroll for that employee. Now this is fixed.
BA-4014 Previously, once you arrived at the Retirement Match Rules form for the first time for a client, and clicked the Benefit Group hyperlink, the selector showed only one benefit group. However, if you visited the Benefit Groups form and clicked the Benefit Group hyperlink, the selector showed all the applicable benefit groups. Now when you revisited the Retirement Match Rules form for the same client, and clicked the Benefit Group hyperlink, the selector showed all the applicable benefit groups. Now, this is fixed.
BA-4003 Previously, when you accessed the Benefit Adjustments form for an employee via the Enhanced Dashboard option, and then for a listed Benefit Plan once you changed the number of Cycles, the listed Benefit Plan ID disappeared once you returned to the Adjustment Details form after you clicked the Adjust button. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3923 Previously, when Relation was set up as a required field either on the New Hire and Dependent Field Overrides form or on the New Hire and Dependent Required Fields (Global) form, then on the Employee Dependents form if you selected the – Select – option after selecting any other option from the dropdown, then you received an incorrect error message stating Since the Relation Type is (D)ependent, you must indicate the Dependent Relation Code for this person! Press F3 for help. Now, this is fixed. On the Employee Dependents form, you only get an error message stating Relation is required when setting up a Dependent if you try to save a dependent without assigning a Relation from the dropdown.
BA-3905 Previously, users who did not have access to employee payroll vouchers were still able to view them using the Voucher hyperlink under the Account Activity section on the Employee Flexible Spending Accounts Inquiry form. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3889 Previously, on the Benefit Rules form, the description of the selected Benefit Group and Benefit Plan fields still displayed on the right even after it was included in the dropdown. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3880 Previously, the Retirement Plan field on the Employee Retirement Loans form was not disabled for an existing employee loan. Now, the Retirement Plan field on the Employee Retirement Loans form is disabled for an existing employee loan.
BA-3849 Previously, if you had Inquiry access to the Employee Retirement Plan Register form, you could not select the dropdown options for the fields on the form. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3465 Previously, on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form, if an Alternative Contribution Rate Group was entered but if there was no value in the Alternate Contribution Plan field, then upon Save, the values, if any, on the Employee Contribution Rules section were not getting cleared out. Now, on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form, if an Alternative Contribution Rate Group is entered but if there is no value in the Alternate Contribution Plan field, then upon Save, the value in the Alternative Contribution Rate Group field and the values if any on the Employee Contribution Rules section will clear out. You will receive a message stating An Alternate Contribution Plan has not been defined. The Alternative Contribution Rate Group and the Contribution Rules table (if applicable) will be cleared out.
BA-3000 Previously, mid year HSA plans with deduction carryover were not stopping HSA Matches when reaching tax year limit. Now, for mid year HSA plans, once the combined Company/PEO Match and Employee Contributions have met the tax year limit, no further Company/PEO Match and Employee Contributions are taken. Only ‘Standard’ HSA Match types are supported at this time.

BA-4314 Previously, mid-year HSA Deduction Carryover was calculating incorrect estimated total tax year amounts. Now, this is fixed. Only Standard HSA Match types are supported at this time.
BA-4152 Previously, in some scenarios, the Network ID dropdown on Employee Benefits Enrollment form displayed as blank and incorrectly generated an error stating 0 is not a valid network for plan . Now, this is fixed.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/BA_Fixes_202501_MR.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/BA_Fixes_202501_MR.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the January 2025 monthly release.

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
BA-4264 Previously, on the Group Benefit Plans form, all fields other than the Benefit Plan ID field cleared out when the browser was resized down. Now, this is fixed.
BA-4258 Previously, for Pre-Pay plans, when a Deduction Start Date was prior to the Coverage Starts Date, an incorrect benefit adjustment was being created Now, this is fixed.
BA-4178 Previously, on the Benefit Group Change form, if you entered a Benefit Group Start Date and then removed it, even before you saved the form, an error message stating New Job Start Date is mandatory displayed which was not correct. Now, on the Benefit Group Change form, under a similar circumstance, the error message reads New Start Date is mandatory.
BA-4165 Previously, when a future-dated Cafe Dollar contribution was added to an employee’s Benefit Group, that contribution was incorrectly applied to the employee’s current deduction. Now, future-dated Cafe Dollar contributions will not be applied to an employee’s benefit deduction until the effective date of that contribution.
BA-4110 Previously, on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form, after you had selected an Employee and without making any changes on the form clicked on the Import Retirement Plan Adjustment Quicklink under the Retirement Register Adjustments section, you got an error stating You have unsaved changes. Are you sure you want to leave? which was incorrect. Now, this is fixed.
BA-4097 Previously, when you had a Benefit Plan ID selected on the Group Benefit Plans form, and then you used the Back Office button to navigate to the Group Benefit Plans form again, you received an error stating Record BENEFIT.PLANSMAINT is not on file BENEFIT.PLAN.TYPES*. However, you could access the Group Benefit Plans form again using the search bar above without any error. Now, this is fixed.
BA-4084 Previously, if you got a message stating Create Your PrismONE ID either on My Home or on the Enhanced dashboard, upon closing the message the dashboard did not display the required information. Now, this is fixed.
BA-4068 Previously, though the Employee Benefits Rule Overrides form opened in a collapsed state until you selected a Benefit Plan or an existing plan to expand it, upon Save, Delete or Cancel, the form did not return to its initial collapsed state but remained in the expanded state. Now, this is fixed.
BA-4065 Previously, when you accessed the Employee Benefit Overview form using the [Image: screenshot] menu from the Employee Details form, the Dependent and the Coverage History information for the selected employee did not populate on the form in the first selection. Now, this is fixed.
BA-4029 Previously, on the Benefit Plan Setup form, after you had selected Flexible Spending as the Plan Class, once you checked the Use Benefit Groups field, a white space appeared below the section. This was purely a display issue with no impact on functionality. Now, this is fixed.
BA-4018 Previously, if you had INQUIRY access only to the Employee Retirement Plan Register form, if you opened a payroll voucher and then closed it on the form for an employee, then the Plan Year and Plan Year Period dropdowns wiped out and all applicable data. Now, this is fixed.
BA-4002 Previously, on the Adjustment Details form, you were able to adjust Cycles to a value lower than Cycles Billed which was incorrect. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3999 Previously, when an employee had been in multiple retirement plans and had transactions processed in a plan that was not the plan he was currently enrolled in, then on the Retirement Register Adjustment form, if you selected the prior transaction, the Plan ID populated with the current enrollment plan and not the plan the transaction was for. This was a display only issue and the data were correct. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3972 Previously, the system allowed you to incorrectly assign employees using the Employee Details form to a Benefit Group which had a Stop New Use On date in the past. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3766 Previously, enabling the PENDING-BILL-RATE-CLIENT or PENDING-BILL-RATE-GLOBAL custom feature codes created a field display issue on the Benefit Plans Setup form. When you changed the Plan Class on the Benefit Plans Setup form from Group Benefits to any other Plan Class, two fields related to the custom feature codes (Pend Prem Rate Group and Pend Prem Rate Group Effective Date) that previously displayed in the Group Benefits Setup section of the Benefit Plans Setup form moved to the top of the form. The fields appeared to be “floating” as they were no longer anchored to a section of the form. Now, this is fixed.

Other Fixes

The following are some other issues that we’ve fixed in the January 2025 monthly release.

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
WSP-1288 Previously, on the Benefit Rules form, after you had selected the Benefit Group, Benefit Plan and the Effective Date fields, if you resized the window, then the Contribution Rules section disappeared from the form. You had to reselect all the above fields to make it reappear on the form. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-1283 Previously, on the Benefit Plan Setup form, for Plan Class selected as Flexible Spending and the Use Benefit Groups field being checked, if you opened the Eligibility by Benefit Group form using the [Image: screenshot] menu and the closed it, then a drop-down incorrectly displayed in the gray area at the bottom of the form. Now, this is fixed.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/BA_Fixes_202503_QR.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/BA_Fixes_202503_QR.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the March 2025 quarterly release.

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
BA-4525 Previously, on the Employee Details form, under the Work tab, if the Retirement Benefit Group field had no value, then on the Benefit Utilities form, under the Results section for SH2 Auto Enroll utility, the Retirement Benefit Group column displayed the value of Benefit Group field. Now, this is fixed. On the Employee Details form, under the Work tab, if the Retirement Benefit Group field is not assigned for an employee, then the Retirement Benefit Group column in the Results section of Benefit Utilities form is displayed as blank.
BA-4440 Previously, on the Employee Details form, under the Pay tab, once you changed the Benefit Salary amount using the Change hyperlink and made another change to the Benefit Salary with the same effective date, the Benefit Salary field displayed the original change amount. It did not update the changed benefit salary to the newest record. This was a display issue only on the Pay tab as the last updated Benefit Salary History record displayed the updated amount. Now, this is fixed.
BA-4437 Previously, when a Check History Import was being done with HSA/FSA deductions, not all HSA/FSA deductions were importing for all employees. Now, this is fixed.
BA-4411 Previously, on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, if the Coverage Starts Date is before the Deduction Starts Date for an Active plan for an employee, and upon Save if you wanted to review the billing adjustments, then when you first arrived on the Benefit Adjustment form, the Filter by Status field was missing. It appeared after you clicked somewhere on the form. Now, this is fixed.
BA-4383 Previously, if you had Inquiry access to the Benefit Group Maintenance form (formerly Benefit Group Change form), you could see and click the New Benefit Group hyperlink which was not desirable. Now, if you have Inquiry access to the Benefit Group Maintenance form (formerly Benefit Group Change form), the New Benefit Group hyperlink is disabled.
BA-4333 Previously, on the Benefit Group Maintenance form (formerly Benefit Group Change form), for a selected employee, if you clicked the New Benefit Group hyperlink in order to change the Benefit Group for the employee, the Select Benefit Group filter only displayed the current Benefit Group for the employee unless you clicked the Reset Search and Filters hyperlink. Now, on the Benefit Group Maintenance form (formerly Benefit Group Change form), for a selected employee, if you click the New Benefit Group hyperlink in order to change the Benefit Group for the employee, the Select Benefit Group filter displays all available benefit groups available for the client.
BA-4124 Previously, upon importing successor retirement deferrals using the Retirement Adjustments Import form, the Successor Retirement Deferral amount on the Retirement Match P.T.D Register Report for some such employees incorrectly showed double the amounts actually imported. Now, upon importing successor retirement deferrals using the Retirement Adjustments Import form, the Successor Retirement Deferral amount on the Retirement Match P.T.D Register Report for all such employees show the exact amounts actually imported.
BA-4069 Previously, when processing a Client Benefit Plan Import, you could not import the Wash Rule Day = EOM. You got an error stating WASH.RULE.DAY IS NOT IN THE RANGE OF 10 TO 20. Now, when processing a Client Benefit Plan Import, you can import the Wash Rule Day = EOM in addition to the current allowed range of 10-20.
BA-3966 Previously, on the Benefits Adjustments form, even after you opened an existing adjustment and while on the Adjustment Details form, the Filter By Status drop-down on the Benefits Adjustments form in the background did not get disabled. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3953 Previously, while on the Benefits Adjustments form, if you changed the client, the form did not clear completely as you would find it when you first arrived at the form. Now, this is fixed.
BA-3936 Previously, if the Stamp Date Used as Override Stop Date When EE is Terminated field on the Flex Spend Account Types form was set to Employee’s Date of Termination, then on the Employee Flexible Spending Accounts form, the Override Stop Date field reflected the Employee’s Date of Termination even for plan years which did not include the Employee’s Date of Termination. Now, the Override Stop Date will only populate when the Employee’s Date of Termination falls within the current FSA/HSA plan year or is before a future plan year.
BA-3836 Previously, in some scenarios, the age reduction was not occurring correctly if on the Group Benefit Plan form, under the Other Processing Parameters section, the Age Calculation Month was set to be Calculate as of 1st of Month of Employee’s birthday. Now, this is fixed.
BA-2991 Previously, on the Data Import Tool form, using the Import Template named Plan Comparison Data, if you tried to upload a .txt file, you would receive an error stating NO data was extracted from the file.$ and under the Messages tab an Error Message stating Error: The column headers in the data file do not match the headers set up for the offer type . Now, this is fixed.
BA-2876 Previously, on the Benefit Import Maintenance form, for a selected an Import Definition ID, under the Action Translations section, for the Standard Action Codes field you could not select DEPEN- option from the Select Benefit Import Action Codes filter and would receive an error message stating The Benefit Import Field ‘DEPEN-’ does not exists! Now, this is fixed.

Other Fixes

The following are some other issues that we’ve fixed in the March 2025 quarterly release.

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
WSP-1318 Previously, using the Offer Type template of the Data Import Tool, if you downloaded the data file with the Prepopulate file (all plans with BLANK Offer Type) field checked, then system incorrectly stripped the commas in the Plan Description field of the downloaded data file. So when you tried to populate the Offer Type and upload the data file, the system generated an error stating Plan Description on Line # may not be changed using this import. Now, this is fixed.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/BA_Fixes_202506_MR.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/BA_Fixes_202506_MR.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the June 2025 monthly release.

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
WSP-1710 Previously, the Remaining Plan Year Election Amount was calculated incorrectly where the system incorrectly used values for Total Plan Year Deductions to Date as the sum of Total Plan Year EE Deductions to Date, Total Plan Year Company Match to Date, and Total Plan Year PEO Match to Date. Now, this is fixed. The calculation of Remaining Plan Year Election Amount now takes the value used for Total Plan Year Deductions to Date as the Total Plan Year EE Deductions to Date only. Additionally, Standard Company HSA Match Contribution Method is the only method supported in preventing the limit from being exceeded. The other methods of Fixed, Scheduled, or Tiered are not supported in preventing the limit from being exceeded.
WSP-1711 Previously, on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form, after you have selected an Employee and entered a Retirement Plan, and then when you select an Effective Date and save the form, a pop-up message stating, Please re-enter the detail effective date. was displayed which was incorrect. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-1870 Previously, on the Employee Deduction Arrears form, toggling between employees caused the form to stuck on the first selected employee’s display. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2089 Previously, on the Data Import Tool form, when you selected the Import Template as Plan Comparison Data and then selected an Offer Type, then on importing, the plan information was not being imported on the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2139 Previously, on the Benefits Import form, when you selected an Import Definition Template that did not contain any $DEPN fields, then an error message stating, Import definition does not include $DEPN_SSN but file includes dependents was displayed. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2140 Previously, when you accessed the Retirement Plan Enrollment form in a modal form through Navigation Search and when you selected an existing Effective Date under the Election Details section, a warning message stating, A detail record for that date already exists. Select it from the dropdown list. was displayed. Upon the display of the warning message, the data on the form cleared out and the Financial Details section was disabled, which was incorrect. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2145 Previously, on the Retirement Adjustments Import form, when you uploaded a changed import file, the changes made on that import file were not displayed under the Preview section. You had to refresh the browser to view the changes made on the uploaded file. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2175 Previously, when a Benefit Plan Setup for HSA Contribution is configured with Contribution Applies to for all HDHP-enrolled employees without an HSA account added to their Flex Spending Account Setup Elections, then the system automated the addition of an HSA account with a $0.00 Plan Year Election in the employee’s Employee Flexible Spending Account setup, even when the employee was already enrolled in an FSA plan. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2176 Previously, when the Custom Feature Code USEWEEKLYBENEFITS was enabled, then on the Employee Deduction Arrears form, when an employee had enough deduction arrears to create a scroll, the scrolling caused the arrears to not display at the bottom of the page. Once a user selected the arrears checkbox, then only the hidden arrears record were displayed. Now, this is fixed.

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the July 2025 monthly release.

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
WSP-2197 Previously, on the Enhanced Dashboard screen, from the At a Glance drop-down list, when you select Employee Benefit Enrollments and then navigate to the Actions column and select Employee Details modal form, then the Save & Close and the Close buttons overlapped on each tabs except the Name tab. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2233 Previously, on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, when you changed the employee, the Enter New Date field was pre-populated with the date value from the previous employee’s enrollment details, which was incorrect. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2234 Previously, on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, when you selected an Employee and choose an active Benefit Plan and then again selected the same employee, the screen retained data for some of the fields from the previous active plan that was selected for the employee, instead of refreshing the data. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2255 On the Benefit Plan Setup form, under the Company HSA Contribution section, when you selected Contribution Applies To as All HDHP Employees, the system did not execute the auto-enrollment functionality for employees who did not meet all the eligibility criteria outlined in all fields of the Eligibility Criteria section. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2262 Previously, the Notification Audit Report form allowed to filter results only by Client ID and Employee ID. This caused issues while running reports for larger clients. Now, two additional fields named Start Date and End Date has been added where you can provide a date range which must be within 1 year range to run and view the generated reports efficiently. Additionally, these newly added fields are mandatory.
WSP-2329 On the Employee Benefit Overview form, under the Billing History section, when different Benefit Plans have the same description, then the report combined the Billing Amounts under one of the Plans that had the duplicate plan description. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2335 Previously, on the Benefit Billing Detail Report form, when you selected the Defined Ranges option as Last Batch and set the Primary Sort to Employee and the Secondary Sort to Benefit Plan, and then run the report, the report that was displayed sorted the results by Benefit Plan as the primary sort, which was incorrect. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2338 Previously, on the Benefit Billing Detail Report form, under the Sort Parameters section, when you set Primary Sort to Location, Secondary Sort to Benefit Plan, and select Report Type as Detail and then run the report, then in the results that was displayed, the Total line displayed Total For Department instead of Total For Location, which was incorrect. Now, this is fixed.

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the August 2025 monthly release.

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
WSP-1704 Previously, the system calculated a Non-Elective Match for the payroll even after the employee had attained or crossed the Compensation Limit under the Plan Year Deferral Limits section on the Retirement Plans form when the Non-Elective Match field on the Retirement Match Rules form is blank for the corresponding retirement plan. Now, the system will not calculate a Non-Elective Match for the payroll once the employee has attained or crossed the Compensation Limit under the Plan Year Deferral Limits section on the Retirement Plans form irrespective of whether the Non-Elective Match field on the Retirement Match Rules form is blank for the corresponding retirement plan or not.

But when you selected the Reduce coverage and premium (default is reduce coverage only) checkbox, then the premium was calculated without an issue. Now, this is fixed.

There are employees using this benefit rule with active enrollments. was displayed which was incorrect. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-1874 Previously, on the Benefit Rules Import form, when you uploaded a file and then clicked the Validate Import File button, the screen went blank without returning any values, which was incorrect. Now, this is fixed. While the job control is run an error, if any, is displayed on the job control screen to let you know about the mismatch of headers.
WSP-1976 Previously, on the Employee Deduction Arrears form, the Change Status button was displayed for users even if the Custom Feature Code named USEWEEKLYBENEFITS was not set, which was incorrect. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2344 Previously, on the Employee Details form, under the Actions menu, when users accessed the Benefit Adjustments modal form, the users were unable to select the benefit adjustments record checkbox in a single click. To select the checkbox, users had to click for a second time. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2413 Previously, when you accessed Employee Voucher either from the Process Payroll form or from the Employee Details form, then under the Deductions tab, when you clicked the HSA hyperlink, you could not view the calculations on the voucher and it showed a blank screen instead. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2496 Previously, on the Benefit Utilities form, when you ran any of the orphaned utility options and then changed the option from the Orphaned Record Type drop-down and then resized the browser, the search results from the prior ran utility was displayed. Now, this is fixed.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/BA_Fixes_202510_MR.htm Path: BA/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/BA_Fixes_202510_MR.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the October 2025 monthly release.

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
WSP-1695 Previously, on the Benefit Summary Statement form, the SSN masking option for the client was not applied to the Benefit Summary Statement Report output. Additionally, on exporting to XLS file, the report omitted the SSN in the downloaded file. Now, this is fixed. The Benefit Summary Statement report now considers the client-level selection made for the SSN Mask Override field on the Report Print Options form while displaying the report results. Also, if there is no client-level override, then the Benefit Summary Statement report considers the selection made in the SSN Mask Option field on the System Parameters form while displaying report results.
WSP-2040 Previously, on the Benefit Plan Setup or Retirement Plans form, even when no eligibility rules were setup, the system allowed the enrollment of employees, which was incorrect. Now, this is fixed. On the Benefit Plan Setup form, when you select Plan Class as Retirement, and if the plan class does not have any eligibility criteria defined, then the system now looks at the Retirement Plans form for eligibility criteria. If eligibility criteria is not defined on the Retirement Plans form as well, then no employee is eligibile.
WSP-2281 Previously, on the Flexible Spending Accounts Reimbursement form, when you selected an existing Reference Number record for an employee and then selected the employee from the Employee selector, the values on the screen did not clear. Now, this is fixed. When you select an existing record, the Employee field now displays as a read-only field. Additionally, on saving a new record, the values in all the fields clears including the Employee ID.
WSP-2673 Previously, on the Employee Retirement Loans form, after selecting the Loan Number, under the Adjustments section, when you entered an amount in the Paid Back Adjustment field, then the read-only value displayed in the New balance equals field did not update the amount correctly. This issue was a ‘Display Only’ issue. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2742 Previously, when you accessed an existing retirement loan record from the Employee Retirement Loans modal form, it did not allow to update any changes made to the form. Additionally, the modal form did not allow to delete a retirement loan record. While updating or deleting the record, a message stating, This record cannot be written as not all key parts have been filled was displayed, which was not the correct behavior. Now, this is fixed. The Employee Retirement Loans modal form now allows updating and deleting an existing record without any error.
WSP-2809 Previously, on the Group Benefit Plans form, when you selected a Benefit Plan ID and then reopened the Group Benefit Plans form, the Percent of Gross Wages multivalue grid overlapped on the screen. This issue also occurred while opening the Group Benefit Plans form in a modal window. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2864 Previously, on the COBRA Participant Record form, when you created a Cobra Participant Record, then an error message stating, Error! This enrollee has no company number. You should print out their information, delete this record and then enter it again. was displayed, which was incorrect. Now, this is fixed.

Enhancements

This section describes general enhancements that were made in the PrismHR January 2024 monthly release.

Support for Iowa Form W-4

Read the following article on the Customer Resource Center for more information.

Montana & Iowa 2024 W-4 and Tax Withholding Updates

JIRA # CMP-5363

Support for Iowa State Withholding Tax Rate Table 2024

Effective 1/1/24, Iowa has revised their State Withholding Tax Rate Table. Read the following article on the Customer Resource Center for more information.

Montana & Iowa 2024 W-4 and Tax Withholding Updates

[Image: screenshot]

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: If the IA filing status override method is BLOCK WITHHOLDING no changes are applied.

JIRA # CMP-5365

Support for Montana Form W-4

PrismHR now supports the updated 2024 Montana Form W-4 effective 1/1/2024. Read the following article on the Customer Resource Center for more information.

Montana & Iowa 2024 W-4 and Tax Withholding Updates

JIRA # CMP-5319

Support for Montana State Withholding Tax Rate Table 2024

Effective 1/1/24, Montana has revised their State Withholding Tax Rate Table. PrismHR now supports the 2024 State Withholding Tax Rate Table, including those employees who have a filing status of Married Filing Jointly with Both Spouses Working. Read the following article on the Customer Resource Center for more information.

Montana & Iowa 2024 W-4 and Tax Withholding Updates

[Image: screenshot]

JIRA # CMP-5366

New Form I-9 - Remote Verification Indication

A new field named Remote Verification Used has been added under the Employment Verification section on the Tax tab of the Employee Details form to track if an employee’s I-9 documents are verified remotely or not. When an employee’s I-9 documents are remotely verified, the I-9 approver indicates that in Section 2 of the Form I-9. Then this Remote Verification Used field gets checked automatically.

[Image: screenshot]

JIRA # CMP-5255

Send Company Accounting Record in PTS file

A new field named Send Company Accounting Record in PTS file has been added to the MasterTax Interface Parameters form. If you are a PEO managing multiple client accounts, you can now populate the Company General Ledger record 105 within the PTS file for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients.

  • This field is unchecked by default.

  • Check this field to report the 105 record within the PTS. Once checked the following two fields display:

  • MasterTax Chart of Account Code - Enter the 2 digit alphanumeric code used to identify the company’s G/L chart of accounts.

  • MasterTax G/L Payroll Code - the only drop-down option available at this time is Sub Cost Center.

[Image: screenshot]

JIRA # CMP-5352

105 record now added to the PTS download file

The PTS download file has been updated to add the 105 record. This record only appears when the Send Company Accounting Record in PTS file field is checked on the MasterTax Interface Parameters form. This will be included in the 100 record for the PTS download.

  • For every 100 record there will be a corresponding 105 record.

  • When the 100 record references a C | CL | CR code, we will populate the sub cost center of the client being reported:

  • When the 100 record references an E code (Employer report) PrismHR will populate the sub cost center of the employer.

  • Within the PTS file, the 100 block will include a corresponding 105 record with the following information:

  • Pos 1-3 = 105

  • Pos 4-13 = Code used in 100 block

  • Pos 14-15 - The 2 digit alphanumeric code in the MasterTax Chart of Accounts Code field if populated in the MasterTax Interface Parameters form. This code should correspond to the MasterTax Chart of Accounts Code already set up within MasterTax.

  • Pos 16-135 blank

  • Pos 136-175 -The sub cost center. If the code is too long, the code is cut at position 175.

  • Pos 176-420 blank

Note: Note: At this time, the F code 100 record will be blank from positions 16-420.

JIRA # CMP-5307

Changes to Campbell Country Occupational License Fee

Effective 1/1/2024, Campbell County, KY has updated their Occupational License Fee. Campbell County Occupational License Fee of 1.05% will no longer be calculated under a single tax code. The tax will be broken out into three new tax IDs, with differing rates and maximum wages:

  • General Occupational License Fee of 0.9% and annual maximum tax of $1,517.40.

  • Campbell County General Occupational License Fee - tax code 18037-44.

  • Mental Health Occupational License Fee (Tax ID 538) of 0.1% and annual maximum tax of $168.60.

  • Campbell County Mental Health Tax - tax code 18037-34.

  • Senior Citizen Occupational License Fee (Tax ID 511 of 0.05% and annual maximum tax of $25.00.

  • Senior Citizen Occupational License Fee - tax code 18037-32.

JIRA # CMP-5313

New Client Custom Feature Code DISABLE.OVERTIME.EXCEPTION.PAY

A new client level custom feature code named DISABLE.OVERTIME.EXCEPTION.PAY is now available in PrismHR. It is available on the Custom Features form which you can access from the Actions menu on the Client Details form. You can either enter this client level custom feature code directly on the form or click the Feature Code link and select it from the Select Available Feature Codes dialog box.

To support AL Overtime exemption effective 1/1/24, the custom feature code OVERTIME.EXCEPTION.PAY must be enabled at the system level. Prior to the client level custom feature code, you could enable this functionality for the entire system or none of the system. Now using this client level custom feature code, you can disable the logic for certain clients if they choose not to change their payroll method to support the automated calculations. For example, when OVERTIME.EXCEPTION.PAY is entered at the system level, the AL OT logic is activated. Adding DISABLE.OVERTIME.EXCEPTION.PAY in addition to the system code then deactivates the logic for that client only.

[Image: screenshot]

JIRA # CMP-5362

Updated Maryland State EFW2 export file

For tax year 2023 and beyond, the state of Maryland requires the RW (Employee) Record in the EFW2 download file. PrismHR now supports this update. The EFW2 download file for employees for the state of Maryland will now include the RW (Employee) Record in the specified format as per SSA Publication No. 42-007 EFW2 for Tax Year 2023.

JIRA # CMP-5288

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/MR202402/CMP-Enhancements%20Feb-2024%20MR.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/MR202402/CMP-Enhancements Feb-2024 MR.htm

Enhancements

This section describes general enhancements that were made in the PrismHR February 2024 monthly release.

Updates to VisionSTD_SP_FullPTO to Incorporate Custom Check Formatting

To support varying requirements in California and other states, a new check format named VisionSTD_ER_SP_FullPTO has been added to the Default Report Form dropdown in the Print Service Check Maintenance form. This new format will be included in the standard Compliance check options.

[Image: screenshot]

This format is similar to the existing format VisionSTD_SP_FullPTO; however, the memo section includes additional information regarding the Employer. On the Print Service Options form, when the Source of Name/Address on Checks field is set to Use Employers Address the memo section will report the Employer using the Client Legal Name and Address. The standard Service Provider information will be listed below the memo.

[Image: screenshot]

This format is available for specific use cases and may not be necessary for everyone.

JIRA # RRT-5648, CMP-5160

Updates to Form W-4 for Georgia

The state of Georgia updated its employee state withholding certificate (Form W-4) to indicate any changes in marital status, allowances, or other withholding considerations. PrismHR now supports the changes to support the data flowing from Employee Portal or Onboarding, and options presented in the New Hire and Employee Details forms.

In the Employee Details form, under the Tax tab, under the State Tax Filings section, when GA is selected as the State, and you click the Filing Status link:

  • The Filing status selections for GEORGIA will now reflect only the following options:

  • S: Single

  • H: Head of Household

  • MB: Married Filing Separate or Spouse Works

  • MO: Married Filing Joint 1 Spouse Work

  • Personal Allowances determined by filing status have been removed. The Primary Allowance field is no longer valid for the State of Georgia.

  • When entering a new hire manually or updating the employee detail tax record for the State of Georgia, starting tax year 2024, the total GA allowances should be entered as Additional Allowances in the Secondary Allowances field.

[Image: screenshot]

[Image: screenshot]

JIRA # 5402

Updates to MTA-305 Report (Zone 1 and 2)

The state of New York updated the specifications for their New York Form MTA-305 Tax download electronic file. Effective July 1, 2023, for purposes of the MCTMT (Metropolitan Commuter Transportation Mobility Tax), the MCTD (Metropolitan Commuter Transportation District) is now divided into the following two district zones:

[Image: screenshot]

A summary of the changes are as follows:

[Image: screenshot]

Employers must file quarterly MCTMT returns if they are required to withhold New York State income tax from wages paid to employees and their payroll expense for all covered employees in the MCTD exceeds $312,500 in any calendar quarter.

For tax filing periods Q3 2023 and later, PrismHR now support the changes which result in the following changes to the New York Form MTA-305 Tax download electronic file:

  • Separation of Zone 1 and Zone 2 including:

  • Employee Counts

  • Payroll Expense

  • Tax Rate

  • Tax Due

JIRA # CMP-5169
