Enhancements

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/MR202404/CMP-Enhancements%20Apr-2024.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/MR202404/CMP-Enhancements Apr-2024.htm

Enhancements

This section describes general enhancements that were made in the PrismHR April 2024 monthly release.

Added County to the 601 record for WV unemployment

In MasterTax V46 and above (for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients), the 601 record for West Virginia (tax code 49-24) now includes the county worked in for the employee in positions 400-414. For example positions 400-414 will report Kanawha if majority of the employee’s job duties were performed in the Kanawha County.

The system will use the county name of the home location in the state of West Virginia.

In the event the employee’s home location has been changed when the RTS is run and is no longer in WV, the system will blank fill the record. For example, an employee’s home location was WV and the employee had WV SUTA to report. When the RTS is run, home location is now any state other than WV. The system will blank fill the record and will not report the county of the other state.

JIRA # CMP-5587

Position-based Union Fringe Benefits Enhancement

When employees work between multiple local areas with different unions and between multiple jobs such as electrical, structural, etc. you now have more flexibility to leverage the Position based union override to manage fringe benefits. When the Labor Union is not applied to the Employee Detail record and the Labor Union is applied to the Position Code:

  • Non-cash Fringe Pay codes that are calculated as a percentage of gross wages will be calculated based on the position code entered in the timesheet.

  • If there are multiple positions in a single payroll, the calculation is now limited to the earnings applied to that position.

JIRA # CMP-5432

Added SOC codes/Job Title to the RTS for WA and WV

In the Positions form, if:

  • there is an SOC Code, then the RTS will report this in positions 114-119. Dashes will be omitted. Position 415-474 will be left blank.

  • there is no SOC Code, then positions 114-119 in the RTS will be blank. Positions 415-474 will report the Job Title.

For more information on SOC code reporting for multiple states, please refer to to the article titled Updating SOC Codes on the Customer Resource Center.

JIRA # CMP-5526

Updates to WH347 Report

The WH-347 form generated by PrismHR has been updated to the latest version with an expiration date of 9/30/2026.

JIRA # CMP-5659

Changes to Employer Quarterly SUTA Tax Export - South Carolina

The state of South Carolina now requires the Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Code and Hours Worked on this report. The system has been enhanced to incorporate this for both versions of the available reports.

  • Number of Hours Worked - Positions 342-344 (rounded to the nearest full number)

  • SOC Code - Positions 376-377 (first 2 digits of the SOC Code); Position 378 will be a dash; Positions 379-382 (last 4 digits of the SOC Code). The SOC code is determined by the Client/ Change/ Positions: SOC code. If blank, the file will produce a blank record.

Enhancements

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/MR202410/CMP-Enhancements%20Oct-2024%20MR.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/MR202410/CMP-Enhancements Oct-2024 MR.htm

Enhancements

This section describes general enhancements that were made in the PrismHR October 2024 monthly release.

Addition to PrismHR Work Centers

Under the PrismHR Work Centers, under the Tax section, a new group named PrismHR Tax Processing is added. This is a central location to access the PrismHR tax setup and reporting forms.

WARNING: This work center is currently released as BETA with further functionality to be released in 2025. The parameters and reports should only be used by customers who are engaged in the BETA testing of the JSON exports. Existing customers should continue to use the CSV report downloads at this time.

[Image: screenshot]

The following two sections are available under PrismHR Tax Processing work center:

  • Setup - this section contains the following two forms:

  • PrismHR Tax Client Setup Export - Use this form to build the PrismHR Client Setup JSON export file. This will create an initial JSON export for setting up an initial group of client data in PrismHR Tax.

  • PrismHR Tax Parameters - Use this form to set up parameters to be used for various needs in the PrismHR Tax files. This form is currently informational only with future development planned for future quarters.

  • File Exports

  • Quarterly Tax JSON Export - The quarterly tax JSON export will be supported in a future release. More information will be available in a future release.

JIRA # CMP-5981

PrismHR Tax Client Setup Export

Use this form to build the PrismHR Client Setup JSON export file. This will create an initial JSON export for setting up an initial group of client data in PrismHR Tax.

Note: Note: Client Access Group security is not enabled on this form.

WARNING: This form is currently released as BETA with further functionality to be released in 2025. This form should only be used by customers who are engaged in the BETA testing of the JSON exports. Existing customers should continue to use the CSV report downloads at this time.

To access this form, on the Work Centers under Tax, click PrismHR Tax Processing. Under Setup, click PrismHR Tax Client Setup Export.

To set up an initial group of client data in PrismHR Tax:

  1. Complete the following fields:

Field Name — Description

Tax Date Start — Enter the starting tax date of the group of clients to be included in the client setup files.

Tax Date End — Enter the ending tax date of the group of clients to be included in the client setup files. > Note: Note: We suggest using a period that does not exceed a single quarter for each setup export.

  1. Click Build to build the PrismHR Client Setup JSON export file for the selected tax year and the tax quarter.

  2. Click Cancel to clear this form at any time.

Enhancements

This section describes general enhancements that were made in the PrismHR March 2024 quarterly release.

Updated CA Pay Data Reporting to Support TY 2023 Reporting Period

On February 1, 2024, California released the FAQs for Tax Year 2023 Pay Data Reporting. New this year is the requirement to report whether an employee is a remote employee. You must also report whether they are remote within CA or outside of CA. To support this requirement, PrismHR released an updated reporting template for tax year 2023 that now includes the additional reporting fields: Employees that do not work remotely, Remote employees located within California, Remote employees located outside of California. Additionally, the EEO Export has been modified to include a new data record Remote Employee.

To determine a Remote Employee, the new logic is based on the most prevalent configuration and assumes:

  1. All remote employees are assigned to home worksite locations that are distinctly for remote employees only.

  2. Employees are assigned to remote worksite locations with an address matching their states of residence.

  3. These remote worksite locations are configured with an EEO Override Location, as all remote employees should be reported under the physical establishment to which they report.

  4. No physical establishments contain an EEO Override Location.

The table below depicts if and how employees will be reported on PrismHR California Pay Data files based on the state(s) of their home worksite locations and the associated EEO Override Location.

[Image: screenshot]

For more information, please refer to the article named 2024 California Pay Data Updates on the Customer Resource Center.

JIRA # CMP-5370, 5371

Prevailing Wage Calculation Logic Enhancement

When processing certified payrolls and using the option “Use Higher of Prevailing Wage Rate or Employee’s Pay Rate” , the pay rate for the position is determined based on the higher of the employees standard hourly rate or the prevailing wage of the position on the project. In some instances, the calculated overtime rate for the prevailing wage is less than the calculated overtime rate for the employee’s standard hourly rate. A new Custom Feature Code has been created (OTPREVAILINGWAGE) to compare the calculated prevailing wage overtime rate with the standard hourly overtime rate. When the standard overtime rate is greater, the pay rate will equal their regular overtime rate. If the regular prevailing wage rate is higher, this will still be used and only the overtime rate would follow the employees standard hourly rate.

This section describes general enhancements that were made in the PrismHR June 2024 quarterly release.

Changes to the Labor Unions form

The Labor Unions form has been enhanced to allow assignment of union dues table rules to a unique union deduction code. When using Position Union overrides, you can now apply multiple union deduction codes to an employee based on the timesheet sensitive position code entered and allocate deductions amounts appropriately. When using position based Union code overrides, you can now differentiate between the union deductions without requiring the union applied to the employee directly.

An additional column named Union Dues Table Rules has been added to the union deduction code table.

[Image: screenshot]

For a Union Deduction Code that does not have Union Dues Table set as the Calculation Method for that union deduction code on the Deduction Codes form, you will see the

[Image: screenshot]

icon. If you click the

[Image: screenshot]

icon, you will get an error message stating The deduction code has an invalid calculation method. The code must have a calculation method of Union Dues Table to be assigned union dues table rules.

For a Union Deduction Code that has Union Dues Table set as the Calculation Method for that union deduction code on the Deduction Codes form, you will see the

[Image: screenshot]

icon. When you click it, a new form named Included Union Dues Table Rules will open. This form allows you to associate specific Union Dues Table Rules with a specific Union Deduction Code.

[Image: screenshot]

  • On the Included Union Dues Table Rules form, you can:

  • Add any Union Dues Table Rules from the drop-down for the selected Union Deduction Code provided it is listed in the Union Dues Table on the Labor Unions form. Click Accept to close the form. Click the Save button on the Labor Unions form to file the changes.

  • Delete any Union Dues Table Rules from the drop-down for the selected Union Deduction Code. Click Accept to close the form. Click the Save button on the Labor Unions form to file the changes.

  • If from the Included Union Dues Table Rules drop-down you are trying to select a rule that is not included in the Union Dues Table, you will get an error message stating Not allowed, this Rule and Rate is not included in the Union Dues Table. Click OK to acknowledge the error and redo your selection.

  • From the Union Dues Table on the Labor Unions form, you cannot delete a rule if it is associated with a Union Deductions Code on the Labor Unions form. After deleting, when you click Save on the Labor Unions form, you will get an error message stating This rule is assigned to Union Deduction Code, and must be removed prior to removing from the Union Dues Table. You must delete the Union Deductions Code first to be able to delete any associate rule from the Union Dues Table on the Labor Unions form.

OR

Using the Included Union Dues Table Rules form, if you remove the rule assigned to the Union Deduction Code, you can remove the rule from the Union Dues Table.

  • If you add a rule on the Union Dues Table which does not use pay codes, you will get the [Image: screenshot] icon for that rule under the Pay Codes Included column. When you click the [Image: screenshot] icon, you will get an error message stating This rule does not use pay codes.

  • If you add a rule on the Union Dues Table which does not use pay codes, you will get the [Image: screenshot] icon for that rule under the Pay Codes Excluded column also. When you click the [Image: screenshot] icon, you will get an error message stating This rule does not use pay codes.

With the enhanced Labor Unions form, you can now have unique union deduction codes with the calculation of union dues table to differentiate between various union deductions allowing unique deductions for better visibility to clients and employees. This enhancement will allow for better reporting will continue to be enhanced in our September Quarterly Release. Watch out for more on this in our future releases.

Use this new form to recalculate the overtime payroll hours and wages that are exempt from income tax for employees in the state of Alabama for a client.

You must enable the system level custom feature code OVERTIME.EXCEPTION.PAY and disable the client level custom feature code DISABLE.OVERTIME.EXCEPTION.PAY for this form to work correctly for the client, else you will get an error message stating Overtime Exemption Pay is not enabled or is disabled for this client.

Click OK to acknowledge the message.

PrismHR Path Payroll>Payroll\ Action>Recalculate Alabama Income Tax Exempt Wages

Security

  • Service Provider only.

JIRA # PORT-5449, 5630

EFW2C Download Enhancements - Corrected Wages & W2 Box Values in EFW2C file

If there is an employee W2c record where the wages or the W-2 box values have been corrected, the EFW2C file output has been refined to meet specifications for the Social Security Administration.

  • When correcting federal wages or income tax withholding, only the original and corrected amounts will appear.

  • When correcting FICA wages, both Social Security and Medicare wages are required to report together. When a change is made to only one of these amounts, both will be reported.

  • When correcting Box 10 or 12 values, only the original and corrected values will appear.

Note:

  • These values will be reported in the RCW (Employee record) and the corresponding RCT (Totals record).

  • We do not currently support the Box 13 changes; however, this will be addressed in a future enhancement.

JIRA # CMP-5230

Correcting Employee SSN & Name in EFW2C file

If the W-2 and W2c data are the same, but there has been an SSN change that is necessary to report to the SSA, the file will now only populate the original and corrected value for the SSN change. Money fields are blank filled.

If the W-2 and W2c data are the same, but there has been a Name change that is necessary to report to the SSA, the file will now only report the original and corrected values for the name change. Money fields are blank filled. The employee SSN if same as the original W-2 is populated in positions 13-21.

Following are a few frequently asked questions that you might find helpful.

  • How to complete the Social Security Number (SSN) fields when correcting a SSN?

If the Employee’s Originally Reported SSN is entered in the RCW (Employee) Record (positions 4-12), then the Employee’s Correct SSN (positions 13-21) must also be entered.

If the Originally Reported SSN and Name is entered in the RCW Record, the Correct SSN and Name must also be entered.

  • Correcting Employee Name and Social Security Number (SSN) I reported a W-2 where all money fields were correct but the employee’s name and/or SSN was reported incorrectly. How do I correct this?

For an SSN/Name correction, only one RCW (Employee) correction report is needed.

Complete the RCW (Employee) Record original “Social Security Number”, original “Employee First Name”, original “Employee Middle Name or Initial” and original “Employee Last Name” fields for all SSN/Name corrections.

  • When/How do I report or correct an employee’s name?

Enter the name exactly as shown on the individual’s Social Security card. If you are correcting the employee’s name, the employee’s originally reported first name, middle name or initial and last name fields must be completed as originally submitted.

To support PTM customers who are using both the full service option and the self-service option, a new field name PTM Identifier Number has been added under the Employer Details section of the Employer Details form to provide the ability to record two different PTM Identifiers.

  • The PTM Identifier Number field must be set at the system level on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, for the PTM Identifier Number field to be available on the Employer Details form.

  • If no PTM Identifier Number is set at the system level on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, then no PTM Identifier Number will display on the files.

  • If an employer PTM Identifier Number on the Employer Details form exists for an employer and the same or a different PTM Identifier Number is set at the system level on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, then the employer PTM Identifier Number will override the system level PTM Identifier Number. Then:

  • The employer PTM Identifier Number on the Employer Details form will appear on all PTM reports including the Daily Tax Export (including PTM Agency export), the Monthly Tax Export and the Quarterly Tax Export reports.

  • If an employer PTM Identifier Number does not exist on the Employer Details form, but a system level PTM Identifier Number exists on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, then the system level PTM Identifier Number on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form will appear on all PTM reports like the Daily Tax Export (including PTM Agency export), the Monthly Tax Export and the Quarterly Tax Export reports.

JIRA # CMP-5399, 5479

Form I-9 remote verification enabled at the client level

A new field named Enable I9 Remote Verification is now available under the Process Controls section under the Control tab on the Client Details form.

[Image: screenshot]

  • This field will only display if the Enable E-Verification? field is checked.

  • By default, this box will be unchecked.

  • Check this box if you want to enable Form I-9 remote verification for all worksites of this client who are authorized to remotely verify Form I-9s for their employees. When you check this box a message pops up stating E-Verify will be enabled for all locations. You can exclude a location from E-Verify on the Worksite Location under Other Parameters. Click OK to continue.

If you want to disable Form I-9 remote verification for any particular worksite, you can do so using the Enable Remote Verification for this Location field under the Other Parameters section on the Worksite Locations form for that worksite.

[Image: screenshot]

This option will allow I-9 Approvers to remotely examine supporting documents for a new hire’s Form I-9 using an alternative procedure authorized by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). Now you can select one of the following options:

  • Select - Any worksite location not enabled or disabled will follow the client level setting.

  • Enable - Use this option to enable remote verification for this location. This is only required when the Enable I9 Remote Verification option under the Process Controls section under the Control tab on the Client Details form is not selected.

  • Disable - Use this option to disable remote verification for this location when the Enable I9 Remote Verification option under the Process Controls section under the Control tab on the Client Details form is selected for the client.

JIRA # CMP-5364

Support for 1099 contractor reporting

To support 1099 contractor Federal and State Income Tax reporting, when the Custom Feature Code 1099WITHHOLDING is enabled, the wages and tax withholdings for a 1099 contractor will NOT be included in the Employer 941 Quarterly Report for any 1099 contractor with tax withholding. Additionally, release enhancements for the PTS and RTS to support 1099 withholding will only be present in the files using the NEC tax code when the Custom Feature Code 1099WITHHOLDING is enabled.

Note: Note: When leveraging the Custom Feature Code 1099WITHHOLDING, you will need to have a separate Employee ID for any 1099 contractor who has tax withheld. Previously, the system allowed a 1099 Contractor in one client and a W-2 employee in a second client using the same Employee ID. For purposes of 1099 income tax withholding and reporting, the 1099 contractor must NOT be a W-2 employee in any other client.

JIRA # CMP-4886, 5676

Changes to calculation of Boone County, KY, Mental Health tax

Boone County KY Mental Health tax historically calculated on the locality level which affected the maximum county based tax when employees work between various localities in Boone County. As a resolution, a Custom Feature Code BCKYMHCAP has been created which will transfer the local tax to the county level tax deduction code 180150000-34. When calculated on the county level, the maximum tax amount will be honored regardless of where the employee worked in Boone County, KY. If enabling this custom feature mid-year, the Boone County Mental Health tax register will restart. User Action will be required to move taxable wages out of the locality tax deduction code to the county level tax code to ensure employees who have already met the maximum tax do not have tax withheld with the addition of the CFC.

  • If you do not use the Custom Feature Code BCKYMHCAP, there will be no change to Boone County tax codes in tax year 2024. The system will continue to calculate on the locality level. However, the above logic will automatically begin starting with the first payroll in January 2025.

  • If you use the Custom Feature Code BCKYMHCAP:

  • All Boone County local tax codes are redirected to 180150000-34 county level tax.

  • The generated geocode for the Mental Health tax for all localities that fall in Boone County will be 180150000-34.

  • When employees work in multiple localities in Boone County, the tax will be capped at $25 across all locations within the County.

  • This change will restart tax registers for Boone County, KY under 180150000-34. Tax adjustments will be required by customers to move the old tax code to the new one.

JIRA # CMP-5584, 5668

Support for Vermont Childcare Employee Tax Rate

As an employer in the state of Vermont, effective 7/1/24 you are required to pay a 0.44% tax on wages paid to an employee in the state of Vermont. You can pay the full 0.44% or you may choose to deduct and withhold a maximum of 25 percent of the required contribution (0.11% of wages paid) from the employee.

To support this Vermont Childcare rate shifting, a new field named State Misc 2 Employee Rate has been added to the following forms. This field is only to be used for Vermont Childcare Employee Tax Rate bearing tax code 48-27.

  • Employer Tax Rates (SUTA) form AND

[Image: screenshot]

  • State Tax Rates (SUTA) form

[Image: screenshot]

  • Vertex will support this tax using tax code 46-27 for the employee and tax code 46-28 for the employer.

  • If a rate is applied to State Misc 2 Employee, this will be calculated using Tax Code 46-27 with the defined rate. The employer tax will continue to calculate using Tax Code 46-28.

  • If no tax rate is entered for the employer, but a tax rate is entered for the employee, you will see the full amount for the employer calculated at 0.44%. The employee tax rate does not offset the employer tax rate. So, you must enter both tax rates for both the employer and the employee if using overrides.

  • If Client reported, then use the State Tax Rates (SUTA) form. Enter the employer tax (tax code 46-28) rate in the State Misc2 Rate field and the employee tax (tax code 46-27) rate in the State Misc 2 Employee Rate. Both rates must be filled up in the form.

  • If Employer reported, then use the Employer Tax Rates (SUTA) form. Enter the employer tax (tax code 46-28) rate in the State Misc2 Rate field and the employee tax (tax code 46-27) rate in the State Misc 2 Employee Rate. Both rates must be filled up in the form.

  • This field will be optional in both the forms mentioned above. A rate can be added and removed. The audit will reflect the changes made appropriately.

Note: Note: The functionality for supporting the employee tax rate override may not be included in the Wave 1 release. However, it will be added to the release prior to the time-line to calculate July 1, 2024 payrolls.

Other Enhancements

Change to Default Value of Non-Residency Certificate

On the Employee Details form, in the Local Tax Filings panel under the Tax tab, the Local Non-Residency Certificate field no longer defaults to “Yes” when you create a new row in the grid. Instead, the field defaults to the neutral “‑‑Select‑‑” option.

JIRA # WSP-209

Employer Details form now Validates FEINs

The system now validates entries in the Federal EIN and Common Pay Agent EIN fields, located on the Employer Details form.

Valid values now must be in one of two formats:

  • nine consecutive digits (#########), OR

  • two digits followed by a hyphen, followed by seven digits (##-#######).

Note: Note: If an existing employer FEIN does not follow this format, you will receive an warning message the next time you open Employer Details and try modifying any data for that employer. After you fix the affected FEINs, you can save all the changes.

JIRA # WSP-179

End Dates for State Unemployment and Income Tax

The State Tax panel of the Employer Details form now includes two new fields: Rpt Entity End Date and SIT End Date. This override applies to any payroll calculations that occur before the end dates. On the day after its end date, the tax reverts back to the default State Rules setting.

[Image: Highlighting new Rpt Entity and SIT End Dates in State Tax panel of Employer Details.]

Note: Note: These new fields may be overridden by the client reporting fields on the Client Details > Tax tab: “Client Reporting Start Date” and “Client Reporting End Date”, located under State Tax Setup.

JIRA # WSP-182

Enhancements to Change SUTA Flag On Vouchers (PEO/Client)

The Change SUTA Flag on Vouchers (PEO/Client) form provides two new settings:

  • Rebuild Vouchers Flag

  • Send to MasterTax

These settings mimic the behavior of the “Rebuild Vouchers Flag” and “Send adjusting entries to MasterTax PTS file” options located on the Change Employer IDs for a Voucher form.

You can choose to “Update Existing Vouchers” with the new SUTA flag, or “Create New Adjustment Vouchers” for this change. If you choose to create new vouchers and you need to represent these changes on the MasterTax PTS file, set Send to Mastertax to “Yes”. The PTS file will indicate the original wages/taxes with a negative value and the new, correct wages/taxes with a positive value.

JIRA # WSP-114

Review and Download Historical SUTA Recalculation Reports

The Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers form now provides an archive of previously generated previews. Click the Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers Report History link to open a modal form containing the past reports. Preview reports are only saved when the Update Tax Values option is enabled.

This form is only available to Service Provider users who have user role access to the parent form. The link does not display for users who have their form access set to Inquiry.

Note: Note: If a user’s Client Access Group restricts access to one or more clients, they cannot access this new form. Only users with total client access can view these historical reports.

JIRA # WSP-178

Start and End Dates for System-wide Tax Suppression

You can now set tax suppression date ranges on the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form (located in the Actions menu of the System Parameters form).

In the Suppress Tax Code grid, enter an optional From Date and To Date. These fields specifically denote start and end pay dates.

The system suppresses the specified tax code only during this period (inclusive of the start and end pay dates).

Enhancements

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/CMP-Enhancements%20Sep-2024.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/CMP-Enhancements Sep-2024.htm

Enhancements

This section describes general enhancements that were made in the PrismHR September 2024 quarterly release.

Changes to Alabama Overtime Exemption rule

Alabama updated the OT wage exemption to include Salary non-exempt employees and exclude Hourly exempt effective 10/1/2024. PrismHR will now support this change. For any pay date 10/1/24 or greater, AL OT exempt wage logic will apply to:

  • Salary Non-exempt employees, so that wages for hours worked over 40 in a workweek will be exempt from AL state income tax.

  • Hourly exempt employees, so that they will no longer be eligible for exempt wages due to hours worked over 40 in a work week.

For more information, please visit the article named Alabama Overtime Exemption Amendments on the Customer Resource Center.

JIRA # CMP-5921, CMP-5939

Changes to the W-2 Form Layout form

For tax year 2023 and forward, the W-2 Form Layout form in PrismHR will have the following additional fields:

  • For the W2 Form Type S, the Form Adjustment section at the bottom will now have the following two fields:

  • Top Section - The added form adjustment numbers each represent a line and will adjust the corresponding section. With the default being a 3, a setting of 1 or 2 will adjust the section(s) up in comparison whereas a 4 or 5 will adjust the section down on the page.

  • Bottom Section - The added form adjustment numbers each represent a line and will adjust the corresponding section. With the default being a 3, a setting of 1 or 2 will adjust the section(s) up in comparison whereas a 4 or 5 will adjust the section down on the page.

  • For the W2 Form Type LB and GHF the Form Adjustment section at the bottom will now have the following three fields:

  • Top Section - The added form adjustment numbers each represent a line and will adjust the corresponding section. With the default being a 3, a setting of 1 or 2 will adjust the section(s) up in comparison whereas a 4 or 5 will adjust the section down on the page.

  • Middle Section - The added form adjustment numbers each represent a line and will adjust the corresponding section. With the default being a 3, a setting of 1 or 2 will adjust the section(s) up in comparison whereas a 4 or 5 will adjust the section down on the page.

  • Bottom Section - The added form adjustment numbers each represent a line and will adjust the corresponding section. With the default being a 3, a setting of 1 or 2 will adjust the section(s) up in comparison whereas a 4 or 5 will adjust the section down on the page.

  • Click the Reset button to reset the above values to 3 for all the fields in the Form Adjustment section.

  • Click Save to save your changes to be able to print the W-2 Forms using the Print W-2 Forms form.

Note: Note: At this time this option is available for printing W2 Form Type S, LB and GHF only.

JIRA # CMP-5569, CMP-5724, CMP-5845

Changes to Common Pay Agent for Form W-2 Processing

On the Employer Details form, the layout of the Common Pay Agent for Form W-2 Processing section has been updated as follows:

[Image: screenshot]

To display Common Pay Agent information on the Form W-2 or Form W-2c PDF, even if this was used in the past, you will need to select a Report Option and Save the changes on the Employer Details form.

The grid has the following columns:

  • Year - The year for which this setup will apply. For example, for 2023 you have a common pay agent and reporting option is Agent only. For every year starting 2023 the Form W-2 or Form W-2c will report only the common pay agent information until you change it. If you make any changes later, you will need to add a line, enter the year and make the changes. For example, for 2025 you change the Report Option to Agent|Employer. You would then see the Common Pay Agent information reported on the Form W-2 only for 2023, 2024, and in 2025 you would see the Agent|Employer information reported on the Form W-2 or Form W-2c. (It is not required to add the 2024 record for common pay agent to continue)

Note: Note: This field can be blank only if there is no data. If there is data in the grid, then this field needs to be filled up. If you already had data for this section earlier, now you will need to go in and update the year and save the record. The screen defaults to 2023 since before 2023 PrismHR did not report the common pay agent on the Form W-2 or Form W-2c PDFs.

  • Agent FEIN - The unique 9 digit Federal Employer Identification Number of the agent.

  • Agent Name - The name of the agent.

  • Address - The street address of the agent.

  • City - The city of the agent.

  • State - The two digit state of the agent.

  • Zip - The zip code of the agent.

  • Report Option - Select is the default option which will only report the employer information. You need to select one of the following options:

  • Agent|Employer - Select this option to report the Common Pay Agent and Agent for {Employer}.

  • Agent only - Select this option to report only the Common Pay Agent.

Note: Note: Common Pay Agent Name Control is not applied to W2’s built by Client Federal Entity Registers for SBEA W2 Reporting.

JIRA # CMP-5660, CMP-5711

Changes to the FLSA Exempt Compensation Report form

The following highlighted fields are added to the FLSA Exempt Compensation Report form.

[Image: screenshot]

  • State - Select the Work State of the employee/s from the drop-down for the Pay Period, Quarter or the Payroll Number. Leave this field blank if you want to display employees from all states for the Pay Period, Quarter or the Payroll Number. The FLSA Exempt Compensation Report now displays the Work State as shown below.

[Image: screenshot]

  • Minimum Standard Salary - For Standard FLSA Type, enter the minimum salary here.

  • Minimum Highly Compensated Salary - For Highly Compensated FLSA Type, enter the minimum salary here.

Note: Note: Depending on whether the employee is paid weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly or monthly, PrismHR will divide this Minimum Salary by 52 or 26 or 24 or 12 to get the Period Minimum. The Period Minimum multiplied by Pay Per Date Range (5 for a 5 day work week) will provide the Total Compensation Expected on the FLSA Exempt Compensation Report. The difference between the Total Compensation Expected and the Actual Total Compensation is the Deficiency on the FLSA Exempt Compensation Report.

JIRA # CMP-5695, CMP-5696, CMP-5699, CMP-5700

Changes to the ACA Offered Employees form

  • The following two new filter options have been added to the ACA Offered Employees form.

  • Stability Period Includes - This field is optional. When you enter a date here, the report displays only those employees whose start and end date either begins, ends or falls in between the date entered. If there are multiple records for an employee, the report will only show the record in which the date falls. A single employee could potentially have two stability periods - On-Going and New Hire.

  • Offer of Coverage - This field is optional. If you do not select any option, the report will display all eligible employees for ACA coverage for the client. If you select one of the following options:

  • Yes - The report will display only those employees who have had an offer of coverage.

  • No - The report will display only those employees who have not had an offer of coverage.

  • A new column named ACA Offer of Coverage is added to the grid after the column named Type. This column is read only at this time. It is available through the API and will later be updated through the Data Import Tool.

  • Y = The employee has had an offer of coverage.

  • N = The employee has not had an offer of coverage.

[Image: screenshot]

JIRA # CMP-5482, CMP-5650

Override State added for Creditor Wage Garnishment

There are instances when a creditor garnishment needs to follow the withholding limit requirements of the issuing state rather than the employee’s work state. PrismHR now supports this option.

On the Employee Garnishments form, when Creditor Wage Garnishment is selected from the drop-down under the Category field, then under the Limit Overrides section, a new field appears named Override State Code. This field is optional.

When an Override State Code is selected for an employee on the Employee Garnishments form for Creditor Wage Garnishment, the employee creditor wage garnishment will follow State Garnishment Rules for the selected Override State on the Employee Garnishments form and not the SUTA state. For example, if an employee is working in NY with NY SUTA and has a creditor garnishment with GA selected for the Override State Code field on the Employee Garnishments form, then creditor garnishment for that employee will be calculated based on State Garnishment Rules for GA instead of NY.

The creditor garnishment will now follow the withholding limits based on the State Garnishment Rules form for the state selected in the Override State Code above instead of the employee’s SUTA state.

JIRA # CMP-5783, CMP-5586

Employee Details Garnishments form

Previously from the Employee Details form, when you clicked Garnishments under Actions menu, the Employee Garnishments form opened. Then you had to select a Docket Number to open a docket for an employee. This form included all dockets for all applicable employees for a single client. These dockets were not specific to the employee record. There was no easy way to find all the garnishments for an employee under one form.

To solve this, a new form named Employee Details Garnishments is introduced. Once you select an employee on the Employee Details form, click Garnishments under Actions menu to open this form. If no garnishments are applied to this employee a message will appear: “No garnishments for this employee”.

Note: Note: This new form must be added to the User Roles for user. You cannot find this form using normal search means.

Security

  • Uses Client Access Group security and Data Entity security.

  • Worksite Managers, Worksite Trusted Advisors and Service Providers can access the form.

[Image: screenshot]

Use this form to view all garnishments associated with the selected employee on the Employee Details form.

The form will show the following information in a table:

  • Docket Number - You can click this hyperlink to open this docket in detail on the Employee Garnishments form. You can also click on the Garnishment Maintenance hyperlink to open the Employee Garnishments form.

  • Category - This denotes the type of garnishment.

  • B = Bankruptcy Order

  • C = Child Support

  • FTB = Franchise Tax Board

  • I = IRS Tax Levy

  • O = Creditor Wage Garnishment

  • S = State Tax Levy

  • SL = Student Loan

  • SP = Spousal Support

  • Receipt Date - The date when this docket was received from the authorities.

  • Start Date - The start date of this garnishment.

  • Stop Date - The stop date of this garnishment.

  • Payee - The payee for this garnishment.

  • Withholding Amount - The flat amount withheld for the garnishment. The withholding amount will be blank if not a flat amount.

Click Close to close this form and return to the Employee Details form for the employee.

Adding the Employee Details Garnishments Form to User Roles

To begin using this new form, you must first add it to the user role(s). (Note: If you have more than one user role to add to this new form, use the Bulk Role Update instructions.)

To add this menu item to a user role, do the following:

  1. Click

[Image: screenshot]

(Back Office). Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  1. Select or enter the Role ID.

  2. Click Add. The User Role Maintenance form displays.

  3. Select the Employee Details Garnishments form from the list. (To quickly find this item, select HR in the Type Filter

box.)

  1. Click Accept.

  2. Click Save. Log out and login for this action to take effect.

To change the role’s access to Inquiry or Deny for this item (the default is Full), click the Access item (the access changes to Inquiry, click it again to change the access to Deny). Click Save.

To add this menu item to multiple user roles, do the following:

  1. Click

[Image: screenshot]

(Back Office). Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  1. Select Bulk Role Update from the

[Image: screenshot]

Actions menu. The Bulk Role Update form opens.

  1. Click Form and then select EMPLOYEE.GARNISHMENTSEE.SPECIFIC.GARNISHMENTS from the Search Processes list. (To quickly find this item, enter Employee Details Garnishments in the Form Description* field and click Refine, then select the form that displays.)

JIRA # WSP-387

Validating School District ID and Tax Code on Tax Adjustments form

Previously, you could enter more than one line for school taxes on the Tax Adjustments form. When this information was posted to the registers, the system only included the first line item because the posting program did not expect any tax code duplications.

The system now validates that you cannot enter more than one line for a school tax in the same state, which prevents entering duplicate tax codes.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202411/CMP-Enhancements%20Nov-2024.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202411/CMP-Enhancements Nov-2024.htm

Enhancements

This section describes general enhancements that were made in the PrismHR November 2024 quarterly release.

Changes to the MasterTax RTS & PTS

For both SBEA and non-SBEA clients, the MasterTax v47 RTS will include Work Out of State Flag which is either Y or N in position 15 for the 500, 501, 601, and 616 records for Pennsylvania resident tax codes not including Philadelphia. This does not apply to Philadelphia residents and this position will remain blank for Philadelphia locality taxes.

For both SBEA and non-SBEA clients, the MasterTax v29 PTS will include Work Out of State Flag which is either Y or N in position 15 for the 210 and 500 records for Pennsylvania resident tax codes not including Philadelphia. This does not apply to Philadelphia residents and this position will remain blank for Philadelphia locality taxes.

JIRA # CMP-6016, CMP-6018

Changes to the State Rules form

When processing Global PTO for states that have different state and local requirements for PTO, you now have the ability to limit enrollment and accrual to the local plan when an employee is working in a specific locality. On the State Rules form, under the Global PTO section a new field named Apply Local PTO Plan Only when applicable is added.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: The client must be enabled for Global PTO.

When this field is:

  • Unchecked - During payroll, both the state and the applicable local global PTO plans will accrue.

  • Checked - During payroll, when the Geocode on the timesheet for an employee:

  • falls within the range listed for the Local Plan ID, the employee is enrolled in the specified Local Plan and accruals are calculated as per that specified Local Plan. The employee is not enrolled, and accruals are not calculated as per state plans listed.

  • does not fall within the range listed for the Local Plan ID but works within the state for an existing Global PTO plan, the employee is enrolled, and accruals are calculated as per applicable state plans listed.

Note: Note: If an employee is enrolled in a local plan with no state plan, and then moves to a location which is without a local plan but is subject to the state plan, then PTO will accrue according to the state plan from the time the employee has moved. Prior payroll vouchers for the employee will remain unaffected on account of this change.

JIRA # CMP-4983

Changes to the EES Puerto Rico W-2 Export

From now on, EES Puerto Rico W-2 Export generated by PrismHR will end at position 1600 with a total of 13 zero filled positions (position 1587 to 1600) at the end of the file as required.

JIRA # CMP-5424

Alabama exempt overtime wages added to Form W-2

Alabama Department of Revenue proposes that exempt overtime wages be reported in Box 14 of employees Form W-2 using “EX OT WAGES” as the indicator, for example, EX OT WAGES- $15,250. PrismHR now supports this.

From tax year 2024, EX OT WAGES with the dollar amount will be reported in Box 14 on the employee the Form W-2. If a recalculation was applied this amount may differ from the voucher amounts.

Form Type GHF name changed

On the Print W-2 Forms form, the Form Type “GHF - LB Custom Legal Size, Simple, Four” is updated to “GHF - Legal Size, Simplex, Four-Up, Self-Mailed w/ EE ID and Address Panel on Bottom”. The form output remains the same.

JIRA # CMP-5571

VT Childcare (EE tax withheld) added to W2 Build

From tax year 2024, for both SBEA and Non-SBEA clients, the YTD employee portion of the Vermont Child Care Contribution (tax code 46-27) will be added to Box 14 on the Form W-2 and Form W-2c generated by the system. This will report as VT CCC with the dollar amount. This information will reflect on the following forms:

  • Employee Tax Summary

  • Update Employee W-2 Forms

  • Update Employee W-2C Forms

JIRA # CMP-5454

Form 1099 generated by PrismHR- updated

From tax year 2024, for an employee who is a 1099 contractor and has federal or state income tax withheld by the employer, the employee 1099 Build process in PrismHR will include the following information apart from Non-Employee Compensation:

  • Federal Income Tax Withheld

  • Federal Income Taxable

  • State Tax Withheld

  • State Income Taxable

JIRA # CMP-4890

Layout changes to EFW2 File for tax year 2024

For the tax year 2024 there are record layout changes. RO (Employee Optional) Record & RU (Total Optional) Record were updated to add BOX 12 code II Income from Exclusion of Medicaid Waiver Payments. PrismHR has updated the EFW2 format to support this change. From tax year 2024, the EFW2 output file will have record RO positions 144 - 154 and RU positions 190 - 204 zero-filled.

JIRA # CMP-5897

Employee Child Care Contribution amount added to the VT EFW2 File

Effective 7/1/24, an employer in the state of Vermont is required to pay a 0.44% tax on subject wages paid to an employee in the state of Vermont and is allowed to deduct up to 0.11% from the employee’s pay. For more information on this, please refer to the knowledge article named Vermont Child Care Contribution Tax on the Customer Resource Center.

Beginning in Tax Year 2024, the Vermont EFW2 RS record positions 338 - 348 will contain the Vermont Employee Child Care Contribution amounts to tax code 46-27 (Employee Withholding) and will remain blank if there is no employee withholding.

JIRA # CMP-5835

Secure 2.0 Increased Catch Up Contributions

As a result of the Secure 2.0 Act of 2022, effective 1/1/2025, for employees who will turn 60, 61, 62 or 63 as of 12/31 of the defined tax year, are permitted to contribute an additional amount to their catch-up contribution. To support this change, the increased contribution amount should be entered in the 60-63 Catch Up field on the following forms for the employee contribution to be treated as a pre-tax amount:

  • Benefit Plan Maintenance / Retirement Plans / Retirement Plans (under section Plan Year Deferral Limits)

  • Benefit Plan Maintenance / Retirement Plans / Tax Year Limits Maintenance

  • The value entered in this field will be the total amount such employees can contribute for the tax year.

  • For tax year 2025, it is the greater of 150% of Catch-Up Contribution limit OR $10,000.

• In the December Maintenance release, additional functionality will be available to suppress this amount on the client level retirement plan.

JIRA # CMP-5834

Changes to Oregon Creditor Garnishment calculation

From 1/1/2025 up to 06/30/2027, Oregon Creditor Garnishment calculations have been programmed by effective date to use the following exempt amounts as defined by Oregon State Law based on the pay period for each of the effective dates. These amounts will be applied when the Minimum Wage Rate Multiplier field for the state of Oregon is set to 30.

Pay Period Weekly Bi-Weekly Semi-Monthly Monthly
01-Jan-2025 thru 30-Jun-2025 $305 $611 $655 $1309
01-Jul-2025 thru 30-Jun-2026 $338 $675 $737 $1458
01-Jul-2026 thru 30-Jun-2027 $400 $832 $912 $1792

On July 1, 2027, calculations will default to State Garnishment Rules for the state of Oregon:

Note: Note: It is recommended that for the state of Oregon, on the State Garnishment Rules form, the Minimum Wage Rate Multiplier field be set to 30 until July 2027.

JIRA # WSP-345

Change to the Employee Types form

A new field named Tax Exemption has been added to the Employee Types form.

This field is optional. You can enable a specified form of income tax suppression for the selected Employee Type instead of setting income tax suppression at an employee level. You can select one of the following options:

Enhancements

This section describes general enhancements that were made in the PrismHR February 2025 monthly release.

Changes to the EFW2 for the state of Maryland

Maryland changed the requirements of their state EFW2. The following changes are implemented for Employer Reporting of Form W-2 so that your files do not get rejected:

  • RE record positions 222-248 will report the Tax Contact Name from the Tax tab on the Employer Details form.

  • RE record positions 249-263 will report Tax Contact Phone number from the Tax tab on the Employer Details form.

  • RE record positions 279-318 will report Tax Contact Email address from the Tax tab on the Employer Details form.

  • RE record positions 497-504 will report date created (this is reported in other records of the file).

  • RE record positions 505-512 will report time created (this is reported in other records of the file).

  • RV record positions 149-160 will report the same as the taxes withheld in positions 161-172.

JIRA # CMP-6342

Changes to the EFW2C Download and Maintenance form

Previously using this form, though you could generate downloads that reported the original and corrected employee Form W-2c data. Since this download was run many times in a tax year, you kept getting the original group of employees over and over. There was no option to automatically deselect the employees for whom the Form W-2c data was already successfully submitted to the Social Security Administration earlier and was not needed to be resubmitted. This required your manual intervention to segregate the Form W-2c data for the right employees and potentially caused errors.

To mitigate this, starting tax year 2024 and beyond, this form will generate the download files in batches, with each batch identified by a system generated Filename on the Generated EFW2C Files section. One batch will not include any employee from another batch, thus reducing your manual intervention and chances of errors.

The following changes have been made to this form.

[Image: screenshot]

  • Submission Type - the following options are now available:

  • Original EFW2C - This is default option once you arrive on this form. Use this option generate the file when you want to submit an employee’s Form W-2c data for the first time to the Social Security Administration.

  • Regenerate Processed EFW2C Export - Select this option if you want to regenerate an existing file (the original submission had errors or did not get submitted correctly for some reason) to re-submit an employee’s Form W-2c data to the Social Security Administration. Once you select this option, a drop-down field appears listing all the files having a Status of Regenerate on the Generated EFW2C Files grid below.

  • File Description - This is not a mandatory field. However, you may choose to provide a file name here to identify a particular file better. This file name will appear under the Description field in the grid below for the corresponding system generated Filename. If you name/rename a file, use the .txt extension.

  • Generated EFW2C Files - This grid lists all the batches of files generated for the selected tax year and other parameters selected on this form. Only the first four files will be display in the grid. If there are more, you need to scroll down. This grid has the following columns:

  • Filename - This is a system generated file name for a batch.

  • Description - The file description entered on the File Description field above. It will be blank if nothing was entered.

  • Status - Displays the current status of the file. If you want to change the status of a file, click the status of that file to open the Edit EFW2C File Status form for that file and edit the status. For example, once you have submitted an unsent file to the Social Security Administration, you may want to change the status of that file from Unsent to In Process. A file will have one of the following statuses:

  • Unsent - Once you click Create Export File to generate a file for a batch for the first time for an original EFW2C submission, it will be listed as Unsent in the grid with a new file name. Using the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you cannot edit information for any employee on this file.

  • In Process - A file that has been submitted to the Social Security Administration but is yet to be accepted by them. You can enter the Receipt ID received for that file submission on the Edit EFW2C File Status form for that file. Using the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you cannot edit information for any employee on this file.

  • Accepted - A file that was submitted successfully to the Social Security Administration and accepted by them. Using the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you cannot edit information for any employee on this file.

  • Rejected - A file that was rejected upon submission by the Social Security Administration. Using the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you can edit information for any employee on this file, and the values will be pre-populated for that employee.

  • Regenerate - A file that was regenerated prior to submission to the Social Security Administration. Using the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you can edit information for any employee on this file, and the values will be pre-populated for that employee.

  • Cancelled - A generated file that is not currently under submission the Social Security Administration and cancelled owing to some reason. Using the Update Employee W-2C Forms form, you can edit information for any employee on this file. However, you will need to re-enter all the values since all the fields will be blank for that employee.

  • WFID - The unique Wage File Identifier on the notice sent to you by the Social Security Administration for every initial submission.

  • Ver - When a EFW2C batch is initially created, this will be version 1. If the file is then cancelled and regenerated, the original version 1 will be replaced with version 2 and so on.

  • Create Date - The date when this batch was first created.

  • Create Time - The time when this batch was first created.

  • Last Modified on - The date when this file was last modified.

JIRA # CMP-5956, CMP-6366

The Edit EFW2C File Status form

Use this form to change/update the Status of the EFW2C download file in the Generated EFW2C Files grid on the EFW2C Download and Maintenance form mentioned above.

[Image: screenshot]

  • The following fields will be read only on this form:

  • Tax Year

  • Submitter ID

  • File Name

  • File Description

  • You can change/updated the current Status using the drop-down which has the options shown above. If you select

  • In Process then you have the option to enter/updated the Receipt ID for that file.

  • Rejected then you have to enter/updated the Resubmission WFID for that file.

  • You can also change/update the file description using the New File Description field.

Click Save to save the changes made on this form so that it reflects correctly on the Generated EFW2C Files grid on the EFW2C Download and Maintenance form. If you do no wish to save the changes, then you can close this form using the

[Image: screenshot]

button on the top right of this form.

JIRA # CMP-6276, CMP-6338

CFC ACADATABUILD is now activated in PrismPrismHR

Previously, the Custom Feature Code ACADATABUILD used to be activated anytime when someone logged in to HRPyramid to build the ACA data for the prior month. Now, this Custom Feature Code ACADATABUILD is activated in PrismHR. The purpose of this CFC is to allow ACA data to build from the beginning of the year in an ongoing manner because when trying to build for the entire year the process sometimes can take many days for larger companies. This CFC will now incrementally build data used for ACA reporting throughout the year. This however does not replace the need to use the Rebuild ACA Data process already existing in PrismHR. You may still need to use the Rebuild ACA Data process if data for employees change or if the client is not set up as a large employer in PrismHR.

JIRA # CMP-6162

PrismHR now shelters local wages under the 60-63 Catch Up

Previously, PrismHR did not shelter local wages under the 60-63 Catch Up for Secure 2.0 when the contributions were Pre-Tax. It only sheltered up to the regular Catch Up Limit. Enhancements made to PrismHR now shelters local wages under the 60-63 Catch Up for Secure 2.0 when the contributions are Pre-Tax.

For payrolls available for processing in 2025:

  • for an employee aged between 60-63 as of 12/31/2025, and

  • enrolled in a 401k plan with contributions and catchup amount, and

  • payroll has enough wages to have employee meet the 60-63 Catch Up amount, and

  • on the Tax Year Limits Maintenance form the 60-63 Catch Up amount for that Year is higher than the Catch Up Limit,

PrismHR includes the full catchup amount in all Federal, State, and Local sheltered earnings.

In MasterTax V48 and above, for Tax Year 2025 and beyond, every instance of tax code 20-40 (ME PFML Employee Contribution) will be reported as a major tax code ME0000-014 (Maine Paid Family and Medical Leave) both on the Employer and the Client level for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients.

JIRA # CMP-6458

MasterTax V48 - DE PFML

In MasterTax V48 and above, for Tax Year 2025 and beyond, every instance of tax code 08-40 (DE PFML Employee Contribution) will be reported as a major tax code DE0000-014 (Delaware Paid Family and Medical Leave) both on the Employer and the Client level for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients.

  • This will be reported in positions 16-35 in the 601 records (Employee Wage Detail).

  • Positions 116 - 118 calls for the employer contribution rate.

  • Employee wage detail (601) records must be imported for tax code DE0000-014 for MasterTax to report this tax correctly.

  • A summary Reconciliation Amounts (500) record is required for tax code DE0000-014 for MasterTax to associate the employee wage detail with this tax.

For customers required to submit Certified Payroll Reports, new payroll voucher fields have been created for future reporting requirements. JIRA # CMP-6212

Changes to the Client EEO-1 & Pay Data Files form

To support Illinois Equal Pay Registration Certificate reporting, the Client EEO-1 and Pay Data form has been enhanced with the IL Pay Data Report option. This report includes employees who worked at your factory/facility/office in Illinois plus the 100% remote employees who report directly to Illinois management.

[Image: screenshot]

This form has been enhanced to support the reporting of Illinois Pay Data for your employees. Under the Generate File section on this form:

  • The EEO File Type field now has an additional dropdown named IL Pay Data Report.

  • The EEO Pay Period End Date will be 12/31 of the year selected.

  • The EEO Pay Period Start Date will be 01/01 of the year selected.

Following is a sample IL Pay Data Report:

[Image: screenshot]

  • This report will have the following columns:

  • Company - The Client ID. (This is added for ease of reference and will need to be removed before submitting to the State of IL.)

  • Employee ID - The employee ID of the Illinois employee. (This is added for ease of reference and will need to be removed before submitting to the State of IL.)

  • FirstName - First name of the Illinois employee.

  • LastName - Last name of the Illinois employee.

  • SSN - The last 4 digits of the Social Security number of the Illinois employee.

  • Gender - if data is incomplete, then the report will display choose not to identify.

  • Race - if data is incomplete, then the report will display choose not to identify.

  • Ethnicity - will display either Hispanic/Latino or Not Hispanic or Latino.

  • Wages - Total wages earned by the Illinois employee.

  • Hours Worked - Hours worked as an Illinois employee.

  • Hire Date - The date when the employee became active as an Illinois employee.

  • Termination Date - The date when the employee became inactive as an Illinois employee.

  • Job Classification - Job classification of the Illinois employee.

  • Job Title - Job title of the Illinois employee.

  • County - The worksite county in the state of Illinois of the employee.

JIRA # CMP-6178, CMP-6179

Garnishment Capping Logic extended to State Tax Levy

From now on, when the Enhanced Garnishment Capping field is checked on the System Parameters form, the system will ensure that the garnishment amount for a State Levy docket does not exceed the flat amount of a given State Levy docket minus the sum of all garnishment deductions made for said docket, during the applicable pay cycle. If an employee has been paid in a previous payroll batch for the same pay period with garnished wages, the State Levy garnishment will only deduct the difference of the total flat amount less the amount garnished on a prior batch for that period. If the State Levy garnishment is reduced to zero, then the system will not calculate garnishment fee for the State Levy as the garnishment for State Levy on current payroll is not deductible.

JIRA # CMP-6138

Changes to the State Garnishment Rules form

Certain states have varying requirements on how to calculate a State tax levy when an employee has other garnishments. To allow flexibility to better support states allowing other garnishments including creditor garnishment deduction before calculating the amount due to the state levy, a new option has been added to the form. To support this feature, a new field named Allow Creditor Garnishment deduction before State Levy is added under the Rules for Calculating Withholding for Creditor Garnishments section on this form. This field is a checkbox.

[Image: screenshot]

If for a selected state, this checkbox is:

  • Checked - then the order of priority for deduction of garnishments will be as follows:

  1. Child Support (Spousal Support)

  2. Bankruptcy

  3. Levies (IRS Tax Levy, FTB)

  4. Creditor Wage Garnishment / Student Loan

  5. State Tax Levy

  • Unchecked - then the order of priority for deduction of garnishments will be as follows:

  1. Child Support (Spousal Support)

  2. Bankruptcy

  3. Levies (IRS Tax Levy, FTB)

  4. State Tax Levy

  5. Creditor Wage Garnishment / Student Loan

Note: Note: When using the new option to prioritize Creditor Wage Garnishments prior to the State Tax Levy, you should ensure that the State Tax Levy maximum percent has been entered for the applicable State Code on the State Garnishment Rules form.

This field is a dropdown. Select one of the following options:

  • Disabled - This is the default option. When disabled, then the system will not prompt you to enter a reason for record update when you make changes to any one of the critical forms listed above.

  • Optional - This option will provide you with the following prompt (as shown below) to enter a reason when you make changes to any one of the critical forms listed above. However, you can still save your changes without providing a reason.

Employer override to PEO when the State is set to combined reporting

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202504/Employer%20override%20to%20PEO%20when%20the%20State%20is%20set%20to%20combined%20reporting.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202504/Employer override to PEO when the State is set to combined reporting.htm

Employer override to PEO when the State is set to combined reporting

Previously, when a state was set as for SUTA reporting based on the PEO but reported on the client level (in the State Rules form the SUTA PEO/Client Based field was selected as SUTA is PEO Based and the Client SUTA Report Only field was checked and on the Employer Details form, under the State Tax section, the SUTA Rpt Entity is selected as PEO for that state) then the system did not remove the Client Reporting only flag resulting in CR on the tax reporting rather than reporting under the Employer. On the employee payroll voucher, under the Employer Tax section for that state tax code the Client Reporting Only field for that state tax code displayed Y.

From now on, when a state has an override on the Employer Details form (as indicated above) to report at the PEO level, the Tax Basis will be P and the Client Reporting Only field for that state tax code display N.

Note: Note: If an override for the state exists on the Client Details form, then the state will be Client Reporting (tax basis - C) only when under the Tax tab, under the State Tax Setup section, a Client Reporting Start Date is entered for that state, otherwise it will be ignored.

Changes to the Create Employee W-2C Forms form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202505/Changes%20to%20the%20Create%20Employee%20W-2C%20Forms%20form.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202505/Changes to the Create Employee W-2C Forms form.htm

Changes to the Create Employee W-2C Forms form

As a service provider, you now have the option to import a list of employees for which Form W-2cs are to be created using the Create Employee W-2C Forms form.

[Image: screenshot]

A new button named Upload Employees is now available beside the Employee table.

  • If you have full access to the Create Employee W-2C Forms form, you will be able to see this button and use it to upload employees. Use the File Upload dialog box to upload your list of employees for whom you need to generate Form W-2cs. Click the Add Files button to select the import file from your system. Click the File Upload button to upload the employers and employees.

  • When uploading an employee list containing an invalid Employer ID / Employee ID combination, the Employee ID is not added to the Employee Table but is noted on the upload Transaction Report as “Failing” the upload process.

  • When uploading a list containing a valid Employer ID/ Employee ID combination where the Employer ID had not yet been added to the Employer Table, the upload process adds both the Employer ID and the Employee ID to their respective tables.

  • When uploading a list containing a valid Employer ID/ Employee ID combination where the Employer ID has already been added to the Employer Table, the upload process adds only the Employee ID to its respective table.

  • Your import file should:

  • be a csv or text-tab-delimited file

  • have two columns namely:

  • Employee ID

  • Employer ID

  • not contain more than 500 employees

  • If you have inquiry access to the Create Employee W-2C Forms form, you will be able to see this button, but you cannot use it.

Changes to the Labor Unions form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202506/Changes%20to%20the%20Labor%20Unions%20form.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202506/Changes to the Labor Unions form.htm

Changes to the Labor Unions form

On the Labor Unions form, on the Union Deduction Code table, after the Union Dues Table Rules column, there is a new column named Periods as shown in the screenshot below. The GLOBAL custom feature code UNIONDEDPERIOD must be turned on for this field to display and being editable. If the GLOBAL custom feature code UNIONDEDPERIOD is turned off the Periods column will still display, but you cannot edit it.

[Image: screenshot]

Period here refers to the deduction period which references the week of the month for the payroll. For instance, if your weekly Pay Date was 02-28-2025 which was a Friday and 02-28-2025 was the 4th Friday of February, so Deduction Period will be 4. The Periods column indicates this Deduction Period for the corresponding Union Deduction Code.

  • This column cannot be empty for any given Union Deduction Code. If you try to delete the Periods column for any Union Deduction Code and save the Labor Unions form, you will receive an error stating The Union period(s) must be specified.

  • The default value is 12345. You can edit appropriately for the corresponding Union Deduction Code. So if there is a union deduction override on the Labor Unions form that would apply to the employee’s recurring deduction record, then just removing the GLOBAL custom feature code UNIONDEDPERIOD on the Systems Parameters form will not reset it to the default value of 12345. Any employee that already has a recurring deduction record that is updated for a certain period will remain in place. Before removing the GLOBAL custom feature code UNIONDEDPERIOD on the Systems Parameters form, you need to update the labor union record itself if you intend to go back to all periods. So please ensure the labor Union deduction periods are accurate before removing the custom feature code.

  • You can enter multiple deduction periods once between 1-5 or O. O indicates a one-time deduction for the month.

  • You cannot enter the same deduction period twice for the same Union Deduction Code. If you try to enter the same deduction period twice for any Union Deduction Code and save the Labor Unions form, you will receive an error stating A period can only be entered once.

MasterTax PTS update for West Virginia local employees

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202506/MasterTax%20PTS%20update%20for%20West%20Virginia%20local%20employees.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202506/MasterTax PTS update for West Virginia local employees.htm

MasterTax PTS update for West Virginia local employees

The MasterTax PTS 500 record for West Virginia locals (tax code 49XXXXXXX-32) will now include the payroll frequency indicator in position 184 for the following payroll frequencies:

  • W - Weekly

  • B - Biweekly

  • S - Semi-Monthly

  • M - Monthly

  • for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients

If there is more than one frequency, it will default to the most frequently used frequency in the record. For example, if the PTS 500 record represents 100 vouchers, and 99 of those vouchers are on a monthly pay schedule while one voucher is on a weekly schedule, then the frequency code in position 184 will contain “M” for monthly. This is because monthly is more frequent than weekly.

Also, if a voucher has a Daily frequency, then the system will ignore those. This is because for any frequency other than W/B/S/M, we should leave position 184 blank. Thus, if 99 vouchers have a daily frequency while one voucher has bi-weekly, then the system will set the MasterTax PTS code to “B” for bi-weekly. Similarly, if all the vouchers are on a daily schedule, then position 184 will be blank.

Railroad Unemployment Insurance Act Tax

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202506/Railroad%20Unemployment%20Insurance%20Act%20Tax.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202506/Railroad Unemployment Insurance Act Tax.htm

Railroad Unemployment Insurance Act Tax

The Tax tab of the Client Details form now has a new field named RUIA Rate as shown in the screenshot below.

[Image: screenshot]

  • If you have full access to the Tax tab on the Client Details form and have:

  • full access to the RUIA Rate field, then you can see the RUIA Rate field, and edit it.

  • inquiry access to the RUIA Rate field, then you can see the RUIA Rate field, but you cannot edit it.

  • disabled access to the RUIA Rate field, then you can see the RUIA Rate field, but you cannot edit it.

  • hidden access to the RUIA Rate field, then you cannot see the RUIA Rate field.

  • If you have inquiry access to the Tax tab on the Client Details form and have:

  • inquiry access to the RUIA Rate field, then you can see the RUIA Rate field, but you cannot edit it.

  • disabled access to the RUIA Rate field, then you can see the RUIA Rate field, but you cannot edit it.

  • hidden access to the RUIA Rate field, then you cannot see the RUIA Rate field.

RUIA Rate is Railroad Unemployment Insurance Act Tax rate. When a client is set up as a Railroad Employer, payrolls processed under the client will not include employer FUTA or FICA withholding and will instead implement RUIA withholding at the rate entered in the RUIA Rate field under the Tax Parameters section under the Tax tab on the Client Details form. The taxes withheld for RUIA will be reported on the MasterTax RTS, PTS, and PrismHR Periodic and Quarterly Files. The existing translation for core FICA tax codes to the Railroad equivalent will remain the same:

Employee Tax Employer Tax
00-60 RAILROAD TIER 1 SOC SEC EE 00-61 RAILROAD TIER 1 SOC SEC ER
00-62 RAILROAD TIER 2 SOC SEC EE 00-63 RAILROAD TIER 2 SOC SEC ER
00-64 RAILROAD TIER 1 MEDICARE EE 00-65 RAILROAD TIER 1 MEDICARE ER

  • You can only save a value in this field if the Railroad Employer field above is checked.

  • If the Railroad Employer field is not checked and if you try to save this form with a value in the RUIA Rate field, you will receive an error stating Record cannot be saved with an RUIA Rate present for a non-railroad employer.

  • If there is an existing value in the RUIA Rate field, and if you un-check the Railroad Employer field, then the RUIA Rate field will be cleared out.

  • This field will only accept numeric characters up to 2 decimal places. Values entered with more than 2 decimal places will be rounded off.

Changes to the Recalculate Alabama Income Tax Exempt Wages form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202508/Changes%20to%20the%20Recalculate%20Alabama%20Income%20Tax%20Exempt%20Wages%20form.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202508/Changes to the Recalculate Alabama Income Tax Exempt Wages form.htm

Changes to the Recalculate Alabama Income Tax Exempt Wages form

Previously, for any Overtime wages earned in June 2025 but paid in July 2025, the Alabama Overtime exemption was not honored. The recalculation utility did not recalculate on pay dates in July with June charge dates.

Now, for any wages earned in June 2025 but paid in July 2025, the Alabama Overtime exemption will be honored. Exempt overtime wages earned on or before June 30 but not paid until July 2025 may be reported on the July 2025 Form A-6 or the September Form A-1 if quarterly filing. The Alabama income tax exemption applicable to overtime wages ended on June 30, 2025.

When recalculating the exempt overtime amounts for Alabama wages earned in June but paid in July, you may also need to process corresponding tax adjustments. The Recalculate AL Overtime utility will be applied to the employees W2 and quarterly tax reports. The Recalculate utility will not adjust an employee’s taxable wages or tax amounts. After running the Recalculate AL Overtime utility, you can leverage Report Center to review the employees taxable wages with the exempt overtime amounts. This report can be created using the Employee Payroll Voucher data set with the field exempt_ot.

[Image: screenshot]

Recalculate Global PTO Vouchers

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202508/Recalculate%20Global%20PTO%20Vouchers.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202508/Recalculate Global PTO Vouchers.htm

Recalculate Global PTO Vouchers

A new form named Recalculate Global PTO Vouchers is introduced as shown in the screenshot below.

[Image: screenshot]

Use this form to update any existing vouchers that need to be included in the Flat Amount by Hours Worked Global PTO accrual calculations when enabling Global PTO functionality mid-year for a client. This process will not calculate accruals or create PTO registers. You should use this process when you enable Global PTO mid-year and need to account for accruals in the past. So, when you enable Global PTO mid-year, this process allows the look-back calculation method the ability to pick up the vouchers in the past to accurately represent the YTD accrued balances for Global PTO.

Note: Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form. PrismHR

To access this form, click the Payroll menu. Under Action, click Recalculate Global PTO Vouchers.

To recalculate Global PTO vouchers in PrismHR:

  1. Complete the following field:

Field Name — Description

Start PAY Date — Enter the starting date of the pay date range from when you want to recalculate Global PTO for payroll vouchers.

  1. Click Preview. A job progress window opens and shows the total number of records to be updated. Click Close. You will see a preview consisting of the following columns:

  • VOUCHER : Payroll number

  • EMPLOYEE ID : The employee id

  • EMPLOYEE NAME : The employee name

  • ORIG PTO PLANS : The original Global PTO Plans assigned to the employee

  • NEW PTO PLANS : The new/changed Global PTO Plans assigned to the employee

  • ORIG PTO TYPES : The original Global PTO Plan types assigned to the employee

  • NEW PTO TYPES : The new/updated Global PTO Plan types assigned to the employee

  • MESSAGE : Any message provided

  1. Click the Download hyperlink to download the above information in a .CSV format.

  2. Click Update to update the Global PTO information on the required payroll vouchers. You will receive a warning message stating You are going to apply these changes to these vouchers. Do you wish to proceed?

  • Click Yes to update the selected payroll vouchers. A job progress window will appear showing the progress. Once completed, you will be returned to the main screen

  • Click No to go back without making any changes.

  1. Click Cancel to cancel the above operation. You can enter a different Start PAY Date and redo the process.

When the permanent SSN is issued, the New Hire Reporting Date may need to be cleared so that those employees are included in the next reporting cycle. This enhancement allows you to do this.

On the Clear New Hire Reporting Dates form, after you enter the date range and a Client ID a grid now appears as shown in the screenshot below.
