Garnishment Calculation Available After Posting Payroll

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202509/Garnishment%20Calculation%20Available%20After%20Posting%20Payroll.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202509/Garnishment Calculation Available After Posting Payroll.htm

Garnishment Calculation Available After Posting Payroll

From now on, the garnishment calculation report will be available for all initialized, posted and finalized payroll vouchers for Service Providers and Worksite Managers.

  • Selecting the posted voucher garnishment hyperlink will display the garnishment calculation module with the calculations as they were at the time of payroll.

  • The data on the report will reflect the state of the data at the time the voucher was posted or finalized.

  • Changes made to the Garnishment record AFTER the voucher was posted or finalized, such as the deduction amount or any other data affecting garnishment calculations, will NOT be reflected on the report when viewed.

  • New garnishment records entered after the voucher was posted or finalized will not be reflected on the garnishment calculation report.

  • The garnishment report will be available on all posted payroll voucher types that include garnishment deductions.

New York Form MTA-305 Tax Reporting rate update

Effective Q3 2025 and beyond, the NY MTA-305 download been updated based on new requirements. Please note that the report will continue to calculate the payroll expense and included detail records with no change - the following changes to New York Form MTA-305 Tax Reporting rate are applicable to the Rate tier by zone:

  • Zone 1

  • Position 93-98 displays the Zone 1 Tax Rate.

  • Tax rate determined based on the total payroll expense reported in positions 79-92.

  • The tax rate ranges have been updated for Q3 2025. Also note that there is a 4th tier.

  • Position 98-107 calculates the amount using the following updated rate.

Payroll Expense attributable to Zone 1 Metropolitan Commuter Transportation Mobility Rate
Over $0 but not over $375,000 0.055% (0.00055)
Over $375,000 but not over $437,500 0.115% (0.00115)
Over $437,500 but not over $2,500,000 0.60% (0.0060)
Over $2,500,000 0.895% (0.00895)

  • Zone 2

  • Position 127-131 displays the Zone 2 Tax Rate.

  • Tax rate determined based on the total payroll expense reported in 113-126.

  • The tax rate ranges have been updated for Q3 2025. Also note that there is a 4th tier.

  • Position 132-141 correctly calculates the amount using the following updated rate.

Payroll Expense attributable to Zone 2 Metropolitan Commuter Transportation Mobility Rate
Over $0 but not over $375,000 0.055% (0.00055)
Over $375,000 but not over $437,500 0.115% (0.00115)
Over $437,500 but not over $2,500,000 0.34% (0.0034)
Over $2,500,000 0.635% (0.00635)

  • Positions 175-188 reflect the cumulative total payroll for both zones (79-92) + (113+126).

  • Position 194-203 correctly reports the total due based on the factors above (98-107) + (132-141).

Note: Note: To be subject to the MCTMT for the quarter, the employer must have payroll expense in the entire MCTD greater than $312,500. For PEO reporting, this is assessed on the client level. This means Zone 1 + Zone 2 must exceed US$312,500. BUT the rate is determined by the payroll expense by zone.

  • New York - Increased the Zone 1 maximum Metropolitan Commuter Transportation Mobility Tax rate from 0.6% to 0.895%, effective 7-1-25. The following counties are affected:

  • New York 33-061-0000

  • Dutchess 33-027-0000

  • Nassau 33-059-0000

  • Orange 33-071-0000

  • Putnam 33-079-0000

  • Rockland 33-087-0000

PrismHR now supports the production of a Form W-2 for railroad employees

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202510/Railroad%20Reporting%20Update.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202510/Railroad Reporting Update.htm

PrismHR now supports the production of a Form W-2 for railroad employees

Railroad employers use Form W-2 to report wage payments to employees and to SSA. RRTA taxes are shown on the employee Form W-2 in Box 14, Boxes 3, 4, 5, 6 and 7, relating to FICA and Medicare, should be blank. When an employee is covered under the RRTA and has payroll processed in PrismHR as a railraod employee, the FormW-2 created for the employee will now include the required information in Box 14. To support the required W-3 reporting requirements for Railroad employers, an employee cannot be both an employee covered under the RRTA AND FICA within the same employer. Additionally, we suggest a railroad employer should not have both FICA and RRTA employees.

If your employer has both types of employees, you will need to manually review and adjust the Form W-3 which will by default combine these types of employees. If an employee who has both FICA tax codes (00-11 or 00-15) and Railroad tax codes (00-60, 00-62 or 00-64) for the same tax year:

  • The system will not generate a Form W-2 for that employee for that tax year. The Error Report will include this issue stating Employee has W2 and Railroad taxes. The “NO FORM GENERATED” column will indicate “Y”.

  • In the W-3 Totals Report, the W3 data will need to be adjusted to exclude the railroad wages if an employer has FICA and RRTA employees.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202401/CMP-Fixes%20Jan-2024%20MR.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202401/CMP-Fixes Jan-2024 MR.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the January 2024 monthly release.

JIRA Number Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-5374 Previously, the overtime exemption for the state of Alabama in PrismHR was based on charge date. Now, the overtime exemption for the state of Alabama in PrismHR is based on pay date regardless of when the hours were worked.
CMP-5361 Previously, when an employee working in the state of Alabama had sheltered and exempt earnings that were greater than their taxable earnings, in some scenarios we saw the exempt and sheltered earnings exceeding the total wages on the voucher. When this happened, we also saw negative taxable wages and negative over-limit wages. The calculated tax amount remained 0.00. Now, when an employee working in the state of Alabama has taxable earnings that are less than the exempt overtime amount, the exempt amount is capped at the taxable wages. PrismHR will not display negative taxable wages or negative overlimit wages.
CMP-5329 Previously, for an employee who lives and works only in the state of Ohio, and the Form W-2 reported only Ohio wages, the EES (CIC) download incorrectly displayed PA in positions 1084-1085. Now, for an employee who lives and works only in the state of Ohio, and the Form W-2 reports only Ohio wages, the EES (CIC) download correctly displays OH in positions 1084-1085.
CMP-5253 Previously, the matching 401(k) contribution from the employer was not included in the taxable earnings listed on the employee’s voucher and was not included in the tax calculation for employees working in Oregon Tri-Met district and Lane County mass transit district. This is fixed. The matching 401(k) contribution from the employer is included in the taxable earnings listed on the employee’s voucher and is included in the tax calculation for employees working in Oregon Tri-Met district and Lane County mass transit district.
CMP-4746 Previously, for the Colorado Occupational Privilege Tax, the system incorrectly reported the gross taxable over the limit in box 18-20 on Form W-2 for SBEA clients. Now, for the Colorado Occupational Privilege Tax, the system correctly reports the gross taxable up to the wage limit in box 18-20 on Form W-2 for SBEA clients.
CMP-4733 Previously, on the local EFW2 download report in PrismHR, the report was generating a tax type R instead of C for Philadelphia local tax codes even when the tax type was set to local tax authority, a EFW2 code was entered, and a city code was set on the tax authority ID. The download file also generated 00 instead of 42 in positions 3 and 4 on the RS line. This is resolved. Now, for Philadelphia, PrismHR now generates a tax type C for all local tax codes on the local EFW2 download report. The download file also generates 42 instead of 00 in positions 3 and 4 on the RS line.
CMP-3278 Previously, when a memo pay code was set to a Labor Union, the memo pay code displayed as part of Gross Earnings which could imply the memo pay code is taxable. > Note: Note: This did not affect taxation of the pay, only the display of the gross earnings amount. Now, memo pay codes tied to labor unions are not included in the display for Gross Earnings.

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the February 2024 monthly release.

JIRA Number Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-5418 Previously, for a non-resident employee working in the state of Alabama, when using FLSA Ruleset, Overtime reported separately and hours worked in Alabama are over 40, the premium pay was not being flagged as exempt. Now, for any employee working over 40 hours in the state of Alabama, when using FLSA Ruleset, Overtime reported separately, the premium pay for Alabama overtime hours will also be exempt from Alabama state income tax regardless of the employee’s resident state.
CMP-5409 Previously, when printing multipage Form W-2s from the Employee Portal, the last page of the Form W-2s did not print the employer’s name and address in Box C. Now, when printing multipage Form W-2s from the Employee Portal, all pages of the Form W-2s correctly print the employer’s name and address in Box C.
CMP-5397 Previously, in some scenarios PrismHR faced a rounding issue when calculating overtime exemption for the state of Alabama. It also displayed a negative value in the Taxable Over Limit column on the employee voucher which also flowed into PTS. Now, PrismHR correctly calculates the new attributes for overtime calculation for the state of Alabama.
CMP-5389 Previously, if an employee had work week hours in the state of Alabama and lived in a non-taxing state such as Florida, PrismHR incorrectly combined the hours worked in those non-taxing states calculate the total work week hours for the state of Alabama. Now, if an employee has work week hours in the state of Alabama and is a resident of a non-taxing state that does not impose state withholding for example Florida, then PrismHR will not include any hours worked in those non-taxing states to calculate the total work week hours for the state of Alabama.
CMP-5386 Previously, payroll calculation failed in PrismHR if an ASO client redirected employee to employee or employer to employer taxes. Now, PrismHR allows an ASO client to redirect employee to employee or employer to employer taxes.
CMP-5384 Previously, when building W2 data on the Client Federal Entity Register for SBEA Employers, if an employee had worked under more than one employer in the state of New York for the tax year, PrismHR incorrectly added all Box 1 wages across each of the employer’s W-2s and reported them as NY wages on the Form W-2 in Box 16, which could overstate Box 6 NY state wages. Now, when building W2 data on the Client Federal Entity Register for SBEA Employers, when an employee has worked under more than one employer in the state of New York for the tax year, PrismHR displays the box 16 wage amount for the reporting employer which matches the Box 1 wage amount on the Form W-2.
CMP-5073 Previously, when completing a tax adjustment, with the flag “Adjust Client Tax Register” checked, Tax Identifier code (-37) did not update in the client tax register. It still displayed on the employer tax register. Now, when completing a tax adjustment, if the flag “Adjust Client Tax Register” is checked for Tax Identifier code (-37), it correctly updates in the client tax register.
CMP-4763 Previously, the Local EFW2 file for Lancaster County, PA generated by PrismHR displayed the tax authority name in positions 338-343 of the RS record instead of the employee’s resident PSD code. Now, the Local EFW2 file for Lancaster County, PA generated by PrismHR displays the full 6 digit PSD code in positions 338-343 of the RS record.

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the October 2024 monthly release.

JIRA Number Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-6080 Previously, PrismHR ignored the selections made under the Special Rules section on the Tax tab of the Employee Details form while calculating the Multnomah County Tax and the Portland Metro Tax. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-5995 Previously, on the MasterTax RTS: - The 500 records for tax codes 38-40 and 38-41 incorrectly included the sheltered amounts in positions 123-136 and 137-150 respectively and - The 601 record for tax code 38-24 (OR PMFL) incorrectly included the exempt amount in positions 428 - 441. Now, on the MasterTax RTS: - The 500 records for tax codes 38-40 and 38-41 will report: - QTD Gross Taxable Wages in positions 123-136 and - YTD Gross Taxable wages in positions 137 - 150. - The 601 record for tax code 38-24 (OR PMFL) will report: - Gross Taxable Wages for OR PFML in positions 428 - 441.
  • The 500 records for tax codes 38-40 and 38-41 incorrectly included the sheltered amounts in positions 123-136 and 137-150 respectively and
  • The 601 record for tax code 38-24 (OR PMFL) incorrectly included the exempt amount in positions 428 - 441.
  • The 500 records for tax codes 38-40 and 38-41 will report:
  • QTD Gross Taxable Wages in positions 123-136 and
  • YTD Gross Taxable wages in positions 137 - 150.
  • The 601 record for tax code 38-24 (OR PMFL) will report:
  • Gross Taxable Wages for OR PFML in positions 428 - 441. | CMP-5792 | Previously, for Washington Labor & Industries , the 211 record on the MasterTax PTS file displayed two separate values for tax codes 48-23 (Employee) and 48-26 (Employer) which is incorrect. | Now, for Washington Labor & Industries , for tax codes 48-23 (Employee) and 48-26 (Employer), the 211 record on the MasterTax PTS file displays the composite rate WA0000-150 (gross rate) code in positions 50-57. | | CMP-5706 | Previously, the Quarterly Tax Export .csv file incorrectly reported Y on columns P, Q & R when the employee did not have taxable wages for a tax code for a pay period that did not include the 12 of the month. | Now, the Quarterly Tax Export .csv file reports Y on columns P, Q & R when the employee only has taxable wages for a tax code for a pay period that includes the 12 of the month. | | CMP-5639 | Previously, NY MTA- 305 client records incorrectly reported individual employee counts by client in the C record when the state requested total employee count by PEO. | Now, the NY MTA 305 client records report 0 employee count by client with the total employee count reported by PEO in the C record. | | CMP-5513 | Previously, the Employer Quarterly SUTA Tax Export for West Virginia did not include the employee Job Title, SOC Code, and County of Employment as required on the S record. | Now, the Employer Quarterly SUTA Tax Export for West Virginia includes the employee Job Title, SOC Code, and County of Employment as required on the S record. | | CMP-4506 | Previously, the New Hire Reporting file within PrismHR did not match the required New Hampshire new hire record specifications. The CSV format did not support the record layout information mentioned on the NH employment security services portal. | Now, this is fixed. | ========================================================================

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202412/CMP-Fixes%20Dec-2024.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202412/CMP-Fixes Dec-2024.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the December 2024 monthly release.

JIRA Number Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-6225 Previously, if a W-2 employee had a line 2 in their Resident Address but no line 2 in their Mailing Address, then the EES W2 Export was incorrectly combining the line 2 in their Resident Address as line 2 in their Mailing Address. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-6211 Previously, when cash wages such as Fringe Vacation or Holiday were also reported in the Fringe Summary the Net Wages Paid for the pay period did not display correctly on the Certified Payroll Report. Now, when cash wages such as Fringe Vacation or Holiday are also reported in the Fringe Summary the Net Wages Paid for the pay period matches the Net Voucher Amount on the Certified Payroll Report unless the Allocate Deductions/Taxes by Project field is checked on the Certified Payroll Report Format Parameters form.
CMP-6198 Previously, the EES Puerto Rico W-2 Export file had the Carriage Return at position 1600. Now, the EES Puerto Rico W-2 Export file has 1600 positions for all records with the carriage return at position 1601.
CMP-5744 Previously, when a Labor Union Affiliation code was assigned to the Employee Details form but no Union Code Override existed for any of the positions set on the client on the Positions form, then a change to the Union Deduction Codes on the Labor Union form did not correctly update the details on the Recurring Deduction form without saving the Employee Details record. Now, when a Labor Union Affiliation code is assigned to the Employee Details form but no Union Code Override exists for any of the positions set on the client on the Positions form, then a change to the Union Deduction Codes on the Labor Union form will correctly update the details on the Recurring Deduction form without saving the Employee Details record.
CMP-5632 Previously, for both ASO and PEO clients, for tax code 22-20 when the tax basis was employer, the MasterTax RTS file incorrectly showed zero for the client 500 and 501 records. Now, for both ASO and PEO clients, for tax code 22-20 when the tax basis is employer, the MasterTax RTS file does not show zero for the client 500 and 501 records.
CMP-5314 Previously, when an employee had a worksite location which is a remote location and had hours worked in a separate location which is not remote through either pay allocations or detailed timesheet entry, the wages earned were incorrectly taxed in the resident location only. Now, when an employee has a worksite location which is a remote location and has hours worked in a separate location which is not remote through either pay allocations or detailed timesheet entry, the wages earned are incorrectly taxed in the respective locations.
CMP-4990 Previously, for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients, when a 1099 contractor had federal or state income tax withheld, the W2 build process was picking up this 1099 contractor and reported the federal and state wages on a Form W-2. This meant that the W-2 Detail Report and the Form W-3 Totals Report also included this 1099 contractor which was incorrect. Now, when custom feature code 1099WITHHOLDING is set for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients, when a 1099 contractor has federal or state income tax withheld, the W2 build process will not pick up this 1099 contractor. The W-2 Detail Report and the Form W-3 Totals Report will not have such 1099 contractors.
CMP-4809 Previously, when an employee lived in Oregon and worked in another state and the OR Transit Tax (tax code 38-27) or the Multnomah County Income Tax (tax code 38051-30), was set to Calculate/Report at the Client Level (PEOs Only), on the Tax Deductions form, then the tax deduction code on the voucher was reported to the ER (tax basis, P) instead of the Client (tax basis, C). Now, when an employee lives in Oregon and works in another state and the OR Transit Tax (tax code 38-27) or the Multnomah County Income Tax (tax code 38051-30), is set to Calculate/Report at the Client Level (PEOs Only), on the Tax Deductions form, then the tax deduction code on the voucher is reported to the Client (tax basis, C).

Other Fixes

The following are some other issues that we’ve fixed in the December 2024 monthly release.

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
WSP-939 Previously, for the state of Ohio, on the Employer Quarterly SUTA Tax Export for PEO reported taxes or an ASO and on the Quarterly Tax Processing / Government Exports / Ohio export for Client reported taxes, the Adjustment Reason Code in the S Records in positions 248 - 249 were missing. Now, for the state of Ohio, on the Employer Quarterly SUTA Tax Export for PEO reported taxes or an ASO and on the Quarterly Tax Processing / Government Exports / Ohio export for Client reported taxes, the Adjustment Reason Code in the S Records in positions 248 - 249 contain zeros.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/QR202403/CMP-Fixes%20Mar-2024%20QR.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/QR202403/CMP-Fixes Mar-2024 QR.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the March 2024 quarterly release.

JIRA Number Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-4921 Previously, when generating the CA Pay Data using the Build EEO-1 & Pay Data form, if under the Build Options, the Employee Filter field is set to “Paid more than $0 during the reporting period”, the system incorrectly showed Y for California for employees who had CA SUTA in a previous reporting year also. Now, when generating the CA Pay Data using the Build EEO-1 & Pay Data form, if under the Build Options, the Employee Filter field is set to “Paid more than $0 during the reporting period”, the system correctly displays Y for California for the employee only if the employee has CA SUTA for the current reporting period.
CMP-3101 Previously, the Daily Tax Export download did not display the Subject Wages, QTD Wages, QTD Subject Wages, QTD Taxable Wages, QTD Tax Amount, YTD Wages, YTD Subject Wages, YTD Taxable Wages and YTD Tax Amount for school district tax. Now, the Daily Tax Export download correctly displays the Subject Wages, QTD Wages, QTD Subject Wages, QTD Taxable Wages, QTD Tax Amount, YTD Wages, YTD Subject Wages, YTD Taxable Wages and YTD Tax Amount for school district tax.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/QR202406/CMP-Fixes%20Jun-2024%20QR.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/QR202406/CMP-Fixes Jun-2024 QR.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the June 2024 quarterly release.

JIRA Number Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-5644 Previously, when the employee tax for the Paid Family and Medical Leave tax for the state of Colorado (tax code 06-40) or Oregon (tax code 38-40) or Washington (48-40) was redirected to a different tax code (say 06-22) for Colorado or (say 38-22) for Oregon or (say 48-22) for Washington, the taxable wage limit was not honored after the tax limit was met. Now, when the employee tax for the Paid Family and Medical Leave tax for the state of Colorado or Oregon or Washington is redirected to tax code ending with -22, the taxable wage limit is honored after the tax limit is met. > Note: Note: Resolution to support all redirect tax codes is currently in progress and will be released as soon as possible.
CMP-5638 Previously, the system did not always correctly calculated the Alabama overtime exempt earnings amount when an employee had worked over 40 hours and multiple pay codes were used. Now, when using multiple pay codes for regular rate over 40 hours, the exempt amounts will calculate a blended rate.
CMP-4939 Previously, if an employee was enrolled in a benefit plan having Medical class that was used for a plan that was not a medical plan such as accident, the system incorrectly calculated the taxable wages for Modified Business Tax (tax code 29-41) for the state of Nevada. Now, the system correctly calculates the NV MBT 29-41 taxable wages as gross wages less employer contributions to pretax deductions (medical, dental, vision). Any benefit plans with a class of medical that are not for a medical plan and flagged as “Do Not Include in ACA Reporting” will not be included in the calculation.
CMP-3387 CMP-5592 Previously, on the Tax tab of the Employee Details form, when an employee under the Federal Tax Filing section had a value in the Other Income field and a large Voluntary Deduction or Retirement Flat amount in the Recurring Deductions form, the system presented a payroll error and the payroll would not process. Now, this is fixed.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/QR202409/CMP-Fixes%20Sep-2024.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/QR202409/CMP-Fixes Sep-2024.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the September 2024 quarterly release.

JIRA Number Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-5908 Previously, for SC SUTA Quarterly Export, positions 320-321 in the RE record did not display the two-digit last month of the quarter. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-5866 Previously, when an employee was working for two clients with the same non-CPEO employer, and had additional medicare wages in one of the clients but not the other, the Quarterly Tax Summary displayed Additional Medicare wages and tax for the client without T2 Medicare. Additionally, a credit for the T2 Medicare tax was shown in the ‘Adjustment for fraction of cents’. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-5860 Previously, any change made to the Client Details form would uncheck the Enable Remote Verification for this Location field under Other Parameters section on the Worksite Locations form for the client. This is resolved. Now only if you uncheck the Enable E-Verification? field in the Process Controls section under the Control tab of the Client Details form, then it will uncheck the Enable Remote Verification for this Location field under the Other Parameters section on the Worksite Locations form for the client.
CMP-5270 Previously, when the Additional Medicare Calc Method field was checked on the MasterTax Interface Parameters form, if an employee had additional medicare wages and a negative tax adjustment was entered, the 941 Quarterly Report did not update line 5d (Taxable wages and tips subject to Additional Medicare Tax). Now, this is fixed.
CMP-5019 Previously, when and employee worked for two clients under the same employer with Additional Medicare Calc Method selected on the MasterTax Interface Parameters form, and had over $200k in taxable wages under only one client, the Quarterly Tax Export incorrectly showed a negative value for 00-11ADD that did not have T2 Mdicare. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-2964 Previously, on the Quarterly Tax Summary form, the additional Medicare Tier 2 tax amount incorrectly populated to the Adjustment for fraction of cents field instead of the Wages subject to additional Medicare tax or the Calculate additional Medicare tax due fields. Now, this is fixed.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/QR202411/CMP-Fixes%20Nov-2024.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/QR202411/CMP-Fixes Nov-2024.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the November 2024 quarterly release.

JIRA Number Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-6099 Previously, the system incorrectly reported taxable wages entered for Third Party Sick Pay and Tax Adjustments in T2 Medicare for employees with less than $200K in taxable wages. Now, the system does not report taxable wages entered for Third Party Sick Pay and Tax Adjustments in T2 Medicare for employees with less than $200K in taxable wages.
CMP-5656 Previously, when a client did not have a client level PTO Benefit Plan, the Global PTO Auto Enroll Payroll Batch Report did not include the employees for the client even though the Global PTO Plan Auto Enroll & Accrue field is selected for that client under the Other tab on the Client Details form. Now, even if a client does not have any client level PTO Benefit Plan, the Global PTO Auto Enroll Payroll Batch Report will include the employees for the client when the Global PTO Plan Auto Enroll & Accrue field is selected for that client under the Other tab on the Client Details form.
CMP-5529 Previously, when all the report parameters like Gender, Ethnicity and Employee Address (two lines) were selected for inclusion on the Certified Payroll Report Format Parameters form, then the CSV version of the Certified Payroll Report did not display the check number for that payroll for the employee. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-5420 Previously, on the Create Employee W-2 Forms form, under the Options section, if Suppress Third Party Sick Pay field was selected for an employee, and any Taxable Sick Pay adjustment was entered for that employee, but no income tax was withheld on the Third Party Sick Pay Adjustment form, then the Taxable Sick Pay amount did not get suppressed on the employee Form W-2. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-5391 Previously, both for SBEA and non-SBEA clients, the Employee W-2 Box Report did not display the Box c Employer Name. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-5323 Previously, when an S-Corp employee changed employers within a selected benefit tax adjustment year, the system did not account for vouchers under the previous employers during that benefit tax adjustment year. Now, this is fixed, and the system will calculate adjustments based on all vouchers related to all employers for the employee during that benefit tax adjustment year.
CMP-5317 Previously, on the State Rules form, if SUTA is PEO Based and Client SUTA Report Only was selected, then the MasterTax PTS did not report the 210 CR record unless a Client SUTA rate was added. Now, on the State Rules form, if SUTA is PEO Based and Client SUTA Report Only is selected, then the MasterTax PTS will report the 210 CR record even if a Client SUTA rate was not added since the accrual rate follows the Employer Tax Rate.
CMP-5259 Previously, for both SBEA and non-SBEA employers in the state of Nevada, the MasterTax RTS file under 601 record did not report the tips under tax code 29-24 in position 100-113. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-5075 Previously, when running the 941 Quarterly Report for a client with multiple employers, the report did not produce results based on the employer ID entered. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-3506 Previously, when an employee had a Form W-2 that was created manually, then the physical Form W-2 did not print the employee name in Box E as required. Now, this is fixed.

Other Fixes

The following are some other issues that we’ve fixed in the November 2024 quarterly release.

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
WSP-945 WSP-849 Previously, the EES W-2 Export for any year incorrectly reported the Common Pay Agent set for the current year, instead of the Common Pay Agent set for the reporting year. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-941 Previously, on the 1094C Report Download form, when you hovered over the checkbox beside the Generate All Clients field, the screen incorrectly displayed a No symbol. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-867 Previously, on the Create Employee W-2 Forms form, PrismHR did not generate an error report if an employee had a negative OASDI tax (tax code 00-12) for that tax year. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-866 Previously, the BDS/SOLV W-2 Export for any year incorrectly reported the Common Pay Agent set for the current year, instead of the Common Pay Agent set for the reporting year. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-851 Previously, the EES Virgin Islands W-2 Export for any year incorrectly reported the Common Pay Agent set for the current year, instead of the Common Pay Agent set for the reporting year. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-850 Previously, the EES Puerto Rico W-2 Export for any year incorrectly reported the Common Pay Agent set for the current year, instead of the Common Pay Agent set for the reporting year. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-783 Previously, the W-2C Box Report in PrismHR did not populate any data if an employee had a Form W-2c in the system for that tax year. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-709 Previously, when the Custom Feature Code ALLOW999SSNS was not enabled, then on the New Hire Form and for the New Employee Imports form, if you entered an SSN or an ITIN having any number between 50-65 on the 4th and 5th positions, you received an error. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-622 Previously, when income tax withholding was enabled for a 1099 contractor both on the Client Details form under the Tax tab, and also on the State Rules form under the State Tax Parameters section, and taxes were suppressed on the Client Details form and/or on the Tax Calculation Overrides form for the 1099 contractor, PrismHR still did not suppress either the federal or the individual state income tax. Now, this is fixed.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/MR202501/CMP-Fixes%20Jan-2025.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/MR202501/CMP-Fixes Jan-2025.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the January 2025 monthly release.

JIRA Number Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-6258 Previously, when an employee had AL OT Exempt wages and a zero Exempt Pay for a different state income tax, then on the Form W-2 for the employee, Box 14 was blank. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-6232 Previously, the Work Out of State Flag for PA changed after a tax deduction was processed resulting in incorrect tax files for MasterTax RTS. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-6191 Previously, when a tax adjustment was created for an ASO client for an employee-paid tax code with the Calculate/Report at Client Level (PEO’s Only) field checked on the Tax Deductions form, the tax was incorrectly reported with a ‘C’ Tax Basis on the employee payroll voucher. Now, when a tax adjustment is created for an ASO client for an employee-paid tax code with the Calculate/Report at Client Level (PEO’s Only) field checked on the Tax Deductions form, the tax is correctly reported with a ‘P’ Tax Basis on the employee payroll voucher.
CMP-6181 Previously, if for an employee a large amount was entered on the Other Income field under the Tax tab on the Employee Details form, the payroll calculation for that employee failed with an incorrect error message stating Insufficient cash earnings to pay taxes. Now, if for an employee a large amount was entered on the Other Income field under the Tax tab on the Employee Details form, the payroll process reduces the federal income tax withholding on the payroll to the precise amount necessary to reduce the employee’s net pay to “0” and processes the payroll for that employee without error.
CMP-6173 Previously, the Employer Quarterly SUTA Tax Export file for Colorado was missing the 0 or 1 indicator in the S records, positions 212, 213, and 214 indicating if the employee worked in a pay period that included the 12th of the applicable month during the quarter. Now, the Employer Quarterly SUTA Tax Export file for Colorado will report a 0 or 1 in the S records, positions 212, 213, and 214 indicating if the employee worked in a pay period that included the 12th of the applicable month during the quarter.
CMP-6079 Previously, when a client had payrolls under more than one employer, and you had allowed a particular client access to the Quarterly Tax Summary form, then it only reported the wages under the Employer ID assigned to that particular client. Now, when a client has payrolls under more than one employer, the Quarterly Tax Summary form will display the totals for the client as a whole including all Employer IDs.
CMP-5674 Previously, the Record ID in the ACA transmission file for each transmission was not in sync with the corresponding Federal Transmission Information on the Edit Employee 1095 Form for that employee. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-4147 Previously, when the employee portion of WA PFML (tax code 48-40) was redirected to the employer, the MasterTax RTS file did not accurately report the Weeks Worked and Hours Worked. Now, this fixed.

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the February 2025 monthly release.

CMP-6325 Previously, when an employee had CO, OR, or WA PFML (tax codes 06-40, 38-40 or 48-40), redirected to tax codes 06-22, 38-22, or 48-22 for a private plan the tax amount was incorrectly populated in Box 14 on the Form W-2 for both SBEA or non-SBEA clients. CMP-6324 Previously, when using a Common Pay Agent, the RE record on the EFW2 files for federal and states was incorrect. Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/QR202503/CMP-Fixes%20Mar-2025.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/QR202503/CMP-Fixes Mar-2025.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the March 2025 quarterly release.

JIRA Number Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-6453 Previously, in some scenarios, for the state of Iowa, the system was not calculating the income tax correctly. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-6404 Previously, for the state of Maryland, the EFW2 RV record positions 197-208 from the second record onwards were overstated as it reported the running total of the employers’ tax due amount instead of the tax due amount for that employer only which that line corresponded to. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-6336 Previously, the EES W-2 Export did not apply the prior year record for reporting Common Pay Agent which resulted in the Form W-2 PDF not matching the EES download for current tax year if there was a change in the Common Pay Agent data for the current year. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-6270 Previously, when the employer paid NY SDI tax code 33-25 was suppressed using the Tax tab on Client Details form, the system incorrectly also suppressed the employee paid NY SDI tax code 33-21 even though it was set up to calculate. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-5822 Previously, the system did not allow local tax code 18037-44 to report at the client level (Tax Basis of C) with any current overrides. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-5669 Previously, in some scenarios the system was not reporting the New York Metropolitan Commuter Transportation Mobility Tax correctly. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-5421 Previously, the EEO-1 Export Data included transferred employees of the client who were not active for the client during the reporting period. Now, this is fixed. This fix will be applied when the custom feature code EEOENHANCE is added to the System Parameters form.
CMP-4727 Previously, when for the state of CO, DE, ME, OR or WA an override rate for PFML was entered either on the Employer Tax Rates (SUTA) or the State Tax Rates (SUTA) form, the State Misc3 Rate (Employer contribution) and State Misc 3 Employee Rate (employee contribution) did not populate correctly in the PTS file on the 210 records in positions 71-76. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-2014 Previously, a negative garnishment amount could occur when the Student Loan Type was selected as Apply Federal Limits Minus Medical with percentage was applied to a Student Loan Garnishment. Now, a Student Loan Garnishment will not have a negative deduction amount.
CMP-412 Previously, on the Employee Details form and the New Hire form, a Native American Tribal document required an expiration date. Now, it does not.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/R_202504/CMP-Fixes%20Apr-2025.htm Path: CMP/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/R_202504/CMP-Fixes Apr-2025.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we try to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed in the April 2025 release.

JIRA Number Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-6487 Previously, when a Union was associated with certified payroll, in the Form WH-347 and Certified Payroll Report, the system did not accurately calculate the Project Totals. Additionally, the Project Totals were miscalculated when multiple positions with unions were included on the same payroll voucher. Now, when using Position based Unions with certified payroll reporting, the Project Total reflects all cash pay codes and fringe benefit pay codes as part of the Project Total pay for that Project and Position combination. The Project Total separates out the pay based on the different Project and Position combinations.
CMP-6478 Previously, using the Create Employee W-2 Forms form, when you ran the build Form W-2 process for an employee, the Form W-2 build process deleted all existing Form W-2s built for all employees for that employer. Now, using the Create Employee W-2 Forms form, when you run the build Form W-2 process for selected employees, the Form W-2 build process will delete the existing Form W-2s which were built for only those selected employees for that employer. > Note: Note: This was released as a hotfix on March 19, 2025.
CMP-6405 Previously, when an employee completed their LA state tax form through Onboarding or Employee Portal, the elections were not displaying under the Tax tab on the Employee Details form for the employee. Now, this is resolved.
CMP-5960 Previously, the CSV output of the Certified Payroll Report displayed only four Fringe Pay Codes even if more than four Fringe Pay Codes were displayed on the PDF output. Now, the CSV output of the Certified Payroll Report displays the same number of Fringe Pay Codes as displayed on the PDF output.
CMP-5312 CMP-6477 Previously, when an employee had a child support garnishment and a pretax deduction exceeding the gross pay, the system did not follow the Maximum Percent of Disposable Pay calculation for that state as per the State Garnishment Rules form. Now, when an employee has a child support garnishment and a pretax deduction exceeding the gross pay, the system does not stop payroll but provides a soft warning stating Warning: has a garnishment that should be reviewed. There are insufficient cash earnings to calculate all deductions on Voucher# . An adjustment may be needed.
CMP-5031 Previously, when an employee had a state tax levy garnishment set as a flat amount, during payroll calculation, the system did not follow the limits set on the State Tax Levy Maximum Percent of Gross Pay/Disposable Pay field on the State Garnishment Rules form for that state. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-3507 Previously, for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients, the Form W-2c listed a correction to the locality when two localities with the same name appeared on the Form W-2 even if a change was not made to the locality. Now, for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients, the Form W-2c does not list a correction to the locality when two localities with the same name appear on the Form W-2 unless a change was made to the locality.

Other Fixes

The following are some other issues that we’ve fixed in the April 2025 release.

WSP-1687 Previously, you were able to access the Change Reason History form from the navigation menus, which did not allow them to indicate the client/state/employer record in the displayed form. Now, the Change Reason History form no longer displays on the navigation menus, so you can only access this form by selecting it on the Actions menu in the Client Details, Employer Details, and State Rules forms, where the client/employer/state record already displays.
WSP-1752 Previously, the Change Reason History form could be added to Favorites which was incorrect. Now, the Change Reason History form cannot be added to Favorites.

CMP-6540 Previously, when the Form W2C only had a change relating to the state or local values, a blank record for that employee appeared on the EFW2C download. This caused the total record to be wrong and employer information to be repeated in the file. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-6472 Previously, when the Certified Payroll Report was generated for multiple projects, the Project OT rate did not display correctly for all the projects. Now, the Project OT rate displayed on the Certified Payroll Reports (both PDF and CSV formats) will reflect the correct Project OT rate from the corresponding Certified project, ensuring no Project OT rates from other projects are included.
CMP-6468 Previously, for the state of Iowa (tax code 61-24) that consider the Employer HSA match as taxable for SUTA, the taxable billing did not reflect the employer HSA contribution. Now, on employee payroll vouchers, when the employer HSA contributions are taxable, both the taxable accrued and the taxable billing sections reflect the employer HSA contributions in the taxable earnings and the tax amounts.
CMP-6454 Previously, when a pay group was deleted that had payroll activity in the same year, then the annual average number of employees in the OSHA300A report was inflated. CMP-6434 Previously, the net wages on the XML version of the Certified Payroll Report did not match its PDF version when an employee was paid with a Fringe Pay Code across two projects. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-6384 Previously, when using a pay code with the weighted average setup to be used for a pay period, if there were no other payroll hours other than the regular hours of pay to include in the weighted average, then the system incorrectly calculated the pay rate as zero. Now, if an employee is paid with the weighted average calculation method for a pay code and has no other payroll hours, then the pay rate will default to the employee’s regular hourly pay rate.
CMP-6294 Previously, for an employee working in a location that triggers GLOBAL PTO accrual, when an FLSA ruleset calculated HALF time or blended overtime rates, the GLOBAL PTO accrual did not pick up those hours. Now, for an employee working in a location that triggers GLOBAL PTO accrual, all pay codes that exist on the GLOBAL PTO Benefit plan (Included pay codes) are included in the accrual calculation, with or without FLSA ruleset calculations.
CMP-6243 Previously, the MasterTax RTS 601 record for CT0000-040 (CT PFML) positions 100 - 113 reported the Year-To-Date (YTD) earnings subject to CT PFML for the employee (EE) including earnings from subsequent quarters which was incorrect. Now, the MasterTax RTS 601 record for CT0000-040 (CT PFML) positions 100 - 113 reports the Year-To-Date (YTD) earnings subject to CT PFML for the employee (EE) as of the conclusion of the reporting quarter. It is important to note that this record will not account for any earnings from subsequent quarters.
CMP-6195 Previously, for both SBEA and non-SBEA employers in the state of Nevada, the MasterTax RTS file under 601 record did not report the tips under tax code 29-24 in position 100-113 for an ASO or any company with ER-reported NV SUTA. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-5286 Previously, even for an employee living in the state of New York, the tax code XXXXX-37 for NY Metro Commuter tax did not have a C tax basis when the Tax Authority was set to report on the Client. Now, this is fixed.

Upload Documents Using the Mastertax Bulk Import Tool

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/DM/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202403/MasterTaxBulkInput.htm Path: DM/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202403/MasterTaxBulkInput.htm

Upload Documents Using the Mastertax Bulk Import Tool

Users can now upload multiple Mastertax documents at once using the Bulk Import Tool. When documents are uploaded using this tool, formatted Mastertax Zip files can be processed in a batch, automatically inspected for errors, and reprocessed or rolled back from a single form.

What you Need

Before you begin, make sure you have:

  • Permissions to access the Bulk Upload tool. This tool requires specific permissions for each individual to use the tool, and cannot currently be added to a User Role. If you do not have the proper permissions, contact the administrator.

  • A Zip file from Mastertax containing the files you want to upload, and files containing the proper naming convention. For more information about the required formats, see the next section.

Correct Zip File Format

For the Bulk Import tool to read the documents in the Zip file correctly, the files must conform to certain naming conventions. Mastertax should already deliver the Zip file in the format below.

The name of the Zip file does not affect the upload, but the name will be used for the Description field for all the documents imported in that upload. For best practices, you should give the Zip file a name that describes the documents, such as “Q1 2024 Mastertax Upload” for first-quarter 2024 tax documents.

The naming convention of the tax files is very important for the files to be read correctly. Mastertax files should be named according to the following rules:

  • The document name must be in the following format: xxxxx_C1234_xxxxx.abc
  • The first and last sections of the document name (marked “xxxxx” above) can be any alphanumeric characters. They cannot contain spaces or special characters.
  • The client ID (marked “C1234” above) must first contain a “C” or an “E”, followed by the Client ID number.
  • The file extension (marked “.abc” above) can be any supported document type, such as pdf, doc, or txt.

For example, if the Client ID is 3245, the tax file should look like this: “Q12024_C3245_mastertax.pdf”.

How to Access the Bulk Import Tool

You can access the Bulk Import tool through Document Management.

To access the Bulk Import tool:

  1. Click [Image: screenshot] (Back Office).

  2. From Client|Change select Manage Documents. The Manage Documents form displays.

  3. Click the [Image: screenshot] (Bulk Import) icon. The Bulk Import form displays.

The Bulk Import Form

The Bulk Import form displays the status of past bulk imports, and can be used to add a new bulk import.

[Image: screenshot]

The following fields display on this form:

  • Bulk Import Name: Displays the name of the bulk import job.
  • Status: Displays the status of jobs that are Done, or jobs that have been Cancelled/Rolledback.
  • Started Date: Displays the time that the bulk import began.
  • Last Record Processed: Displays the time the bulk import completed.
  • Processed Percent: Displays the percent completion of the project as it is processed.
  • Total: Displays the total number of files contained in the Zip file.
  • Processed: Displays the number of files that were successfully processed.
  • Errors: If the system encountered errors during processing, the number of errors displays as a link. Click the link to display the Import Errors form, which displays each file that encountered an error and the source of the error.
  • Action: Using the Action buttons, you can roll back a completed bulk import or reprocess errors encountered during the import.

How to Perform a Bulk Import

To perform a bulk import:

  1. On the Bulk Import form, click Add Import. The New Bulk Import form displays.

  2. Enter a name for the import in the Bulk Import Name field. This name is used as a description for the import in the system.

  3. Select a category for the import in the Target Category field. The field only displays categories that you have permission to access.

  4. Click Select Zip File. A file selection form displays.

  5. Select the Zip file that has been prepared according to the formatting standards listed above.

  6. Click Start Bulk Import.

The bulk import begins processing, and the Bulk Import form displays, where you can review the status of the import.

How to Review and Reprocess Errors on a Bulk Import

When you run a bulk import, the system displays the total number of files to be imported, the number successfully processed, and the number of files that were not imported due to errors.

Note: Note: Errors due to mistakes in formatting, unsupported file types, or files that contain 0 bytes cannot be fixed directly using the reprocessing method. To fix these errors, you will need to make changes to the documents on the Zip file and redo the import.

To review errors on a bulk import:

  1. On the Bulk Import form, select the import that has processing errors.

  2. Select the link in the Errors field.

The Import Errors form displays.

Each file with a processing error displays on this form. The File Name field displays each file, and the Exception field displays the corresponding error message.

Bulk import errors can be fixed according to the type of error:

  • If the error indicates the user does not have access to the client, the user must obtain the proper permissions to access that Client ID.
  • If the error indicates the Client ID does not exist in the system, one of the documents is likely named incorrectly and must be renamed.
  • If the error indicates the file did not match the expected format, the document from the Zip file must be corrected.
  • If the error indicates the file type is not supported, the Zip file contains incompatible file types, which could not be processed.
  • If the error indicates that a system timeout or connectivity issue prevented the file from being imported properly, the file can be re-imported using the Reprocess button.

To reprocess a bulk import:

  1. On the Bulk Import form, select the import that has processing errors.

  2. Click Reprocess Errors.

The system attempts to reprocess files that returned errors. Any errors which remain after reprocessing are likely due to file formatting, file type, or permissions issues, and can be reviewed on the Import Errors form.

How to Roll Back a Bulk Import

If you need to undo a bulk import, you can roll back the documents.

To roll back a bulk import:

  1. On the Bulk Import form, select Rollback.

The Confirm Rollback button displays.

  1. Select Confirm Rollback.

The rollback commences, and all processed files from the import are removed from the system.

Enhancements to Advanced Search for Clients and Employees

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/DM/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202406/Active_Companies_By_Default.htm Path: DM/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202406/Active_Companies_By_Default.htm

Enhancements to Advanced Search for Clients and Employees

When a manager uses the Advanced Search form to search for clients or employees can now toggle between active and inactive clients or employees. By default, searches only apply to active records, improving the performance of the search.

The new Active Companies field can be used to switch between active companies and inactive companies.

The new Active Employees field can be used to switch between active, terminated, and on-leave employees.

Using these new fields, managers can perform searches for active records more quickly while retaining the ability to search for inactive records when needed.

Bulk Downloads in Document Management

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/DM/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202409/Bulk_Download_Tool.htm Path: DM/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202409/Bulk_Download_Tool.htm

Bulk Downloads in Document Management

Managers and Service Providers can now download documents in bulk using the Bulk Download process in Document Management. To download a large number of files, users can perform a bulk download to compress selected documents into a ZIP file, which can then be downloaded at any time from the new Bulk Download form.

To access bulk downloads, access the Manage Documents form. Select multiple documents and click the

[Image: screenshot]

(Download) icon to display the Confirm Download prompt, which informs the user that this download may take a significant time and offers the option to run the process in the background. Click Run in Background to perform the download and exit the prompt. The download progress displays on the

[Image: screenshot]

(Bulk Download) icon, and the user can continue performing other duties while the download processes. Once the download is complete, the Bulk Download icon displays a checkmark.

[Image: screenshot]

Click the

[Image: screenshot]

(Bulk Download) icon at any time to display the Bulk Downloads form. This form lists all bulk downloads performed by the current user, as well as the status, timestamps, processing percentage, size, errors, and available actions. Users can cancel a download that is currently in progress or click the Download button to download documents. The download link can also be shared with other users. In addition, the user can return to the Bulk Documents form at any time to redownload files.

If any errors occur during the download process, the Errors column displays a number as a link. Click this link to download a TSV file with a list of errors that occurred during the download.

Using this new process, managers and service providers can save time downloading large quantities and file sizes of documents and continue with their other duties while the download is processed.

JIRA # DM-999, DM-1002, DM-1003, DM-1005

Payroll Approval Form in Employee Portal

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/MR_202403/ADMP_Payroll_Approval.htm Path: EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/MR_202403/ADMP_Payroll_Approval.htm

Payroll Approval Form in Employee Portal

Managers can now use the Payroll Approval form to view, download, approve, or deny payrolls in Employee Portal. To access this form, select Payroll Approval from the menu while in Manager mode.

[Image: screenshot]

The Payroll Approval form displays a list of payrolls in Pending Client Approval status that are ready for review and approval. This form displays summary information for each payroll, including the number, description, pay date and type, and invoice amount. Using this form, the manager can view details on the payroll, approve it, or deny it.

Select Review Payroll to display the Payroll Summary form, where the manager can review more specific details for the payroll. The Payroll Summary section on this form shows additional information, such as the pay period and deduction period.

[Image: screenshot]

The Payroll Detail tab on the Payroll Summary form displays payment records for individual employees on the payroll. The Unpaid Employee Detail tab shows information about any employees who are marked as unpaid on the payroll. The Invoice tab shows a complete breakdown of payment amounts, taxes, and fees on the invoice. Information from each of these tabs can be downloaded as a CSV file by clicking the Download button.

Managers can approve a payroll by clicking the Approve button for the payroll on the Payroll Approval form, or by displaying the Payroll Summary form for a payroll and clicking the Approve button on the bottom of the screen. Managers can also deny the payroll using the same processes. If a manager denies a payroll, the Deny Payroll # form displays, where the manager must enter a reason to deny the payroll.

Note: Note: A manager only has access to approve or deny a payroll if they have access to all employees on the specific payroll. If the manager does not have access to one or more employees on a payroll, that payroll does not display on the manager’s Payroll Approval form. The employees a manager can access are determined by the Data Security settings for the client.

Note: Note: Invoices on the Invoice tab are sorted according to the sorting rules configured on the Billing tab of the Client Billing form in Prism.

JIRA # ADMP-39, ADMP-40, ADMP-161, ADMP-164, ADMP-170, ADMP-172, ADMP-177, ADMP-181, ADMP-182, ADMP-183, ADMP-195, ADMP-250, ADMP-252, ADMP-255, ADMP-264

Rehire Form in Employee Portal

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/MR_202403/ADMP_Rehire.htm Path: EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/MR_202403/ADMP_Rehire.htm

Rehire Form in Employee Portal

Managers can now use the Rehire form to rehire a previously terminated employee and return the employee to a normal work status. To access this form, select an employee on the My Employees form who has the Terminated Status. On the Employee Details form that displays, select HR Actions > Return to Work.

[Image: screenshot]

The Details panel on this form shows the status and the employment type. The History panel displays the history of the employee’s statuses, including the status type, reasons for changes, and effective dates. To rehire an employee, click the Start Rehire Process button. The Proposed Change section displays, where a manager can enter information for an employee’s rehiring.

[Image: screenshot]

The form is divided into sections, much like hiring an employee. In the Proposed Change section, the manager fills in the employee’s new status, employment type, rehire date, and reason, as well as selecting whether to use previous information for deductions, direct deposits, and benefits. In the Employment Details section, the manager fills in the employee’s new location, position, benefit groups, and organizational information such as department, division, or shift. In the Pay Details section, the manager fills in the employee’s new pay group, method, rate, and standard hours. In the Personal Information section, the manager fills in a personal email address, work email address, and mobile phone number for the employee, as well as confirming whether to use previous information for E-Verification, Onboarding, and Benefits Enrollment. If the New Hire process includes custom questions, these questions also appear on the Rehire form.

Once these fields are completed, click Save to return the employee to a work status.> Note: Note: All security for the Rehire form, including viewing an employee’s current pay rate in the form, follows the security set for the Rehire process ID on the User Roles form in Prism.

Using this form, managers can carry out the rehire process completely from Employee Portal to rehire previously terminated employees.

JIRA # ADMP-114, ADMP-124, ADMP-125, ADMP-126, ADMP-128, ADMP-129, ADMP-130, ADMP-131, ADMP-153

Total Compensation Form for Employee Portal

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/MR_202403/EP_Total_Compensation_Form.htm Path: EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/MR_202403/EP_Total_Compensation_Form.htm

Total Compensation Form for Employee Portal

The new Total Compensation form is now available for employees in Employee Portal. This form can be accessed by selecting Pay > Total Compensation. On this form, employees can select a year to view total compensation for that year and specify individual quarters to focus the results further.

[Image: screenshot]

The Overview tab contains an overview of all compensation, including the worth of the employee’s total compensation, their pay, their benefits contribution, and their taxes. The tab also includes a visualized breakdown of their compensation.

The Pay tab contains a breakdown of the employee’s pay. The visualization and table display the worth of the employee’s regular pay, as well as compensation such as holidays, PTO, and vacation. It also displays the total worth of any bonuses, such as incentives, referrals, or commissions.

The Benefits tab contains details on the employee’s benefit plans, displaying the contribution to each plan by both the employee and the company.

The Taxes tab contains details on taxes paid by both the employee and the company for the employee’s compensation. The visualization and tables show specific values for taxes paid, such as federal and state income, FICA, Medicare, etc.

Using this new form, employees can review detailed information about their total compensation from the employer for their financial records.

Time Sheet Entry in Employee Portal

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202406/ADMP_TimeSheetEntry.htm Path: EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202406/ADMP_TimeSheetEntry.htm

Time Sheet Entry in Employee Portal

Managers can now review, edit, and approve time sheets directly from Employee Portal using the new Time Sheets form. To access this form, select Time Sheets from the menu while in Manager mode.

[Image: screenshot]

The Time Sheets form displays a list of time sheets which are in progress and ready for review and approval. This form displays summary information about each time sheet, including the pay date, pay group, payroll type and number, the cutoff date, and status. Using this form, managers can view details of the time sheet and apply manual edits.

Select Start or Edit to display the Time Sheet Summary form, which displays information for each employee on the time sheet. Select View to review time sheets which have been submitted for calculation.

Manually Editing a Time Sheet

Using the Time Entry tab, managers can view details for each employee, including their pay rate, regular pay hours, overtime, PTO, and other details on the Time Entry tab. Managers can use the Leave Requests tab to apply leave to the time sheet and view leave that has been applied to the time sheet.

A blue dot next to the employee’s name indicates that additional entries are on the Pay Details Time Entry form.

A yellow triangle icon next to an employee’s name on the Summary Time Sheet indicates that there is a Leave Request for this employee that needs to be applied to the time sheet.

The Search field can be used to search for a specific employee by name or identifier. The Filter button can be used to narrow the list of employees based on Pay Method, Employment Type, Pay Group, Location, Department, Division, or FLSA status. Filters can be used together. For example, to see all part time employees in a specific department search by Department and Employment Type.

[Image: screenshot]

Time sheets can be edited directly from the Time Entry tab by clicking on specific cells. In addition, a manager can edit a specific employee’s time sheet record by selecting the employee name on the Time Entry tab to display the Pay Details form, where the employee’s time sheet record can be edited directly.

The Pay Details form is used to add time using different allocations, for example, if an employee worked at a different location. It is also used to add an entry for a Pay Code not shown on the Summary form.

[Image: screenshot]

Managers can lock specific employees by clicking on the

[Image: screenshot]

(Lock) icon. In addition, managers can view the Employee Details form for a specific employee by clicking on the

[Image: screenshot]

(Employee Details) icon.

Note: Note: If the time sheet record for an employee is locked, editing a cell on the Summary saving changes on the Pay Details form will unlock the record.

Applying Approved Leave to the Time Sheet

The Leave Requests tab displays approved leave requests that must be applied to the time sheet.

Note: Note: The Leave Requests tab does not display if there are no employees with leave that needs to be applied to their time sheet.

[Image: screenshot]

Click Apply Leave to apply the approved leave to the time sheet. Click Details to display the Leave Details form, where leave can be applied to the employee’s time sheet record. Managers can review the leave on this form to verify that the PTO has been allocated properly, then apply the leave to the time sheet.

[Image: screenshot]

The Leave Details form lists the leave dates, approved hours, and leave balance. The Adjusted Hours field defaults to the approved hours but can be changed to apply a different amount to the time sheet. If the Adjusted Hours field is changed, a comment must be added.

The Hours section displays the Current Hours and Updated Hours. The Current Hours is the amount currently on the time sheet for that leave code, and the Updated Hours show what will be on the time sheet when the Apply Leave button is clicked. Current Hours will only show if leave is set up with a Leave Offset Pay Code.

Pay Rate Changes and Time Sheets

If the employee has a pay rate change during the pay period covered by the time sheet, a warning message displays indicating that the time sheet must be corrected. This process must be done in the PrismHR software, and is not available for managers through Employee Portal at this time. Applying pay rate changes to time sheets will be added to Employee Portal in a future release.

Reviewing Details of a Time Sheet

Once edits to a time sheet are complete, click Review to access the Review tab, which displays summary information for the time sheet. Using this form, managers can review the gross pay and hours of the time sheet, as well as charts that break down the time sheet into elements such as Pay Codes, Departments, Locations, or Employment Types.

[Image: screenshot]

Click the View By field to change the graph to display different variables. In addition, click the Download button to download the time sheet as a CSV file.

If any employees on the time sheet have not been allocated pay, they display in the Unpaid Employees section. Managers should review this section and click Return to Time Sheet to make any necessary corrections before submitting the time sheet.

Once the time sheet is finalized, click Submit for Calculation to submit the time sheet for processing.

Note: Note: Once Submit for Calculation has been clicked changes can no longer be made, although the time sheet can still be viewed. To make any changes to the time sheet once it has been submitted for calculation, contact your Service Provider.

View Total Balance on PTO Summary

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202406/EP_PTO_Summary_Total_Balance.htm Path: EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202406/EP_PTO_Summary_Total_Balance.htm

View Total Balance on PTO Summary

The PTO Summary chart on the Paid Time Off form in Employee Portal now displays the total balance of all remaining PTO. In addition, it displays the Available value, which shows the total balance of all remaining PTO, taking into account any regulations that restrict the maximum PTO usage per year.

The Total Balance value is calculated according to Total Accrued + Carry Over – Planned – Taken.

The Available value is calculated according to Total Accrued + Carry Over – Planned – Taken, with a maximum cap according to regulations.

Employee Termination HR Action

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202406/EP_Termination_HR_Action.htm Path: EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202406/EP_Termination_HR_Action.htm

Employee Termination HR Action

Managers can now use the Termination form to terminate an employee’s position at the company. To access this form, select an employee on the My Employees form. On the Employee Details form that displays, select HR Actions > Termination.[Image: screenshot]

The Details panel on this form shows the status and type of the employee. The History panel displays the history of the employee’s status changes at the company.

[Image: screenshot]

To begin the termination process:

  1. On the Employee Details form for a selected employee, navigate to HR Actions > Termination.
  2. Click Terminate Employee. The Proposed Change section displays.
  3. Enter the Termination Status, Termination Date, Termination Reason, and Last Day Worked.
  4. In the Okay to Rehire? field, select if the employee is eligible for rehiring.
  5. Select whether to deactivate direct deposits in the Turn Off Direct Deposit (if Active) field.
  6. In the Reassign Pending Approvals field, select another employee. The terminated employee’s approvals queue will be reassigned to the selected employee.
  7. In the Termination Explanation field, add a reason for the employee’s termination to be added to the employee’s record.
  8. Review the Unpaid PTO section. This section displays any unpaid PTO for the employee, which is handled by state regulations.
  9. Click Save. The proposed change is added to the system to terminate the individual’s employment.

Using this new form, managers can conduct employee terminations directly through Employee Portal, as well as handle necessary steps to record the termination, deactivate direct deposits, and reassign approvals.

JIRA # EP-7398

My Approvals in HR Actions

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202409/HR_Actions_My_Approvals.htm Path: EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202409/HR_Actions_My_Approvals.htm

My Approvals in HR Actions

Managers can now access HR Action approvals from the My Approvals form in Employee Portal. Managers can review details for each request by clicking the Down Arrow icon and accept or deny the request directly from this form. Using the selection menu, managers can refine results to display specific approvals or categories.

In addition, the Approvals widget on the dashboard has been enhanced to display HR Action approvals. Managers can click the Review button to view details for each approval, as well as accept or deny the request from the dashboard.

The following HR Actions now display on the My Approvals form and the Approvals widget:

• Leave of Absence

• Return to Work

• Position Change

• Pay Rate Change

• Status Type Change

• Termination

• Rehire

Using this enhanced form and widget, managers can quickly review and make decisions for HR Actions that require approval.

Pay Rate Change on Time Sheet in Employee Portal

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202409/Pay_Rate_Change_EP.htm Path: EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202409/Pay_Rate_Change_EP.htm

Pay Rate Change on Time Sheet in Employee Portal

Managers can now approve time sheets that include a pay rate change using the Time Sheet Entry form in Employee Portal. When a time sheet includes a pay rate change that was made during the pay period, the manager can allocate hours on the time sheet to the appropriate pay rates.

To allocate hours on a time sheet with a pay rate change, select the Time Sheet Entry tab. If an employee has a pay rate change during the pay period, a yellow warning icon displays next to the employee’s name. Select the Pay Rate Change tab to review a list of all employees with pay rate changes during the pay period.

[Image: screenshot]

To allocate hours for each pay rate, click Allocate Hours on the corresponding row. The Allocate Hours form displays. On this form, enter the total number of hours for each pay rate. Once the hours are split between the two pay rates, click Apply Change, and the summary entry converts into two entries, one for each pay rate.

Using this new method, managers can easily allocate hours to account for pay rate changes directly from Employee Portal to make time sheet entries more efficient.

Time Sheet Import

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202409/Time_Sheet_Import.htm Path: EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202409/Time_Sheet_Import.htm

Time Sheet Import

Managers can now import time sheets in Employee Portal on the Time Sheets form. This method can be used for external timekeeping services or other means of logging time. To import a time sheet, select Time Sheets, then select Import. The Import Time Sheet form displays.

[Image: screenshot]

On this form, select an import template from the dropdown menu. After a template is selected, a text box listing requirements and notes displays, and a file can be selected for import. Valid file types include TXT and CSV files, and the file must be no more than 10MB in size. Once the file is uploaded, click Next.

The system processes the imported file immediately, and the information displays on the Review and Apply step. Review the information on this step to verify that the time sheet information is correct.

[Image: screenshot]

The Summary tab displays each line of the time sheet. The Warnings tab displays any warnings from the import, with a description of any errors from the file. If one or more warnings prevented the file from being imported completely, click the Restart button to redo the import process.

Once the time sheet is verified, click Import to import the time sheet. The Import Results step displays a summary of the file and any messages from the import. Managers can download the summary, warnings, or messages from the import using the corresponding buttons for record keeping.

JIRA # ADMP-2, ADMP-320, ADMP-322, ADMP-581, ADMP-585, ADMP-590

Trusted advisors do not have access to the Employee/Manager toggle, as they do not have access to the employee menus or widgets in Employee Portal.

Hide Employee Portal Navigation

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202411/Hide_EP_Features.htm Path: EP/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202411/Hide_EP_Features.htm

Hide Employee Portal Navigation

Administrators can now hide the header, navigation menu, and breadcrumbs for Employee Portal, allowing them to embed the EP application into their own application.

Administrators can configure a single sign-on URL with the new “?hideNavHeader=true” parameter to display an Employee Portal form without headers, navigation, or breadcrumbs.

For example, to access the Pay History form without a header, menu or breadcrumb, you could use a URL like “https://abc-ep.prismhr.com/uex/#/ess/pay-history?hideNavHeader=True”.
