Enhancements to Remote Verification for Form I-9

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/OBE/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202406/Remote_Verification_Enhancements.htm Path: OBE/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202406/Remote_Verification_Enhancements.htm

Enhancements to Remote Verification for Form I-9

The Remote Verification section of Form I-9 Section 2 has been enhanced with additional logic to determine that it displays under specific, proper circumstances. The section displays based on the combination of the Enable I-9 Remote Verification field on the Client Details form and the worksite location using the following logic:

  • If Enable I-9 Remote Verification is enabled and the Worksite Location field is set to Select or Enable, the Remote Verification section displays.
  • If Enable I-9 Remote Verification is enabled and the Worksite Location field is set to Disable, the Remote Verification section does not display.
  • If Enable I-9 Remote Verification is disabled and the Worksite Location field is set to Enable, the Remote Verification section displays.
  • If Enable I-9 Remote Verification is disabled and the Worksite Location field is set to Select or Disable, the Remote Verification section does not display.

ACA Life Event

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/OBE/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202409/ACA_Life_Event.htm Path: OBE/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR_202409/ACA_Life_Event.htm

ACA Life Event

Service providers can now use the new ACA life event to provide eligible employees with ACA benefits elections. By initiating this life event for an employee, the employee can enroll in selected ACA coverage options.

If an employee qualifies for ACA benefits based on their hours worked within a certain time period, the employees are added to a list of qualifying individuals. Service providers can view this list on the ACA Offered Employees form.

If the employee is not eligible for on-line benefits enrollment due to their employee type, service providers can still initiate the ACA life event for the employee as long as the employee is listed on the ACA Offered Employees table. This override is only available for the ACA life event.

Service providers can customize which coverage options appear on the ACA life event using the Life Event Maintenance form.

Benefits Enrollment In Spanish

Employees can now view the Benefits Enrollment workflow in Spanish as well as English, based on their preferred language. Employees can switch their preferred language using a new option on their account dropdown menu. When an employee selects Spanish as their preferred language, this choice is respected throughout the enrollment process.

Service providers can customize the Spanish text of the Benefits Enrollment workflow using the Workflow Library form. Selecting the Edit icon on the Process tab or the Forms and Documents tab displays an option to edit both the English label and the Spanish label.

Note: Note: All configuration options require an English text version, with the exception of supporting documents. Users can add supporting documents specifically for the Spanish language.

Note: Note: Employees only see the documents available for their preferred language. If a service provider has multiple supporting documents in English but only one in Spanish, Spanish users only see the single document. Service providers can upload the additional documents in the Spanish section as well as English to make them available to everyone, if necessary.

Aggregate Spouse Maximum Life Benefits

The system now takes into account the Employer Paid Life coverage amount for the employee and the Voluntary Life coverage amount to combine the amounts when the Use Aggregate Spouse Maximum box is checked to limit the spouse from electing more than 50% of the employee’s total coverage, rounded down to the nearest 10,000.

The employee is not required to enroll in Voluntary Life in order for the Spouse to enroll in Voluntary Life, however the Spouse’s election is limited to 50% of the employee’s Employer Paid Life election.

Calculate Life Event Benefits Window From Life Event Date

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/OBE/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR202503/Calculate_Life_Event.htm Path: OBE/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR202503/Calculate_Life_Event.htm

Calculate Life Event Benefits Window From Life Event Date

When a Life Event is launched, there is now an option to calculate the End Date of the Workflow from the Life Event Date instead of the date the Life Event workflow is created.

Previously, the system applied the 60-day window length from the Start Date of the Life Event Workflow. For example, if an employee had a baby on 10/11/2024 and the Life Event Workflow was created on 10/25/2024, the system allowed the employee to complete their enrollment until 12/24/2024.

With this update, the 60-day window will now be calculated from the Life Event Date (i.e. 10/11/2024), ensuring the employee has until 12/10/2024 to complete their enrollment. This change ensures timely recording of elections to gain coverage.

JIRA # OBE-6105

Clone a Life Event

(Edit) and

Enhancement to Edit New Hire Form

Service providers can now select the Variable Salary option in the Pay Method field on the Edit New Hire form to accurately track the hours that employees actually work. For example, non-profit companies could use this option to track the work hours of their employees who are paid a standard salaried amount, so they can use these hours and their allocations for grant purposes. (See Enhancements to Employee Details Form.)

Note: The Variable Salary option in the Pay Method field only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form. (Custom feature codes are only available for service providers.)

To set the Variable Salary option as the Pay Method:

  1. Enable the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code on the System Parameters form.

  2. Set the Workflow Type on the Workflow Maintenance form to Onboarding and the Action to Edit New Hire.

  3. After filtering by Client ID and selecting Search, select a new hire employee to edit in the Search Results list. The Edit New Hire form displays.

  4. Select the Variable Salary option in the Pay Method field. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Save.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHROnboarding User Guide.

Changes to I-9 Forms for Non-Applicable Fields

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202401/Changes_to_I9_Forms.htm Path: OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202401/Changes_to_I9_Forms.htm

Changes to I-9 Forms for Non-Applicable Fields

I-9 Forms have been updated to comply with new regulations regarding fields which are not applicable to the employee. I-9 Forms no longer accept N/A as an entry, and must either include information or be left blank.

To comply with this change, I-9 Forms are no longer populated with “N/A” for fields where neither the employer or employee have any input. Fields that are not applicable are now left blank on the form.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202401/OB_Fixes_MR_202401.htm Path: OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202401/OB_Fixes_MR_202401.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we strive to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed.

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
EERT-2256 When new users are required to enter a personal email address and a new employee is going through the onboarding using the new UEX, the Personal Email field did not display as a required field. In addition, if the field was left blank and the employee attempted to submit their details, they could not complete the process. This is fixed.
EERT-2272 When a user selected a form in the Form Library and attempted to open a pdf in the PDF Integration section of the General tab, the pdf form did not open properly. This is fixed.
EERT-2283 When a new employee in the Onboarding in Progress status attempted to exit the Benefits Enrollment, a 404 error occurred. This is fixed. The employee is now directed to the Employee Portal login form.
EERT-2288 When a user created a business rule in the Business Rules Library and saved the rule without selecting an operator in the Choose Operator field, that rule became a global rule for the client. Any custom form created with the same business rule would be visible to all employees. This is fixed. Users can no longer save a business rule without selecting an operator.
EERT-2289 When a user added a new custom form to the Onboarding process, the form did not display during the onboarding workflow. This is fixed.
EERT-2318 When a user attempted to upload a PDF document to the Document Repository, an error message displayed, and the action could not be completed. This is fixed.
OBE-7215 When a user reviewed Disability cards during Benefits Enrollment, the “Enter Coverage Amount” text on cards with editable amounts could be clicked, which caused the card to be selected. This is fixed.
OBE-7302 When a user accessed Benefits Enrollment using the Proxy Login feature, attempting to email the Benefits Confirmation Statement PDF caused the PDF to display with missing data and incorrect formatting. This issue only occurred in the Unified Employee Experience (UEX). This is fixed.

========================================================================

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202402/OB_Fixes_MR_202402.htm Path: OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202402/OB_Fixes_MR_202402.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we strive to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed.

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
EERT-2169 When an employee displayed the Enrollment Statement for benefits and a custom form was included at the end of the benefit enrollment workflow, the enrollment statement would include a duplicate offer type. This is fixed. Custom forms no longer cause a duplicate offer type in the enrollment statement.
EERT-2299 When an employee during onboarding had Download PDFs selected in their Chrome browser settings, the preview of the I-9 Section 1 document did not display properly and could not be downloaded. This is fixed.
EERT-2316 When a client with no rehire approval policy created a rehire approval in Employee Portal, the approval record would sometimes be left in the “P” (Pending) status, and the approval was not automatically cleared from the system. This is fixed.
EERT-2336 After an employee submits a benefits enrollment workflow, the confirmation statements could not be properly sent to the employee via email on the Employee Last Confirmation form or the Employee Confirmation Statements form. This is fixed.
EERT-2344 When a user previews forms in the Form Library or goes through the Onboarding process, the names of the form hyperlinks could change, disappear, or appear on the incorrect form. This is fixed.

========================================================================

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202404/BE_Fixes_202404_MR.htm Path: OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202404/BE_Fixes_202404_MR.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we strive to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed.

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
EERT-2313 If an employee was previously assigned a Benefit Group with no Benefit Rules and the employee was then assigned to a future-dated Benefit Group, network information was not properly pulled into the new group. This is fixed.
EERT-2360 When an employee attempted to review their benefit confirmation statement on the Benefit Confirmation Statements form in Employee Portal, clicking the link displayed a blank page. This is fixed.
EERT-2369 If an employee refreshed a form during Benefits Enrollment, the name of the form reverted to the most recent form name, regardless of the form name assigned during workflow creation. This is fixed.
EERT-2389 When a user enrolling in benefits attempted to waive benefits on the Gap Insurance form in the new UEX, and all plans were unavailable due to dependencies, the waive selection was not properly saved. In addition, on certain benefits enrollment forms in the new UEX, if the employee waived benefits, clicked Next, and then clicked Back, the Waived status on plans was changed to Not Available. This is fixed. When no benefit plans are available due to dependencies, no waive selection is available, and the form is automatically counted as complete. This behavior mirrors the behavior of the Legacy user interface.
EERT-2399 When a new employee during Onboarding attempted to add a personal email address that had more than five characters in the top-level domain, the email address could not be saved. For example, name@company.design would return as an invalid email address, despite being a valid address. This is fixed. The Onboarding email address field now supports top-level domain addresses of any length.
EERT-2419 When an employee unchecked the Approve every employee enrollment field on the Edit Workflow form in the Workflow Library, the employee could not save the form. This is fixed.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202404/OB_Fixes_MR_202404.htm Path: OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202404/OB_Fixes_MR_202404.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we strive to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed.

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
EERT-2334 When a user completed Section 1 of the I-9 Form in the new UEX, sent it for approval, and started Section 2, the user could continue to edit Section 1. This is fixed. Section 1 is now properly locked after it is completed and sent for approval.
EERT-2367 When a new employee attempted to use a foreign passport and I-94 form as documentation on the I-9 form during Onboarding, the system would require them to submit an I-20 form or DS-2019 form. Neither the I-20 form, nor DS-2019 form are specifically required for a new employee with a foreign passport. This is fixed. Employees submitting a foreign passport and I-94 form are no longer required to submit a third document for verification.
EERT-2381 The new UEX did not properly display markdown formatting and fonts on certain forms. As a result, certain customer forms that used the markdown formatting did not display correctly. This is fixed. The new UEX now features full support for the markdown formatting used by customer forms.
EERT-2386 When an employee using the Direct Deposit form during Onboarding attempted to clear the form by selecting the Cancel button, the Cancel and Save options would become grayed out, and nothing would happen. This is fixed. When the user cancels their direct deposit, they are returned to the main Direct Deposit form.
EERT-2394 When an Onboarding Complete Notification included the Hire Date substitution variable, the notification displayed an incorrect date instead of the actual hire date. This is fixed.
EERT-2399 When a new employee during Onboarding attempted to add a personal email address that had more than five characters in the top-level domain, the email address could not be saved. For example, name@company.design would return as an invalid email address, despite being a valid address. This is fixed. The Onboarding email address field now supports top-level domain addresses of any length.

EERT-2405 After an employee submits a benefits enrollment workflow, the confirmation statements could not be properly sent to the employee via email on the Employee Last Confirmation form or the Employee Confirmation Statements form if the sender was a Worksite Manager. Service Providers and Trusted Advisors could still send the confirmation statements normally. This is fixed.
EERT-2437 When an employee completed signing their onboarding forms or benefit confirmation statements, the IP address was not properly saved in the record. This is fixed.

When technical difficulties surface, we strive to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed.

EERT-2466 When an employee went through the Onboarding process for a Minnesota worksite location and filled out the state form, the field for number of days in a pay period was populated with incorrect information. This is fixed.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202408/OB_Fixes_MR_202408.htm Path: OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202408/OB_Fixes_MR_202408.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we strive to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed.

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
EERT-2390 The Elect W-2 form’s acknowledgment did not display in the new UEX electronic signature format, and it displayed differently than other custom forms with an e-signature acknowledgment. This is fixed.
EERT-2397 When a user approved an I-9 Section 2 document using the same browser that was used to complete the onboarding process, the worksite employee’s name displayed on the I9 audit instead of the approver’s name. This is fixed.
EERT-2489 When employees went through the benefits enrollment process for certain providers, the FSA election section did not display properly. This is fixed.
EERT-2512 When a Service Provider or Worksite Manager submitted a Life Event workflow that has a documentation requirement via proxy, the Confirmation Statement was sent to the email address on the employee record rather than the recipient email address entered. This is fixed.
EERT-2545 When an employee enrolled in a Flexible Spending plan through Benefits Enrollment, the employee could continue after entering an Annual Election amount greater than the Plan Year Limit. This is fixed.
EERT-2550 When an employee’s Onboarding process is suspended from the Workflow Maintenance form, and the option to allow access to Employee Portal is selected, the Onboarding in Process flag was not properly cleared from the employee record. This is fixed.
EERT-2552 When an employee going through Benefits Enrollment made selections for Life and Critical Illness costs, the calculation experienced latency, causing the form to display $0 premiums on the confirmation statement and Benefits Enrollment forms. This is fixed.
EERT-2567 When a user entered information for the I-9 Section 2 form, the user could enter spaces into the First Supporting Document field, which could create errors in the system. This is fixed.
EERT-2580 When a user duplicated a form in the Form Library and removed an attached PDF from the copied form, the PDF file was deleted from the client’s documents and would no longer display on the original version of the form. This is fixed.
EERT-2594 When a user duplicated a workflow with a version number of 2.0 or greater, the new workflow was not saved as version 1, and an error occurred when the new workflow was assigned to an employee. Workflows with a version number starting with 1 could still be duplicated and saved without error. This is fixed.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202410/OB_Fixes_MR_202410.htm Path: OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/MR202410/OB_Fixes_MR_202410.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we strive to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed.

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
EERT-2537 The Substitute Variable <> in Benefits Enrollment notification templates did not pull data properly to display the employee’s personal email address. This substitute variable did work properly in Onboarding notification templates. This is fixed.
EERT-2557 When an employee completing the I-9 workflow provided Supporting Documents and uploaded files, then changed their answer to indicate they would provide documents to employer in person, the uploaded documents were not all properly removed. The first supporting document was removed, but the second was not, and the uploaded document was saved to the employee’s I-9 Documents folder. This is fixed. When an employee changes their selection, all previously uploaded files are now removed.
EERT-2597 Users with Inquiry access to the Web Enrollment Configuration form could delete and archive an employee’s Benefit Enrollment Workflow. This is fixed. Users with Inquiry access are now properly restricted from making changes on this form.
EERT-2639 If errors occurred during the Rehire Approval process, the Rehire Approval was not properly removed when a new approval record was created. This resulted in unnecessary approval records remaining in the system. This is fixed. When a new Rehire Approval record is created, any additional Rehire Approval records for that same user are removed from the system.
EERT-2648 When a user going through Benefits Enrollment selected both Limited FSA and Dependent Care FSA, and at lease one option had Terms and Conditions, those Terms and Conditions did not display properly on the Summary page. As a result, the user could not complete their Benefits Enrollment. This is fixed.
OBE-8656 When a user filled out underwriting questions during Benefits Enrollment and then switched their preferred language, their selected responses were not properly saved on the form. This is fixed.
OBE-8677 In a previous release, the Pet and Legal offer types were changed to no longer display an option to select Dependents, as neither plan included them. However, if an employee had added dependents to a Pet or Legal plan previously, the dependents were incorrectly retained on the plan during the Benefits Enrollment posting process. This is fixed. If any unnecessary dependent data exists on a Pet or Legal benefit plan, the dependent data is removed during the Benefit Enrollment posting process.
OBE-8680 When a Spanish version of the plan summary and additional documents were added to a benefits plan on the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form, these documents did not display properly when a user set their preferred language to Spanish and went through Benefits Enrollment. This is fixed. The Spanish versions of the plan summary and additional documents now display properly when the preferred language is set to Spanish.

EERT-2702 In the Benefit Enrollment workflow, documents linked to a benefits plan using the Benefit Enrollment Plan Detail form displayed the document category instead of the document name and description. This is fixed.
OBE-8850 On the Benefit Enrollment Plan Details form, the English and Spanish text boxes for Evidence of Insurability were not independent, and editing one text box would change the other. This is fixed.
OBE-8856 Spanish characters in the text for the Onboarding and Benefits Enrollment workflows displayed incorrectly as a ? symbol. This is fixed. Please note that some invalid ? characters may still exist in the Form Library and Benefit Enrollment Plan Details forms which will be addressed in a future release.
OBE-8911 On the Benefit Enrollment Plan Details form, the Spanish Underwriting Questions Yes/No response displays as S? instead of Si’. This is fixed.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/QR202403/BE_Fixes_202403_QR.htm Path: OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2024/QR202403/BE_Fixes_202403_QR.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we strive to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed.

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
EERT-2297 When the Electronic Enrollment flag was disabled on the Control tab of the Client Details form, open enrollment workflows were still generated electronically. These workflows would display on the dashboard and result in notifications being sent to employees about their open enrollment in the system. This is fixed.
EERT-2324 When a user selected Benefits Enrollment for an employee on the Web Enrollment Configuration form, the Next Open Enrollment Effective Date field displayed ‘N’ instead of the appropriate date. This is fixed.
EERT-2329 When a user generated an Enrollment Status by Workflow/Client report, two u-umlauts (üü) were added to the entries in the Enrollment Status field. This is fixed.
EERT-2330 When a user attempted to enter an election amount on the Health Savings Account Form Name form during Benefits Enrollment, the form would refresh after the user typed each individual character. This is fixed. A message now displays indicating that the plan cost is being updated when changes are made to the election amount.
EERT-2333 When a user created a new form in the Form Library and uploaded a mapped pdf file, the pdf-mapped fields did not display on the Layout tab unless the user returned to the General tab and reopened the Layout tab. This is fixed.
EERT-2359 When a user accessed the Life Event Maintenance form, the form header and the Add Life Event button did not display properly. This is fixed.
EERT-2413 When an employee previously enrolled in $0 Employee Life Insurance Coverage, the employee coverage was updated to a salary multiplier or maximum coverage during the posting process. This is fixed. When an employee is enrolled at $0 Employee Life Coverage, the posting process keeps the employee coverage at $0 accordingly.
OBE-7643 During Benefits Enrollment, switching between forms and comparing statements on each form could result in the Compare bar becoming stuck. If the user compared planned on the Whole Life Prebuilt form, then compared plans on the Basic Life form, then returned to the Whole Life Prebuilt form and compared plans, they would be unable to remove selected plans or close the comparison. This is fixed.
OBE-7913 When an employee had a non-conforming dependent enrolled on their medical, dental, or vision benefits plans, the employee needed to complete required documentation. However, the documentation link did not display in the standard style for URLs, which could create confusion. This is fixed. The table has been restyled, and the URL now looks like a standard link.

OBE-8044 When an employee attempted to remove uploaded documents during the Onboarding process, the warning message text referred to the button incorrectly. This is fixed.

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we strive to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed.

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
EERT-2617 The Web Enrollment Configuration can be manually created with a future Start Date; however, employees were able to access the workflow before this date. This is fixed.

EERT-2779 During the Onboarding process, the I-9 Section 2 Approval record would sometimes not be properly generated, preventing the I-9 process from being completed. This is fixed.
EERT-2785 In the Life Event workflow, employees could remove spouse and dependents from CRL plans even if the Allow Unenrollment option was not enabled. This is fixed.
EERT-2798 On the Bulk Launch Benefit Workflow form, the Return To The Pre-Filter Selections Page button did not function properly. This is fixed.
EERT-2818 When an employee’s preferred language was set to Spanish, the employee’s beneficiaries did not display on the Employee Confirmation Statement. This is fixed.
EERT-2844 When a user configured pay methods in the Business Rules Library form, Variable Salary was not available as a payment method. This is fixed.
EERT-2865 When a client used the Rules Engine, the Non-Conforming Dependent Benefit acknowledgment message did not display during Benefits Enrollment. This is fixed.
OBE-9139 When an employee displayed the Benefits Summary, and the language was set to Spanish, the English description for FSA/HSA plan types displayed instead. This is fixed.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/OB_Fixes_R202505.htm Path: OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/OB_Fixes_R202505.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we strive to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed.

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
EERT-2771 When a user selected the Define Plan Level Setup option on the Benefits Enrollment Plan Details form and attempted to save a record with attached documents, an error occurred. This is fixed.
EERT-2778 When an employee was enrolled in multiple voluntary benefit plans and viewed all options during Benefits Enrollment, options the employee was not enrolled in did not display properly. This is fixed.
EERT-2821 When an employee submitted Employee Information during the Onboarding process, employee records were sometimes not generated properly, resulting in an error message. This is fixed.
EERT-2839 When a user made edits to a workflow in the Workflow Library by removing forms from a category and deleting that category, the category was not properly deleted unless the removed forms were added to a different category. This is fixed.
EERT-2840 When a user made a change to a form which had a Business Rule attached to it in the Form Library, the Business Rule was removed from the form. This is fixed.
EERT-2845 When a user attempted to download a batch of enrollment statements using the Download Enrollment Statements form, an error occurred. This is fixed.
EERT-2846 When an employee submitted a Benefit Enrollment workflow, then made changes to their state of residence that made them ineligible for those benefits, the employee was prompted properly to redo their enrollment. However, the employee’s original benefit selection remained active in the system. This is fixed.
EERT-2847 When an employee selected the Child Only plan for life insurance coverage, the option to make their spouse a dependent could still be selected. This is fixed.
EERT-2852 When a user attempted to set up a new plan on the Benefit Plan Details form or make changes to an existing plan, an error occurred when the employee attempted to save the record. This is fixed.
EERT-2855 When a user had multiple VOL enrollments on the Life Events form, and Allow Un-Enrollment was not enabled, the user could still unenroll from all but one VOL offer. This is fixed.
EERT-2879 When the Onboarding process was initiated for a new hire, the Onboarding email message was sent to inactive Service Provider email addresses. This is fixed. Inactive Service Provider users are now excluded from the Onboarding email messages.

Fixes

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/OB_Fixes_R202506.htm Path: OBE/Release-Notes/Fixes/2025/OB_Fixes_R202506.htm

Fixes

When technical difficulties surface, we strive to resolve them right away. The following are recent known issues that we’ve fixed.

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
EERT-2863 For certain clients, the substitution variable for email messages did not work properly, and the Onboarding message did not contain the proper link for the new employee to start the Onboarding process. This is fixed.
EERT-2869 When an employee attempted to run the Enrollment Status by Workflow/Client report, the report did not process and display properly. This is fixed.
EERT-2878 When a Benefit Group was future-dated on an employee record, Network benefit plans did not take this new group into consideration. This is fixed.
EERT-2896 For certain clients, the electronic consent form did not display properly during the Onboarding process. This is fixed.
EERT-2900 When a user with an apostrophe in their name attempted to complete their I9 form using an Apple device, an error occurred. This is fixed.
EERT-2929 When an employee completed the Symmetry Tax forms, the document ID was not properly stored in the Prehires record. As a result, when the workflow was submitted, the workflow data review process reopened the Tax form. This is fixed.
OBE-9474 Employees were able to proceed through the tax form in the Onboarding workflow even when required fields on the Employer Details record (e.g., telephone number) were missing. This resulted in the tax forms reopening during the final submission of the workflow. This is fixed. Employees can no longer continue past the tax form until all required fields are completed. Important Note: After acknowledging the error message, employees will currently be redirected to the Onboarding Summary page instead of the next incomplete form in the workflow. If there is an unfinished form prior to the tax form, they will be taken to that form instead. We are actively working on a future update to ensure employees are directed to the next incomplete form in the workflow as intended.

EERT-2921 When a Dependent adult was added as a Beneficiary to certain plans within the Benefits Enrollment workflow and the workflow was saved, the Beneficiary was also added as a Covered Dependent on the plans, despite being over the age limit. This is fixed.

Alternate ID for Independent Contractors

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2023/MR202302/CPR-3847_Alternate_1099_ID.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2023/MR202302/CPR-3847_Alternate_1099_ID.htm

Alternate ID for Independent Contractors

You can use the new Alternate ID field to assign an alternative identifier to independent contractors (1099 employees).

This new field is located on the Employee Details > Work tab, under the Miscellaneous panel.

This is intended for any service provider that needs to store a second identification number for independent contractors. For example, you might be required to associate contractors with their Social Security number and their business FEIN. Any value entered is masked automatically.

[Image: Alternate ID field on the Miscellaneous tab of Employee Work]

Note: Note: The field displays even if the employee is not a contractor (in other words, if the 1099 Contractor field is not selected). You can also hide this option from users by enabling field-level security on the User Roles form.

JIRA # CPR-3847

Enhancement to ACH Batch Control Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/MR202407/System/ACH_Batch_Control_Form_Enhancement_MR202407.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/MR202407/System/ACH_Batch_Control_Form_Enhancement_MR202407.htm

Enhancement to ACH Batch Control Form

After a batch posts, the ACH Batch Control form now displays the total number of detail lines in the ACH file, along with the total number of debits and credits. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: You can access the ACH Batch Control form by selecting a transaction in the ACH Processing form.

These new fields are helpful in determining the total count because they might be different from the totals that display in the Summary Information panel due to:

  • Deposits for garnishments insert extra lines in the file to identify on whose behalf the deposit is being made, which increases the detail count.

  • Checking accounts with an offset account insert extra lines for the offset transactions, which can change the total credit and debits from the initial amounts.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRACH User Guide.

Enhancements to Commission Maintenance Form

The following enhancements now reside on the Commission Maintenance form, which is available on the Client|Change menu:

  • Previously, users could apply both a client-specific setup and a system-level plan on the same line at the client level of commissions on the Commission Maintenance form. When this occurred, only the system-level plan was applied to the reporting process when commissions were computed. For example, the client-level plan consists of the Amount, Flat or Percent, and Based On field selections and the system-level plan consists of the Based On Plan field selection:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: You can access the Commission Maintenance form by selecting Commissions on the Action menu in the Client Details form.

When setting up commissions on the client level, users are no longer allowed to set up both client and system-level plans on the same line. If they attempt this setup and click Accept, an error message now displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: After clicking OK, the system returns to the form without saving the line.

  • A new column, Based on Items, now resides on the client-level Commission Maintenance form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use this column to apply additional based-on types to commission rules at the client level, such as Percent of Bill Code, Profits on Admin, Workers’ Comp Profit, Benefit Commission Type, and Benefit Commission Percentage.

  • Five new Based On options, Benefit Commission Type, Benefit Commission Percentage, Workers Compensation Profit, Percent of Bill Code, and Profits to Admin (Enter Bill Code in Based On), are now available at the client level. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

These options do the following:

  • Benefit Commission Type: Benefits-based commission for a specific benefit type. (You must enter the benefit type code in the Based on Item field.)

  • Benefit Commission Percentage: Percentage based on the benefit list. (You must enter the specific group benefit plan ID in the Based on Item field.)

  • Workers Compensation Profit: Checks bill code 005 and computes the profit, and also checks for information entered on losses.

  • Percent of Bill Code: Fixed percentage for the amount charged on a specific bill code. (You must enter the percentage in the Based on Item field.)

  • Profits to Admin (Enter Bill Code in Based On): The system uses the specified Bill Code and then subtracts the cost associated with that Bill Code. That amount (profit or loss) is used in the percent computation. For example, if you choose Bill Code 004 (SUTA) and specify 5% of profits, and there was $1000 in sales and $960 in costs, the payout would be $2.00 ($40.00 x 0.05).

Note: If both a client-level and a system-level plan are applied, then the system calculates the commissions based on the system-level plan.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

After saving a commission plan, the system no longer applies any updates to the plan if it is already in use at the client level. For example, if you create commission plan A and apply it to client 123, then update commission plan A and save the updates the system displays an error message:

Note: You can make updates to any plans at the system level that are not applied to clients. After you apply the plan to a client, it cannot be updated.

  • Existing commission plans already in use at the client level cannot be deleted. For example, if you click the Delete button for a client-level plan and then select Yes, an error message displays:

[Image: screenshot]

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

Enhancements to Compute Commissions Form

The following enhancements now reside on the Compute Commissions form, which is available on the Operations|Action menu:

  • Two new columns, Client ID and Salesperson, now display on the Commission Report, which you can run on the Compute Commissions form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

These new columns can help assist you in understanding the information produced in this report. For example, there could be several salespeople for one client in an invoice, so each salesperson now has their own line item associated with their calculated commission.

  • The total amounts for the Gross Pay and Admin Fee columns that originally displayed in the Totals row no longer display.

  • A new link, Download Pay File, now displays after computing the commissions and closing the on-screen report. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Click the Download Pay File link to download a .csv file that contains the commission data that was just calculated. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • You can use this file to import information into the timesheet.

  • The system displays information from the Commission Details form in this downloaded file.

  • Four system-level Based On options now work at the client level:

  • Gross Wages: Total gross wages of the client payroll invoice.

  • Admin Fees: Total amount of administrative fees on the client payroll invoice.

  • Average Active Employee Count: Average number of active employees during the commission cycle.

  • Fixed Per Paid Employee: Fixed amount per paid employee.

Note: The system calculates these options using the same process at the client level that is currently done at the system level in conjunction with the Based On Item option.

Enhancements to Employee Details Form

The following enhancements now reside on the Employee Details form, which is available on the HR|Change menu:

  • Worksite trusted advisors can now assign a manager from a different client to an employee as a PTO Approver or a Manager on the Work tab.

  • The field names and their boxes in the Federal Tax Filing panel on the Tax tab now display in left-aligned format, so the information is easier to scan. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  • To help users properly maintain HSA deposit accounts, the system now displays a warning when you set up and save an employee’s HSA account without also setting up the company’s HSA account on the Deposit tab in the Employee Details form. For example, if the employee’s record indicates the EE HSA to Checking direct deposit type, then that record must also have the Co HSA to Checking direct deposit type indicated on that form.

If you do not set up both accounts on the Deposit tab, the following warning displays:

[Image: screenshot]

This warning is useful to remind users that if the company makes HSA contributions to employee accounts but they did not set up the company’s HSA deposit account associated with the employee’s record, then funds become lost.

  • The Employment Verification panel that resided on the Tax tab has moved to the Work tab, with no impact to its functionality. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  • Three fields that resided on the Tax tab, Non-Resident Alien, Alien Registration Number, and Alien Registration Expiration Date, have moved to the Work tab, with no impact to their functionality. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  • Three fields that resided on the Personal tab, E-Verify Case No, E-Verify Case Status, and Submit to E-Verify, have moved to the Work tab in the E-Verify panel, with no impact to their functionality. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  • A new button, Save & Close, now saves the information you enter and closes the employee record. (This button displays on every tab in the form.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Clicking the Save button saves the current employee changes, but does not close the employee record.

  • A new save banner, “The current record has been saved,” now displays at the top of the form after you make an update and click Save.

Note: Note the following about the save banner:

  • Does not display if you click Save & Close

  • Displays on every tab in the form when you click Save

  • Disappears in a few seconds

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRHuman Resources User Guide.

The following enhancements now reside on the Employee Fields Import form, which is available on the Operations|Action menu:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use these field codes to perform a mass update of the tax information for employees in their Employee Details record.

Observe the following guidelines when importing values for these field codes:

Field Code Description
Deductions You must enter a dollar amount.
Federal Claim Dependents You must enter a dollar amount.
FICA Exempt This is a Yes/No option. > Note: Note the following: - Yes, No, Y, and N are acceptable. - A blank field is equal to No.

  • Yes, No, Y, and N are acceptable.

  • A blank field is equal to No. | FICA Exempt Thru Date | You must enter a valid date. | | Other Income | You must enter a dollar amount. | Note: The following error messages display in these instances:

  • If you do not enter Yes, No, Y, or N in FICA Exempt, “Value must be Yes or No.”

  • If you do not enter a date in FICA Exempt Thru Date, “Value must be a valid date.”

  • Five new miscellaneous field codes, 1099 Contractor, Agricultural Worker, Auto Accept T/S, Default T/S Hours, and S-Corp Principal, now display on the Select Field list, which is accessible by selecting Field Code in the Generate Import Spreadsheet section. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

[Image: screenshot]

You can use these field codes to perform a mass update of information for employees in their Employee Details record.

Observe the following guidelines when importing values for these field codes:

Field Code Description
1099 Contractor This is a Yes/No option. > Note: Note the following: - Yes, No, Y, and N are acceptable. - A blank field is equal to No.

  • Yes, No, Y, and N are acceptable.

  • A blank field is equal to No. | Agricultural Worker | This is a Yes/No option. > Note: Note the following: - Yes, No, Y, and N are acceptable. - A blank field is equal to No. |

  • Yes, No, Y, and N are acceptable.

  • A blank field is equal to No. | Auto Accept T/S | This is a Yes/No option. > Note: Note the following: - Yes, No, Y, and N are acceptable. - A blank field is equal to No. |

  • Yes, No, Y, and N are acceptable.

  • A blank field is equal to No. | Default T/S Hours | You must enter a numeric value. | | S-Corp Principal | This is a Yes/No option. > Note: Note the following: - Yes, No, Y, and N are acceptable. - A blank field is equal to No. |

  • Yes, No, Y, and N are acceptable.

  • A blank field is equal to No. Note: The following error messages display in these instances:

Note: After you delete a template, you can reuse the template name and ID to create a new template.

Enhancement to Bill Pending Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Bill_Pending_Form_Enhancement_QR202403.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Bill_Pending_Form_Enhancement_QR202403.htm

Enhancement to Bill Pending Form

The system now applies an E-Verify fee in the Bill Pending form for each new hire when the Submit for E-Verification field is enabled on the New Hire form. After saving the new hire, the system automatically creates a bill pending fee using the new EV-FEES bill code. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • This simplified process is similar to the new hire E-Verify fee process, but uses a different code for the bill pending fee.

  • Billing can be set up globally or have an override at the client level. (The override takes precedence over the global setup, if in place.)

  • You must name the Bill Event Code EV-FEES.

  • For the first 30 days of service for new clients, if you enable Skip Employee Fees for New Clients on the Billing Templates form the system does not create the EV-FEES bill code.

  • If the Employer Start Date on the New Hire form is greater than the Hire Date, then the system uses the Employer Start Date as the EV-FEES bill date.

  • The bill pending date is based on the employee’s hire date and populates the location and employee on the bill pending fee.

  • When the client and worksite location is set up for E-Verify, the system generates an E-Verify fee. However, if the worksite location is excluded, then the system does not generate a fee.

  • This fee structure does not apply to rehires or those who have a different code/fee structure for the employee type.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Processing Guide.

Enhancements to Data Import Tool

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Data_Import_Tool_Enhancements_QR202403.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Data_Import_Tool_Enhancements_QR202403.htm

Enhancements to Data Import Tool

The following enhancements now reside in the Data Import Tool, which is available on the Operations|Import Processing menu:

  • New Backup Account Assignment import template: You can use this import template to import backup account assignments for the client to reduce the amount of manual work required. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The Backup Account Assignment import template is only available for service providers.

To import this data, select Backup Account Assignment from the Import Template menu, and then click Find File to upload the file.

Note: Note the following:

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Company Account form cannot import data using the Backup Account Assignment import template. (You can access the Company Account form by selecting the Account tab on the Client Details form.)

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Company Account form can view the Backup Account Assignment import template, but cannot import data.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

  • Users who do not have access to a particular company through client access groups are unable to import data into that company.

  • If you enter a role/user combination that the system has already applied to the client it’s overridden and a warning displays, “User <XXXX> already exists with role <XXX> for client <XXXX>, this record will be overridden.”

  • New Client Benefits import template: You can use this import template to import yearly information into the ACA Large Employer Year grid for the client to reduce the amount of manual work required. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The Client Benefits import template is only available for service providers.

To import this data, select Client Benefits from the Import Template menu, and then click Find File to upload the file.

Note: Note the following:

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Client Benefit form cannot import data using the Client Benefits import template. (You can access the Client Benefit form by selecting the Benefits tab on the Client Details form.)

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Client Benefit form can view the Client Benefits import template, but cannot import data.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

  • Users who do not have access to a particular company through client access groups are unable to import data into that company.

  • If you enter a year that has already been applied for the client on the Client Details form, the system does not override the information and the import displays an error message, “Year <XXXX> already exists for client <XXXX>, this record will be skipped.”

  • New Client Commissions import template: You can use this import template to import commissions for the client to reduce the amount of manual work required. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The Client Commissions import template is only available for service providers.

To import this data, select Client Commissions from the Import Template menu, and then click Find File to upload the file.

Note: Note the following:

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Commission Maintenance form cannot import data using the Client Commissions import template. (You can access the Commission Maintenance form by selecting Commissions on the Action menu in the Client Details form.)

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Commission Maintenance form can view the Client Commissions import template, but cannot import data.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

  • Users who do not have access to a particular company through client access groups are unable to import data into that company.

  • A new field, Client Category, now displays on the Client Details import template in column 3, and in the downloadable sample header file in the Data Import Tool. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use this new field to define the client’s work category, such as CON for Construction.

Note: Note the following:

  • If you enter an invalid code an error message displays, “Client Category <XXX> is not a valid code.”

  • If the code you enter is already applied to the client on the Client Details form a warning displays after import, “Client Category <XXXX> already exists for client <XXXX>, this record will be overridden.”

  • New Employer Tax Rates (SUTA) import template: You can use this import template to import employer tax rates for the client to reduce the amount of manual work required. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The Employer Tax Rates (SUTA) import template is only available for service providers.

To import this data, select Employer Tax Rates (SUTA) from the Import Template menu, and then click Find File to upload the file.

You can also access this new import template by clicking the Import icon that now displays on the Employer Tax Rates (SUTA) form, accessible from the Employer|Change menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Employer Tax Rates (SUTA) form cannot import data using the Employer Tax Rates (SUTA) import template and subsequently, the Data Import Tool icon will not display on this form.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Employer Tax Rates (SUTA) form, but whose user role is also set to DENY for the Data Import Tool cannot view the Import icon on the Employer Tax Rates (SUTA) form.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Employer Tax Rates (SUTA) form can view the Employer Tax Rates (SUTA) import template, but cannot import data.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

  • Users who do not have access to a particular company through client access groups are unable to import data into that company.

  • New Pay Code Total Compensation Category import template: You can use this import template to import pay code total compensation categories for the client to reduce the amount of manual work required. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The Pay Code Total Compensation Category import template is only available for service providers.

To import this data, select Pay Code Total Compensation Category from the Import Template menu, and then click Find File to upload the file.

You can also access this new import template by clicking the Import icon that now displays on the Pay Codes form, accessible from the System|Change menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Pay Codes form cannot import data using the Pay Code Total Compensation Category import template and subsequently, the Data Import Tool icon will not display on this form.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Pay Codes form, but whose user role is also set to DENY for the Data Import Tool cannot view the Import icon on the Pay Codes form.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Pay Codes form can view the Pay Code Total Compensation Category import template, but cannot import data.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

  • A new field, Remote Location, now resides on the Worksite Locations import template in column 31, and in the downloadable sample header file in the Data Import Tool. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use this new field to define whether the worksite geocode will be ignored and taxes will be based on the employee’s resident geocode. (Workers Compensation will also follow the resident geocode when enabled on the Benefit tab in the Client Details form.)

For more information, see the in-product help, PrismHREmployer Administration Guide, PrismHR Payroll Administration Guide, or PrismHRPayroll Setup Guide.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Payroll_Calculation_Error_Message_Enhancement_QR202403.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Payroll_Calculation_Error_Message_Enhancement_QR202403.htm

Enhancement to Payroll Calculation Error Message

Previously, when an employee received pay less than zero ($0), the system displayed a payroll calculation error message that did not specify the employee ID or the data tested, “Employee BENEFIT TESTING has a total pay < zero. Not Allowed!”

JIRA # PD-14214

========================================================================

Enhancements to Payroll Notes Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Payroll_Notes_Form_Enhancements_QR202403.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Payroll_Notes_Form_Enhancements_QR202403.htm

Enhancements to Payroll Notes Form

The following enhancements now reside on the Payroll Notes form, which you can access on the Client|View menu or by selecting Payroll Notes on the Actions menu in the Client Details form.

New Filters Section

A new section, Filters, now displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the new filters and Find Payroll Notes button to narrow an employee search for the current client.

To narrow an employee search, use the following methods:

  • To search for a specific employee, select Employee, then select Find Payroll Notes. The list re-displays the employee who matches that selection.

  • To further narrow the search for employees who display in the list, select the Employee Status, Pay Group, Employee Type, or Location Code, then select Find Payroll Notes. The list re-displays the employees who match those selections.

Note: Note the following when using the filters:

  • You can only select an employee from the Employee filter in the list that displays. (You cannot enter an employee name in this filter.)

  • The Employee Status and Employee Type filters only display if you are allowed access the current client.

  • After selecting the Pay Group or Location Code, the pay group’s or location code’s description displays next to the filter.

Reordered Columns

For easier review, the columns on this form were reordered and now display as follows:

  • Ref #

  • Employee ID

  • Employee Name

  • Note Details (only the first 30 characters of the note display)

  • View Count

  • Display Mode

  • Urgent

  • Expires On

  • Date Entered

  • Time Entered

  • Entered By

Update to Display Mode and Urgent Columns

To make the list of payroll notes easier to review, the Display Mode and Urgent columns now display the data’s description, not the code. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

These columns now display the following descriptions:

Column Description (Code)
Display Mode One Time (Y) All Payrolls (N) Scheduled Payrolls (S)
Urgent Yes (Y) No (N)

New Cancel Button

A new button, Cancel, now displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Click Cancel to clear any filters that you set, which resets them to the default setting.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration Guide.

JIRA # PD-16001, PD-16006, PD-16008, and PD-16014

========================================================================

Enhancement to Payroll Status Report Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Payroll_Status_Report_Form_Enhancement_QR202403.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Payroll_Status_Report_Form_Enhancement_QR202403.htm

Enhancement to Payroll Status Report Form

The report parameters on the Payroll Status Report form and the Payroll Status Report output, which is available on the Operations Payroll|Report menu, have been updated to allow for better monitoring of payrolls and their progress. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

The report parameters were updated as follows:

  • The Call In Date field was replaced by two fields in the new Run By panel (select one):

  • Cutoff Date: Enter or select an end date by which the hours need to be entered into the system. (Leave this field blank to include all dates.)

  • Pay Date Range: Enter or select a pay date range. (Leave these fields blank to include all dates.)

Note: The values must be entered in date format. In addition, the start date cannot occur after the end date and the end date cannot occur before the start date.

  • A new panel, Payroll Step, now displays, where you can select specific payroll steps. (Leave this field blank to include all payroll steps.)

Note: Selected steps do not display in the report header.

The following column updates now reside in the output on the Payroll Status Report:

  • The Batch Breaks column was removed.

  • The former “Call In” column headers now display as “Cutoff.”

  • The Cutoff Time column now populates using the Remote Cutoff Time entered on the Payroll Control form.

  • A new column, Pay Date, now displays. This column represents the date the payroll was paid.

  • The “Last Step” column header now displays as “Payroll Status.”

  • The “Last Step Date” column header now displays as “Step Date.”

  • The “Last Step By” column header now displays as “Step By.”

For example:

[Image: screenshot]

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Reports guide.

Enhancement to Recurring Deductions and Scheduled Deductions Forms

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Recurring_Deds_Sched_Deds_Enh_QR202403.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Recurring_Deds_Sched_Deds_Enh_QR202403.htm

Enhancement to Recurring Deductions and Scheduled Deductions Forms

Previously, users were able to manually enter deduction codes and save the record in the Recurring Deductions and Scheduled Deductions forms if the codes existed at the global level even though they did not display on the Deduction Codes list in the Control tab on the Client Details form.

To prevent users from manually entering restricted deduction codes in the Recurring Deductions and Scheduled Deductions forms a warning now displays when users click Save, “Warning - <deduction code> is not a deduction code defined on the <client> Client Detail Control tab.” Click OK to continue.

Note: Note the following:

  • The system does not perform retroactive data validation, so any clients currently using deduction codes not assigned to the client will remain in place.

  • If the ALLPAYCODESINT custom feature code is enabled, then internal payroll users can enter or select from all pay codes.

For more information, see the in-product help, PrismHRPayroll Overrides Guide or PrismHRPayroll Administration Guide.

Enhancement to Reprinting Payroll Checks

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Reprinting_Payroll_Checks_Enhancement_QR202403.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Reprinting_Payroll_Checks_Enhancement_QR202403.htm

Enhancement to Reprinting Payroll Checks

Previously, worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors who were assigned the Payroll - Prints Checks HR Role in the Users form had to click the question mark icon in the Payroll Reports form and then click the Rebuild field in the Reprint Payroll Checks form to reprint payroll checks.

To make printing and rebuilding payroll checks more user-friendly for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors, these users can now simply select the Reprint Payroll Checks link in the Payroll Reports form.

Enhancement to Scheduled Payments Form

The system now prevents users from entering or selecting client-restricted pay codes (those codes not assigned to the client) in the Pay Code field on the Scheduled Payments form, which is available on the Payroll|Change menu. (These restricted pay codes include those restricted at the client level on the Control tab in the Client Details form in the Pay Code field. If deduction codes are set, then only those codes are available for that client.)

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Overrides Guide.

JIRA # PD-15261

Enhancement to Tax Adjustment Import Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Tax_Adjustment_Import_Form_Enhancement_QR202403.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Tax_Adjustment_Import_Form_Enhancement_QR202403.htm

Enhancement to Tax Adjustment Import Form

Three new fields, Location, Special Options Code, and Residential Geocode Override, which display at the end of the import, can now be imported using the Tax Adjustment Import form, which is available on the Payroll|Change menu.

Note: You can configure the settings for these fields on the Tax Adjustments form, which is available on the Payroll|Change form.

Note: Note the following about these fields:

  • Location: If you do client reporting by location and need to adjust that type of register, this field must have a valid location code.

  • Special Options Code: Indicates the code to modify the tax adjustment process. Valid options include:

  • Group-Term Life: Adjustment to group-term life

  • Sick Pay Adjustment: Adjustment to sick pay

  • Uncollect Tax Adjustment: Uncollected Medicare or OASDI tax adjustments

  • Residential Geocode Override: If you are making an adjustment that affects Pennsylvania local taxes, this field indicates the nine-digit Residential Geocode Override code that the system should use to determine the resident PSD code. (If you do not indicate a value, the system uses the employer’s value.)

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Adjustment Processing Guide.

Enhancements to Time Sheet Entry Form

The following enhancements now reside on the Time Sheet Entry form on the Payroll|Action menu:

Accepting Leave Requests

As an extension to working with Global PTO Plans, leave requests made in the Employee Portal that the system pulls into timesheets using the red dot can now be accepted there. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The Global PTO Plans feature allows you to set up PTO plans on the system level and automatically assign those plans to employees based on work location.

Entering a Payroll Note

[Image: screenshot]

icon. Clicking this icon opens the Payroll Notes form, where you can click New Note to add a note. For example:

Enhanced Payroll Notes

========================================================================

Enhancement to Unbundled Billing Additional Details Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Unbundled_Billing_Additional_Details_Form_Enhancement_QR202403.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/Payroll/Unbundled_Billing_Additional_Details_Form_Enhancement_QR202403.htm

Enhancement to Unbundled Billing Additional Details Form

To suppress the billing (delivery fee) for a manual check that occurs when a billing rule is processing live checks, a new field, Exclude From Manual Check, now displays on the Unbundled Billing Additional Details form when the Use If Any Check field is selected. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: You can access the Unbundled Billing Additional Details form by selecting Additional Conditions from the Actions menu on the Billing Rules (Unbundled) form.

To suppress the billing (delivery fee) for a manual check:

  1. Select one of the following rules in the Based On field in the Billing Rules (Unbundled) form:

  • Amt per Check (One Per Voucher will Fire)

  • Flat Amount

  • Flat Amount / Paid EE (only once per EE)

  1. Select Use If Any Check in the Unbundled Billing Additional Details form.

  2. Select Exclude From Manual Check to prevent the system from processing billing on a manual check.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Setup Guide.

The following enhancements now reside on the Update Payroll Notes form that make it easier to enter a payroll note:

Enhancements to Employee PTO Register Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/PTO/Employee_PTO_Register_Form_Enhancements_QR202403.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/PTO/Employee_PTO_Register_Form_Enhancements_QR202403.htm

Enhancements to Employee PTO Register Form

You can now archive a PTO register for an employee using the Employee PTO Register form, which is available on the Work Centers|PTO Adjustments and Maintenance|Maintenance menu.

Archiving a PTO Register for an Employee

You can now archive a PTO register for an employee using the new Archive button. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Clicking Archive terminates a PTO register for an employee while keeping an historical record of that register so you can refer to this information when seeking answers about what was done in the past.

Note: You must select an Employee and Register Type to enable the Archive button.

When you click Archive a warning displays describing what happens to pending PTO requests. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

After clicking OK, the following message displays:

[Image: screenshot]

Clicking Yes clears the fields on the form. (Click No to return to the form to make updates.)

Note: After archiving a PTO register, the plan no longer displays in Employee Portal (EP) and the system no longer makes additional accruals.

After Archiving a PTO Register for an Employee

After archiving a PTO register, the system places it into an Archived folder as a read-only record. You can review the archived register’s historical information, including the Benefit End Date. However, you cannot make any adjustments to the archived register. (At this time, the Save and Delete buttons are disabled.)

When you select the Register Type field for an archived record, the list displays “Archived” at the end of the register type. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • The archived record’s numbering is based on the client, not the employee. Therefore, each number is unique.

  • Archived records display at the bottom of the list beneath any active records.

For more information, see the in‑product help or PrismHR Paid Time Off User Guide.

Enhancements to PTO Benefit Plans Form

The following enhancements now reside on the PTO Benefit Plans form, which is available on the Work Centers|PTO|PTO Plan Setup and Enrollment menu:

  • A new panel, First Year Prorated Amounts, now displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The First Year Prorated Amounts panel only displays if you select Flat Amount in the Calculation Basis field.

You can use the First Year Prorated Amounts panel to change the number of hours employees will receive in their first year of employment, which helps handle numerous PTO changes to ensure employee records are correctly maintained. For example, if a client allows five hours of PTO to accrue per pay period, they might only allow three hours to accrue per pay period for the employee’s first year, if they were hired from July to December.

Note: Note the following when using the First Year Prorated Amounts panel:

  • The system uses the employee’s hire date to determine which month accrual to use.

  • If the employee is a rehire, the system uses the last hire date to calculate their prorated amount.

  • The prorated information is only used for flat accrual plans.

  • To save the information, you must enter both a Month and a Flat Accrual Amount. Otherwise, an error message displays, “In row 1, Both a Month and Flat Accrual Amount must be selected.”

  • You can only add numeric values for the Flat Accrual Amount. Otherwise, an error message displays, “A valid number is required.”

  • The Add To Balance On First Accrual amount now only applies to plans with a Calculation Basis of Flat Amount, Flat Amount by Hours Worked, or Months Worked. (Plans that use other Calculation Basis options will display Add To Balance On First Accrual as read-only.)

In addition, a new tool tip now displays next to the Add To Balance On First Accrual field when you click the question mark (

[Image: screenshot]

). For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • If you enter a Add To Balance On First Accrual amount before selecting a Calculation Basis option, after selecting an option the system removes that amount.

  • If a current PTO Benefit Plan contains a Add To Balance On First Accrual amount, when you access that plan and select an unsupportedCalculation Basis option and click Save, the system removes that amount.

For more information, see the in‑product help or PrismHR Paid Time Off User Guide.

Data Security Restrictions for Terminated Clients

When a client is terminated in Prism, access to that client is now removed from Data Security.

In addition, if a Worksite Trusted Advisor (WTA) only had access to the terminated client, the WTA User is deactivated. If the client is set to be terminated in the future, the WTA is set to deactivate at the same time.

Note: Note: If a client is reactivated in the system, WTAs who were deactivated as part of the same process are not automatically reactivated. After reactivating the client, the administrator must also reactivate the corresponding WTA records.

Enhancement to Users Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/System/Users_Form_Enhancement_QR202403.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202403/System/Users_Form_Enhancement_QR202403.htm

Enhancement to Users Form

A new option, Commission Details, now displays on the Actions menu in the Users form for service providers with the Sales Representative Account Management role. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Selecting Commission Details opens a new form where you can record the Client ID and Employee Identifier. This information helps the system capture additional salesperson details to create an import pay file. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Adding the Commission Details Form to User Roles

To begin using this new form, you must first add it to the user role(s). (Note: If you have more than one user role to add to this new form, use the Bulk Role Update instructions.)

To add this menu item to a user role, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select or enter the Role ID.

  3. Click Add. The User Role Maintenance form displays.

  4. Select Commission Details from the list. (To quickly find this item, select System in the Type Filter box.)

  5. Click Accept.

  6. Click Save.

To change the role’s access to Inquiry or Deny for this item (the default is Full), click the Access item (the access changes to Inquiry, click it again to change the access to Deny). Click Save.

To add this menu item to multiple user roles, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select Bulk Role Update from the Actions menu. The Bulk Role Update form opens.

  3. Click Form and then select HRP.USERS*COMMISSION.DETAILS from the Search Processes list. (To quickly find this item, enter Commission Details in the Form Description field and click Refine, then select the form that displays.)

  4. A list of user roles displays.

  5. Grant access to each user role in the Access column. You can grant full access (Full) or read-only access (Inquiry). To deny access, click Deny.

  6. Click Accept. The User Roles form displays.

  7. Click Save.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRSystem Administration Guide.

JIRA # PD-16477
