Enhancements to Client Details Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Client/Client_Details_Form_Enhancements_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Client/Client_Details_Form_Enhancements_QR202406.htm

Enhancements to Client Details Form

The following enhancements now reside on the Client Details form, which is available on the Client|Change menu.

New Business Entity Type Option

A new option, B-Corporation, is now available as a classification option in the Business Entity Type field on the Classifications panel. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the B-Corporation option when classifying a for-profit corporation that has been certified by B Lab, which is a non-profit company that measures a company’s social and environmental performance against the standards in the online B Impact Assessment.

New Payroll Tab Fields

Two new fields, Days Until Prenote Auto-Activate and Prenote On Next Pay Date, now reside on the Payroll tab in the Client Details form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use these fields to override the system-level parameters at the client level:

  • Days Until Prenote Auto-Activate: Enter the number of days after which the system activates prenoted accounts that were successfully processed through a payroll. (If set to zero (0), this value indicates no prenote process.)

  • Prenote On Next Pay Date: Select the option to run a test case of direct deposit information before an EFT occurs:

  • No: Runs the prenote on the current date and does not wait until the next pay date.

  • Next Pay Date: Runs the prenote on the next scheduled pay date for an employee.

  • Next Banking Day: Runs the prenote on the next banking day.

Note: Note the following:

  • These field options determine if a client is going to run the prenote process. (Some clients do not need to run this process.)

  • When these fields are first added to the client level the Days Until Prenote Auto-Activate field is set to Null (blank) and the Prenote On Next Pay Date field is set as –Select– ,so the system continues to use the system-level values.

  • If there are values in the Days Until Prenote Auto-Activate and Prenote On Next Pay Date at the client level, the system uses them instead of the values at the system level.

Setting Field Security for Three Account Tab Fields

You can now set field security for the Payroll Check Account, Garnishment Check Account, and Receipts Account fields on the Account tab, so these fields that are normally required can be hidden for specific users.

To set field security for these fields:

  1. Access the User Roles form on the System|Change menu and select a Role ID.

  2. Locate the COMPANY.MASTER*MAINT.ACCOUNT process and select Field in the Security column. The Field Security Maintenance form displays.

  3. Click Add. The Field Security Selection form displays.

  4. Select the CHECK.ACCT, CHECK.ACCT.GARN, and INV.RECPT.ACCT fields checkboxes in the list and click Accept. The Field Security Maintenance form redisplays.

  5. Change the permissions for the fields to Hidden and the Required field to N. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Updating the permissions to Hidden and the Required field to N displays a message, “Warning: This is a required field. Hiding could prevent user from saving form.” Click OK to continue.

  1. Click Save. The User Roles form redisplays.

  2. Click Save.

New Time Sheet Tab Tool Tip

To help users understand how data is stored for projects with phases, a new tool tip now displays in the Detail Time Entry Parameters panel on the Time Sheet tab. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

This tool tip summarizes that the Detail Time Entry form in Employee Portal (EP) does not include the Project with phase field due to how the system stores data for phases, where the same phase code can be used with different projects or no project. Therefore, a “project with phase” is only available in the PrismHR core product.

New Contractors 1099 DOB Required Field

A new field, Contractors 1099 DOB Required, now resides on the Other tab. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can enable the Contractors 1099 DOB Required field to override an enabled Do not require DOB field (located on the System Parameters form). This is helpful if you require 1099 contractors to perform the onboarding process using Employee Portal (EP), which requires an employee’s date of birth.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

Enhancement to Divisions Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Client/Divisions_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Client/Divisions_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm

Enhancement to Divisions Form

A new panel, Misc GL, now resides on the Divisions form, which is available on the Client|Change menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the Misc GL panel to replace predefined wildcards with miscellaneous GL segments for divisions using the following columns:

  • Misc GL Count: The predefined wildcards display in nine rows in the Misc GL Count column, where the codes are always EEMDV01 through EEMDV09. (The program that evaluates the wildcards only looks for those values.)

  • Misc GL Description: This column’s values are for reference only. (These descriptions are stored in the client’s record.) The system automatically loads these values each time a division record displays.

Important! Any changes made to the descriptions affect all divisions in the active client.

  • Misc GL Segment: If appropriate, you can enter the Misc GL Segment value that replaces the Misc GL Count wildcard.

Note: During payroll processing, the system substitutes the GL segments for wildcards in GL account codes. These wildcards must also be included in the following setups:

  • GL setup in order to be processed into payroll accounting. (You can configure them in the G/L Setup form.)

  • PEO client accounting setup in order to be processed into client accounting. (You can configure them in the PEO Client Accounting form.)

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

Three new fields, Misc GL Count, Misc GL Description, and Misc GL Segment, now reside on the Projects form, which is available on the Client|Change menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use these fields to replace predefined wildcards with miscellaneous GL segments for projects in payroll accounting and PEO client accounting using the following columns:

  • Misc GL Count: The predefined wildcards display in nine rows in the Misc GL Count column, where the codes are always EEMDV01 through EEMDV09. (The program that evaluates the wildcards only looks for those values.)

  • Misc GL Description: This column’s values are for reference only. (These descriptions are stored in the client’s record.) The system automatically loads these values each time a project record displays.

Important! Any changes made to the descriptions affect all projects in the active client.

  • Misc GL Segment: If appropriate, you can enter the Misc GL Segment value that replaces the Misc GL Count wildcard.

Note: During payroll processing, the system substitutes the GL segments for wildcards in GL account codes. These wildcards must also be included in the following setups:

  • GL setup in order to be processed into payroll accounting. (You can configure them in the G/L Setup form.)

  • PEO client accounting setup in order to be processed into client accounting. (You can configure them in the PEO Client Accounting form.)

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Client/Worksite_Locations_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Client/Worksite_Locations_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm

A new panel, Misc GL, now resides on the Worksite Locations form, which is available on the Client|Change menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the Misc GL panel to replace predefined wildcards with miscellaneous GL segments for worksite locations using the following columns:

  • Misc GL Count: The predefined wildcards display in nine rows in the Misc GL Count column, where the codes are always EEMDV01 through EEMDV09. (The program that evaluates the wildcards only looks for those values.)

  • Misc GL Description: If appropriate, enter the Misc GL Description. For example, EEMDP01 = Segment 1 and EEMDP02 = Segment 2. (You can apply these misc segments to account codes for other areas besides pay, such as taxes or deductions.)

Important! Any changes made to the descriptions affect all worksite locations in the active client.

Note: This column’s values are for reference only. (These descriptions are stored in the client’s record.) The system automatically loads these values each time a worksite location record displays.

  • Misc GL Segment: If appropriate, enter the Misc GL Segment value that replaces the Misc GL Count wildcard.

Note: During payroll processing, the system substitutes the GL segments for wildcards in GL account codes. These wildcards must also be included in the following setups:

  • GL setup in order to be processed into payroll accounting. (You can configure them in the G/L Setup form.)

  • PEO client accounting setup in order to be processed into client accounting. (You can configure them in the PEO Client Accounting form.)

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

JIRA # PD-17095

========================================================================

Enhancements to Employee Details Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/HumanResources/Employee_Details_Form_Enhancements_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/HumanResources/Employee_Details_Form_Enhancements_QR202406.htm

Enhancements to Employee Details Form

The following enhancements now reside on the Employee Details form, which is available on the HR|Change menu.

Using a Worksite Trusted Advisor’s User ID as PTO Approver or Manager

Service providers can now enter a worksite trusted advisor’s user ID (who has access to the client) as the PTO Approver or Manager for the selected employee on the Work tab. (Previously, you could only enter an employee ID in these fields.)

Note: Note the following:

  • After a service provider enters a worksite trusted advisor’s user ID and presses Tab or Enter the following message displays, “The ID entered is for a user that is not an active employee in this client.” Click OK to continue.

  • You cannot select a worksite trusted advisor’s user ID from the Select Employee list, which displays after selecting the PTO Approver or Manager field.

  • After entering the worksite trusted advisor’s user ID, the Name recorded on the Users form displays next to the user ID.

  • An error message displays if the PTO Approver or Manager doesn’t exist, “User ID <XXX> was not found for <role>.”

  • An error message displays if the PTO Approver or Manager exists but does not have access to the client, “User ID <XXX> for <role> is not allowed for <client>.”

Using New Deduction Options

Selecting the new Deduction 1, Deduction 2, or Deduction 3 option in the Type field on the Deposit tab automatically populates the Method field as Fixed and the Amount field as 0.00. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors can select one of these options to associate the deduction code with the direct deposit information.

Note: Note the following when using the Deduction 1, Deduction 2, or Deduction 3 option type:

  • You must enable the VOLUNTARYDEDACH custom feature code on the System Parameters form to display these option types. (See Enhancements to Employee Deduction Details Form.)

  • If you select another option in the Method field the following message displays, “Only Fixed Method can be specified for a Deduction line.” Click OK to continue.

  • If you enter another value for the Amount field the following message displays, “The amount must be zero (0) for a Deduction line.” Click OK to continue.

  • You cannot set the Limit if you select one of these option types.

  • During ACH processing, the system processes the deduction (direct deposit) the same as it does for checking accounts, where it displays as a credit in the ACH reports and through to the bank file. (Note: These deduction options only apply to a checking account.)

Setting Field Security for Employee SSN and Benefits Thru Date Fields

You can now set field security for the Employee SSN field on the Personal tab and the Benefits Thru Date field on the Work tab, so these fields that are normally required can be hidden for specific users.

To set field security for these fields:

  1. Access the User Roles form on the System|Change menu and select a Role ID.

  2. Locate the EMPLOYEE.PER*MAINT.PERSONAL process and select Field in the Security column. The Field Security Maintenance form displays.

  3. Click Add. The Field Security Selection form displays.

  4. Select the EMPLOYEE.SSN and UNMASKED.SSN fields checkboxes in the list and click Accept. The Field Security Maintenance form redisplays.

  5. Change the permissions for both fields to Hidden and the Required field to N. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Save. The User Roles form redisplays.

  2. Locate the EMPLOYEE.PER*MAINT.WORK process and select Field in the Security column. The Field Security Maintenance form displays.

  3. Click Add. The Field Security Selection form displays.

  4. Select the PAID.THRU field checkbox in the list and click Accept. The Field Security Maintenance form redisplays.

  5. Change the permissions for the field to Hidden and the Required field to N. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Save. The User Roles form redisplays.

  2. Click Save.

New Tax Calculation Override Link

A new Tax Calculation Override link now displays in the Federal Tax Filing panel on the Tax tab when an employee has a tax override, such as an active tax override, a one-time record, or a miscellaneous tax override. (This enhancement applies to all tax overrides.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

When you select the Tax Calculation Override link, the Tax Calculation Overrides form opens, displaying the employee’s income tax overrides.

Note: The Tax Calculation Override link displays for service providers, worksite managers, and worksite trusted advisors who have Full access to both the Employee Details form and the Tax Calculation Overrides form. (This link also displays for users who have Inquiry access to these forms, but does not display if their access is set to Deny.)

Working with Termination Explanation After Employee Termination

You can now add, update, or delete a Termination Explanation on the Other tab after an employee has been terminated.

Note: This enhancement is only available for service providers.

Before adding, editing, or deleting a Termination Explanation for a terminated employee, you must first enable the new EDITTERM custom feature code in the System Parameters form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Required School District Error Message Updated on Tax Tab

The error message that displays when you save information on the Tax tab without entering a School District when this field is required has been updated. The error message now displays as follows:

[Image: screenshot]

New Worksite Manager Proxy Option on Actions Menu

You can now directly login as a worksite manager/worksite trusted advisor by selecting the new Worksite Manager Proxy option on the Actions menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Selecting Worksite Manager Proxy opens the Proxy Login form, where the Worksite Manager/Trusted Advisor option displays in the Activity field and the selected employee’s username displays in the User ID field. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

For more information, see the in-product help, PrismHR Client Administration Guide, PrismHRHuman Resources User Guide, PrismHR Onboarding User Guide, or PrismHR System Administration Guide.

Enhancements to Employee Fields Import Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/HumanResources/Employee_Fields_Import_Form_Enhancements_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/HumanResources/Employee_Fields_Import_Form_Enhancements_QR202406.htm

Enhancements to Employee Fields Import Form

The following enhancements now reside on the Employee Fields Import form, which is available on the Operations|Action menu:

  • Four new fields, Geocode, Override Geocode, Override Geocode ThruDate, and PSD Code, are now available to use during imports.

Note: Note the following:

  • You must spell these field names in the external data file exactly as shown above.

  • The Geocode and Override Geocode entries must be exactly nine digits in length.

  • The Override Geocode ThruDate entry must be a valid date. For example, 2/29/2024 is a valid date, but 2/29/2023 is not because there was no “leap year” for February 2023. Also, you must include either a forward slash (/) or a dash (-) in the date.

  • The PSD Code entry must be exactly six digits in length.

  • The system skips any invalid data and generates error messages in the report.

  • When you complete an import in the Employee Fields Import form that moves an employee to a new pay group, the system now updates the Pay Period in addition to the Pay Group on the Pay tab in the Employee Details form, so these types of errors no longer display during the payroll process.

  • Service providers can now enter a PTO Approver and Manager as a worksite trusted advisor (who has access to the client), using user IDs, in an import. (Previously, you could only use employee IDs.)

Note: Note the following:

  • User IDs are always in lowercase.

  • An error message displays if the PTO Approver or Manager doesn’t exist, “User ID <XXX> was not found for <role>.”

  • An error message displays if the PTO Approver or Manager exists but does not have access to the client, “User ID <XXX> for <role> is not allowed for <client>.”

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRHuman Resources User Guide.

Enhancement to Bill Pending Details Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Bill_Pending_Details_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Bill_Pending_Details_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm

Enhancement to Bill Pending Details Form

You can now place a bill-pending item on hold (taking it out of “in-progress” status and returning it to “time-entry” status) by editing its Bill Date, Event, and Bill Rate in the Bill Pending Details form.

Important! This process is not available for restartable payrolls.

To edit a bill-pending item to place it on hold:

  1. Reset the Payroll Calculation: Complete status to Payroll Calculation: Ready on the calculated payroll by finalizing the timesheets again in the Process Payroll form. (This step deletes any initialized vouchers, so the payroll is no longer initialized.)

  2. Select the bill-pending item on the Bill Pending form. The Bill Pending Details form displays.

  3. Update the Bill Date and other pertinent information, which places the bill-pending item on hold.

  4. Click Save. After initializing the payroll again, the edited bill-pending item no longer displays in the initialized invoice.

Note: Note the following:

  • You cannot edit or delete an item that is “complete” (on a posted invoice).

  • You cannot edit or delete an item “in-progress” (on an initialized invoice).

  • You can edit or delete an item that was “in-progress,” if the timesheets are finalized (this forces payroll to reinitialize).

  • You can edit or delete an item that is “pending” (does not appear on any invoice).

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Processing Guide.

Enhancements to Data Import Tool

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Data_Import_Tool_Enhancements_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Data_Import_Tool_Enhancements_QR202406.htm

Enhancements to Data Import Tool

The following enhancements now reside in the Data Import Tool, which is available on the Operations|Import Processing menu:

  • A new import template, Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers, is now available. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers import template is only available for service providers.

To import this data, select Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers from the Import Template menu, and then click Find File to upload the file.

Note: Note the following:

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers form cannot import data using the Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers import template.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers form, but whose user role is also set to DENY for the Data Import Tool cannot view the Import icon on the Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers form.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers form can view the Employer W/C Accrual Modifiers import template, but cannot import data.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

  • If the Employer, State, and Effective Date fields already have a record in the system a warning displays, “There were duplicates found. The duplicates form will now be displayed and provide details.” Click OK to commit the update.

  • Two new fields, Keep Existing User Data and Remove Existing User Data, now reside on the Backup Account Assignment import template. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use these fields as follows:

  • Keep Existing User Data (default): Enable this field to keep all existing data.

  • Remove Existing User Data: Enable this field to override the existing list of users that are currently assigned to the client.

  • The Client Benefits import template now displays as Client Details (Benefits). For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the Client Details (Benefits) import template to import NAICS codes for the client to reduce the amount of manual work required.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration Guide.

Enhancements to Employee Deduction Details Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Employee_Deduction_Details_Form_Enhancements_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Employee_Deduction_Details_Form_Enhancements_QR202406.htm

Enhancements to Employee Deduction Details Form

The following enhancements now reside on the Employee Deduction Details form.

Note: You can access this form by selecting the Edit Detail icon (

[Image: screenshot]

) for an employee in the Recurring Deductions form.

  • A new field, ACH Options, now displays. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the ACH Options field to associate a deduction with a direct deposit account.

Note: Note the following:

  • You must enable the VOLUNTARYDEDACH custom feature code on the System Parameters form to display the ACH Options field.

  • Only one deduction type is allowed at a time. (An error displays if you try to select the same deduction type several times.)

  • The ACH Options field only displays for deduction code types that are Voluntary with one of the following Calculation Methods, as configured on the Deduction Codes form:

  • % of Gross Pay

  • % of Gross Earnings

  • Fixed Amount

Processing Deductions for ACH Account

When you select a deduction option in the ACH Options field and run a payroll the deduction process works as it always has, where the system recognizes the deduction code setup. However, instead of just recognizing the deduction, the system now routes the deduction amount to a direct deposit account.

After running the payroll process, the deduction amount displays on the Employee Voucher Deductions form in the voucher on the Deductions tab, where the status is DD1, DD2, or D*D3 on the Banking tab, according to the option selected on the Employee Deduction Details form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The deduction’s taxation is determined by the deduction code details set on the Deduction Codes form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  • You can now review an audit log to track changes made to the Employee Deduction Details form.

To view changes made to this form, select the Audit option on the Actions menu. The Audit Log Display form opens. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: You must add access to the Employee Deduction Details form in your user role to access the Audit option on the Actions menu in this form.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Administration Guide.

Enhancement to Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Employee_Payroll_Voucher_Reversal_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Employee_Payroll_Voucher_Reversal_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm

Enhancement to Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal Form

The system traditionally treats reversals (voids) done in the Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal form as if they are a regular checking or savings account.

To accommodate the new ACH deduction codes, Deduction 1, Deduction 2, and Deduction 3, the system processes them as it does for all other ACH types. Selecting Yes to the prompt that displays during ACH reversals ensures that the bank file includes a debit to the account, which takes the funds from the employee’s account. (Selecting No displays the ACH amount as the usual credit in the bank file.)

Note: See Enhancements to Employee Details Form for more information about the new ACH deduction codes.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Administration Guide.

Enhancement to Payees Form

Previously, users could only enter numeric characters (0-9) and the dash (-) character in the Bank Account Number field for the Garnishing Authority payee type in the EFT Parameters panel and the State Disbursement Unit payee type in the State Disbursement Unit Parameters panel on the Payees form. Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Payroll_Reversal_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Payroll_Reversal_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm

Enhancement to Payroll Reversal Form

The system traditionally treats reversals (voids) done in the Payroll Reversal form as if they are a regular checking or savings account.

To accommodate the new ACH deduction codes, Deduction 1, Deduction 2, and Deduction 3, the system processes them as it does for all other ACH types. (See Enhancements to Employee Details Form for more information about the new ACH deduction codes.)

During the payroll reversal process, the system now automatically reverses all ACH postings.

Note: This process does not reverse HSA ACH transactions.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration Guide.

Enhancements to Payroll Validation Report

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Payroll_Validation_Report_Form_Enhancements_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Payroll_Validation_Report_Form_Enhancements_QR202406.htm

Enhancements to Payroll Validation Report

The Payroll Validation Report, which is accessible on the Payroll|Reports menu, has been enhanced as follows:

  • You can now run this report for a manual payroll batch.

In addition, when you run the Payroll Validation Report the first time, the system now captures more errors for SUTA and workers’ compensation. (Previously, you had to run the report multiple times after fixing individual issues.) For example, the system now captures the following issues:

  • SUTA accrual rate not set up for the state

  • SUTA billing rate not set up for the state

  • Workers’ compensation class not set up on the Positions Classification record for the job

  • Workers’ compensation accrual modifier not set up for the state

  • Workers’ compensation billing modifier not set up for the state

  • Workers’ compensation template rate not set up for the job class and state

  • As part of the payroll validation process, the system now validates accounting for clients who use G/L templates and optionally, a PEO client account template, which are set up on the Control tab in the Client Details form. (During this validation, the system checks for new pay codes and deduction codes.)

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Reports guide.

Enhancements to Process Payroll Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Process_Payroll_Form_Enhancements_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Process_Payroll_Form_Enhancements_QR202406.htm

Enhancements to Process Payroll Form

The following enhancements now reside on the Process Payroll form, which is available on the Payroll|Action menu:

  • The message that displays when self-service payroll clients process payroll to the service provider has been enhanced.

The following message now displays, “You cannot make any changes once you submit payroll for processing. Are you sure you want to submit?”

  • Previously, if users did not set up workers’ compensation modifiers for a state, payroll initialization would fail and the system reported the accrual modifier as missing. If users then set up workers’ compensation modifiers, payroll initialization would fail again and report that the billing modifier was missing.

To help users understand this situation in a timelier fashion, the program that calculates workers’ compensation premiums now displays both errors on the first pass.

  • The payroll error message that displays after calculating a payroll with the RESTART-PAYROLL-CLIENT enabled where an employee is paid out of two payrolls now includes the employee’s name in the error message. (Previously, a zero (0) displayed in the error message instead of the employee’s name.)

For more information about the Process Payroll form, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Processing Guide.

Enhancements to SuperBatch Form

The following enhancements now reside on the SuperBatch form, which is available on the Operations|Action menu:

  • A new filter option, Cost Center, now resides in the ribbon on the SuperBatch form, which is available on the Operations|Action menu.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following when using the Cost Center filter option:

  • The cost centers listed in the Cost Center filter option are defined on the Cost Centers form.

  • Cost centers are assigned to clients in the Cost Center field on the Client Details form.

  • After selecting a cost center, the system filters the payrolls so only clients with the selected cost center display.

  • You can now adjust the lookback period for the SuperBatch process by enabling the SUPERBATCHLOOKBACK custom feature code on the System Parameters form. Enabling this custom feature code displays the SuperBatch Lookback Period field on the System Parameters form, where you can enable this field and enter the lookback period for the SuperBatch process. (Any numeric value entered here changes the lookback period the system uses for the Cutoff Date Up To field on the SuperBatch form.)

Note: For more information, see Enhancements to System Parameters Form.

  • You can now run the Unpaid Employees Report from an initialized payroll report review. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The payroll must be in the Payroll is ready for review state (

[Image: screenshot]

) for this report option to display.

Clicking Unpaid Employees Report opens the report parameters form, where you can display payroll information for employees who received no earnings in a specific payroll or during a payroll period.

  • Clients who are set up as Self-Service Payroll on the Payroll tab in the Client Details form and select No in the prompt that displays when submitting their payroll to processing now displays that payroll in the Payroll is ready to calculate state ( [Image: screenshot] ) instead of the Payroll is ready for review state ( [Image: screenshot] ) on the SuperBatch form. This ensures that they still have the ability to change the payroll and does not appear to service providers that it’s ready for review.

  • The buttons on the SuperBatch form now display a modern button style, which improves visibility.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Processing Guide.

Enhancement to Tax Calculation Overrides Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Tax_Calculation_Overrides_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Tax_Calculation_Overrides_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm

Enhancement to Tax Calculation Overrides Form

Two new fields, Status and Voucher, now reside on the Tax Calculation Overrides form, which you can access on the Payroll|Action menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the Status field to control how the system handles overrides during payroll processing using one of the following options:

  • Active (default): Processes overrides as they were originally done.

  • Inactive: Ignores overrides during payroll processing. (You can later reactivate an inactive override by changing this status.)

  • Onetime: Applies the override to one payroll processed within the entered date range.

Note: After a payroll processes with the Status set to Onetime, the override status changes to Inactive and the voucher number displays in the Voucher field. (You cannot edit or reactivate a onetime override after it is used. However, you can enter a new override for the same tax authority.)

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Overrides Guide.

Enhancement to Unbundled Billing Additional Details Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Unbundled_Billing_Additional_Details_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/Payroll/Unbundled_Billing_Additional_Details_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm

Enhancement to Unbundled Billing Additional Details Form

You can now use the Flat Amount / Invoice option in the Based On field on the Billing Rules (Unbundled) form to suppress the billing (delivery fee) for a manual check that occurs when a billing rule is processing live checks by enabling the Exclude From Manual Check field on the Unbundled Billing Additional Details form. (Previously, the Exclude From Manual Check field only displayed when the Amt per Check (One Per Voucher will Fire), Flat Amount, or Flat Amount / Paid EE (only once per EE) option was enabled.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • You must also enable the Use If Any Check field to display the Exclude From Manual Check field.

  • You can access the Unbundled Billing Additional Details form by selecting Additional Conditions from the Actions menu on the Billing Rules (Unbundled) form.

To suppress the billing (delivery fee) for a manual check:

  1. Select one of the following rules in the Based On field in the Billing Rules (Unbundled) form:

  • Amt per Check (One Per Voucher will Fire)

  • Flat Amount

  • Flat Amount / Invoice

  • Flat Amount / Paid EE (only once per EE)

  1. Select Use If Any Check in the Unbundled Billing Additional Details form.

  2. Select Exclude From Manual Check to prevent the system from processing billing on a manual check.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Setup Guide.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/PTO/PTO_Benefit_Plans_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/PTO/PTO_Benefit_Plans_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm

Enhancement to PTO Benefit Plans Form

A new field, Max Per Year, now resides in the First Year Prorated Amounts panel on the PTO Benefit Plans form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Enter the employee’s Max Per Year PTO hours for their first year of employment, so that employee no longer accrues PTO once they reach their maximum PTO hours. For example, this enhancement is helpful when you hire employees from January to March who will receive 24 hours of PTO, but employees hired in April would only receive 12 hours of PTO. Therefore, those employees hired in April will accrue 12 hours of PTO on their first payroll and then stop at 12 hours and will not receive the full 24 hours of PTO that the earlier-hired employees will receive.

For more information, see the in‑product help or PrismHR Paid Time Off User Guide.

Enhancement to Notification Control Panel Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/System/Notification_Control_Panel_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/System/Notification_Control_Panel_Form_Enhancement_QR202406.htm

Enhancement to Notification Control Panel Form

A new panel, ACH Processing, now resides on the Notification Control Panel form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the ACH Processing panel to schedule this time-based process and produce the ACH files.

Note: You must use the options in the ACH Processing panel in conjunction with multiple ACH processing.

To specify the daily start time for ACH processing, simply enter the User ID and the start time in the Daily ACH Start Time field (this field defaults to 05:00:00). Valid entries for this field must be entered in military time. For example, to start ACH processing at 1:00AM, enter 01:00:00.

To the right of the Daily ACH Start Time field a display-only process status displays, which matches the same control number that displays in the BE Notify panel.

In addition, the display-only Last Run Date/Time field displays the last date and time the process ran.

Note: Note the following:

  • If the notifications engine is already running, select BE Stop, then select BE Start before using the ACH Processing panel.

  • The User ID must have access to the ACH Processing form for external payroll.

  • The ACH processing start times only apply to the ACH Processing form for external payroll.

For more information about this enhancement, see the in-product help and the PrismHR ACH User Guide.

Enhancements to Purge Clients Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/System/PP_Purge_Client_Form_202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/System/PP_Purge_Client_Form_202406.htm

Enhancements to Purge Clients Form

The Purge Clients form has been enhanced with additional features and usability improvements. These enhancements make it easier and more intuitive for service providers to comply with laws regarding how long they can retain client and employee data, and allows clients to easily search for inactive clients, remove records, and download reports of purged records.

The Years of Inactivity field is used to select the number of years since the Client Status Date and the last employee voucher pay date. Selecting a value in this field populates the table with matching records.

Click Clear List to remove all items from the list.

Select the Rebuild Registers option to have tax registers rebuilt during the purge process with the purged employee voucher data removed.

Select Purge Clients to display a confirmation message. Select yes to begin the purge process, which removes the clients from the system.

Note: Note: This process cannot be reversed.

Once a purge is complete, the Download Purge Reports button can be used to download a report of clients removed from the system.

JIRA # PP-1299

New Tax Register Audit Inquiry Utility

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/System/PP_Tax_Register_Inquiry_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/System/PP_Tax_Register_Inquiry_QR202406.htm

New Tax Register Audit Inquiry Utility

Service providers can access a new utility to review tax amounts in registers and compare them to the total tax in payroll vouchers and check for any discrepancies. This utility automatically processes an audit once a week.

Note: This feature is only available for service providers.

Service providers can review the audit by accessing the Tax Register Audit Inquiry form by clicking System > View > Tax Register Audit Inquiry. This form displays a report including the number of registers that did not match the voucher tax totals, as well as all relevant clients, employees, and tax codes.

[Image: tax]

Note: Note: To have access to this form, the HRPY.WORK*REG.AUDIT.INQUIRY process ID must be added to the user role.

Click a link in the Register Type column to display a detailed report of all registers for the selected client or employee.

Using this form, service providers can verify if any registers have discrepancies with payroll vouchers and determine which registers need to be rebuilt.

JIRA # PD-16889

Enhancements to System Parameters Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/System/System_Parameters_Form_Enhancements_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202406/System/System_Parameters_Form_Enhancements_QR202406.htm

Enhancements to System Parameters Form

The following enhancements now reside on the System Parameters form, which you can access on the System|Change menu.

New Custom Feature Codes

Two new custom feature codes are now available:

  • SUPERBATCHLOOKBACK: Enabling this custom feature code displays the SuperBatch Lookback Period field, where you can adjust the lookback period for the SuperBatch process. (Any numeric value entered here changes the lookback period the system uses for the Cutoff Date Up To field on the SuperBatch form.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • This enhancement is only available for service providers.

  • The default for the SuperBatch process is the standard 95-day lookback period.

  • If you enable this field but do not enter a numeric value, the system defaults to the standard 95-day lookback period.

  • If you remove the SUPERBATCHLOOKBACK custom feature code, the system hides the SuperBatch Lookback Period field and reverts to the standard 95-day lookback period.

  • VOLUNTARYDEDACH: Enabling this custom feature code sets a voluntary deduction code to be paid through a specific direct deposit account. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The VOLUNTARYDEDACH custom feature code can only be set at the system level and is only available for service providers.

Select Feature Code List Updates

In addition to sorting the Feature Code column in the Select Feature Code list, you can now sort the Feature Description column. (Select Custom Feature Codes to access this list.) Also, you can now search for custom feature codes using the new Refine Search section. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

New Independent Contractors Section

A new section, Independent Contractors, is now available. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

The fields in the Independent Contractors section indicate how to pay 1099 contractors, so you can easily manage large groups of these employee types:

  • Do not require tax withholding: Enabling this field indicates that there is no federal or state tax required when an employee record is set as a 1099 contractor. After selecting this field, you can save employee details and process payroll without error if there are no federal and state taxes indicated for the employee.

  • Do not require DOB: Enabling this field indicates that an employee’s date of birth is not required when an employee record is set as a 1099 contractor. After selecting this field, you can save employee details and process payroll without error if there is no date of birth indicated for the employee.

Note: Note the following about the Independent Contractors section:

  • These fields do not apply to the New Hire form.

  • You can enable the 1099WITHHOLDING custom feature code to override an enabled Do not require tax withholding field, if there is an outstanding loan set on an employee record, which indicates that you must also enter state tax withholding.

  • You can override an enabled Do not require DOB field using the new Contractors 1099 DOB Required field on the Other tab in the Client Details form. This is helpful if you require 1099 contractors to perform the onboarding process using Employee Portal (EP), which requires an employee’s date of birth.

For more information, see the in-product help, PrismHR Payroll Processing Guide, or PrismHR System Administration Guide.

Enhancements to Client Details Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Client/Client_Details_Form_Enhancements_QR202409.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Client/Client_Details_Form_Enhancements_QR202409.htm

Enhancements to Client Details Form

The following enhancements now reside on the Client Details form, which is available on the Client|Change menu:

  • A new field, Bill Pending Location, now resides on the Billing tab. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To better automate any billing that is processed through the Bill Pending form, you can now enter or select the billing location in the new Bill Pending Location field.

Note: Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the Client Details form displays this field in read-only format and cannot enter or select a billing location.

  • A new panel, Notification Settings, now resides on the Other tab. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: This panel consists of a new Payroll Reminder Notifications field and the existing Payday Notifications and Payroll Submission Notifications fields that previously resided in the Other Options panel.

Service providers can now set payroll reminders at the client level using the Payroll Reminder Notifications field to send payroll reminders to worksite advisors and worksite trusted advisors if the payroll is still in timesheet entry status as the payroll’s completion date gets closer to the cutoff date. For example, if the payroll will no longer be available to worksite advisors and worksite trusted advisors as of 4/15/2024 and it is not completed, the system sends a reminder to those users on 4/13/2024 that payroll is almost due.

Note: When setting up payroll reminders, to enable notifications at the system level, you must select the Enable payroll reminder notifications field on the System Parameters form. (See Enhancements to System Parameters Form.)

However, if you enable Enable payroll reminder notifications on the System Parameters form, the system sends payroll reminders for all clients, except those that have the client-level Payroll Reminder Notifications field disabled.

  • A new field, Benefit Parent Client, now displays in the Other Options panel on the Other tab. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Assigning a numeric value in the Benefit Parent Client field allows you to group clients together for benefit purposes.

  • An updated error message now displays when users enter a worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor for the Payroll, Human Resources, Benefits, Risk, Sales, Coordinator, Broker, and Backup Assignments employee representative account types in the Account Assignments panel on the Account tab. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: You can only enter service providers in these employee representative account type fields.

  • To help automate the reverse wire process, a new field, Reverse Wire Account, now displays on the Account tab. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can enter a checking account in the Reverse Wire Account field that is associated with a reverse wire transfer.

Important! The reverse wire process does not work for internal processing. (You cannot make an entry in the Reverse Wire Account field if the active client is set up for internal ACH processing on the System Parameters form.)

Note: The system validates this checking account, so you cannot enter an account that is linked to an ACH originator set up for a reverse wire transfer in any other bank account fields, except for the reverse wire transfer account.

After entering the checking account number, the following warning displays:

[Image: screenshot]

Click OK to continue, then perform the tasks listed in the warning.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

Enhancement to Commission Maintenance Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Client/Commission_Maintenance_Form_Enhancement_QR202409.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Client/Commission_Maintenance_Form_Enhancement_QR202409.htm

Enhancement to Commission Maintenance Form

Previously, users were able to select a Based On option in the Commission Maintenance form that did not work with the selected Flat or Percent option, which resulted in the system calculating the gross wages flat commission as a percentage in the report output. (For example, the system calculated the commission as 50% of gross wages instead of a flat $50.)

Note: To access the Commission Maintenance form, select Commissions on the Actions menu in the Client Details form.

The system now validates that the following Based On options do not work with the selected Flat or Percent option:

  • Percent option:

  • Fixed Amount Group 1

  • Fixed Amount Group 2

  • Fixed Amount Group 3

  • Fixed Amount Group 4

  • Fixed Amount Group 5

  • Fixed per Paid Employee

  • Flat option:

  • Gross Wages

  • Admin Fees

  • Benefit Commission Type

  • Benefit Commission Percentage

  • Workers Comp

  • Workers Compensation Profit

  • Average Number Lives

  • Gross Profit

  • Tax Profit

  • Percent of Bill Code

  • Profits to Admin [Enter Bill Code in Based On]

Note: If you make these types of selections, an error message displays and you cannot save the record.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

Modernized Button Style on Forms

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Client/Updated_Button_Style_on_Forms_Enhancement_QR202409.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Client/Updated_Button_Style_on_Forms_Enhancement_QR202409.htm

Modernized Button Style on Forms

Buttons that display on some of the PrismHR forms have been modernized, which helps you accomplish tasks more quickly and efficiently. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Buttons on the following forms now display the modern style:

  • Global User Defined Fields: Use this form to create global user-defined fields.

  • Client User Defined Fields: Use this form to set user-defined fields on a client level.

Enhancement to ACH Originators Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Payroll/ACH_Originators_Form_Enhancement_QR202409.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Payroll/ACH_Originators_Form_Enhancement_QR202409.htm

Enhancement to ACH Originators Form

To help automate the reverse wire process, a new option, Reverse Wire Transfer, now displays in the Third Party Format field. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Performing a reverse wire transfer allows clients to determine the payment amount prior to posting payrolls, so the system places those funds into a file that is sent before payroll is completed/posted. (This ensures that the client has the funds before payroll is posted.)

Important! The reverse wire process does not work for internal processing. (System validation on the Reverse Wire Account field on the Account tab in the Client Details form will not allow users to make an entry in this field if the active client is set up for internal ACH processing on the System Parameters form.)

In addition, after you save a reverse wire transfer, you cannot use the ACH originator for employee direct deposits.

Note: You cannot make changes to a reverse wire payroll whose payment has been marked as received because the funds were already sent. (These payrolls display with green checkmarks, marking them as lockedPayment Received payrolls when viewing them in the SuperBatch and Process Payroll forms.)

After selecting Reverse Wire Transfer, the following new fields display:

  • Bank Name (required): Name of the program to generate the output .csv file to the bank (not the bank name).

Note: The client is responsible for setting up the title of the output file, which should include the file’s creation date and timestamp.

If you select the Wells Fargo option, the following new fields display:

  • Wells Fargo Sender Name (required)

  • Wells Fargo Sender Address 1 (required)

  • Wells Fargo Sender Address 2

  • Wells Fargo Sender City (required)

  • Wells Fargo Sender State

  • Wells Fargo Sender Postal Code

  • Days Before Invoice Date (required): Number of offset days before the invoice date that the system uses to calculate the effective date for a transaction. (The default is -1, which equals one day before the invoice date.)

Note: If you enter a positive number a message displays, “Are you sure? Usually, this process is run before the invoice date.” Click OK to continue.

Note: Note the following:

  • After selecting the Reverse Wire Transfer option, the following warning displays:

[Image: screenshot]

Click OK to continue, then perform the tasks listed in the warning.

  • If you change the Reverse Wire Transfer option to another option in the Third Party Format field, the following warning displays:

[Image: screenshot]

  • If you enable Generate Cachet ACH File Format in the Cachet panel, you cannot select the Reverse Wire Transfer option. If you try to select both options, the following warning displays:

[Image: screenshot]

Click OK to continue.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Setup Guide.

JIRA # PD-16209

========================================================================

Enhancement to Billing Rules (Unbundled) Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Payroll/Billing_Rules_Unbundled_Form_Enhancement_QR202409.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Payroll/Billing_Rules_Unbundled_Form_Enhancement_QR202409.htm

Enhancement to Billing Rules (Unbundled) Form

A new option, Per Active Employee Per Month, is now available in the Based On field on the Billing Rules (Unbundled) form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

The Per Active Employee Per Month option calculates the admin fee based on the client’s employee count on the first regular payroll of the month, using a tiered charge format. (The second payroll captures any new employees.)

Enabling the Per Active Employee Per Month option bills active employees for the month. For example, if the first payroll of the month has 100 active employees, they will be billed for 100 employees. On the second payroll if there is a new hire and a termination, they will still be billed for one employee on that payroll, since the new hire needs to be billed and the termination was active for part of the month.

Note: An edge case could occur that is currently not supported. When you calculate a payroll, the system determines the number of employees that are active at that time and once the payroll is posted, it commits counts to the employee records. If you calculate the payroll and add several employees or terminate employees and then post without recalculating, the system misses the new employees added/removed in the billing cycle.

Selecting the Per Active Employee Per Month option automatically initiates the following field updates that cannot be changed:

  • Batch Type: The Regular option is enabled.

  • The following fields are inactive:

  • Employee

  • Employee Type

  • Position

  • Home Location Code

  • Benefit Plan

  • Pay Class Equal To

  • Pay Class Not Equal To

  • Pay Code Equal To

  • Pay Code Not Equal To

  • Voucher Types

  • The following fields are hidden:

  • Benefit Offer Type

  • Benefit Plan Class

  • Benefit Plan Type Equal To

  • Benefit Plan Type Not Equal To

  • Position Equal To

  • All fields on the Unbundled Billing Additional Details form are inactive

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Setup Guide.

Enhancements to Data Import Tool

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Payroll/Data_Import_Tool_Enhancements_QR202409.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Payroll/Data_Import_Tool_Enhancements_QR202409.htm

Enhancements to Data Import Tool

The following enhancements now reside on the Data Import Tool:

  • Two new fields, Repeat Thru Date and Repeat Cycle, now reside on the Bill Pending import template in columns 16 and 17, and in the downloadable sample header file. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use these new fields to do the following:

  • Repeat Thru Date: Indicates when the recurring event starts and stops. (Use the MM/DD/YYYY date format.)

  • Repeat Cycle (required if Repeat Thru Date is used): Indicates billing frequency, which can be one of the following:

  • W = Weekly

  • B = Biweekly

  • M = Monthly

  • Q = Quarterly

  • A = Annually

  • The existing Global W/C Classification Rates import template is now available on the Import Template field. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Previously, you could only access this import template from the W/C Classification Rates form.

You can use the Global W/C Classification Rates import template to import changes to W/C rates at the system level.

  • Three new fields, Union Code, Track Phases, and Other W/C Coverage In Place, now reside on the Projects/Cost Codes import template in columns 9, 10, and 11, and in the downloadable sample header file. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use these new fields to do the following:

  • Union Code: Indicates the union code for the project. (The Union Project field must be enabled on the Projects form.)

  • Track Phases: Indicates if the phases of this project are tracked for job costing purposes.

  • Other W/C Coverage In Place: Indicates if Workers’ Compensation Insurance Coverage has been established for this project.

  • Four new fields, EEO Unit Number, EEO Override Location, EEO Federal Contractor and EEO Unique Entity ID, now reside on the Worksite Locations import template in columns 32, 33, 34, and 35, and in the downloadable sample header file. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use these new fields to do the following:

  • EEO Unit Number: The seven-character EEO Unit Number assigned to this location by the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission for reporting purposes.

  • EEO Override Location: The EEO Override Location if employees should appear under a different location on the alternate EEO download.

  • EEO Federal Contractor: Indicates if this worksite location of the client is a federal contractor and differs from the client or other worksite locations of the client.

  • EEO Unique Entity ID: Identifies the 12-character (no special characters) Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) number issued by the System for Award Management (SAM) to identify businesses and other entities that do business with the federal government. (This field is only necessary if the worksite location differs from other locations.)

Note: Only applies if the worksite location of the client is an EEO Federal Contractor.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Administration Guide.

JIRA # PD-17292

Enhancement to Detail Time Sheet Entry Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Payroll/Detail_Time_Sheet_Entry_Form_Enhancement_QR202409.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Payroll/Detail_Time_Sheet_Entry_Form_Enhancement_QR202409.htm

Enhancement to Detail Time Sheet Entry Form

Previously, when a salaried employee’s pay was split between two or more pay codes and the pay codes were marked to round to the period pay so the total amount of the salaried employee’s pay equals their standard pay, the system displayed the last detail time entry as a paid amount that was a few cents off the other detail entries.

Now, the system adjusts the last detail time entry so the time entry’s total matches the salaried employees’ actual salary amount. Therefore, the last detail time entry might be different due to rounding to ensure the total matches the employee’s salary. For example, when the system adds them and calculates to three cents more than the salary, it subtracts three cents from that last entry.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Processing Guide.

The following enhancements now reside on the Message Templates form, which is available on the System|Change menu:

JIRA # PD-17707

========================================================================

Enhancements to Notification Control Panel

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Work-Centers/Notification_Control_Panel_Enhancements_QR202409.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2024/QR202409/Work-Centers/Notification_Control_Panel_Enhancements_QR202409.htm

Enhancements to Notification Control Panel

The layout/processing of the Notification Control Panel, which is available on the Work Centers|Onboarding & Benefits|Workflow Setup menu, has been updated to make it more user-friendly and efficient. In addition, the labels and buttons that display in this form have been relocated in the sections, so you can easily identify if a process is running and enabled or disabled. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

New Notification Control Panel Layout

To process the notifications more efficiently, OB Notify and BE Notify now run as separate processes, so you can run them independently. As an outcome of this separation, the form layout and buttons more clearly show how the form functions:

  • The form layout now displays as two distinct sections: OB Notify displays as a separate section in the top half of the form, and the rest of the processes display in a separate section in the bottom half of the form.

Note: As part of this update, you can now run the BE Notify, Payday Notifications, and ACH Processing processes independently.

As part of the form layout, the background process now automatically runs BE Notify, Payday Notify, ACH Processing, and Payroll Reminders.

Note: If BE Notify is turned off, the other processes continue to run.

  • Updates to buttons:

  • The OB Start and OB Stop buttons were moved to the OB Notify section and display as Start and Stop, respectively.

  • The BE Start and BE Stop buttons were moved to the second section and display as Start and Stop, respectively.

Note: After clicking Start the system starts the processes and the button re-displays as Stop.

Updated Labels

To easily identify the state of processes and the location of their Stop/Start buttons in the Notification Control Panel, labels and their respective buttons now display as follows:

  • Each section now displays a label, ENABLED or DISABLED, that identifies their processing state.

  • The Start button displays the NOT RUNNING label next to it.

Note: When you click Start and then Save, the RUNNING label displays next to it.

  • The Stop button displays the RUNNING label next to it.

Note: When you click Stop, the SHUTDOWN REQUESTED label displays next to the RUNNING label. After clicking Save, the NOT RUNNING label displays.

New Payroll Reminders Process

You can now use the Payroll Reminders panel to schedule payroll reminders for worksite advisors and worksite trusted advisors if the payroll is still in timesheet entry status as the payroll’s completion date gets closer to the cutoff date. For example, if the payroll will no longer be available to worksite advisors and worksite trusted advisors as of 4/15/2024 and it is not completed, the system sends a reminder to those users on 4/13/2024 that payroll is almost due.

Note: This feature is only available for service providers.

To schedule a payroll reminder:

  1. Click Back Office. Select Notification Control Panel on the Operations|Action menu.

  2. In the Payroll Reminders panel, enter the number of hours before the payroll cutoff date and time to send the reminder in the Payroll Reminder Timing field.

  3. Click Save.

For more information about the Notification Control Panel, see the in-product help, PrismHR Onboarding User Guide, or PrismHR Benefits Enrollment User Guide.

  • Work Shift: Change the work shift for the selected employee in the new Shift Change form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  • Project Change: Change the project for the selected employee in the new Project Change form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  • Work Group: Change the work group for the selected employee in the new Work Group Change form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • An error message displays if you enter a past date.

  • When the future date occurs, the system automatically makes the employee’s change in the Employee Details form and in the payroll that it generates after the change is effective. (That is, if the payroll that coincides with the effective date of the change has already been generated, the new values do not automatically update. However, when that payroll posts, the change occurs in the next payroll that is auto-generated.)

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRHuman Resources User Guide.

Enhancements to Data Import Tool

The following enhancements now reside in the Data Import Tool, which is available on the Operations|Import Processing menu:

  • A new import template, Employee Resident Address, is now available. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The Employee Resident Address import template is only available for service providers.

To import this data, select Employee Resident Address from the Import Template menu, and then click Find File to upload the file.

Note: Note the following:

  • Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Employee Address form cannot import data using the Employee Resident Address import template.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Employee Address form can view the Employee Resident Address import template, but cannot import data.

  • Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data.

  • If the import file includes an address that fails validation or USPS-accepted address status, the system displays a dialog during the import process, Database File Import dialog entry, so you can either replace the incorrect address with a validated version or skip (keep) the current address. (The invalid address cannot be imported in any circumstances.)

Note: A prompt displays in this instance, “Click Replace to use the suggested address or Skip to not import the employee’s address.”

  • The Database File Import dialog entry does not display in the following instances:

  • When the address in the import file is a valid address with no address suggestions (this is equivalent to entering an address in the Employee Details form when no dialog displays suggestions to update the address).

  • When the fields in a row in the import data display an error (for example, characters instead of numbers in a zip code).

  • The Database File Import dialog entry does display when the address in the import file is a valid address and there is a suggested update (for example, address line 1 is 555 Elm and the suggested address is 555 Elm Drive).

  • A new field, ACA Offer Of Coverage, now resides on the ACA Offered Employees import template in column 6, and in the downloadable sample header file in the Data Import Tool. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use this new field to define an offer of coverage for eligible employees.

Note: Valid values for this required field are N, Y, YES, NO, No, Yes, yes, no, n, and y.

  • The system now displays an error message if you try to import an invalid code for the Bill on Wages or Hours field in the downloaded sample header file (column J) when using the W/C Billing Modifiers import template, “Processing Error on 4. Invalid code entered. Bill on Wages or Hours must be W or H.”

Note: The valid code for the Bill on Wages or Hours field must be either W to represent wages or H to represent hours.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration Guide.

JIRA # WSP-557

========================================================================

Enhancement to PTO Classes Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/MR_202501/Client/PTO_Classes_Form_Enhancement_MR202501.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/MR_202501/Client/PTO_Classes_Form_Enhancement_MR202501.htm

Enhancement to PTO Classes Form

Two new fields, Linked Accrual and Transfer To, now reside on the PTO Classes form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: This enhancement is part of the new Linked Accrual Plans Feature.

These new fields perform as follows:

  • Linked Accrual (default is disabled): Enable this field to mark the selected PTO Class Code as a linked accrual.

  • Transfer To: Transfers the selected PTO Class Code to another PTO class. (This field only displays if Linked Accrual is enabled.)

For example, if class A is linked/transferred to class B, class A does not display on the Transfer To list for other classes to transfer to (effectively preventing anything from transferring to it).

Note: Note the following:

  • The system will transfer the prior year accrued hours from the accrual register to the balance register for employees enrolled in a Linked Accrual PTO Register when the plan year is triggered.

  • If you set up a transfer to another PTO class code more than once an error message displays, “Transfer to <xxx> is already in use.” (You cannot have two PTO classes transferred to the same PTO class because this is a 1:1 relationship.)

  • If you enable Linked Accrual but do not select the Transfer To PTO class an error message displays when you click Save, “Transfer To PTO Class is required.”

  • The system tracks changes made to PTO Classes in the audit log.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

JIRA # PD-18270 and PD-18272

========================================================================

Enhancement to PTO Register Types Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/MR_202501/Client/PTO_Register_Types_Enhancement_MR202501.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/MR_202501/Client/PTO_Register_Types_Enhancement_MR202501.htm

Enhancement to PTO Register Types Form

A new option, Prior Year Accrual, is now available in the Trigger Method field on the PTO Register Types form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

The Prior Year Accrual method triggers the balance register to move the accrued PTO hours from the accrual plan to the balance plan. The system initializes the trigger date when the pay period crosses over into the year’s end. The plan is triggered at year end from the accrual plan to the balance plan, which could be an anniversary date or a fiscal date, and uses the option set in the Year-End Basis field. (Either way, the transfer of hours happens during the pay period in which that year-end date occurs.)

Note: This enhancement is part of the new Linked Accrual Plans Feature. The system will transfer the prior year accrued hours from the accrual register to the balance register for employees enrolled in a Linked Accrual PTO Register when the plan year is triggered.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

New and Improved Task Sheets

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/MR_202501/Documentation/New_Task_Sheets_MR202501.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/MR_202501/Documentation/New_Task_Sheets_MR202501.htm

New and Improved Task Sheets

To provide a better customer experience, new or improved task sheets are available in the in-product Help. In the table of contents, you can select the Task Sheets topic (located just below User Guides) to display a list of the most current task sheets. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

The following new task sheet was created:

  • Linking PTO Accrual Plans: This article details how to set up Linked Accrual Plans.

You can use the Linked Accrual Plans Feature to accrue employee PTO hours for transfer once the plan year ends. This feature consists of two PTO plans that you must set up so employees can accrue time for a plan year in one register that they cannot use until the plan year ends. After the plan year ends, the accrued hours move to a new register where employees can use their PTO hours. (Employees can have several different linked accrual plans, one for sick time, one for vacation time, and so on.)

To print any task sheet, right-click on the topic and select Print. You can also find PDFs of these task sheets on the Customer Resource Center.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/Billing/Billing_Rules_Unbundled_Form_Enhancements_QR202503.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/Billing/Billing_Rules_Unbundled_Form_Enhancements_QR202503.htm

Enhancements to Billing Rules (Unbundled) Form

The following enhancements now reside on the Billing Rules (Unbundled) form, which is available on the Client|Change menu:

  • An updated selector now displays when you select Billing Rule. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

The updated Select Billing Rules selector provides a more efficient way to search for a billing rule, allowing you to search by rule number or description, and filter obsolete billing rules (the default is No).

  • Two new fields, Obsolete and Obsolete Date, are now available. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use these fields as follows:

  • Obsolete: Enable this field to set the selected Billing Rule as obsolete. (The default is disabled.)

  • Obsolete Date: Enter or select the date when the Billing Rule becomes obsolete. (If you enable the Obsolete field and do not enter or select the Obsolete Date, the system automatically defaults to the current date.)

Note: The system tracks changes made in these fields in the audit log.

In addition, the system no longer displays the fees on payrolls for rules that are marked as Obsolete and does not calculate it through payroll.

  • Previously, unbundled billing rules with the Based On setting of Per Employee Per Monthdid not allow a credit.

The system now allows a credit for unbundled billing rules set to Per Employee Per Month, so these billing rules can now handle a negative amount.

For more information, see the in-product help, PrismHRBilling User Guide, or the PrismHR Payroll Setup Guide.

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The Variable Salary option only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form. (Custom feature codes are only available for service providers.)

You can use the Variable Salary option to accurately track the hours that salary-exempt employees actually work. For example, non-profit companies could use this option to track the work hours of their employees who are paid a standard salaried amount, so they can use these hours and their allocations for grant purposes. Note: Note the following:

  • The Auto Holiday Override Hours display on the employee’s timesheet when the criteria for the Auto Holiday Pay Rule and the Override Date exists in the current regular payroll after it is created.

  • Employees with Auto Accept Time Sheet hours have the Auto Holiday Pay hours deducted from their standard pay code hours.

  • Holiday Rules only apply to regular payrolls when the timesheet is created for a regular payroll.

  • Holiday Rules do not apply to payrolls marked as “replaces a scheduled batch.”
