New and Improved Task Sheets

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/Documentation/New_Task_Sheets_QR202503.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/Documentation/New_Task_Sheets_QR202503.htm

New and Improved Task Sheets

To provide a better customer experience, new or improved task sheets are available in the in-product Help. In the table of contents, you can select the Task Sheets topic (located just below User Guides) to display a list of the most current task sheets. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

The following existing task sheets were updated:

  • Rehiring a Terminated Employee: This task sheet outlines the steps for rehiring a terminated employee in PrismHR.

You can rehire an employee who was previously terminated using the Rehire form.

  • Setting General System Parameters: This task sheet outlines the steps for setting up system parameters in PrismHR.

You can set up general parameters on the System Parameters panel.

  • Setting Up Flat Amount PTO Accrual in PrismHR: This task sheet details how to set up a flat amount PTO accrual method by hours worked in PrismHR.

PTO benefit plans support a flat amount per hours worked PTO accrual calculation basis that complies with state-mandated paid sick leave laws.

  • Using SuperBatch: This task sheet outlines the enhanced SuperBatch process in PrismHR.

SuperBatch, a payroll processing hub, helps payroll processors oversee each payroll assignment without adding extra work or time. Using a streamlined workflow, you can accomplish all your payroll tasks—entering time data, checking for errors, finalizing and printing—directly from the SuperBatch.

  • Using the Enhanced Dashboard: This task sheet describes the Enhanced Dashboard in PrismHR.

The Enhanced Dashboard provides quick access to company information, favorite forms, and work centers from a central location.

  • Working with Deduction Codes: This task sheet outlines how to create a new deduction code, along with how to view and edit deduction code information on the Deduction Codes form.

Use the Deduction Codes form to maintain global deduction codes.

  • Working with Pay Codes: This task sheet outlines how to establish pay code information in PrismHR.

Use the Pay Codes form to establish pay code information and processing parameters required to process pay information in PrismHR.

The following task sheet was removed:

  • Understanding the SuperBatch Status Icons: SuperBatch Legacy, the original version of SuperBatch, has been removed from the system. Therefore, this task sheet that compared the SuperBatch Legacy icons against the enhanced SuperBatch icons, which was introduced in 2024, has been removed.

To print any task sheet, right-click on the topic and select Print. You can also find PDFs of these task sheets on the Customer Resource Center.

Enhancements to Employee Details Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/HumanResources/Employee_Details_Form_Enhancements_QR202503.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/HumanResources/Employee_Details_Form_Enhancements_QR202503.htm

Enhancements to Employee Details Form

The following enhancements now reside on the Employee Details form:

  • A new option, Variable Salary, now displays in the Pay Method field on the Pay tab. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The Variable Salary option only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form. (Custom feature codes are only available for service providers.)

You can use the Variable Salary option to accurately track the hours that salary-exempt employees actually work. For example, non-profit companies could use this option to track the work hours of their employees who are paid a standard salaried amount, so they can use these hours and their allocations for grant purposes.

Note: Employees whose Pay Method is set to Variable Salary will always be paid their per pay period amount regardless of the number of hours worked.

The following example explains the difference between standard salary pay and variable salary pay:

An employee makes $2,000 per pay period, with a standard hours of 80 hours, so their hourly rate is $25. They will work a variable amount of time, which should be reflected for allocation purposes, but they will always need to be paid $2,000 per pay period.

For the bi-weekly pay period, if they worked 80 hours they would receive $25 per hour or their standard pay of $2000. However, this employee might work RegA 40 hours and RegB 60 hours, so the company needs to track those hours but still pay the employee $2000. If they are listed as variable salary pay, I would expect the following to happen:

Standard salary pay:

Pay Code Hours Wages
Reg 80 25
Total 80 2000

Variable salary pay:

Pay Code Hours Wages
RegA 40 800 (40/100)*200
RegB 60 1200 (60/100)*200
Total 100 2000
  • You can now update the current payroll timesheet’s Work Shift value directly from the Work tab when updating the current employee shift assignment.

Note: This enhancement does not apply when using a Future Date.

When you enter or select a new Work Shift value, a message now displays to confirm whether you want this value to display on the current timesheet after clicking Save. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Updates to the current payroll timesheet are effective for:

  • Hourly employees when Auto Accept T/S is disabled on the Pay tab.

  • Hourly employees when Auto Accept T/S is enabled on the Pay tab.

  • Salaried employees when Auto Accept T/S is disabled on the Pay tab.

  • Salaried employees when Auto Accept T/S is enabled on the Pay tab.

  • You can now update the current payroll timesheet’s Project value directly from the Work tab when updating the current employee project.

Note: This enhancement does not apply when using a Future Date.

When you enter or select a new Project value, a message now displays to confirm whether you want this value to display on the current timesheet after clicking Save. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Updates to the current payroll timesheet are effective for:

  • Hourly employees when Auto Accept T/S is disabled on the Pay tab.

  • Hourly employees when Auto Accept T/S is enabled on the Pay tab.

  • Salaried employees when Auto Accept T/S is disabled on the Pay tab.

  • Salaried employees when Auto Accept T/S is enabled on the Pay tab.

  • A new section, Related, now resides in the Miscellaneous panel on the Work tab. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: This feature is only available for service providers.

After enabling the FAMILY_RELATIONSHIP custom feature code on the System Parameters form, you can use the Related section to track employees who are related to each other. (If you select a user who does not exist in the database an error message displays, “Employee ID <XXX> doesn’t exist.”)

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRHuman Resources User Guide.

Enhancements to Employee Fields Import Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/HumanResources/Employee_Fields_Import_Form_Enhancements_QR202503.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/HumanResources/Employee_Fields_Import_Form_Enhancements_QR202503.htm

Enhancements to Employee Fields Import Form

The following enhancements now reside on the Employee Fields Import form, which is available on the Operations|Action menu:

  • Three new fields are now available to use during imports:

  • Electronic 1095C Form: You can use the Electronic 1095C Form field to import a form that lists employees for a specified year, along with their Form 1095-C register status and the identity of the individual designated to receive an electronic Form 1095-C.

  • Retirement Year and Retirement Status: You can use the Retirement Year and Retirement Status fields to import employee retirement year and status information.

For example:

[Image: screenshot]

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following when importing these fields:

  • You must import both the year and the status at the same time (cannot import fields separately).

  • The Electronic 1095C Form value must be either Y, N, y, n, YES, NO, Yes, No, yes, or no.

  • The retirement year must be a valid year and can only be entered once (for example, 2021 can only display once).

  • The retirement status must be either N, E, or N,E.

  • The system skips any invalid data and generates error messages in the report.

  • An error message displays if the Electronic 1095C Form value is not valid, “Electronic 1095C Form Code <XXX> is invalid.”

  • An error message displays if the retirement year is not valid, “Retirement Year <XXX> is not a valid year.”

  • An error message displays if the retirement status is not valid, “Retirement Status <X> is not a valid status.”

  • An error message displays if the retirement year is already entered, “Retirement Year <XXX> is already on the Employee Record.”

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The Variable Salary option in the Pay Method field on the Employee Details form only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form. (Custom feature codes are only available for service providers.)

The Variable Salary pay method accurately tracks the hours that employees actually work. For example, non-profit companies could use this pay method to track the work hours of their employees who are paid a standard salaried amount, so they can use these hours and their allocations for grant purposes. (See Enhancements to Employee Details Form.)

JIRA # PD-17968

========================================================================

Updates to Backdated Leave Request Feature

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/Payroll/Backdated_Leave_Request_Updates_QR202503.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/Payroll/Backdated_Leave_Request_Updates_QR202503.htm

Updates to Backdated Leave Request Feature

To ensure that backdated leave requests are processed in a timely manner, the following updates now reside on the system:

  • Approval Pending on the Time Sheet Entry and SuperBatch forms now displays as Pending Actions. In addition, the yellow indicator on the Time Sheet Entry form now displays the number of employees in a regular payroll with pending backdated leave requests. (Backdated leave requests are those whose dates occur before the current timesheet’s pay period start date.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

[Image: screenshot]

To view pending backdated leave requests for all employees in the payroll who have backdated leave requests that display on the Backdated Leave Request Processing form, click the yellow indicator or the Outstanding Approval icon. A form now displays the Pending Backdated Leave Requests section, which provides more details. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Worksite managers who do not have access to an employee due to data entity security can still view that employee on the Approvals Pending form. However, they cannot view that employee on the Backdated Leave Request Processing form.

Note: Note that backdated leave requests only display on the Backdated Leave Request Processing form in the following conditions:

  • Only salaried employees display.

  • The backdated leave request must be approved.

  • The date of the backdated leave request must occur before the current timesheet pay period.

  • The employee must be part of the current timesheet.

  • The payroll for that timesheet must be in Time Entry status.

  • The payroll is a regular batch.

  • The backdated leave request pending actions do not display on the SuperBatch form when there are no pending approvals.

  • Pending Approvals on the Process Payroll form now displays as Pending Actions. In addition, the yellow indicator now displays the number of employees in a regular payroll with pending backdated leave requests. (Backdated leave requests are those whose dates occur before the current timesheet’s pay period start date.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The notes listed above for the Time Sheet Entry and SuperBatch forms also apply to this Process Payroll form update.

  • A new attribute, Backdated Leave Request, now displays on the Manual Check Entry form when you enter or select an existing manual check entry in the Reference field that was created by processing a backdated leave request. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: This enhancement is helpful in determining whether a manual check entry is for a backdated leave request or was entered manually by a user, so you can suppress administrative fees for manual checks created by Backdated Leave Request processing.

For more information, see the in-product help, PrismHR Human Resources User Guide, PrismHR Payroll Administration Guide, or PrismHR Payroll Processing Guide.

Enhancement to Employee Voucher Report

The system now displays the new Variable Salary option as “V - VSalary” in the Employee Voucher Report on-screen and .xls report output for those employees assigned this option as their Pay Method. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The Variable Salary option in the Pay Method field on the Employee Details form only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form. (Custom feature codes are only available for service providers.)

The Variable Salary pay method accurately tracks the hours that salary-exempt employees actually work. For example, non-profit companies could use this pay method to track the work hours of their employees who are paid a standard salaried amount, so they can use these hours and their allocations for grant purposes. (See Enhancements to Employee Details Form.)

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Reports guide.

Enhancement to Manual Check Entry Form

Previously, users could not create a zero pay stub when creating a manual check entry. To resolve this issue, you can now create a zero-dollar, non-negotiable pay stub after completing a manual check entry, which the system records. (You can print the pay stub by accessing the voucher from either the Process Payroll form or the Employee Voucher form.)

Note: This feature is only available for new payrolls, not previously processed payrolls.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration Guide.

Enhancements to Payroll Deduction Custom Export Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/Payroll/Payroll_Deduction_Custom_Export_Form_Enhancements_QR202503.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/Payroll/Payroll_Deduction_Custom_Export_Form_Enhancements_QR202503.htm

Enhancements to Payroll Deduction Custom Export Form

The following enhancements now reside on the Payroll Deduction Custom Export form when you select Essential Staff Care in the Output Format field:

  • Two new fields, Save Benefit Groups and Delete All Benefit Groups and the accompanying panel, now display. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the new fields to filter the report by benefit group for the Essential Staff Care carrier:

  • Save Benefit Groups: Enter new benefit groups by selecting Benefit Groups in the panel and then select groups from the list that displays. Select Save Benefit Groups to save them in the system. (Leaving Benefit Groups blank runs the report for all benefit groups.)

  • Delete All Benefit Groups: Select this field to delete existing benefit groups.

  • A new field, Only include MED, DEN, VIS Offer Types for the listed Benefit Groups, now displays in the new panel described above. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Enabling the Only include MED, DEN, VIS Offer Types for the listed Benefit Groups field allows you to only include this type of information for the Payroll Number or the pay date range for the Benefit Groups listed in the panel. (If you do not enable this field, the system includes all offer types for the listed Benefit Groups.)

Note: This field setting cannot be saved and if needed, it must be enabled each time you run the report.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Reports guide.

System Level Setting Client Level Setting Behavior
Disabled –Select– No warning
Disabled Enabled Warning functionality triggered
Disabled Disabled No warning
Enabled –Select– Warning functionality triggered
Enabled Enabled Warning functionality triggered
Enabled Disabled No warning

The Variable Salary option accurately tracks the hours that employees actually work. Removal of SuperBatch Legacy

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/Payroll/SuperBatch_Legacy_Removal_QR202503.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/Payroll/SuperBatch_Legacy_Removal_QR202503.htm

Removal of SuperBatch Legacy

SuperBatch Legacy, the original version of SuperBatch, has been removed from the system. Instead, you must use SuperBatch, the enhanced payroll processing hub, which was introduced in 2024.

Note: SuperBatch Legacy will no longer be searchable in PrismHR and you cannot add the SuperBatch Legacy form to any user roles. In addition, SuperBatch Legacy will no longer display in existing user roles or in menus.

For more information about using SuperBatch, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Processing Guide.

Enhancements to System Parameters Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/System/System_Pararmeters_Form_Enhancements_QR202503.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/System/System_Pararmeters_Form_Enhancements_QR202503.htm

Enhancements to System Parameters Form

The following enhancements now reside on the System Parameters form:

  • A new field, Enable payroll live check calculation warning, is now available. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Selecting the Enable payroll live check calculation warning field displays a warning message during payroll calculation to indicate that the system will create a live check. (This field is helpful in case the client never wants to create a live check during payroll processing.)

Note: The Enable payroll live check calculation warning field is disabled by default at the system level, but can be overridden at the client level.

  • A new field, Require Manual Payroll Reason, is now available. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

When you enable the Require Manual Payroll Reason field (default is disabled), the system sets the payroll Reason field as required on the Payroll Control form for manual payrolls.

  • A new option, Clear All Backup Account Assignments, now displays on the Actions menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: This option is only available for service providers.

Selecting Clear All Backup Account Assignments opens a form where you can clear all backup account assignments regardless of which clients are listed in the import file. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Clicking Process and then selecting Yes removes all backup account assignments, so they no longer display when you select Backup Assignments on the Account tab in the Client Details form. Use the Data Import Tool to import new backup account assignments.

Important! This process cannot be reverted.

Note: Note the following:

  • Users must have Full access to the Clear All Backup Account Assignments form and the System Parameters form to access this new form.

  • Client Access Security is not available on the Clear All Backup Account Assignments form.

  • The system does not create an audit log on the Clear All Backup Account Assignments form, but removing backup account assignments displays in the Client Details form.

For more information, see the in-product help, PrismHR Payroll Processing Guide, or PrismHRSystem Administration Guide.

JIRA # PD-18346, PD-18353, PD-18503, and WSP-974

Enhancement to Notification Control Panel

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/Work%20Centers/Notification_Control_Panel_Enhancement_QR202503.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/QR_202503/Work Centers/Notification_Control_Panel_Enhancement_QR202503.htm

Enhancement to Notification Control Panel

You can now set a user’s field-level security for the Start and Stop buttons on the Notification Control Panel using the Field option on the User Roles form. For example, you could hide these buttons to prevent users from starting or stopping the notifications engine during enrollments.

[Image: screenshot]

To set field-level security for the Start and Stop buttons on the Notification Control Panel:

  1. Go to the User Roles form on the System|Change menu.

  2. Enter or select the Role ID. (Note: If the user’s role is set to Inquiry for the Notification Control Panel, you cannot set field-level security even if the field security is set to grant access. If the user’s role is set to Full, you can only access the fields set in the field security settings.)

  3. Select Field for the Notification Control Panel (see screenshot above). The Field Security Maintenance form displays.

  4. Click Add. The Field Security Selection form displays.

  5. To enable field-level security for the Start and Stop buttons, click the following checkboxes:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Accept. The selected fields display in the Field Security Maintenance form.

  2. Select Enable in the Permissions column for each field. The permissions for these fields changes to Disable.

  3. Click Save. The User Roles form re-displays.

  4. Click Save.

For more information about the Notification Control Panel, see the in-product help.

Enhancements to Client Details Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202504/Client/Client_Details_Form_Enhancements_R202504.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202504/Client/Client_Details_Form_Enhancements_R202504.htm

Enhancements to Client Details Form

The following enhancements are now available on the Client Details form:

  • To ensure bills are correctly paid electronically for ACH clients, the following warning messages now display in these scenarios when setting the ACH Status in the Electronic Billing panel on the Billing tab:

  • When you select the Active option:

[Image: screenshot]

  • When you select the ACH by Location option:

[Image: screenshot]

  • When you select the ACH by Division option:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note: Click OK to continue, then enter the required information mentioned in the option’s warning message.

  • A new field, Maximum ACH Amount, now displays on the Control tab. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Important! The Maximum ACH Amount field is a placeholder for future development. At the time of this release, the field’s functionality is not working.

  • Two new fields, Miscellaneous Invoice Notification and Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal Notification, now display on the Other tab. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Enabling these new fields sends a notification for the client to emails listed in the additional notification emails for Payroll Finalization Notifications on the Control tab and to worksite managers/worksite trusted advisors who have the Payroll Approver H/R Role when the system creates a Miscellaneous Invoice Notification or an Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal Notification.

Note: Note the following:

  • The system defaults to sending the notification when the –Select– option displays.

  • If the Miscellaneous Invoice Notification field or the Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal Notification field is set to Enabled and the Payroll Finalization Notification field on the Control tab is set to No, the system does not send the email notification.

  • If the Miscellaneous Invoice Notification field or the Employee Payroll Voucher Reversal Notification field is set to Disabled and the Payroll Finalization Notification field on the Control tab is set to Email or No, the system does not send the email notification.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

Enhancement to PTO Register Types Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202504/Client/PTO_Register_Types_Form_Enhancement_R202504.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202504/Client/PTO_Register_Types_Form_Enhancement_R202504.htm

Enhancement to PTO Register Types Form

A new option, First of Quarter, is now available in the Trigger Method field on the PTO Register Types form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Selecting the First of Quarter method triggers when the pay period includes the first day of a new quarter for employees enrolled in a PTO Benefit Plan that has a calculation basis of Flat Amount. For example, if the first pay date in Q4 occurs on 10/7/2024, PTO accrual occurs during that payroll. (Quarters are typically calendar quarters: Q1 = January - March, Q2 = April - June, Q3 = July - September, and Q4 = October - December.)

Note: Note the following:

  • A warning message displays when you select First of Quarter, “Warning: Flat amount is the only PTO Benefit Plan Calculation basis supported for First of Quarter Trigger Method.” Click OK to continue.

  • You can only select the new Pay Date option as the Trigger Date if you select First of Quarter.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

Enhancement to Portal New Hire Import Form

The system now imports the Variable Salary option as a valid Pay Method during imports in the Portal New Hire Import form. When you use the Pay Method field code in an import, the Variable Salary option displays in the downloaded spreadsheet as “V.”

Note: The Variable Salary option in the Pay Method field on the Employee Details form only displays if the VARSALMETHOD custom feature code is enabled on the System Parameters form. (Custom feature codes are only available for service providers.)

The Variable Salary pay method accurately tracks the hours that employees actually work. For example, non-profit companies could use this pay method to track the work hours of their employees who are paid a standard salaried amount, so they can use these hours and their allocations for grant purposes.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRHuman Resources User Guide.

Enhancement to Cash Receipts Form

Previously, a warning message displayed in the Cash Receipts form when users entered several deposits for the same invoice. This message stated that the invoice number had already been used. (Users were required to click OK to continue and then manually enter the invoice number.) Users can now select duplicate invoice numbers, so this warning message no longer displays.

In addition, when users tried to enter an additional row by selecting the invoice number from the Outstanding Invoices list for the same invoice number, the system removed the cash receipt row that was entered. Users can now select an invoice number in this scenario without deleting the row.

Corresponding SFTP ACH File Now Written for SFTP Directory

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202504/Payroll/Corresponding_SFTP_ACH_File_Now_Written_for%20SFTP_Directory_R202504.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202504/Payroll/Corresponding_SFTP_ACH_File_Now_Written_for SFTP_Directory_R202504.htm

Corresponding SFTP ACH File Now Written for SFTP Directory

After the system writes an ACH file to the SFTP Directory during multiple file ACH processing, it creates a new corresponding SFTP ACH file with a suffix, _STFP_COMPLETE, which it writes to the STFP Directory to ensure that the ACH file is complete.

Note: During multiple file ACH processing the system now displays “STFP complete,” indicating this process runs as expected for multiple ACH files.

[Image: screenshot]

JIRA # PD-19250

========================================================================

Enhancements to Users Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202504/System/Users_Form_Enhancements_R202504.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202504/System/Users_Form_Enhancements_R202504.htm

Enhancements to Users Form

The following enhancements are now available on the Users form:

  • A new Human Resources Role, Payroll - Print Garnishment Checks, now displays for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Previously, if the H/R Role for a worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor was set to Payroll - Prints Checks and that user had access to the Payroll Reports form, they could print both regular paychecks and garnishment paychecks.

To prevent worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors from printing regular paychecks and only allow them to print garnishment paychecks, you can now set their role to Payroll - Print Garnishment Checks. In association with this update, those users only assigned the Payroll - Prints Checks H/R Role can no longer print garnishment checks.

Note: After setting the Payroll - Print Garnishment Checks role assignment, it displays when you open the Payroll Reports form, which is only accessible from the Payroll Summary form or by selecting the Recent Payrolls view on the Enhanced Dashboard.

  • A new Account Management Role, Billing Representative, now displaysis now available for service providers. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Important! The Billing Representative option is a placeholder for future development. At the time of this release, the option’s functionality is not working.

The Billing Representative is the user who can approve ACH Billing threshold approvals for global-level and client-level approval policies.

Users can set the Billing Representative Account Management Role as follows:

  • Users with Full access to the Users form can set up a service provider user with the Billing Representative A/M Role, so they can approve ACH Billing threshold approvals.

  • Users with Full access to the Global Approval Policies form can create an approval policy and assign Billing Representative to the A/M Role. When the approval policy is triggered, a user with the Billing Representative A/M Role can successfully approve the action.

  • Users with Full access to the Approval Policies form can create a client-level approval policy and assign Billing Representative to the A/M Role. When the approval policy is triggered, a user with the Billing Representative A/M Role can successfully approve the action.

For information, see the in-product help, PrismHR Human Resources User Guide, or PrismHR System Administration Guide.

Enhancement to Approvals Pending Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202505/HumanResources/Approvals_Pending_Form_Enhancement_R202505.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202505/HumanResources/Approvals_Pending_Form_Enhancement_R202505.htm

Enhancement to Approvals Pending Form

You can now approve or deny approvals for the Maximum ACH Approval Policy, whose approvals display on the Approvals Pending form.

Note: The Maximum ACH Approval Policy is only available for service providers.

Note: Note the following:

  • When the pending approval is approved and the client is set to Disabled in the Worksite Payroll Approval field on the Control tab in the Client Details form, the associated payroll status updates from INITPEND to INITCOMP and the Approval status changes to Approved.

  • When the pending approval is denied, regardless of the client’s setting in the Worksite Payroll Approval field on the Control tab in the Client Details form, the associated payroll status updates from INITPEND to TSOKCOMP and the Approval status changes to Denied.

  • When the pending approval is approved and the client is set to Standard or Multistep in the Worksite Payroll Approval field on the Control tab in the Client Details form, the associated payroll status updates from INITPEND to AP.PEND and the Approval status changes to Approved.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRHuman Resources User Guide.

JIRA # PD-18228 and PD-19242

Enhancement to Process Payroll Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202505/Payroll/Process_Payroll_Form_Enhancement_R202505.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202505/Payroll/Process_Payroll_Form_Enhancement_R202505.htm

Enhancement to Process Payroll Form

The Restartable Payroll and Legacy Payroll features now prevent submitted payrolls (those whose status is set to INITPEND), that exceed a set ACH amount, from processing until they are approved by a Billing Representative. These submitted payrolls are those where the payroll processor clicks Yes when the “You cannot make any changes once you submit payroll for processing. Are you sure you want to submit?” message displays. (Note that this message does not display when payrolls are submitted in SuperBatch.)

Note: This enhancement is only available for service providers. In addition, existing Payroll Calculation Maximum check approval policies and Worksite approval steps still function as expected in conjunction with the ACH Maximum Approval Policy.

The following preconditions must be met to enforce a threshold amount requiring ACH approval from Billing Representatives:

  • The Maximum ACH Amount is configured at the global or client level on the Control tab in the Client Details form.

Note: For more information about the Maximum ACH Amount field, see Enhancement to Client Details Form.

  • The Payroll ACH amount exceeds the amount set in the Maximum ACH Amount.

  • Self-Service Payroll is enabled and Self-Service Restrictions is set to Finalize & Print on the Payroll tab in the Client Details form.

  • Enable the LEGACY-PAYROLL-GLOBAL custom feature code to use the Legacy Payroll feature.

Note: Note the following that occurs when the system triggers Maximum ACH Approval for a submitted payroll:

  • The payroll status is set to INITPEND.

  • The payroll status in the Processing Steps panel on the Process Payroll form displays as Payroll Calculation: Pending Approval.

  • An error message displays, “Payroll total ACH amount (<invoice total>) exceeds maximum ACH threshold for Client <client name> Client (<client number>).”

  • Any email services configured for the “ACH Maximum Approval” template type are sent to the configured Maximum ACH Approver.

  • The system creates a pending approval with the following information:

  • Approval Type: ACH Maximum

  • Approval detail: Payroll <payroll ID> total ACH amount (<invoice total>) exceeds maximum ACH threshold for Client <client name> Client (<client number>).

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Processing Guide.

JIRA # PP-1763

========================================================================

New Payroll Variance Analysis Dashboard

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202505/System/PP_Payroll_Variance_R05.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202505/System/PP_Payroll_Variance_R05.htm

New Payroll Variance Analysis Dashboard

The Payroll Variance Analysis dashboard is now available. Using this dashboard, employees can review relevant payroll information and compare two payrolls on a single dashboard to simplify the review process.

[Image: screenshot]

When the Payroll Variance Analysis dashboard is displayed, current payrolls in Calculated status display as tabs. Select a calculated payroll to compare it to payrolls in Finalized status using the Compare to Payroll field.

After selecting the two payrolls to compare, statistics for each payroll and the variance between them displays in the first section of the dashboard. In addition, a second section of the dashboard displays changes in employee records between the two payrolls, such as new hires, pay rate changes, and employment status changes. Select any category to display individual employees with a change between the two payrolls and the resulting variance in payroll totals.

Note: Note: When you select a category and view individual employees, select the Voucher link to display the employee’s Variance Voucher, which shows the difference between the finalized and initialized payroll. You can also select the Detail link to display a file audit of the change to the employee’s payroll.

This dashboard can also be downloaded by selecting Download Variance Detail. Clients can select what variance percentage displays as a warning on this dashboard using the Payroll Variance Percentage Warning field.

JIRA # PP-1860

========================================================================

Enhancement to System Parameters Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202505/System/System_Parameters_Form_Enhancement_R202505.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202505/System/System_Parameters_Form_Enhancement_R202505.htm

Enhancement to System Parameters Form

A new custom feature code, BNKACCTCUTOFFENFORCE, is now available in the Custom Feature Codes column. Enabling this feature code sets a cutoff time at the Bank Account level to override the system-level cutoff time configured in the Same Day Check Cut Off field on the System Parameters form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • This enhancement is only available for service providers.

  • When you enable this feature code and if you associate a payroll with a bank account which is past this cut-off time, then the system enforces the existing functionality to provide an error message and a hard stop when you try to finalize a payroll.

  • When the Payroll Check Account and Direct Deposit Account fields under the Account tab of the Client Details form have the Post Cutoff Time field on the Bank Accounts form set to a time prior to the current system time, then please note the following:

  • If both the Payroll Check Account and Direct Deposit Account accounts have different time set in the Post Cutoff Time field, then the system uses the lesser of the two times to compare with the current system time and then generates a hard payroll stop and displays an error message. However, if the lesser of the two cutoff times is after the current system time, the system allows to finalize the payroll.

  • If you populate the Post Cutoff Time field only for the Payroll Check Account account, then the system uses that as the cutoff time to compare with the current system time and then generates a hard payroll stop and displays an error message. However, if the cutoff time is after the current system time, the system allows you to finalize the payroll.

  • If you populate the Post Cutoff Time field only for the Direct Deposit Account account, then the system uses that as the cutoff time to compare with the current system time and then generates a hard payroll stop and displays an error message. However, if the cutoff time is after the current system time, the system allows you to finalize the payroll.

  • If you leave the Post Cutoff Time field blank for both the bank accounts, then the system defaults to using the cutoff time populated in the Same Day Check Cut Off field on the System Parameters form.

For more information, see the in-product help, PrismHR Payroll Processing Guide, PrismHR System Administration Guide, or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

JIRA # WSP-1407

Purge Clients Form Replaced

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202506/Client/Purge_Clients_Form_Replaced_R202506.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202506/Client/Purge_Clients_Form_Replaced_R202506.htm

Purge Clients Form Replaced

A new form, Inactive Data Deletion, has replaced the Purge Clients form. This enhanced form lets you delete customer data for clients who have been inactive for a certain number of years. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

The Inactive Data Deletion form consists of two panels:

  • Select Inactive Data to Delete: Displays inactive data for clients, so you can easily delete this customer data.

  • History: Search for data deletions using a date range. The system populates this panel based on data from the Batch Control Record. (This panel is collapsed by default.)

Note: Note the following:

  • The Inactive Data Deletion form is only available for service providers.

  • You can access the Inactive Data Deletion form by clicking [Image: screenshot] (Back Office), then select Inactive Data Deletion from the System|Utility Processing menu.

  • Clients must be inactive for at least four years before they can be deleted. The system determines inactivity by the duration of a client’s terminated status or the years since their most recent pay voucher, whichever occurs first.

  • You can search for a particular client (either by Client Name or Legal Name) in the table results using the Search box.

  • You can only select a maximum of 20 clients to delete at a time. If more than 20 clients display after setting the Years of Inactivity a message displays, “Please select a maximum of 20 clients per run.” Click OK to continue.

  • If no clients display after setting the Years of Inactivity, the Delete Client Data button is disabled.

  • If there are no vouchers, the Last Voucher Date and Years Since Voucher columns will be blank.

To delete files for an inactive client:

  1. In the Years of Inactivity field, select the minimum number of years a client must be inactive to display. The clients matching this criteria display.

  2. Select the clients to delete in the Clients table. (Click Client ID to select all clients that display.)

  3. Select Rebuild Employer Registers to allow employee voucher data to be removed from the tax registers. Disable this field to prevent employee voucher data from being removed.

  4. Once all settings have been verified, click Delete Client Data. A warning displays, “Permanently delete all data for the <number> selected clients?” Confirm the action to remove data for the displayed clients by clicking Yes. (Clicking No returns to the form.)

Note: This action cannot be undone.

  1. After a deletion is complete, click a link in the Clients Deleted column in the History panel to download a report of all clients removed from the system.

To search for data deletions within a date range:

  1. Open the History panel by clicking the plus sign ( [Image: screenshot] ).

  2. Enter or select the From and To date range. The system adjusts the display of data deletions to match the criteria.

Note: Note the following:

  • Searches can only return up to 1,000 employees at a time since only 1,000 employees at a time can be deleted.

  • You can click the link that displays in the Clients Deleted and Employees Deleted columns to download a list of records that were deleted. (The records are downloaded to a ZIP file.)

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

Enhancements to Approval Policies and Global Approval Policies Forms

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202507/HumanResources/Appr_Policies_and_Global_Enh_R202507.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202507/HumanResources/Appr_Policies_and_Global_Enh_R202507.htm

Enhancements to Approval Policies and Global Approval Policies Forms

The following enhancements now reside on the Approval Policies and Global Approval Policies forms:

  • A new option, Direct Deposit Change, is now available in the Approval Type field. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the new Direct Deposit Change option to require approval at the client or global level to store direct deposit information in the employee details record.

Important! There must be a client-level or global-level approval policy in place to use this feature. (Without an approval policy, the system immediately records any changes and applies them to the employee record, which is the current method.) In addition, the approval policy only applies when an employee changes, adds, or removes the Transit Number or Account Number in the direct deposit information.

When an approval policy is defined for a client using the Direct Deposit Change option and an employee, worksite manager, or worksite trusted advisor submits a new or updated direct deposit or deletes a direct deposit, the system sets the update to Pending status and an approval is required. (After approval, the direct deposit follows the regular prenote process, if one is in place.) However, if a service provider makes an update, the change does not go through an approval process and is immediately applied to the employee record.

Note: The approval is submitted either from an employee making an update in Employee Portal or from a worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor making an update in Employee Portal or in the Prism Core application.

When an approval is pending and a worksite manager or worksite trusted advisor tries to make a change, the following occurs on the Deposit tab in the Employee Details form:

  • “Approval Pending” displays next to the Direct Deposit Information panel header.

  • If they click Save or Save & Close a message displays, “A prior direct deposit change is waiting for approval. Your updates will discard the previous changes. Do you wish to continue?” Click Yes to discard the previous update.

  • A new Account Management Role, Direct Deposit Approver, is now available in the A/M Role field. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

[Image: screenshot]

You can set the Direct Deposit Approver A/M Role for global-level and client-level approval policies, so the user with this role can approve updates to direct deposits.

For more information, see the in-product help, PrismHRApprovals Guide, or PrismHRHuman Resources User Guide.

Enhancement to Pay Codes Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202507/Payroll/Pay_Codes_Form_Enhancement_R202507.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202507/Payroll/Pay_Codes_Form_Enhancement_R202507.htm

Enhancement to Pay Codes Form

A new field, Unpaid Variable Salary Time, now displays in the Processing Options panel on the Pay Codes form when you enable the Include in Variable Salary Pay field. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can select the Unpaid Variable Salary Time field to reduce an employee’s Variable Salary pay by the percentage of unpaid hours assigned to the Unpaid Pay Code (default is disabled). For example, if an employee makes $3000 per pay period and they submit 100 hours, where 90 hours are worked and 10 hours are unpaid. This indicates that the employee’s wages should be reduced by 10 hours, so the system reduces the wages for the pay period from $3000 to $2700. This calculation works as follows: $3000/10 hours of unpaid time is $300, so $300 is subtracted from the gross pay. (On the voucher, the Unpaid Time hours display as the number of hours in the time sheet entry for the unpaid pay code, but the unit rate and amount display as zero (0).)

Note: The system still allocates wages for the reduced amount, except the pay is reduced by the unpaid hours.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Setup Guide.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202507/System/Users_Form_Enhancement_R202507.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202507/System/Users_Form_Enhancement_R202507.htm

Enhancements to Users Form

The following enhancements are now available on the Users form:

  • A new Account Management Role, Direct Deposit Approver, is now available in the Account Management Roles panel. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: You can only assign this role to service providers.

The Direct Deposit Approver is the user who can approve direct deposit updates stored in the employee details record.

  • A new field, Security by, is now available on the Data Security form, which displays when you select Data Security on the Actions menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The Security by field is available for service providers with access to configure a worksite manager’s (WSM) Data Security.

You can use the Security by field to configure a user’s Data Security access hierarchy, so you can easily manage which employees the user can access.

The following chart displays a high-level overview of the Data Security access hierarchy used in association with the new Security by field:

[Image: screenshot]

The Security by field provides the following options:

  • Entity: User is granted access to all entries.

  • Manager Direct Reports: User is only granted access to their direct reports.

  • Manager Full Hierarchy: User is granted access to their direct reports and any employees that are assigned to or inherited by their direct reports.

  • PTO Approver Direct Reports: User is only granted access to their direct reports.

  • PTO Approver Full Hierarchy: User is granted access to their direct reports and any employees that are assigned to or inherited by their direct reports.

Note: Note the following:

  • The default is set to Entity for all existing users.

  • When you create a new WSM user, the Data Security access hierarchy is set to Entity by default.

  • When you set the Security by field to Entity, you can configure access for entries in the All Defined Entities table.

  • If you select options other than Entity, the table displays the list of employees that are directly related to the selected data security option in read-only format.

For information, see the in-product help or PrismHR System Administration Guide.

JIRA # WSP-2246

Enhancement to Commission Maintenance Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202508/Client/Commission_Maintenance_Form_Enhancement_R202508.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202508/Client/Commission_Maintenance_Form_Enhancement_R202508.htm

Enhancement to Commission Maintenance Form

A new Based On field option, Percent of Target Amount, and a new field, Target Amount, now display on the Commission Maintenance form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: You can access the Commission Maintenance form by selecting Commissions from the Actions menu on the Client Details form.

You can now configure commissions to do the following:

  • Percent of Target Amount option: Indicates that the commission is based on a percentage of the target amount. (This option must be set with the Percent commission amount option. The Flat or Percent field automatically defaults to Percent.)

  • Target Amount field: Enter the commission’s target amount, which is used in conjunction with the Percent of Target Amount option. (You can enter up to two decimals in this field. The system truncates values with more than two decimals.)

The Target Amount field value is an overall dollar figure the system multiplies by the Amount Percent value to calculate the salesperson’s commission payout amount. For example, a Target Amount set to 100,000 for a 30% of Target Amount Commission setup would pay out $30,000 as the Commission amount for the defined commission period.

Note: Note the following:

  • The system calculates the total commission as the Target Amount x Amount (percentage) defined on the Commission Maintenance form, divided by the number of invoices in the applicable timeframe. The calculated commission is split across all invoices in the Compute Commissions period (Begin Date - End Date), which corresponds to the configuration dates on the Commission Maintenance form.

Note: If the commission cannot be split evenly across all invoices, then the sum of all commission amounts across all invoices will still total the exact commission amount.

  • If you do not enter a Target Amount with the Percent of Target Amount option selected an error message displays, “Target Amount must be provided to save the record on line <number>.”

  • If you enter a Target Amount and do not select the Percent of Target Amount option an error message displays, “Target Amount cannot be applied for the Based On option selected. Please correct line <number>.”

  • if you select a Based On Item or Based On Plan option with the Percent of Target Amount option selected an error message displays, “You cannot apply both a client level based on type and a based on plan for the same record. Please correct line <number> to save any changes.”

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

Enhancements to Data Import Tool

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202508/Payroll/Data_Import_Tool_Enhancements_R202508.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202508/Payroll/Data_Import_Tool_Enhancements_R202508.htm

Enhancements to Data Import Tool

The following enhancements now reside on the Client Commissions import template in the Data Import Tool:

  • Three new fields, Keep existing data, Remove existing client commissions data for all client in the import file, and Keep existing data and update duplicates, now display. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Enabling these fields does the following:

  • Keep existing data (default): Retains existing data during the import and only adds or replaces data included in the file to the client.

  • Remove existing client commissions data for all client in the import file: Overwrites existing data in the Commission Maintenance form during the import. (The Commission Maintenance form is accessible by selecting Commissions on the Actions menu in the Client Details form.)

  • Keep existing data and update duplicates: Prior to creating new records, ensures the system looks for duplicates between the existing commissions data and the file upload to permit updates to those matching records for the Amount, Flat or Percent, and Target Amount fields, in addition to uploading new commissions configurations.

  • A new field, Target Amount, now displays as column 10 in the File Format section. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the Target Amount field to indicate the commission’s target amount, which is used in conjunction with the new Based On field option, Percent of Target Amount. (You can enter up to two decimals in this field. The system truncates values with more than two decimals.)

The Target Amount field value is an overall dollar figure the system multiplies by the Amount Percent value to calculate the salesperson’s commission payout amount. For example, a Target Amount set to 100,000 for a 30% of Target Amount Commission setup would pay out $30,000 as the Commission amount for the defined commission period.

Note: See Enhancement to Commission Maintenance Form for more information about the new Target Amount field and Percent of Target Amount Based On option.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration Guide.

Enhancement to Manager User Setup Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202508/System/Manager_User_Setup_Form_Enhancement_R202508.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202508/System/Manager_User_Setup_Form_Enhancement_R202508.htm

Enhancement to Manager User Setup Form

A new field, Security by, is now available in the Data Entity Security panel on the Manager User Setup form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The Security by field is available for service providers with access to configure a worksite manager’s (WSM) Data Security.

You can use the Security by field to configure a user’s Data Security access hierarchy, so you can easily manage which employees the user can access.

The following chart displays a high-level overview of the Data Security access hierarchy used in association with the new Security by field:

[Image: screenshot]

The Security by field provides the following options:

  • Entity: User is granted access to all entries.

  • Manager Direct Reports: User is only granted access to their direct reports.

  • Manager Full Hierarchy: User is granted access to their direct reports and any employees that are assigned to or inherited by their direct reports.

  • PTO Approver Direct Reports: User is only granted access to their direct reports.

  • PTO Approver Full Hierarchy: User is granted access to their direct reports and any employees that are assigned to or inherited by their direct reports.

Note: Note the following:

  • When you create a new worksite manager user, the Data Security access hierarchy is set to Entity by default.

  • Existing worksite managers default to their Data Security access hierarchy as established in the Security by field on the Data Security form, which is accessible by selecting Data Security on the Actions menu on the Users form.

  • When you set the Security by field to Entity, you can configure access for entries in the All Defined Entities table.

  • If you select options other than Entity, the table displays the list of employees that are directly related to the selected data security option in read-only format.

Note: A message displays in place of the list of employees for new users who have direct reports where the user record and user ID have not yet been saved, “User must be saved before we can display employee access.” (The employee list displays after you save the record and the form refreshes.)

For information, see the in-product help or PrismHR System Administration Guide.

JIRA # WSP-2372

========================================================================

Enhancement to Inactive Data Deletion Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202509/Client/Inactive_Data_Deletion_Form_Enhancement_R202509.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202509/Client/Inactive_Data_Deletion_Form_Enhancement_R202509.htm

Enhancement to Inactive Data Deletion Form

The Inactive Data Deletion form has been enhanced, so service providers can now quickly search for inactive Employees to deidentify their customer data. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the new Data Type field to quickly search for Clients or Employees who have been inactive for a certain number of years to potentially delete or deidentify inactive customer data. (Previously, you could only delete files for inactive clients.)

Note: To preserve data integrity, the system deidentifies employee data and removes any Personally Identifiable Information (PII). (The tool tip (

[Image: screenshot]

) displays this information.)

If you enable Employees in the Data Type field, three fields display, Years Terminated, Client ID, and Search, to help enhance your inactive data search. Note the following about these fields:

  • Years Terminated: Select the number of years, 7-20, since the employee was terminated.

Note: After you select a number from the Years Terminated field, the following message displays:

[Image: screenshot]

Click OK to continue.

  • Client ID: Enter or select the employee’s client ID. After entering or selecting this ID and moving your cursor off the field, the system immediately displays all inactive employee data for that ID.

Note: Employee IDs associated with more than one Client ID display. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  • Search: You can now search for client or employee data, depending on which Data Type you select. (Previously, you could only search for client data.) When the employee list displays, you can select all employees by clicking the check box next to the Employee ID column.

Note: To narrow down the list of employees that displays, enter the employee ID or the employee’s first or last name in the Search box. After clicking the magnifying glass icon (

[Image: screenshot]

) or pressing Enter, the employee list redisplays that criteria. (Searches can return up to 1,000 employees at a time since only 1,000 employees can be deidentified at a time.)

To deidentify files for an inactive employee:

  1. Select Employees in the Data Type field.

  2. In the Years Terminated field, select the minimum number of years an employee must be inactive to display. The employees matching this criteria display. In addition, a message displays, “Employee Inactive Data Deletion limited to 1000 employees per run.”

  3. To narrow the search, enter or select the employee’s Client ID. After entering or selecting an ID and moving your cursor off the field, the search immediately displays all inactive employee data for that ID.

  4. Select the employees to deidentify in the Employees table. (Click Employee ID to select all employees that display.)

  5. After verifying the settings, click Deidentify Employee Data. A confirmation message displays, “Deidentify all data for the <number> selected employees?” Confirm the action to remove data for the displayed employees. (The system replaces the attribute values in Column F.)

Note: This action deidentifies employee data (that is, it removes the data instead of deleting it) and cannot be undone.

  1. Once the deidentify process is complete, click a link in the Employees column in the History panel to download a report of all employees removed from the system.

Note: This downloadable report lists the company ID and the employee ID for all employees who were deidentified. However, no PII is shared.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRClient Administration Guide.

Enhancement to Data Import Tool

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202509/Payroll/Data_Import_Tool_Enhancement_R202509.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202509/Payroll/Data_Import_Tool_Enhancement_R202509.htm

Enhancement to Data Import Tool

Three new fields, Remove existing assignments, Replace existing assignments, and Keep Existing Assignments now display on the Client Account Assignments import template in the Data Import Tool. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

These new fields allow you to update existing records or add new records without including the entire list of users.

Enabling these fields during imports does the following:

  • Remove existing assignments (default): Removes existing assignments that are not included in the file.

  • Replace existing assignments: Replaces existing assignments with assignments included in the file but does not remove assignments that are not included in the file.

  • Keep Existing Assignments: Prioritizes keeping existing assignments and adds new assignments included in the file. (That is, if an assignment exists and is included in the file, the upload skips the value in the file and keeps the existing system values.)

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration Guide.

JIRA # PD-14302

Enhancement to Manager User Setup Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202509/System/Manager_User_Setup_Form_Enhancement_R202509.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202509/System/Manager_User_Setup_Form_Enhancement_R202509.htm

Enhancement to Manager User Setup Form

To control access to the Manager User Setup form for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors, service providers can now add field-level security for sMFA device expiration using the Field option on the User Roles form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • If the user’s access to the sMFA Device Expiration field on the Manager User Setup form is set to Enable, they can view that field and update the value.

  • If the user’s access to the sMFA Device Expiration field on the Manager User Setup form is set to Disable, they can view that field but cannot update the value.

  • If the user’s access to the sMFA Device Expiration field on the Manager User Setup form is set to Hidden, they cannot view that field.

To set field-level security on the Manager User Setup form:

  1. Go to the User Roles form on the System|Change menu.

  2. Enter or select the Role ID. (Note: If the user’s role is set to Inquiry for the Manager User Setup form, you cannot set field-level security even if the field security is set to grant access. If the user’s role is set to Full, you can only access the fields set in the field security settings.)

  3. Select Field for the Manager User Setup form (see screenshot above). The Field Security Maintenance form displays.

  4. Click Add. The Field Security Selection form displays.

  5. To enable field-level security for sMFA device expiration, select the Manager User Setup checkbox. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Click Save. The User Roles form re-displays.

  2. Click Save.

Enhancements to Employee Details Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202510/HumanResources/Employee_Details_Form_Enhancements_R202510.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202510/HumanResources/Employee_Details_Form_Enhancements_R202510.htm

Enhancements to Employee Details Form

The enhancements described in this release note are available on the Employee Details form.

Enhancements for Deidentified Employees

The following enhancements are associated with deidentified employees:

  • An error message now displays if you update information for a deidentified employee and click Save or Save & Close:

[Image: screenshot]

Click OK to continue.

Note: To deidentify employees, select Employees in the Data Type field on the Inactive Data Deletion form. (For more information, refer to the “Removing Inactive Customer Data” topic in the PrismHR Client Administration Guide, which displays when you select the help (

[Image: screenshot]

) icon in the Inactive Data Deletion form.)

  • The system now adds an audit log entry that displays the batch date when employees are deidentified and does not display deidentified employees in selector lists. (Deidentified employees can only be accessed by manually entering their user ID or name.)

  • When employees are deidentified, the following information in their employee record no longer displays:

  • Middle Name

  • Preferred Name

  • License Number

  • I9 details

  • Employee Number

  • Clock Number

  • Alternate ID

  • Property

  • Skills

Enhancements for Gender Designation and Preferred Pronouns

The following enhancements now reside on the Other tab:

  • Gender Designation: Only standardized gender codes are now available to set an employee’s Gender Designation Code.

  • Preferred Pronoun: Only standardized pronoun codes are now available to set an employee’s Preferred Pronoun Code.

Note: You can no longer create, update, or delete a Gender Designation Code or Preferred Pronoun Code. Instead, you must select a standard code from the list that displays in the Gender Designation and Preferred Pronoun fields. (See Enhancements to Self Identity Codes Form for a list of available standardized codes.)

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRHuman Resources User Guide.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202510/HumanResources/Self_Identity_Codes_Form_Enhancements_R202510.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202510/HumanResources/Self_Identity_Codes_Form_Enhancements_R202510.htm

Enhancements to Self Identity Codes Form

The following enhancements now reside on the on the Self Identity Codes form:

  • The list of available gender codes has been standardized, so service providers must now use the following codes that display in the Gender Designation search list to set an employee’s Gender Designation Code:
Code Description
A Agender
AP Apathetic
BI Bigender
DN Do Not Disclose
F Female
G Genderfluid
GQ Genderqueer
M Male
MA Maverique
NB Non-Binary
NL Not Listed
T Transgender
TF Transgender Female
TM Transgender Male
TRI Trigender
TWO Two-Spirit

Note: If a gender designation code in this table already exists, the system overwrites the description with the one used in this table. For example, if the code G already exists with the description “Genderqueer,” the system overwrites it as “Genderfluid.”

  • The list of available pronoun codes has been standardized, so service providers must now use the following codes that display in the Select Preferred Pronouns search list to set an employee’s Preferred Pronoun Code:
Code Description
AE ae/aer/aers
CO co/coself
EV ey/em/eirs
FAE fae/faer
H he/him/his
IT it/its
MER mer/mers
NE ne/nem/nirs
NONE I don’t have pronouns
PER per/pers
S she/her/hers
TH they/them/theirs
VE ve/ver/vers
VIR ve/vir/vis
XE xe/xem/xyrs
ZE ze/hir/hirs
ZIR ze/zir/zirs
  • Due to the standardization of the gender codes, the Save and Delete buttons are disabled since you can no longer create, update, or delete a Gender Designation Code or Preferred Pronoun Code. (You can only review the list of standardized codes.)

Note: You can continue to select the employee’s Gender Designation or Preferred Pronoun by selecting from the standardized list that displays on the Other tab in the Employee Details form.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRHuman Resources User Guide.

Enhancement to Pay Schedules Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202510/Payroll/Pay_Schedules_Form_Enhancement_R202510.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202510/Payroll/Pay_Schedules_Form_Enhancement_R202510.htm

Enhancement to Pay Schedules Form

Currently, the system sets the period end date the same as the pay date when a pay schedule is set up as Monthly, the Pay Day is set as End Of Month, and the Pay Period Ends is set to end on this day of the month after/before the pay date (as configured in the On this Day of Month After the Pay Date field).

This process has been enhanced, so you can now create a pay schedule for a monthly payment where the pay date occurs before the pay period. For example, a schedule can be set up with a pay period of 8/1/2025-8/31/2025 for a pay date of 7/31/2025, so the Pay Period Ends date is the same date as the Pay Day date.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Setup Guide.

Enhancements to Payroll Variance Analysis Dashboard

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202510/Payroll/Payroll_Variance_Analysis_Dashboard_Enhancements_R202510.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2025/R_202510/Payroll/Payroll_Variance_Analysis_Dashboard_Enhancements_R202510.htm

Enhancements to Payroll Variance Analysis Dashboard

The following enhancements now reside on the Payroll Variance Analysis dashboard:

  • Two column updates now display in the Batch Selection when you select Compare to Payroll:

  • The pay group description now displays as part of the Pay Group column. For example, BW1 - Biweekly, which indicates the BW1 pay group is biweekly. (Previously, the pay group description displayed in a separate column.)

  • A new column, Payroll Status, now displays the payroll status. For example, INITOK, which indicates the payroll is complete and submitted. (This status displays the same status as shown during payroll processing.)

For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  • The Payroll Variance Percentage Warning field now displays as Payroll Variance Warning, which reports the Amounts or Percentages threshold between the current payroll and the comparison payroll. (Previously, only the Percentages threshold comparison was available.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can now select one of the following variance options in the Payroll Variance Warning field:

  • Amounts: Displays threshold amounts. (There is no maximum amount for this option.)

  • Percentages: Displays threshold percentages between 0-100.

Note: A text box displays next to the Payroll Variance Warning field where you can change the amount or percentage number. (This number defaults to 10.) If you enter a number for Amounts that is greater than 100 and then select Percentages, the number reverts to 10 (default).

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Administration Guide.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2026/R_202603/Client/Positions_Form_Enhancement_R202603.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Enhancements/2026/R_202603/Client/Positions_Form_Enhancement_R202603.htm

Enhancement to Positions Form

A new field, Remote Position Classification, now displays on the Positions form.

You can use the Remote Position Classification field to designate an alternative position classification for remote employees of the same position.

Note: Note the following:

  • Entering a valid Remote Position Classification displays the position’s FLSA Exempt, EEO Position Group, and EEO Position Class details, if they apply to the remote position.
  • Users with FULL access to the Positions form can use the Remote Position Classification field to designate an alternative position classification for remote employees of the same position.
  • Users with INQUIRY access to the Positions form can view the Remote Position Classification field, but cannot designate an alternative position classification for remote employees of the same position.

For more information, see Defining Positions.

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
PD-17896 Worksite managers were unable to assign a cross-hired worksite manager (an employee who was not hired by the client) as a PTO Approver or Manager on the Employee Details form. This is fixed.
PD-18202 The system did not apply the change when users enabled Apply Current Hours Taken before applying Stop-Balance limits in the PTO Benefit Plans form and saved the record. This is fixed.
PD-18233 The system displayed a fatal error message during payroll calculation when an employee had the federal tax Override Type set to Add to Withholding on the Tax tab in the Employee Details form and that employee had zero hours (that is, 0.00) listed on a voucher. This is fixed.
PD-18236 The system displayed a fatal error message during payroll calculation when an employee had a value entered in the Other Income field on the Tax tab in the Employee Details form and a large Voluntary Deduction or Retirement Flat amount. This is fixed.
PP-1607 When a user added a new position classification, the classification displayed on the Client Details Audit form, despite never having been used. This is fixed.
PP-1616 When a user tabbed through the Group Benefit Plans form and there was no data in certain sections of the form as the user tabbed through, data would be incorrectly cleared from the form. This is fixed.
PP-1617 When a user viewed the New Hire form and resized the browser window, data could be deleted from the form. This is fixed.
PP-1624 When a multi-value grid such as the Custom Code Translation Table form had a blank row as a separator, users could navigate to the blank row with tab and make entries. In addition, blank rows were sometimes added to the last page of a multi-value grid. This is fixed.
PP-1626 When a user selected Manual in the Payroll Type field on the Payroll Control form, the user could only add a maximum of six employees to the batch. This is fixed.
PP-1646 When a user attempted to add a User Field for the Delivery Methods feature, the form for a client-level change displayed. This is fixed. Changes to the Delivery Methods feature now display the proper system-level change form.
PP-1655 When a Worksite Manager user selected the Support Team tab on the Enhanced Dashboard, the tab immediately closed after the user selected it. This is fixed.
PP-1658 When a user set the PEO Client Accounting template to Custom and selected Tab as the delimiter, the data opened as a web page instead of a .txt file. This is fixed.
PP-1676 When a user attempted to display the Org Chart form, the form incorrectly displayed a message that there was no available data. This is fixed.
PP-1677 When a new hire was added to a client, the Enhanced Dashboard and My Home forms did not display an updated employee total on charts. This is fixed.
RRT-5867 When users either entered a company ID after entering an employer ID or entered an employer ID after entering a company ID in the Quarterly Tax Export form, the system displayed messages that referenced the “employee ID” when it should have referenced the “employer ID.” This is fixed.
WSP-765 Clicking Cancel in the Global User Defined Fields form did not clear the selected information from the screen. In addition, clicking Cancel after clicking Save displayed the multi-value grid data from the previously selected Page Title, but did not actually select the Page Title or display any saved updates. This is fixed.
WSP-769 The Save and Delete buttons and the selector field links sometimes appeared active (although they did not function) for users whose role was set to Inquiry on the PTO Auto Enroll Rules form. In addition, the Line # links were not available for viewing purposes. This is fixed.
WSP-771 Users whose role was set to Inquiry on the Employee Work form were able to select some of the links in the Employment Verification panel and select a value, then access a different tab and save that update. This is fixed.
