New SuperBatch Process

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202403/Payroll/New_SuperBatch_Process_QR202403.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202403/Payroll/New_SuperBatch_Process_QR202403.htm

New SuperBatch Process

The enhanced version of the SuperBatch form/process is now available. This new interface includes updated icons, fonts, a payroll description, and filters. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To distinguish between the original version and the enhanced SuperBatch form, which resides on the Operations|Action menu, the original SuperBatch form name now displays as “SuperBatch Legacy” in the system.

Note: Note the following:

  • The system now uses the enhanced SuperBatch form as the default superbatch process.

  • All users who currently have access to the legacy version of SuperBatch (HRPY.WORKSUPERBATCH.V1) have been automatically reassigned access to the enhanced version (HRPY.WORKSUPERBATCH). However, to gain access to SuperBatch Legacy, users must now add it to their role.

  • If users enter SuperBatch in the search box or select it on the Operations|Action menu and they only have access to the enhanced version in their user role, only the enhanced SuperBatch form displays.

  • Enhanced SuperBatch uses the same calculation process and print all option, so it still functions the same way that the original SuperBatch (now SuperBatch Legacy) functions. (The system still calculates and prints the payrolls all at once.)

  • To ensure users have access to both forms, update their settings on the User Roles form by providing them access to SuperBatch if they need access to the enhanced version or SuperBatch Legacy to retain access to the original version. (Users may have access to both versions.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Using the Filtering Options

You can use the filtering options in the enhanced version of SuperBatch to limit the payrolls that display:

  • Pay Date Up To: Includes all incomplete payroll batches that require payroll processing and are due on or before that date. (The default is the Friday of the current week.)

Note: Note the following:

  • The system selects all payrolls by the pay date, not the cutoff date.

  • When the Pay Date Up To date is greater than the current date, the system selects all payrolls with a pay date greater than or equal to today’s date (minus 95 days), plus all payrolls from the current date to the entered pay date.

  • When the Pay Date Up To date is less than the current date, the system selects all payrolls with a pay date greater than the entered pay date (minus 95 days).

  • Payrolls will always display for the Pay Date Up To date minus 95 days. For example, if the date entered is 100 days in the past, the system displays payrolls 195 to 100 days in the past.

  • Payroll Processor: Payroll representative who is the current active user. In addition, this filter allows you to select all payroll processors. (The incomplete payroll batches assigned to that payroll processor display.)

  • Self Service: The client processes all or some steps of their own payrolls.

  • Payroll Type: The payroll batch type. For example, payrolls set to Regularly Scheduled are those payrolls automatically created by PrismHR.

The icons in the top-right corner of the SuperBatch form help you perform the following actions:

Icon — Description

Payroll Transfer [Image: screenshot] — Displays the SuperBatch Payroll Transfer form, where you can transfer all currently viewed payrolls or selected payrolls to another payroll processor. (Select the payroll processor and click Update.) Note: If you select multiple payrolls and then click this icon to change to a new payroll processor, only the payrolls you selected are updated, not those in the entire view.

Filter Selection [Image: screenshot] — Displays a search form, where you can enter information to narrow the payroll assignments that display. (Enter the search information and click Apply.)

Refresh Existing Filter [Image: screenshot] — Refreshes payrolls that display based on the existing user and selected filters/settings. Note: This filter can also act as a “reset” for payrolls.

Reset Filters [Image: screenshot] — If you filtered the payrolls to only display payrolls associated with a particular step, select this icon to refresh the display so all payrolls associated with the selected filters redisplay.

Working with the Ribbon

A ribbon displays the steps for the payrolls in-progress. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Each step displays the number of payrolls associated with it.

To further filter the payroll display, click a step in the ribbon to display all the payrolls in that step. (Some of these filters can include several statuses, which you can select as a group or individually.) For example, clicking Ready for Time Entry in the example above displays the payrolls matching that criteria:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: A right-angle arrow displays next to a step when you click it, so you can easily determine which step is selected in the ribbon.

Working in the Client Level Actions Area

You can easily access actions and reports, client and payroll details, and notes in the Client Level Actions area. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To do this: Select this:
Access additional actions for selected client or payroll Ellipsis ( [Image: screenshot] ) icon
Access Client Details form displaying selected client’s details Client name or client ID
Access Payroll Control form displaying selected payroll’s details Payroll number
Access Payroll Notes form for selected payroll or create a new note Notes ( [Image: screenshot] ) icon

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Processing Guide.

New Delete Imported Vouchers Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202403/System/New_Delete_Imported_Vouchers_Form_QR202403.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202403/System/New_Delete_Imported_Vouchers_Form_QR202403.htm

New Delete Imported Vouchers Form

A new form, Delete Imported Vouchers, now exists on the Operations|Utility Processing menu, so you can quickly delete vouchers that you imported using the Check History Import process. (Previously, users had to reach out to PrismHR Customer Support to complete this task.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: This feature is only available for service providers who have access to the payrolls that contain the voucher for deletion.

To delete imported vouchers, enter the Batch ID and click Delete. A warning displays:

[Image: screenshot]

Select Yes to delete the vouchers from the selected payroll.

Note: Only vouchers in completed payrolls can be deleted. If the voucher resides in a payroll that is not complete the following error displays, “Batch ID must be for a completed batch.”

Adding the Delete Imported Vouchers Form to User Roles

To begin using this new form, you must first add it to the user role(s). (Note: If you have more than one user role to add to this new form, use the Bulk Role Update instructions.)

To add this menu item to a user role, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select or enter the Role ID.

  3. Click Add. The User Role Maintenance form displays.

  4. Select Delete Imported Vouchers from the list. (To quickly find this item, select Operations in the Type Filter box.)

  5. Click Accept.

  6. Click Save.

To change the role’s access to Inquiry or Deny for this item (the default is Full), click the Access item (the access changes to Inquiry, click it again to change the access to Deny). Click Save.

To add this menu item to multiple user roles, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select Bulk Role Update from the Actions menu. The Bulk Role Update form opens.

  3. Click Form and then select EMPLOYEE.PAYROLL.VOUCHERS*DELETE.VOUCHER from the Search Processes list. (To quickly find this item, enter Delete Imported Vouchers in the Form Description field and click Refine, then select the form that displays.)

  4. A list of user roles displays.

  5. Grant access to each user role in the Access column. You can grant full access (Full) or read-only access (Inquiry). To deny access, click Deny.

  6. Click Accept. The User Roles form displays.

  7. Click Save.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Administration Guide.

New Copy Client Settings Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202406/Client/New_Copy_Client_Settings_Form_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202406/Client/New_Copy_Client_Settings_Form_QR202406.htm

New Copy Client Settings Form

A new form, Copy Client Settings, is now available on the Operations|Utility Processing menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: This feature is only available for service providers.

You can use the new Copy Client Settings form to copy client settings from one client to another.

To copy client settings:

  1. Enter or select the Copy From Client. The client’s name displays.

  2. Enter or select the Client ID in the Copy to Client panel. The Client Name displays.

  3. Deselect or select the attributes for this client in the What to Copy panel.

  4. Click Copy. The Existing Data panel displays existing client settings.

  5. Select the client settings to copy by selecting individual checkboxes or select the checkbox next to the File Copy column to select all settings.

  6. Click Update Existing. A warning message displays, “This process will override any existing records in the client. Are you sure you want to continue?” Click Yes to continue.

Note: Note the following:

  • Any custom work regarding copying client settings that PrismHR already performed does not apply to this new feature.

  • Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

  • Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the Copy Client Settings form cannot enter or select the Copy From Client or the Copy to Client.

Adding the Copy Client Settings Form to User Roles

To begin using this new form, you must first add it to the user role(s). (Note: If you have more than one user role to add to this new form, use the Bulk Role Update instructions.)

To add this menu item to a user role, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select or enter the Role ID.

  3. Click Add. The Copy Client Settings form displays.

  4. Select Copy Client Settings from the list. (To quickly find this item, select Operations in the Type Filter box.)

  5. Click Accept.

  6. Click Save.

To change the role’s access to Inquiry or Deny for this item (the default is Full), click the Access item (the access changes to Inquiry, click it again to change the access to Deny). Click Save.

To add this menu item to multiple user roles, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select Bulk Role Update from the Actions menu. The Bulk Role Update form opens.

  3. Click Form and then select COMPANY.MASTER*COPY.SETTINGS from the Search Processes list. (To quickly find this item, enter Copy Client Settings in the Form Description field and click Refine, then select the form that displays.)

  4. A list of user roles displays.

  5. Grant access to each user role in the Access column. You can grant full access (Full) or read-only access (Inquiry). To deny access, click Deny.

  6. Click Accept. The User Roles form displays.

  7. Click Save.

For more information, see the in‑product help or PrismHR Client Administration Guide.

New Employee Details Loans Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202406/HumanResources/New_Employee_Details_Loans_Form_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202406/HumanResources/New_Employee_Details_Loans_Form_QR202406.htm

New Employee Details Loans Form

A new form, Employee Details Loans, is now available by selecting Loans on the Actions menu in the Employee Details form. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Previously, selecting Loans displayed the Employee Loans form, which did not display the loans for the selected employee.

Now you can easily view all the loans currently active for the selected employee by accessing the Employee Details Loans form. In addition, you can quickly set up a new loan by selecting the Loan Maintenance link on this form, which displays a blankEmployee Loans form where you can select Set up new loan and complete the loan details.

Note: Note the following:

  • If no loans are available for this employee a message displays, “No loans for this employee.”

  • If the selected employee has an existing loan, clicking the link in the Loan Number column opens the Employee Loans form, where you can update employee loan information, track the payment of the loan, and view loan payments that were deducted from employee paychecks.

  2. Select or enter the Role ID.

  3. Click Add. The User Role Maintenance form displays.

  4. Select Employee Details Loans from the list. (To quickly find this item, select HR in the Type Filter box.)

  5. Click Accept.

  6. Click Save.

To change the role’s access to Inquiry or Deny for this item (the default is Full), click the Access item (the access changes to Inquiry, click it again to change the access to Deny). Click Save.

To add this menu item to multiple user roles, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select Bulk Role Update from the Actions menu. The Bulk Role Update form opens.

  3. Click Form and then select EMPLOYEE.LOANS*SHOW.ALL from the Search Processes list. (To quickly find this item, enter Employee Details Loans in the Form Description field and click Refine, then select the form that displays.)

  4. A list of user roles displays.

  5. Grant access to each user role in the Access column. You can grant full access (Full) or read-only access (Inquiry). To deny access, click Deny.

  6. Click Accept. The User Roles form displays.

  7. Click Save.

For more information about the Employee Details Loans form, see the in-product help or PrismHRHuman Resources User Guide.

New Unbundled Billing Rules Import Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202406/System/New_Unbundled_Billing_Rules_Import_Export_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202406/System/New_Unbundled_Billing_Rules_Import_Export_QR202406.htm

New Unbundled Billing Rules Import Form

A new form, Unbundled Billing Rules Import form, now resides on the Operations|Action menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: This form is only available for service providers.

You can use the Unbundled Billing Rules Import form to import multiple unbundled billing rules for clients associated with a specific bill code.

Note: Client Access Group security is enabled on this form.

To import unbundled billing rules:

  1. Enter or select the Client IDs. (You can select multiple clients from the Select Clients list at once.) The Client Name displays next to each client. (If left blank, the system selects all clients.)

  2. Enter or select the Bill Codes. The Bill Description displays next to each client. (If left blank, the system selects all bill codes.)

  3. Select Download Spreadsheet. A progress dialog displays the processing steps.

  4. Click Close. A separate Downloads window displays the name of the .csv file that the system created. (Click Open file to view the downloaded file.)

Note: The first row in the downloaded file displays information about the first rule and the multi-value fields, which are separated by a pipe delimiter (|).

  1. If necessary, update the information in this spreadsheet before proceeding.

  2. Enter the Import Name.

  3. Select Upload File. Click Add Files and select the file to upload, then click Start Upload.

Note: The file must be in .csv format.

  1. Click Close. The uploaded filename displays.

  2. Click Import. A progress dialog displays the processing steps.

  3. Click Close.

  4. Click Transaction Report to display a link to a report that contains the unbundled billing rules transactions.

Note: The Transaction Report displays “Skipped” for any column in a row that has valid data but was not imported because a required row contained invalid data. (All invalid data displays in the Transaction Report.)

  1. Click Error Report to display a link to a .csv file that details the errors that occurred during the import. (The system does not import any rows listed in the error file and only imports rows where all data in the row is valid.)

Note: The Error Report link only displays if errors occurred during the import, which confirms that the system is unable to perform the import.

Note: Note the following:

  • You can only select active clients in the Client ID field.

  • If you enter an inactive client or a client that you are not allowed to access the following error message displays, “Invalid Client ID.”

Adding New Rules to an Import

Using the import process, you can define new rules that the system adds to the Billing Rules (Unbundled) form. To do this, you must enter the rule as NEW. For example:

  • Row 1 - NEW: Contains all the rule details and all the multi-value details associated using a pipe delimiter

  • Row 2 - NEW: Contains all the rule details and all the multi-value details associated using a pipe delimiter

Note: Note the following:

  • Rules display one row after another using sequential numbers. Therefore, do not use a numeric value after each row.

  • If there are any errors, they display in the error report. (You can view errors by clicking Error Report.)

Define the following information for the import:

Field Details Description
Client ID Unique identifier for the client.
Rule This field is pre-defined. Note: If you create a NEW rule, the next sequential value is selected. Existing Billing Rule ID, or New Rule to create a new unbundled billing rule. The system automatically assigns an ID.
Rule Description This is a free-form field where you can enter the description. Describes the rule. (This description cannot exceed 40 characters.)
Rate Allows numeric value up to 4 decimal places. Billing Rate. The system uses this in conjunction with the Based On value.
Based On Codes used as basis for calculating unbundled billing rules. Based On value, which represents the logic to use when calculating the rate.
Rule Start Date Date format MM/DD/YYYY. Rule Start Date when this rule begins.
Rule End Date Date format MM/DD/YYYY. Rule End Date when this rule ends.
Voucher Types Allowed types: - R: Regular - V: Vacation - S: Supplemental - A: Arrearage - H: Adjustment > Note: Note: - If only Regular applies, use R. - If all types apply, use RVSHA. Voucher Types to which a billing rule applies.
  • R: Regular
  • V: Vacation
  • S: Supplemental
  • A: Arrearage
  • H: Adjustment

  • If all types apply, use RVSHA. | Employee ID | Can use alpha-numerical characters. For example, P12345. | If the billing rule applies to a single employee, use the Employee ID. If the billing rule applies to all employees who do not have another billing rule assigned to them, leave this field blank. | | Batch Type | Allowed types: - R: Regular - S: Special - M: Manual > Note: Note: - If only Regular applies, use R. - If all types apply, use RSM. | Batch Type to which this billing rule applies. |
  • R: Regular
  • S: Special
  • M: Manual
  • If only Regular applies, use R.
  • If all types apply, use RSM. | Employee Type | Can vary by client (F, P, and so on). Setup: System | Change | Employee Types. Note: Obsolete types are not allowed. | Employee Type to which this billing rule applies, if any. For example, FT is a full time employee. | | Pay Group | Can vary by client (W, BW, and so on). If you use a Deduction Period, you must also use a Pay Group unless Based On is set to Flat Amount / Benefit Plan Class. | | | | Position | Varies by client.   • N: No | EE Tax Bill Rate | Allows numeric value up to 4 decimal places. | Bill Rate to charge on the code. | | EE Tax F/P | Allowed values: - F: Flat Rate - P: Percent | Indicate whether the amount is a Flat Rate or a Percent. |
  • F: Flat Rate
  • P: Percent | ER Tax Code | Employer-specific tax deduction codes. Setup: System | Change | Tax Deductions. | Employer tax deduction codes to associate with this billing rule. | | ER Tax Per Employee | Allowed values: - Y: Yes - N: No | Indicate whether to charge the code Per Employee. If not, then the system assesses the charge once per payroll batch. | | |
  • Y: Yes
  • N: No | ER Tax Bill Rate | Allows numeric value up to 4 decimal places. | Bill Rate to charge on the code. | | ER Tax F/P | Allowed values: - F: Flat Rate - P: Percent | Indicate whether the amount is a Flat Rate or a Percent. |
  • F: Flat Rate
  • P: Percent | The following “additional details” fields reside on the Unbundled Billing Additional Details form, which you can access by selecting Additional Conditions on the Actions menu in the Billing Rules (Unbundled) form. | | | | Use If Any ACH | Allowed values: - Y: Yes - N: No | Indicate whether to apply this billing rule on a voucher with ACH. |
  • Y: Yes
  • N: No | Use Per ACH Line | Allowed values: - Y: Yes - N: No | Indicate whether to charge a fee for each ACH line. |
  • Y: Yes
  • N: No | Use If Electronic Stub | Allowed values: - Y: Yes - N: No | Indicate whether to apply only to electronic pay stubs. |
  • Y: Yes
  • N: No | Use If Any Garnish | Allowed values: - Y: Yes - N: No | Indicate whether to apply this rule if there are any garnishments. |
  • Y: Yes
  • N: No | Use Per Garn Item | Allowed values: - Y: Yes - N: No | Indicate whether to charge a fee for each garnishment. |
  • Y: Yes
  • N: No | Use If Any Check | Allowed values: - Y: Yes - N: No | Indicate whether to apply the rule for any pay voucher. |
  • Y: Yes
  • N: No | Exclude From Manual Check | Allowed values: - Y: Yes - N: No | Indicate whether to suppress the billing (delivery fee) for a manual check that occurs when a billing rule is processing live checks. |

The system applies the rule once for any of the plans. To associate a fee with each plan, create a separate rule. | | FSA Plan Type Not Equal To | | Indicate each FSA Plan Type Not Equal To that should not be present to cause the system to apply this rule. | | Retirement Plan Equal To | | Indicate each Retirement Plans Equal To that if found on the voucher applies this rule. | | Retirement Plan Not Equal To | | Indicate the Retirement Plans Not Equal To that if not used on the voucher applies this rule. | ## Updating Existing Rules

When you update an existing rule in the Unbundled Billing Rules Import form, the import must identify the rule number being updated and include details that for the updated rule. For example, Rule 1 defines Pay Group A. If the updated rule then lists Rule 1 as Pay Group B, after the import finishes Rule 1 now uses Pay Group B.

After you import the updated rule, you can view the Transaction Report to determine which values were imported. (You can view errors by clicking Error Report.)

Note: Note the following:

  • Anything included in the file updates the current rule.

  • Running the import updates the rule or adds to the rule depending on the fields completed in the file.

  • Using a blank field removes any existing data. (If you only want to change one field, then you should download the rule, make the update to that field, and then re-import.)

Adding the Unbundled Billing Rules Import Form to User Roles

To begin using this new form, you must first add it to the user role(s). (Note: If you have more than one user role to add to this new form, use the Bulk Role Update instructions.)

To add this menu item to a user role, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select or enter the Role ID.

  3. Click Add. The User Role Maintenance form displays.

  4. Select Unbundled Billing Rules Import from the list. (To quickly find this item, select Operations in the Type Filter box.)

  5. Click Accept.

  6. Click Save.

To change the role’s access to Inquiry or Deny for this item (the default is Full), click the Access item (the access changes to Inquiry, click it again to change the access to Deny). Click Save.

To add this menu item to multiple user roles, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select Bulk Role Update from the Actions menu. The Bulk Role Update form opens.

  3. Click Form and then select HRPY.WORK*UPDATE.UNBUNDLED.BILLING.RULES from the Search Processes list. (To quickly find this item, enter Unbundled Billing Rules Import in the Form Description field and click Refine, then select the form that displays.)

  4. A list of user roles displays.

  5. Grant access to each user role in the Access column. You can grant full access (Full) or read-only access (Inquiry). To deny access, click Deny.

  6. Click Accept. The User Roles form displays.

  7. Click Save.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Setup Guide.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202409/Accounting/New_GL_Import_Entry_Form_QR202409.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202409/Accounting/New_GL_Import_Entry_Form_QR202409.htm

New G/L Import Entry Form

A new form, G/L Import Entry, is now available on the System|Change menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the G/L Import Entry form to quickly import account codes to the G/L setup by uploading a file for import and then viewing any errors that occurred during the import or viewing successfully imported rows.

To import G/L account codes:

  1. Enter or select the GL Template. The template name displays.

  2. Select the GL Type.

  3. Enable Overwrite Existing Account Codes to replace previously imported account codes. Otherwise, leave this field blank and the system will only import new codes.

  4. Select Download Template File to download a .txt file to your computer that contains the headings that match the selected GL Type. A separate window displays the downloaded file link.

  5. Click Open File. The spreadsheet template displays, where you can enter the G/L account codes information.

  6. Select Find File. Click Add Files and select the file to upload, then click Start Upload.

  7. Click Close. A progress window displays.

Note: If an error occurs a message displays, “It may be possible to recover from this error. Do you want to repeat your last action?” Click OK.

  1. Click Close. The import process extracts account codes from the external file.

Note: Note the following:

  • The import process skips any lines that contain invalid codes in the first column and reports them in the error report.

  • If you did not enable Overwrite Existing Account Codes, the import process skips any lines that would overwrite an existing account code and reports them in the error report.

  1. A preview of imported G/L account codes displays in the G/L Import Data panel.

Note: You can download a .csv version of this information by clicking Preview Report.

  1. If the import process encounters errors, you can select one of the following:

  • Done With Errors: Performs the import even though it contains errors.

  • Error Report: Any G/L account code errors from the import process display on this tab. Click Error Report to view them. (A browser window opens where you can download the .csv file that contains the errors.)

New Portal New Hire Import Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202409/HumanResources/New_Portal_New_Hire_Import_Form_QR202409.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202409/HumanResources/New_Portal_New_Hire_Import_Form_QR202409.htm

New Portal New Hire Import Form

A new form, Portal New Hire Import, now resides on the Operations|Action menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: This feature is only available for service providers. In addition, users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the Portal New Hire Import form displays the form in read-only format.

Clients sometimes do not have all the required new hire information, such as a Social Security Number, when they enter a new hire. Therefore, they must enter new hires in Employee Portal (EP), which requires less information. Because some clients must enter up to 500 new hires per day manually, service providers can now use the Portal New Hire Import form to quickly import new hires all at once from several clients who were registered in Employee Portal (EP). After uploading a file for import, you can view any errors that occurred during the import or view successfully imported rows.

Important! This new process applies as follows:

  • This form does not take the place of the New Employee Import process.

  • The imported employees will only display on the New Hire Dashboard in Employee Portal (EP). (See the Employee Portal (EP) online help and the Enabling the New Hire Dashboard article in the Customer Resource Center for more information.)

To import new hires from Employee Portal:

  1. Select Download Spreadsheet Template to download a .csv file to your computer that contains the new hires import headings in row 1. A separate window displays the downloaded file link.

Important! The first row of the import file must contain all the columns in the downloaded spreadsheet template in the same order. (Optional fields with no data can be included, but must be left blank.)

  1. Click Open File. The spreadsheet template displays, where you can enter the new hires information.

The spreadsheet template contains the following columns:

Column Description
Employer ID Employer ID associated with the new hire (required). Note: If the Employer ID or Client ID is not valid, the system does not validate the remaining data in that row. In addition, this Employer ID must be associated with the Client ID.
Client ID Client ID associated with the new hire (required). Note: You must set Electronic On-Boarding to Prompt or Always in the client-level settings on the Control tab in the Client Details form. Otherwise, the entire import will fail and an error message displays, “Client does not use Electronic On-Boarding. New Hires cannot be imported.”
First Name First name of new hire (required).
Last Name Last name of new hire (required).
Middle Name Middle name of new hire (optional).
Employment Status Current employment status associated with the new hire (required). Note: If there are restrictions on the Control tab in the Client Details form, only those employee statuses listed in the form can be used.
Employee Type Employment type associated with the new hire (required). Note: If there are restrictions on the Control tab in the Client Details form, only those employee types listed in the form can be used.
Work Location Work location associated with the new hire (required).
Position Position of new hire (required).
Start Date Date when new hire began employment (required).
Pay Method Pay method associated with the new hire (required): - S = Salary - H = Hourly - D = Driver - C = Commission
  • S = Salary
  • H = Hourly
  • D = Driver
  • C = Commission | Pay Rate | Pay rate that corresponds with the selected Pay Rate Basis for the new hire (required). | | Pay Rate Basis | Determines the new hire’s pay period (required): - H = Hourly - W = Weekly - B = Bi-monthly - S = Semi-monthly - M = Monthly - Y = Yearly |
  • H = Hourly
  • W = Weekly
  • B = Bi-monthly
  • S = Semi-monthly
  • M = Monthly
  • Y = Yearly | Standard Hours | Standard hours worked by the new hire during the pay period (required). | | Benefit Group | Benefit group of new hire that can be used to establish eligibility, coverage, and contribution rules for benefit plans (required). | | Pay Group | Pay Group to which new hire belongs (required). | | Employee Number | Employee number associated with the new hire (optional). | | Work Shift | Work shift associated with the new hire (optional). | | Department Code | Department code associated with the new hire (optional). | | Personal Email Address | Personal email address associated with the new hire (optional). | | Send Email | Email address system uses to send emails to new hire (optional): - Yes - No - Blank Note: If this column contains Yes, Null, or is not included in the import and the Personal Email Address contains an entry, the system sends a welcome email to the new hire. |
  • Yes
  • No
  • Blank | Division Code | Division where new hire works (optional). | | Project | Project associated with the new hire (optional). | | Work Group | Work group associated with the new hire (optional). | | Union | Union to which new hire belongs (optional). | | PTO Approver | Person who approves new hire’s PTO requests (optional). | | Manager | Person that new hire reports to upon employment (optional). | | Mobile Phone | Mobile phone number associated with the new hire (optional). | | Nickname | Alternative name associated with the new hire (optional). | | Seniority Date | Benefit start date associated with the new hire (optional). | | Preferred Language | Preferred language associated with the new hire (optional): - ENG = English - SPA = Spanish Note: Leaving this entry blank defaults to English. |
  • ENG = English
  • SPA = Spanish

  1. Select Upload File. Click Add Files and select the file to upload, then click Start Upload.

  2. Click Close. The uploaded filename displays.

  3. Select Preview Data. (If you select Preview Data before uploading the file, no information displays.) Information displays on the following tabs:

  • Errors: Any errors from the import process display on this tab. (Error messages specify the line number where the error occurred.) Click Error Report to view the new hires errors. (A browser window opens where you can download the .csv file that contains the errors.)

Note: If any field in a row fails, the entire row is not imported.

  • File Content: Any successful rows from the import process display on this tab. The following fields from the import display as a header:

  • Client ID

  • First Name

  • Last Name

  • Position

  • Start Date

  • Pay Rate

  • Benefit Group

Note: If no successful rows display in the file and you select File Content a message displays, “No New Hires to import.”

  1. Click Import Data to import new hires that display on the File Content tab. The “File content successfully imported” message displays. Click OK. The imported new hires display on the New Hire Dashboard in Employee Portal (EP) where the system generates a welcome code, so these new hires can obtain that code in the New Hire Dashboard.

Note: Any additional errors that occur during the import display in the existing errors list on the Errors tab.

  1. Click Confirmation Report to download a .csv report that contains the successfully imported new hires information.

Note: Columns that are blank indicate an unsuccessful data import.

Adding the Portal New Hire Import Form to User Roles

To begin using this new form, you must first add it to the user role(s). (Note: If you have more than one user role to add to this new form, use the Bulk Role Update instructions.)

To add this menu item to a user role, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select or enter the Role ID.

  3. Click Add. The User Role Maintenance form displays.

  4. Select Portal New Hire Import from the list. (To quickly find this item, select Operations in the Type Filter box.)

  5. Click Accept.

  6. Click Save.

To change the role’s access to Inquiry or Deny for this item (the default is Full), click the Access item (the access changes to Inquiry, click it again to change the access to Deny). Click Save.

To add this menu item to multiple user roles, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select Bulk Role Update from the Actions menu. The Bulk Role Update form opens.

  3. Click Form and then select HRPY.WORK*PORTAL.NEW.HIRE.IMPORT from the Search Processes list. (To quickly find this item, enter Portal New Hire Import in the Form Description field and click Refine, then select the form that displays.)

  4. A list of user roles displays.

  5. Grant access to each user role in the Access column. You can grant full access (Full) or read-only access (Inquiry). To deny access, click Deny.

  6. Click Accept. The User Roles form displays.

  7. Click Save.

For more information about the Portal New Hire Import form, see the in-product help or PrismHRHuman Resources User Guide.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202409/Payroll/New_Cash_Receipts_Import_Form_QR202409.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202409/Payroll/New_Cash_Receipts_Import_Form_QR202409.htm

New Cash Receipts Import Form

A new form, Cash Receipts Import, is now available on the Accounts Receivable|Action menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Column — Description

Description 2 — The description associated with the deposit (optional).

Line Type — The line type associated with the deposit.

Deposit Amount — The total amount that was deposited.

Deposit Reference — The unique reference ID associated with the deposit, which can include alphanumeric characters, but not spaces.

Posting Type — The posting type associated with the deposit. (Posting types are established on the Cash Receipt Rules form.)

Invoice Number — The invoice number associated with the deposit.

Amount — The amount that is applied to the deposit.

  1. Select Upload File. Click Add Files and select the file to upload, then click Start Upload.

Note: If you select Preview Data before uploading the file, no information displays.

Note: Any additional errors that occur during the posting display in the existing errors list on the Errors tab.

New Restartable Payroll Feature

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202409/Payroll/New_Restartable_Payroll_Feature_QR202409.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202409/Payroll/New_Restartable_Payroll_Feature_QR202409.htm

New Restartable Payroll Feature

A new payroll calculation process, Restartable Payroll, is now the default payroll process, which has replaced the Legacy Payroll process. The Restartable Payroll process picks up the calculation process when the last successful employee is calculated. (The Legacy Payroll process is still available, if you need to resolve payroll issues.)

Note: The Restartable Payroll process does not require any custom feature codes. However, if you need to use the Legacy Payroll process, you must enable the LEGACY-PAYROLL-GLOBAL custom feature code on the System Parameters form. (See Enhancements to System Parameters Form.)

When you calculate a payroll using the Restartable Payroll process, the previously used progress bar now displays more information in a job progress window. This window displays the calculation progress in stages, so you can easily track how much payroll has been calculated during this process. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

.

Note: During this process, if you calculate payroll and the system encounters an error and then the payroll is recalculated, after you fix the issue the system displays the following message:

[Image: screenshot]

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Processing Guide.

New PTO Accrual Recalculation Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202409/PTO/New_PTO_Accrual_Recalculation_Form_QR202409.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202409/PTO/New_PTO_Accrual_Recalculation_Form_QR202409.htm

New PTO Accrual Recalculation Form

A new form, PTO Accrual Recalculation, now resides on the PTO Adjustments and Maintenance|Adjustments menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: This feature is only available for service providers.

You can use this form to recalculate PTO accruals for the selected PTO Class, Register Type, and PTO Benefit Plan for the current plan year. (The date range automatically adjusts for each employee based on the year-end date in their register.) This form is helpful in case the initial setup was incorrect or you need to make a bulk adjustment.

Note: You must first update the PTO benefit plan/register for a PTO recalculation to appear.

To recalculate PTO accruals:

  1. Enter or select the PTO Class.

  2. Select the Register Type.

  3. Enter or select the Benefit Plan.

  4. Select Preview. The system processes the PTO registers for that client, register type, and PTO benefit plan for the current plan year. (The date range automatically adjusts for each employee based on the year-end date in their register.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  1. Enter a Comment on Adjustment that will display on the PTO adjustment.

  2. Click Process Recalculation. A window opens that displays the processing steps.

  3. Click Close. A message displays, “Update Completed.” Click OK to continue.

  4. Click Download Report to view the PTO accrual recalculation details on-screen. (You can save the file by clicking XLS.) The report displays on-screen. (You can also select Download Report to save this report.)

Note: Note the following:

  • Each employee has one written absence journal where the system writes the actual PTO register once with the adjustment amount.

  • You can update accruals in the current plan year, but cannot close out the plan year or reset the YTD hours taken.

  • This process does not include carryover hours.

  • The adjustment effective date is based on the recalculation date.

  • Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the PTO Accrual Recalculation form cannot access this form.

Adding the PTO Accrual Recalculation Form to User Roles

New Manager User Setup Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202411/Client/New_Manager_User_Setup_Form_QR202411.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202411/Client/New_Manager_User_Setup_Form_QR202411.htm

New Manager User Setup Form

A new form, Manager User Setup, now resides on the Client|Change menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Worksite managers can use this form to set up other worksite managers within their organization, who will be accessed in the Manager User Setup form.

Note: Note the following:

  • This form is only available for service providers and worksite managers. In addition, worksite managers must have access to the worksite managers they are setting up.

  • Information entered in this form is client-specific, so you can only set up a manager for the current client where you have access.

  • If the worksite manager has access to multiple clients and you try to set them up an error message displays, “This user has access to more than one client and needs to be managed under the System User form.”

  • If you enter a user ID that does not exist, the system automatically populates the User Type as Worksite Manager.

To set up worksite manager users:

  1. Perform the following setups:
  1. — On the Client Security form select User Roles and Human Resources Roles that will be allowed for the current client. (These will be the only roles that are available on the Manager User Setup form for worksite managers to assign to worksite managers they are creating.)
b. On the Users form, enable the Manager User Setup Human Resources Role.
  1. Do one of the following on the Manager User Setup form:

  1. — Select the User ID of an existing worksite manager or worksite employee to set up as a worksite manager user. The form populates the user’s information.

  2. — Enter a newUser ID, which automatically sets the User Type to Worksite Manager. (Continue entering information pertaining to the new user.)

Note: Note the following:

  • A message displays if you select an ID whose roles are not set at the client level, “User <ID> has Roles assigned that are not set at the client level. The user must be accessed with the User Maintenance screen.” To resolve this issue, you must assign roles that you will have access to in the Client Security form before you can set up users. (Access this form by selecting Security on the Actions menu in the Client Details form.)

  • If you select a worksite employee a message displays, “Do you wish to promote this user to a Worksite Manager?” Click Yes to promote that employee. (The form populates with the employee’s information and the User Type is automatically set to Worksite Manager.)

  1. Select Requires New Password to set a new password for an existing user or for a new user.

  2. Select an MFA option in the sMFA Device Expiration field.

  3. Define the User Role ID and the Human Resources Role to indicate which roles the worksite manager user is allowed to access.

Note: You must assign at least one user role to save the record.

  1. Select Add Client to define the Data Security entities for the client. The entities display in the Data Entity Security panel.

Note: Only the clients where you have access display. If you have access to multiple clients, you must select Add Company to manage the list of clients. (You must have access to at least one client to save the record.) Also, you can delete a client by selecting the icon in the Delete column.

  1. Select an entity In the Data Entity Security panel to change the access. For example, if Full Access displays, selecting it changes the access to No Access.

  2. Click Save.

Using the Actions Menu Options

The Manager User Setup form provides additional options on the Actions menu:

  • Change to a Worksite Employee: Displays a message, “Are you sure you want to change the User Type for <user ID> to a Worksite Employee?” Click Yes to change the selected worksite manager to a worksite employee. (This option is unavailable when the user role is set to INQUIRY.)

  • Client Device IP Range: Displays the IP Restrictions form where you can restrict the selected user to a specific IP address or range of addresses.

Adding the Manager User Setup Form to User Roles

To begin using this new form, you must first add it to the user role(s). (Note: If you have more than one user role to add to this new form, use the Bulk Role Update instructions.)

To add this menu item to a user role, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select or enter the Role ID.

  3. Click Add. The Manager User Setup form displays.

  4. Select Manager User Setup from the list. (To quickly find this item, select Company in the Type Filter box.)

  5. Click Accept.

  6. Click Save.

To change the role’s access to Inquiry or Deny for this item (the default is Full), click the Access item (the access changes to Inquiry, click it again to change the access to Deny). Click Save.

To add this menu item to multiple user roles, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select Bulk Role Update from the Actions menu. The Bulk Role Update form opens.

  3. Click Form and then select HRP.USERS*MANAGER.USER.SETUP from the Search Processes list. (To quickly find this item, enter Manager User Setup in the Form Description field and click Refine, then select the form that displays.)

  4. A list of user roles displays.

  5. Grant access to each user role in the Access column. You can grant full access (Full) or read-only access (Inquiry). To deny access, click Deny.

  6. Click Accept. The User Roles form displays.

  7. Click Save.

For more information, see the in‑product help or PrismHR Client Administration Guide.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202411/Payroll/New_Overtime_Report_Parameters_Form_QR202411.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202411/Payroll/New_Overtime_Report_Parameters_Form_QR202411.htm

New Overtime Report Parameters Form

A new form, Overtime Report Parameters, is now available on the System|Change menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the Overtime Report Parameters form to determine the data to be included in the Overtime Report, including specific pay codes.

Note: Note the following:

  • This feature is only available for service providers who have FULL access to the Overtime Report Parameters form.

  • Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the Overtime Report Parameters form displays the form in read-only format.

  • Updates made in this form affect what the system reports when you run the Overtime Report.

  • This form does not use Client Access Group security.

  • This form does not produce an Audit log.

To set up overtime report parameters:

  1. Click Back Office. Select Overtime Report Parameters on the System|Change menu.

  2. Enable Include Expense Reimbursements in Regular Earnings to include expense reimbursements in the YTD Regular column in the report.

  3. Enable Include Fringe Benefits in Regular Earnings to include fringe benefit pay amounts in the YTD Regular column in the report.

  4. Enable Include Salaried Employees on Report to include salaried employees in the report.

  5. If necessary, enter each pay code in the Overtime Pay Codes (Optional) field to include in the Batch Overtime column amount in the report. The pay code description displays.

  6. If necessary, enter each earnings pay code in the Earnings Pay Codes (Optional) field to determine what pay and hours will be included in the report. The earnings pay code description displays.

  7. Click Save.

  5. Click Accept.

  6. Click Save.

New Favorites Template Import Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202411/System/New_Favorites_Template_Import_Form_QR202411.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2024/QR202411/System/New_Favorites_Template_Import_Form_QR202411.htm

New Favorites Template Import Form

A new form, Favorites Template Import, now resides on the System|Change menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the Favorites Template Import form to pre-populate user favorites by importing the forms identified in the Template Process IDs panel, with the flexibility to add or remove those favorites templates in the future.

Note: You can identify the forms to import by entering or selecting their process ID in the Process field. After the import finishes, the system adds the identified forms to your existing favorites list.

Note: Note the following when using this feature:

  • This feature is only available for service providers who have FULL access to the Favorites Template Import form.

  • Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the Favorites Template Import form displays the form in read-only format.

  • Users whose role is set to DENY for any forms listed in the Process field will not display in their favorites list after the import finishes.

  • This form does not use Client Access Group security.

  • This form does not produce an Audit log.

To create and import a favorites template:

  1. Expand the Favorites Template panel.

  2. Enter a new Template ID, or enter or select an existing template. Do the following:

  1. — For a new template ID, enter the Template Description (must be one word and only contain alpha-characters).
b. For an existing template ID, the Template Description and Template Process IDs display.

Note: You can update the Template Description, but not the Template ID.

  1. Enter or select the process IDs for the forms to associate with the template in the Process field. (You must select at least one process ID.) If you select the process IDs from the Select User Process list, click Done to add them. The Name displays.

Note: The Select User Process list displays the available Process IDs and their Process Description.

  1. Click Save. A message displays, “Saving an existing Favorites Template will not update Users Favorites. Do you wish to continue?” Click Yes to continue.

  2. To use the sample import file template, select Download Sample Header File and download the template.

  3. Select Upload File in the Import User Favorites panel to upload a new or existing template.

  4. Select Add Files, select the template, then select Start Upload. Click Close. The uploaded template name displays.

  5. Click Import. After the import finishes, the system adds the identified forms to the user’s existing favorites list.

  6. Click View Transaction Report to download the import details. (This report lists whether the update was successful for each User ID and the Template ID.)

Note: If both the User ID and the Template ID in a row are invalid, the report lists the error on a separate line in the report.

Note: To delete an existing favorites template, simply enter or select the template and click Delete in the Favorites Template panel. A message displays, “This will delete the Favorites Template. Do you wish to continue?” Click Yes.

Adding the Favorites Template Import Form to User Roles

To begin using this new form, you must first add it to the user role(s). (Note: If you have more than one user role to add to this new form, use the Bulk Role Update instructions.)

To add this menu item to a user role, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select or enter the Role ID.

  3. Click Add. The User Role Maintenance form displays.

  4. Select Favorites Template Import from the list. (To quickly find this item, select System in the Type Filter box.)

  5. Click Accept.

  6. Click Save.

To change the role’s access to Inquiry or Deny for this item (the default is Full), click the Access item (the access changes to Inquiry, click it again to change the access to Deny). Click Save.

To add this menu item to multiple user roles, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select Bulk Role Update from the Actions menu. The Bulk Role Update form opens.

  3. Click Form and then select FAVORITES.TEMPLATE*IMPORT from the Search Processes list. (To quickly find this item, enter Favorites Template Import in the Form Description field and click Refine, then select the form that displays.)

  4. A list of user roles displays.

  5. Grant access to each user role in the Access column. You can grant full access (Full) or read-only access (Inquiry). To deny access, click Deny.

  6. Click Accept. The User Roles form displays.

  7. Click Save.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRSystem Administration Guide.

Linked Accrual Plans Feature

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2025/MR202501/Client/Linked_Accrual_Plans_Feature_MR202501.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2025/MR202501/Client/Linked_Accrual_Plans_Feature_MR202501.htm

Linked Accrual Plans Feature

A new feature, Linked Accrual Plans, consists of two PTO plans that you must set up so employees can accrue time for a plan year in one register that they cannot use until the plan year ends. After the plan year ends, the accrued hours move to a new register where employees can use their PTO hours. (Employees can have several different linked accrual plans, one for sick time, one for vacation time, and so on.)

Note: Note the following:

  • Employees must be enrolled in two PTO registers (one for accrual and one for balance) to use this feature. If there is no Balance PTO register associated with the linked class for the employee, then the system does not move anything will from the Accrual register to the Balance register. (The hours remain in the Accrual register.)

  • If the Balance PTO Register has a yearly maximum set, the system moves prior year balances from the Accrual register to the Balance register up to the maximum amount. (The remaining amount in the accrual register is lost.)

  • When the system transfers accrued hours from the Accrual register to the Balance register, it places the hours in the Balance register in the YTD Calculated column.

  • Accrual plans accrue for the pay period and then transfer to the Balance plan.

Using Linked Accrual Plans Feature

To use the Linked Accrual Plans feature, you must set up two PTO plans in the PTO Benefit Plans form:

  • Accrual plan: Accrues employee PTO time during the year. At the end of the plan year, the system transfers the hours in the accrual plan to the linked balance plan. (The Accrual plan resets to zero.) Employees can now use the accrued hours in the Balance plan.

  • Balance plan: Contains the transferred PTO accrual time.

The following diagram demonstrates the setup for Linked Accrual Plans:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • The employee’s accrual balance for the current year is the year-to-date PTO hours accrued from the previous year.

  • Employees carry over some hours in some cases, but most plans expire the hours at the end of the plan year.

  • Most of these plans are set up as anniversary plans, not by the plan year.

Setting Up the Linked Accrual Plans Feature

Set up the following:

  1. PTO Class: Use the PTO Classes form to define which PTO classes will be used in conjunction with each other, consisting of a PTO class for the accrual and a PTO class for the balance.

For example:

a. Create a PTO Class Code for the Balance plan. For example, VACBAL.

Note: Do not enable Linked Accrual.

b. Create a PTO Class Code for the Accrual plan. For example, VACACCR.
c. Enable Linked Accrual.
— —
d. In the Transfer To field, select VACBAL.
— —

Note: These PTO classes are now linked and cannot be linked to other classes.

  1. PTO Register: Enable the Prior Year Accrual trigger method on the PTO Register Types form to trigger the balance register to move the accrued PTO hours from the accrual plan to the balance plan.

For example:

a. Create a PTO Type Code register for the Balance plan. For example, VACBAL.

  • PTO Class: VACBAL

  • Year End Basis: Set Anniversary or Fiscal, but should match the Accrual register

  • Trigger Method: Prior Year Accrual

  • Trigger Date: Do not use

  • Print on Check, Pay Stub Name, Paid Absence, Absence Code: Set these fields for the Balance register

b. Create a PTO Type Code register for the Accrual plan. For example, VACACCR.

  • PTO Class: VACACCR

  • Year End Basis: Set Anniversary or Fiscal, but should match the Balance register

  • Trigger Method: Select any trigger method

  • Trigger Date: Select any trigger date

  • Print on Check, Pay Stub Name, Inactive Register, Paid Absence, and Absence Code: Do not use

  1. PTO Benefit Plan: Enroll employees in an Accrual plan and a Balance plan on the PTO Benefit Plans form. The Accrual plan determines the PTO time accrued. The system does not use the Balance plan to determine the accruals, but employees must be enrolled in both plans for the transfer to work correctly.

  1. — Create a PTO Benefit Plan for the Balance plan. For example, VACBAL. (You must select a calculation basis, but the system does not use it to calculate accruals.)

  2. — Create a PTO Benefit Plan for the Accrual plan. For example, VACACCR. (This will hold the settings for the accruals.)

  1. PTO Absence Codes: Set up an Absence Code on the PTO Absence Codes form for employees to use the Balance plan. (No special settings are needed for this plan. The Accrual plan does not require an absence code.)

Transfer Process

When the system transfers accrued PTO hours, the employee register displays the accrued amount in the calculated column in the Balance register and displays an annotation, “Accrual Transfer MM/DD/YY,” in the details. The system then zeroes out the year-to-date accrual amounts in the employee Accrual register and displays an annotation, “XX number of hours moved to linked plan.”

System Enhancements

The following enhancements were made to accommodate the Linked Accrual Plans feature:

Enhancement Description
Enhancement to PTO Classes Form (PD-18270) Two new fields, Linked Accrual and Transfer To, now reside on the PTO Classes form: - Linked Accrual (default is disabled): Enable this field to mark the selected PTO Class Code as a linked accrual. - Transfer To: Transfers the selected PTO Class Code to another PTO class. (This field only displays if Linked Accrual is enabled.) > Note: Note the following: - Once a PTO class is identified as a linked accrual, you can define where the accruals are transferred. - After defining a PTO class as a linked accrual, it cannot be used as the Transfer To option. - Once the PTO balance class is linked to an accrual, it cannot be linked again. (The linking of accruals is a 1:1 relationship. Each accrual class can only be linked to one balance class and only one accrual class.)
  • Linked Accrual (default is disabled): Enable this field to mark the selected PTO Class Code as a linked accrual.
  • Transfer To: Transfers the selected PTO Class Code to another PTO class. (This field only displays if Linked Accrual is enabled.)
  • Once a PTO class is identified as a linked accrual, you can define where the accruals are transferred.
  • After defining a PTO class as a linked accrual, it cannot be used as the Transfer To option.
  • Once the PTO balance class is linked to an accrual, it cannot be linked again. (The linking of accruals is a 1:1 relationship. Each accrual class can only be linked to one balance class and only one accrual class.) | Enhancement to PTO Register Types Form (PD-18271) | A new option, Prior Year Accrual, is now available in the Trigger Method field on the PTO Register Types form. The Prior Year Accrual method triggers the balance register to move the accrued PTO hours from the accrual plan to the balance plan. The system initializes the trigger date when the pay period crosses over into the year’s end. The plan is triggered at year end from the accrual plan to the balance plan, which could be an anniversary date or a fiscal date, and uses the option set in the Year-End Basis field. (Either way, the transfer of hours happens during the pay period in which that year-end date occurs.) | ========================================================================

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2025/QR202503/PTO/New_PTO_Auto_Enrollment_Rules_Import_Form_QR202503.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2025/QR202503/PTO/New_PTO_Auto_Enrollment_Rules_Import_Form_QR202503.htm

A new form, PTO Auto-Enrollment Rules Import, now resides on the Operations|Action menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

To import PTO auto-enrollment rules:

  1. In the Generate Import Spreadsheet section, create an import spreadsheet by entering or selecting the Client IDs. (You can select multiple clients from the Select Clients list at once.) The Client Name displays next to each client. (If left blank, the system selects all clients and bill codes.)

  2. Select Download Spreadsheet. The system creates a spreadsheet that displays in a separate window, which is suitable for editing.

  3. In the Import Data section, enter an Import Name. (This is a required field; you cannot import a file without this information.)

  4. Select Upload File. Click Add Files and select the file to upload, then click Start Upload. (This file must be in .csv format.)

  5. Click Close. A separate Downloads window displays the name of the .csv file that the system created. (Click Open file to view the downloaded file.)

Note: The first row in the downloaded file displays information about the first rule and the multi-value fields, which are separated by a pipe delimiter (|).

  1. Click Import. Processing steps describe the information saved and include a date and time stamp. You can view this as a report or download in PDF or XLS format by clicking Report.

  2. Click Close.

  3. Click Transaction Report to display a link to a report that contains the PTO auto-enrollment rules transactions.

Note: The Transaction Report displays “Skipped” for any column in a row that has valid data but was not imported because a required row contained invalid data. (All invalid data displays in the Transaction Report.)

  1. Click Error Report to display a link to a .csv file that details the errors that occurred during the import. (The system does not import any rows listed in the error file and only imports rows where all data in the row is valid.)

Note: The Error Report link only displays if errors occurred during the import, which confirms that the system is unable to perform the import.

Note: Note the following:

  • You can only select active clients in the Client ID field.

  • If you enter an inactive client or a client that you are not allowed to access the following error message displays, “Invalid Client ID.”

  • You cannot move rules to a new sort order.

  • You can make changes to existing rules.

  • New rules are marked as “NEW” for the Rule Number in the import.

New Redirect Direct Deposit Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2025/R202504/Payroll/New_Redirect_Direct_Deposit_Form_R202504.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2025/R202504/Payroll/New_Redirect_Direct_Deposit_Form_R202504.htm

New Redirect Direct Deposit Form

A new form, Redirect Direct Deposit, now resides on the Payroll|Change menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the Redirect Direct Deposit form to redirect a direct deposit (DD) to a different DD account after the ACH has already been processed for the voucher’s original direct deposit transaction.

After you make the redirects and click Save, the system:

  • Creates an adjustment voucher that cancels out the original direct deposit transactions being moved to a new account.

  • Creates an adjustment voucher for the new direct deposit records for the Send to Account options, with a new ACH Journal record written for each new direct deposit on the adjustment voucher.

  • Displays a confirmation message, “New deposit has been submitted. Adjustment voucher <voucher number> posted.” Click OK to continue.

Note: Note the following:

  • Users whose roles are set to FULL can enter or select a voucher in the Voucher Number field and select or edit an option in the Send to Account field.

  • Users whose roles are set to INQUIRY can only enter or select a voucher in the Voucher Number field. (All other fields are read-only.)

  • If no direct deposit entries exist for the selected Voucher Number a message displays, “There are no direct deposits on this voucher.” After clicking OK in this message, the system clears the Voucher Number field.

  • If open ACH journals exist for the selected Voucher Number a message displays, “There are open ACH Journals for this voucher. Use the ACH Journal Edit/Entry form to update Direct Deposit Information.” After clicking OK in this message, the system clears the Voucher Number field.

  • The Send to Account options automatically display an abbreviated account identifier consisting of the last four numbers of the active checking or savings account number for the selected Voucher Number based on the line’s Transit Number and Bank Account Number. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

However, if there is only one currently active checking or savings account and the only currently active checking or savings account has a transit and routing number that matches the transit and account number, then only the –Select– option displays. In this case a warning displays, “There are no valid alternative Direct Deposit Accounts for this voucher.”

Adding the Redirect Direct Deposit Form to User Roles

To begin using this new form, you must first add it to the user role(s). (Note: If you have more than one user role to add to this new form, use the Bulk Role Update instructions.)

To add this menu item to a user role, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select or enter the Role ID.

  3. Click Add. The User Role Maintenance form displays.

  4. Select Redirect Direct Deposit from the list. (To quickly find this item, select Payroll in the Type Filter box.)

  5. Click Accept.

  6. Click Save.

To change the role’s access to Inquiry or Deny for this item (the default is Full), click the Access item (the access changes to Inquiry, click it again to change the access to Deny). Click Save.

To add this menu item to multiple user roles, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select Bulk Role Update from the Actions menu. The Bulk Role Update form opens.

  3. Click Form and then select EMPLOYEE.PAYROLL.VOUCHERS*REDIRECT.DIRECT.DEPOSIT from the Search Processes list. (To quickly find this item, enter Redirect Direct Deposit in the Form Description field and click Refine, then select the form that displays.)

  4. A list of user roles displays.

  5. Grant access to each user role in the Access column. You can grant full access (Full) or read-only access (Inquiry). To deny access, click Deny.

  6. Click Accept. The User Roles form displays.

  7. Click Save.

For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Adjustment Processing Guide.

JIRA # WSP-1520

New Mass Employee Transfer Import Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2025/R202506/HumanResources/New_Mass_Employee_Transfer_Import_Form_R202506.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2025/R202506/HumanResources/New_Mass_Employee_Transfer_Import_Form_R202506.htm

New Mass Employee Transfer Import Form

A new form, Mass Employee Transfer Import, is now available on the Operations|Import Processing menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

You can use the Mass Employee Transfer Import form to quickly import a list of employees for transfer to new clients.

Note: Note the following:

  • This feature is only available for service providers who have FULL access to the Mass Employee Transfer Import form.

  • Users whose role is set to INQUIRY for the Mass Employee Transfer Import form displays the form in read-only format.

  • Users who do not have access to a particular client as configured in Client Access Groups cannot transfer employees into or out of the client using the Mass Employee Transfer Import form.

To perform a mass employee transfer import:

  1. Click Back Office.

  2. From the Operations|Import Processing menu, select Mass Employee Transfer Import.

  3. Select Download Spreadsheet Template to download a sample (.csv) template file to your computer to use for creating the list of employees to transfer to new clients. A separate window displays the downloaded file link. (The file downloads to the Downloads folder on your system.)

The spreadsheet template contains the following columns:

Column — Description

From Client — The client ID for the client that the employee is transferring from (required).

Employee ID — The ID of the employee whose information requires a transfer (required).

To Client — The client ID for the client where the employee is transferring (required).

To Employer — The employer ID assigned to the new client where the employee is being transferred (required).

To Pay Group — The pay group for the destination client (required).

To Retire Plan — The retirement plan where the employee is being transferred (optional).

To Position — A valid position for the destination client (required).

To Location — A valid location for the destination client (required).

To Client Hire Date — The hire date to use for the company where the employee is being transferred (required). Note: After entering or selecting a date, a message containing that date displays. Select Yes to confirm that date should be used to update the Status, Type, Status Type History, Position History, and Pay History. If you select No, the system updates that information using the most recent date for that record in the From Client employee record after the transfer finishes.

Update historical dates? — Indicates whether to keep status, type, status type history, position history, and pay history dates (required).

Transfer YTD Check Stubs — The year-to-date check stub details to the company where the employee is transferring (required).

Terminate Employee in Original Client — Indicate whether to terminate the employee and their benefits in the original client (required).

Termination Date — The date when the transferring employee will be terminated in their old client (optional).

Termination Reason — A valid termination reason code (optional).

Terminate Benefit Coverage Today — The terminated group benefits for the employee ends coverage today (required).

  1. Click Find File to open the File Upload dialog box.

  2. Click Add Files in the File Upload dialog box.

  3. Select the specified Import File from your system that you have created. Once selected, the Import File will display in the File Upload dialog box.

  4. Click Start Upload to upload the file.

  5. Click Close on the File Upload dialog box.

  6. The uploaded Import File name will display under the File Name field on the form. The content of the file will display under File Content tab. Errors, if any, will display in the Messages tab. Correct the errors and redo the process.

While processing the uploaded file, the following validation occurs:

  • If any mandatory field is missing from the file, the system displays an error message, “<field name> is a required field.”

  • If the system does not associate the Employee ID with the From Client field, it displays an error message, “Employee <Employee ID> not located in client <From Client>.”

  • If the values in the Pay Group, To Retire Plan, To Position, and To Location fields are not valid for the To Client record, then the system displays an error message, “Record <To Client>.<field value> is not on file in <field’s filename>.”

  • In the Termination Reason field, the system identifies a valid value only if the REASON.CODES contain “Termination.” If you provide any other value, the system displays an error message, “<Termination Reason> is not a valid Term Reason Code.”

  1. Click Import to import the content into PrismHR. After the import finishes, the following occurs:

  • If Transfer YTD Check Stubs is enabled, the program transfers the YTD check stubs.

  • If Terminate Employee in Original Client is enabled, the program terminates the employee on the original client using the corresponding Termination Date and Termination Reason from the upload file.

  • If Terminate Employee in Original Client is disabled, the program does not terminate the employee on the original client.

  • If Terminate Benefit Coverage Today is enabled, the program terminates the employee’s benefit coverage.

  • If the uploaded file contains a mix of employees who are successfully validated and employees that fail the validations, those employees that are successfully validated are transferred appropriately and the employees that fail validation are documented in the error log and are not transferred or terminated.

  1. Click Report to view the transaction report. This report contains the following information:

  • Successfully transferred employees display “Success” in the Import Status column.

  • Employees that failed validation and could not be transferred display “Skipped” in the Import Status column. The “Comments” column for the failed transfer employees displays the error message for whichever failed validation event prevented the transfer.

Adding the Mass Employee Transfer Import Form to User Roles

To begin using this new form, you must first add it to the user role(s). (Note: If you have more than one user role to add to this new form, use the Bulk Role Update instructions.)

To add this menu item to a user role, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select or enter the Role ID.

  3. Click Add. The User Role Maintenance form displays.

  4. Select Mass Employee Transfer Import from the list. (To quickly find this item, select Operations in the Type Filter box.)

  5. Click Accept.

  6. Click Save.

To change the role’s access to Inquiry or Deny for this item (the default is Full), click the Access item (the access changes to Inquiry, click it again to change the access to Deny). Click Save.

To add this menu item to multiple user roles, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select Bulk Role Update from the Actions menu. The Bulk Role Update form opens.

  3. Click Form and then select HRPY.WORK*MASS.EMP.TRANS.IMPORT from the Search Processes list. (To quickly find this item, enter Mass Employee Transfer Import in the Form Description field and click Refine, then select the form that displays.)

  4. A list of user roles displays.

  5. Grant access to each user role in the Access column. You can grant full access (Full) or read-only access (Inquiry). To deny access, click Deny.

  6. Click Accept. The User Roles form displays.

  7. Click Save.

For more information, see the in-product help, PrismHRClient Administration Guide, PrismHR Employer Administration Guide, or PrismHR Payroll Administration Guide.

(see New Time Off Type Form).
