  • Clicking [Image: screenshot] in the Time Off Type form (step 1) incorporates the time off type’s description in the header that displays at the top of the Set Up Plans form (that is, Set Up <Time_Off_Type_Description> Plans). For example, if you select the “PTO Accrual” type, the header displays as “Set Up PTO Accrual Plans.”

  • You can move through the panels without selecting any settings. However, you must complete all the required fields in the panels before moving on to step 3, the Confirmation form. (The [Image: screenshot] button is disabled until you complete this step.)

Using the Setup Panels

You can use the panels in the Set Up Plans form to do the following:

  • Accrual Schedule: Set when employees accrue time off. (This panel defaults to open.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following when working in the Accrual Schedule panel:

  • If you select the Use Existing Schedule option, you cannot change data after the system populates it in this panel. (This restriction does not apply if you manually complete the accrual schedule.)

  • Select Create New Schedule to remove populated data and create a new accrual schedule.

  • If you create a new time off plan (see New Time Off Setup Workflow Form) and select an existing Schedule Code for the accrual schedule a warning displays, “<Code> is an existing Accrual Schedule and cannot be changed.”

  • Plans: Set how much time off employees accrue. (You can set up multiple plans, such as a full-time plan and a part-time plan.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Use the buttons in the Plans panel to do the following:

Click — Action

[Image: screenshot] — To create a new plan. A blank plan opens below the current open plan. (This button is located at the bottom of the panel, so you can easily add another plan without scrolling up to the [Image: screenshot] button at the top of the panel if you have many plans open.)

[Image: screenshot] — To create a duplicate plan of the current open plan (displays beneath it), so you can use that plan’s selections to quickly set up another plan.

[Image: screenshot] — To create a new plan, which displays as a blank plan below the current open plan. (This button is located at the top of the panel.)

[Image: screenshot] — To delete the current plan. After clicking [Image: screenshot] a warning message displays, “Are you sure you want to delete this plan?” Click Yes to continue.

  • Pay: Set the pay information for the time off type, which includes the Pay Code and Accrual Schedule. (You must enable Updates Employee’s Time Off Bank to display the Accrual Schedule field.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The system automatically populates the Accrual Schedule field with the following data from the Schedule Code field on the Accrual Schedule panel:

  • New Accrual Schedule: Data created for a new schedule using Create New Schedule.

  • Existing Accrual Schedule: Data from an existing schedule using Use Existing Schedule.

Note: The system re-populates the Accrual Schedule field anytime you update the Schedule Code on the Accrual Schedule panel.

  • Portal Configuration (Optional): Enable the Can Request This Time Off Type in Portal field to allow employees to request time off using Employee Portal (EP). (All settings in this panel are optional.) For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: These settings control how the absence code behaves in Employee Portal (EP). (Absence codes are specialized reason codes that describe the reason for employee absences.)

Navigating in the Set Up Plans Form

Use the buttons in the Set Up Plans form to do the following:

Click — Action

[Image: screenshot] — Opens a panel.

[Image: screenshot] — Collapses an open panel.

[Image: screenshot] — Saves the information in the current open panel, then closes that panel and returns to the panel above.

[Image: screenshot] — Saves the information in the current open panel, then closes that panel and advances to the next panel in the form. For example, if you click [Image: screenshot] in the Accrual Schedule panel, the Plans panel opens. (You can advance to the next panel even if all the fields in the open panel are not complete.)

[Image: screenshot] — Returns to the Time Off Type form.

[Image: screenshot] — Advances to the Confirmation form, which is step 3 in the Time Off Setup Workflow process. Note: You must complete all the required fields in the panels before moving on to step 3, the Confirmation form. (This button is disabled until you complete those fields.)

[Image: screenshot] — Saves your information and returns to the Time Off Setup Workflow form.

For more information about the Time Off Type form, see the in-product help or the PrismHR Paid Time Off User Guide.

New Time Off Setup Workflow Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2025/R202509/PTO/New_Time_Off_Setup_Workflow_Form_R202509.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2025/R202509/PTO/New_Time_Off_Setup_Workflow_Form_R202509.htm

New Time Off Setup Workflow Form

When you use the new Time Off Setup Workflow process (see New Time Off Setup Workflow Process), a new form, Time Off Setup Workflow, now resides on the Client|Change menu. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Note the following:

  • The Time Off Setup Workflow form is only available for service providers.

  • You can access the Time Off Setup Workflow form either by entering the form name in the Search menu or by selecting Time Off Setup Workflow in the Plan Setup column, which you can access on the Work Centers Quick Access panel after selecting PTO Plan Setup and Enrollment. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: The legacy PTO Work Center Plan Setup steps now display in the new Maintenance column.

You can use the Time Off Setup Workflow form to continue setting up in-progress time off plans or create new time off plans. (See New Time Off Setup Workflow Process.)

Important! You cannot update existing plans created in the legacy PTO Work Center using the new Time Off Setup Workflow process. Instead, you must edit existing plans in the legacy PTO Work Center. (Click

[Image: screenshot]

in the header area of the Time Off Setup Workflow form to access the legacy PTO Work Center.)

Using the Time Off Setup Workflow Form

The Time Off Setup Workflow form contains two panels:

  • Client Time Off Setups in Progress: This panel lists the in-progress time off plans in numerical order, which you can Filter by User. The following information displays in this panel:

Column — Description

Batch ID — Displays the batch number that was assigned to the time off plan. (Clicking the time off plan in this column displays the Time Off Type form, which opens the workflow to the last step the user completed.)

Name — Displays the name of the time off plan.

Status — Displays the last step the user completed for the time off plan.

Time Off Type — Displays the time off plan type that was selected in the batch.

Last Modified Date — Displays the date, in MM/DD/YYYY format, when the time off plan was last modified.

Last Modified User — Displays the user ID of the last user who modified the time off plan.

Actions — Select Delete ( [Image: screenshot] ) to delete an in-progress time off plan.

You can create a new time off plan by selecting New Setup. The Add Time Off Setup Batch form displays, where you can name the time off plan.

Note: Note the following:

  • The Batch ID is automatically named “NEW” after clicking Save.

  • Each client starts a Batch ID at 1000, and every new batch they create increments from there.

  • You must create a batch Name before clicking Save.

  • Past Setups: This panel displays time off plans created in the selected time period, so you can search for completed batches to view the batch ID, batch name, when the batch completed, and the user who processed the batch. (The date range defaults to a range of 30 days, where the To date (end date) displays as the current date.)

Selecting the Time Off Type

To start the Time Off Setup Workflow process, make a selection from the Batch ID column in the Client Time Off Setups in Progress panel. The Time Off Type form (step 1 in the Time Off Setup Workflow process) displays the last step the user completed. However, if the type for a time off plan has not been set, you can set it here. (See New Time Off Type Form.)

Note: Click

[Image: screenshot]

in the Time Off Type form to save your time off plan type and return to the Time Off Setup Workflow form.

Understanding the Side Stepper

Each form in the Time Off Setup Workflow process consists of a “side stepper” on the left side of the window and setup panels on the right side of the window.

The side stepper displays your position in this process. As you move through the process, each completed step displays in green. For example, the step shown in green below, Time Off Type, confirms that the time off type was selected (step 1), so you need to complete step 2, Set Up Plans, the next step in the process, which is highlighted in black:

[Image: screenshot]

Note: Steps that display in gray are not complete.

Adding the Time Off Setup Workflow Form to User Roles

To begin using this new form, you must first add it to the user role(s). (Note: If you have more than one user role to add to this new form, use the Bulk Role Update instructions.)

To add this menu item to a user role, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select or enter the Role ID.

  3. Click Add. The User Role Maintenance form displays.

  4. Select Time Off Setup Workflow from the list. (To quickly find this item, select Company in the Type Filter box.)

  5. Click Accept.

  6. Click Save.

To change the role’s access to Inquiry or Deny for this item (the default is Full), click the Access item (the access changes to Inquiry, click it again to change the access to Deny). Click Save.

To add this menu item to multiple user roles, do the following:

  1. Click Back Office. Select User Roles from the System|Change menu.

  2. Select Bulk Role Update from the Actions menu. The Bulk Role Update form opens.

  3. Click Form and then select PTO.WORKFLOW.WORK*DASHBOARD from the Search Processes list. (To quickly find this item, enter Time Off Setup Workflow in the Form Description field and click Refine, then select the form that displays.)

  4. A list of user roles displays.

  5. Grant access to each user role in the Access column. You can grant full access (Full) or read-only access (Inquiry). To deny access, click Deny.

  6. Click Accept. The User Roles form displays.

  7. Click Save.

For more information about the Time Off Setup Workflow form, see the in-product help, the PrismHRClient Administration Guide, or the PrismHRPaid Time Off User Guide.

New Time Off Setup Workflow Process

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2025/R202509/PTO/New_Time_Off_Setup_Workflow_Process_R202509.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2025/R202509/PTO/New_Time_Off_Setup_Workflow_Process_R202509.htm

New Time Off Setup Workflow Process

The original PTO Setup Workflow process has been redesigned as the “Time Off Setup Workflow” process, which provides more user-friendly forms to create employee time off plans for your clients.

Note: Note the following:

  • This feature and its associated forms are only available for service providers.

  • The [Image: screenshot] button is disabled until you complete the current step. (These steps are outlined below.)

  • Click [Image: screenshot] at any time during this process to save the selected information and return later to finish it.

Important! This process only applies to setting up new time off plans, not editing existing plans. (You can only edit existing plans in the legacy PTO Work Center. Click

[Image: screenshot]

in the header area of the Time Off Setup Workflow form to access the legacy PTO Work Center.)

Getting Started

You can use the new Time Off Setup Workflow form to continue setting up in-progress time off plans or create new time off plans. (See New Time Off Setup Workflow Form.)

Note: To set up a new time off plan, click New Setup, which displays the Add Time Off Setup Batch form, where you can name the batch.

Understanding the Process Steps

Setting up new time off plans now involves using the following workflow:

Step/Form Description
Step 1, Time Off Type form After selecting a time off plan in the Time Off Setup Workflow form, the Time Off Type form displays (see New Time Off Type Form). Select one of the standard time off types for the time off plan or add a new time off type. Note: You must select a time off type to proceed to step 2, Set Up Plans form. (The [Image: screenshot] button is disabled until you complete this step.) Selecting Add Type displays the Add Time Off Type form, where you can create a new time off type instead of selecting one of the standard types that display in the Time Off Type form. For example, you can create a new “Personal Holiday” time off type. After selecting the time off type and clicking [Image: screenshot] , the system enables the Time Off Type step on the left side by displaying the step number in green, confirming that this step is complete.
Step 2, Set Up Plans form Clicking [Image: screenshot] in the Time Off Type form displays the Set Up Plans form (see New Set Up Plans Form), where you can set up the following items: - Accrual Schedule: Set when employees accrue time off. (The [Image: screenshot] button is disabled until you set the accrual schedule.) - Plans: Set how much time off employees accrue. (You can set up multiple plans, such as a full-time plan and a part-time plan.) Note: Select Duplicate Plan to copy an existing plan, so you can use that plan’s selections to quickly set up another plan. - Pay: Set the pay information for the time off type, which includes the Pay Code and Accrual Schedule. - Portal Configuration (Optional): Enable the Can Request This Time Off Type in Portal field to allow employees to request time off using Employee Portal (EP). After making these selections and clicking [Image: screenshot] , the system enables the Set Up Plans step on the left side by displaying the step number in green, confirming that this step is complete. Note: You cannot continue to the next step in the process until you complete all panels in step 2. (The [Image: screenshot] button is disabled until you complete this step.)
  • Accrual Schedule: Set when employees accrue time off. (The [Image: screenshot] button is disabled until you set the accrual schedule.)
  • Plans: Set how much time off employees accrue. (You can set up multiple plans, such as a full-time plan and a part-time plan.)
  • Pay: Set the pay information for the time off type, which includes the Pay Code and Accrual Schedule.
  • Portal Configuration (Optional): Enable the Can Request This Time Off Type in Portal field to allow employees to request time off using Employee Portal (EP). | Step 3, Confirmation form | Clicking [Image: screenshot] in the Set Up Plans form displays the Confirmation form (see New Confirmation Form), where you can review and then submit the saved plan details from steps 1 and 2. Note: You can make changes to the plan information by clicking [Image: screenshot] to return to the panels in the Set Up Plans form, then return to the Confirmation form by clicking [Image: screenshot] . | | Finalizing the information | After confirming that the information is correct click Finish Setup in the Confirmation form, which commits the saved time off plans to the system. Important! Clicking Finish Setup finalizes the time off plan information that you made in this workflow. If you need to make more updates, you must now make them in the legacy PTO Work Center. A message displays, “After finishing the setup all future updates will take place outside of this workflow. Do you wish to continue?” Click Yes to continue the process. The Creating Time Off Setups progress window displays. Click Close to return to the Time Off Setup Workflow form. > Note: Note the following: - If any errors display, close the progress window to return to the workflow and adjust the plan. - The time off plans you create display in the appropriate legacy forms: PTO Classes, PTO Register Types, PTO Benefit Plans, and PTO Absence Codes. |
  • If any errors display, close the progress window to return to the workflow and adjust the plan.
  • The time off plans you create display in the appropriate legacy forms: PTO Classes, PTO Register Types, PTO Benefit Plans, and PTO Absence Codes. For more information about the redesigned Time Off Setup Workflow process, see the in-product help or the PrismHR Paid Time Off User Guide.

New Time Off Type Form

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2025/R202509/PTO/New_Time_Off_Type_Form_R202509.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/New-Features/2025/R202509/PTO/New_Time_Off_Type_Form_R202509.htm

New Time Off Type Form

As step 1 in the new Time Off Setup Workflow process (see New Time Off Setup Workflow Process), a new form, Time Off Type, displays when you select a time off plan in the Batch ID column in the Time Off Setup Workflow form (see New Time Off Setup Workflow Form).

Note: Note the following:

  • The Time Off Type form and its accompanying Add Time Off Type form cannot be accessed in the search menu and cannot be added to a user role.

  • Click [Image: screenshot] in the Time Off Type form to save your time off plan type and return to the Time Off Setup Workflow form.

Setting the Time Off Plan Type

You can use the Time Off Type form to set the type for a time off plan by either selecting a standard time off type in the list that displays (the type description displays in highlighted text with the type name displaying underneath) or creating a new type. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

In addition, you can create a new type in the Time Off Type form by selecting Add Type. For example, you can create a new “Personal Holiday” time off type in the Add Time Off Type form that displays (both fields are required):

[Image: screenshot]

After selecting the time off type or saving a new type and clicking

[Image: screenshot]

, the system enables the Time Off Type step on the left side by displaying the step number in green, confirming that this step is complete.

Note: Note the following:

  • You can only select one time off type. If you do not select a time off type and click [Image: screenshot] an error message displays, “Select a Time Off Type.”

  • You cannot duplicate existing time off types. Therefore, if you enter an existing Time Off Type Code the current description displays. If you update the current description, the system processes the updated description after you process the entire workflow.

  • You can edit existing time off types by clicking the pencil icon ( [Image: screenshot] ), which opens the Add Time Off Type form where you can update the Type Description.

For more information about the Time Off Type form, see the in-product help or the PrismHR Paid Time Off User Guide.

PrismHR Release Highlights

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Release-Highlights/2025/Prism_Release_Highlights_QR202403.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Release-Highlights/2025/Prism_Release_Highlights_QR202403.htm

PrismHR Release Highlights

The release highlights consist of the following enhancements, which consist of helpful updates to the current functionality and security improvements:

Highlight — Description

Reprinting Payroll Checks — To make printing and rebuilding payroll checks more user-friendly for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors, these users can now simply select the Reprint Payroll Checks link in the Payroll Reports form. (See Enhancement to Reprinting Payroll Checks.)

Validating Employee’s Hourly Rate — The system now validates that the employee’s Hourly Rate no longer displays in the Employee PTO Detail Report for worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors who have the Time Sheet Entry (w/o Pay Rates) Human Resources role set on the Users form and the PTO Absence Summary Report with Buyback option set on the Employee PTO Detail Report form. (See Enhancement to Employee PTO Detail Report Form.)

PrismHR Release Highlights

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Release-Highlights/2025/Prism_Release_Highlights_QR202406.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Release-Highlights/2025/Prism_Release_Highlights_QR202406.htm

PrismHR Release Highlights

The release highlights consist of the following enhancements, which consist of helpful updates to the current functionality and security improvements:

Highlight — Description

Working with Termination Explanation After Employee Termination (PD-15590) — You can now add, update, or delete a Termination Explanation on the Other tab after an employee has been terminated. Note: This enhancement is only available for service providers.

Using a Worksite Trusted Advisor’s User ID as PTO Approver or Manager (PD-16707) — Service providers can now enter a worksite trusted advisor’s user ID (who has access to the client) as the PTO Approver or Manager for the selected employee on the Work tab. (Previously, you could only enter an employee ID in these fields.)

Enhancement to Global Search Results (PD-16835) — Previously, when performing a global search for an employee the system displayed the preferred name instead of the legal first name. The system now displays an employee’s legal first name in parentheses if there is a preferred name for the employee, which displays first. After the legal first name the middle initial displays, then the last name.

PrismHR Release Highlights

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Release-Highlights/2025/Prism_Release_Highlights_QR202409.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Release-Highlights/2025/Prism_Release_Highlights_QR202409.htm

PrismHR Release Highlights

The release highlights consist of the following enhancements, which consist of helpful updates to the current functionality and security improvements:

Highlight — Description

Enhancements to System Parameters Form (PD-15168) — A new custom feature code, LEGACY-PAYROLL-GLOBAL, is now available on the Custom Feature Codes list, which you can enable to revert to the Legacy Payroll process. (You can use this payroll process instead of the default Restartable Payroll process.)

Enhancement to Employee Payroll Vouchers Form (PD-17210) — Worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors can now reprint multiple vouchers at once that have an associated check in the Employee Payroll Vouchers form, which is available on the Payroll|View menu. Note: To use this feature, worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors must also have user role access to the Reprint Payroll Checks form (MVQ.CONTROL*REPRINT.CHECK.MAINT process ID).

Enhancement to PTO Benefit Plans Form (PD-17295) — You can enable the new Apply Carryover toward Maximum Accrual Per Year field to implement Colorado and Maine paid leave.

Enhancement to Work Groups Form (PD-17419) — A new field, Obsolete, now displays on the Work Groups form, which is available on the Client|Change menu.

Enhancements to Data Import Tool (PD-17580) — The existing Global W/C Classification Rates import template is now available on the Import Template field in the Data Import Tool. Note: Previously, you could only access this import template from the W/C Classification Rates form.

PrismHR Release Highlights

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/PD/Release-Notes/Release-Highlights/2025/Prism_Release_Highlights_QR202503.htm Path: PD/Release-Notes/Release-Highlights/2025/Prism_Release_Highlights_QR202503.htm

PrismHR Release Highlights

The release highlights consist of the following enhancements, which consist of helpful updates to the current functionality and security improvements:

Highlight — Description

= Enhancement to Work Groups Form (PD-15207) — The Employees Assigned to Work Group form, which is accessible by selecting Employees Assigned To on the Actions menu in the Work Groups form with a Work Group selected, now displays in the standard format used throughout the product.

Enhancement to Payroll History Form (PD-17815) — Previously, users who had Deny access to the Payroll Summary form and Full access to the Payroll History form were able to access the Payroll Summary form from the Payroll History form. When users are set to Deny access to the Payroll Summary form and Full access to the Payroll History form, they can no longer access the Payroll Summary form by selecting a payroll listed in the Payroll History form.

Removal of SuperBatch Legacy (PD-18061) — SuperBatch Legacy, the original version of SuperBatch, has been removed from the system. Instead, you must use SuperBatch, the enhanced payroll processing hub, which was introduced in 2024.

New Marketplace Link (PD-18314) — A new link, Marketplace, now displays on the PrismHR menu bar. Selecting Marketplace provides quick access to the PrismHR Marketing|Expanded Services web site, where you can connect with vendors.

Benefits Administration (BA) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
WSP-1819 Group Benefit Plans form Redesign On the Group Benefit Plans form, the paycheck and taxes related fields from different sections have been moved to the newly created Paycheck & Taxes section. This section is displayed for all the insurance classes. [Image: screenshot] The Paycheck & Taxes section has now the following fields which were earlier under different sections: - Pay Stub Name - Suppress Print On Check - Suppress All Processing On Arrears Vouchers - Report On Form W2 - Report Premium Cost On W2 Note: There is no change in the existing functionality.
WSP-2883, WSP-2890 New Plan Anniversary Month and Plan Anniversary Override Month fields On the Retirement Plans form, a new drop-down field named Plan Anniversary Month has been introduced to add new anniversary date to calculate the Next Auto Escalation Date. [Image: screenshot] On the Benefit Plan Setup form, when you select Plan Class as Retirement, then a new field named Plan Anniversary Override Month has been added to allow users to override Plan Anniversary Month selection made on the Retirement Plans form. Additionally, the selection that you make in the Plan Anniversary Month field on the Retirement Plans form is displayed as read-only next to the Plan Anniversary Override Month field. [Image: screenshot] Note: While using Plan Anniversary in the calculation of the Next Auto Escalation Date, the system uses the value defined in the Plan Anniversary Override Month and Day field on the Benefit Plan Setup form. If the plan anniversary override value is not defined, then the system uses the value defined in the Plan Anniversary Month and Day field on the Retirement Plans form. If both the above mentioned fields are left blank, then the system uses the value defined in the Start Date field on the Benefit Plan Setup form as the plan anniversary date.
WSP-2861 Changes to the Retirement Plan Enrollment form On the Retirement Plan Enrollment form, under the Election Details section, a new read-only table named Retirement HPE Status has been added to assist users in identifying why a contribution was redirected. The table is displayed only when you select a plan and provide an effective date. [Image: screenshot]
WSP-2913 New Deemed ROTH and Deemed ROTH Override fields According to the Secure 2.0 Act, employees who meet the HPE Threshold for prior year and make a catchup contribution to a 401k, 403b or 457b plan, must make that contribution on a ROTH basis. This Act is effective starting January 1, 2026. On the Retirement Plans form, a new drop-down field named Deemed ROTH has been added for users to allow plans elect a provision to force Pre-tax contributions to ROTH contributions AND/OR Pre-tax Catchup contributions to ROTH Catchup contributions regardless of whether the 402G limit has been met. [Image: screenshot] The Deemed ROTH drop-down field has the following options: - -Select- - This option uses the same logic as the No (Default) option. - No (default) - Pre-tax Catchup contributions is taken as pre-tax until total pre-tax contributions equals the 402G limit. Once the 402G limit is reached, no further Pre-tax or Pre-tax Catchup will be taken for contributions. Note: For example, if an employee meets the HPE threshold for the prior year (Example: 2025), then the pre-tax contribution is limited to $23,500. Any elected ROTH and ROTH Catchup contributions will continue up to the limits. Any remaining pre-tax Catchup contributions will not be forced to ROTH Catchup contribution. - Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit - Pre-tax Catchup contributions may be taken up to the point when total pre-tax contributions equal the 402G limit. Any further catchup contributions will be taken as a ROTH catchup contribution. Note: For example, if an employee meets the HPE threshold for the prior year (Example: 2025), then the pre-tax contribution is limited to $23,500 with any remaining Catchup contributions taken as ROTH Catchup contribution for the following year (Example: 2026). - Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup before 402(g) limit - Pre-tax Catchup contributions will be taken as a ROTH Catchup regardless of whether the total pre-tax contributions equal the 402G limit. Note: For example, if an employee meets the HPE threshold for the prior year (Example: 2025), then the pre-tax contribution is limited to $23,500. However, all the pre-tax Catchup contributions are taken as ROTH Catchup contribution regardless of whether the total pre-tax contributions equals the 402G limit. - Pre-tax to ROTH and Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit - Pre-tax and Pre-tax Catchup contributions may be taken up to the point when total pre-tax contributions equal the 402G limit. At this point, all pre-tax elections will be taken as ROTH and all Pre-tax Catchup will be taken as ROTH Catchup contributions. Note: For example, if an employee meets the HPE threshold for the prior year (Example: 2025), then the pre-tax contribution is limited to $23,500 with any remaining pre-tax contributions taken as ROTH and pre-tax Catchup contributions taken as ROTH Catchup for the following year (Example: 2026). Please note that currently, the 402(G) limit is equal to the Contribution Limit defined on the Tax Year Limits Maintenance form. The Catch Up Limit is also defined on this form. Additionally, the 402(G) limit and the Catch Up limit can be overridden by defining limits under the Plan Year Deferral Limits section on the Retirement Plans form. On the Benefit Plan Setup form, when you select Plan Class as Retirement, then a new field named Deemed ROTH Override has been added to allow users to override Deemed ROTH selection made on the Retirement Plans form. Additionally, the selection that you make in the Deemed ROTH field on the Retirement Plans form is displayed as read-only next to the Deemed ROTH Override field. [Image: screenshot] Note: When you check Prohibit Deductions for either of the following on the Retirement Plans form: - Roth Post-Tax Deduction Code - Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code then, the following options are not displayed in the Deemed ROTH drop-down options: - Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit - Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup before 402(g) limit - Pre-tax to ROTH and Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit
WSP-2348 Changes to the Benefit Plan Setup form On the Benefit Plan Setup form, when you select Plan Class as Group Benefit, then under the Group Benefits Setup section, a new field named Max Days Back Dating has been added which allows users to override the Max Days Back Dating value defined on the Group Benefit Plans form for the selected Benefit Plan. [Image: screenshot] - This newly added field is an editable field. Additionally, you can only enter numbers between 1 and 999999. - The value assigned to the Max Days Back Dating field on the Group Benefit Plans form is displayed as read-only to the right of the input field on this form. Note: If the Max Days Back Dating field does not have a value defined on the Benefit Plan Setup form, but has a value defined for this field on the Group Benefit Plans form, then the system uses the value defined on the Group Benefit Plans form as default.
WSP-2569, WSP-2571, WSP-2572 Changes to the Employee Benefits Enrollment form On the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, when you manually create a benefit enrollment and in the Coverage Starts field, if you enter a date that is prior to the Current Date minus the value defined for that benefit plan in the Max Days Back Dating field on the Group Benefit Plans form, then an error message is displayed. However, if a client level override value is set for Max Days Back Dating field on the Benefit Plan Setup form, then the input in the Coverage Starts field takes the value setup on client level into consideration. [Image: screenshot] When an Employee Benefits Enrollment record is terminated, the Max Days Back Dating value is used to validate a benefit plan that is to be terminated. The Coverage Ends date now accepts the value which equal to or greater than the current date minus the Max Days Back Dating value assigned at the client level. Additionally, on the Benefits Import form, while importing a benefit plan, the Max Days Back Dating value is used to validate a benefit plan that is to be terminated.
WSP-2812 Changes on the COBRA Participant Record form On the COBRA Participant Record form, when you select a dependent Participant ID, and then click the Edit Cobra Participant Record hyperlink, the Social Security Number field on the Edit COBRA Participant Record modal form is masked based on the option that you choose to mask SSN from the SSN Mask Option field on the System Parameters form. The Social Security Number field is displayed as a read-only field. However, you can edit the SSN by clicking the Edit SSN hyperlink. For example, on the System Parameters form, if you choose Show Last Four (###-##-6789) as the option from the SSN Mask Option field, then on the COBRA Participant Record form, when you select a dependent Participant ID and click the Edit Cobra Participant Record hyperlink, the value in the Social Security Number field will be masked to display only the last four digits as shown in the image below: [Image: screenshot]
WSP-2747, WSP-2749, WSP-2754, WSP-2813, WSP-2814 Changes to the Benefit Utilities form Under the Benefit Utilities section, a new utility named Auto Escalation has been added to identify enrollments that are not flagged as Auto Escalation?. [Image: screenshot] When you select the Auto Escalation utility, the Report Filters section is displayed. Under the Reports Filters section: - Select the Employment Status Class. This filter has the following options: - All Classes - Active - On Leave - Terminated - Select the Enrollment History from the drop-down options. This filter has the following options: - All Enrollments (Default) - Only enrollments without contribution changes - Only enrollments with contribution changes - Client ID - This field is optional. Leave this field blank for this report to run for all clients. If you want to restrict this report to run for selected clients, enter their Client IDs here or click the Client ID link and select them from the Select Clients dialog box. - Retirement Plan ID - This field is required. Enter the Retirement Plan ID or click the Retirement Plan ID hyperlink to select from the Select Plan dialog box. Now, click Search. A job control runs. Once the job control process is completed, click Close to view the list of employee with retirement plan enrollments that are not flagged as Auto Escalation?. The Results section displays the following columns: - Search Employee Name - This input field allows you to search for a specific employee name. Additionally, when you search for an employee, the results are displayed only within the batch selected. - Batch No. - It represents the threshold for the returned records. For example, if the threshold is to display 1000 records in one batch and the total results returned are 2500, then it will be divided into 3 batch, where Batch 1 will have 1000 records, Batch 2 will display the next 1000 records, and Batch 3 will display the remaining 500 records. You can select the batch number from the drop-down list. Note: If you make any changes to any of the records in a certain batch and select a different Batch Number, then the system displays a warning message stating, There are unsaved changes that will be lost. Are you sure you want to change batches? - Click Yes to close the warning message and jump to the selected batch number. Any unsaved changes to the original batch will be lost. - Click No to remain on the original selected batch number. - Client ID - Unique ID of the client with which the employee is associated. - Employee Name - Name of the employee. It is displayed as a hyperlink. Clicking this opens the Employee Details form with the information of the selected employee. - Employment Status Class - Current status of the employee’s employment. - Retirement Plan ID - The retirement plans to which the employees are enrolled. - Status - Status of the retirement plan. - Status Date - The status date. - Retirement Benefit Group - The retirement benefit group in which the employee is enrolled in. - Election Changes Exist - - Last Effective Date - The last effective date from which the retirement plan was active. Select the record(s) that you want to update the Auto Escalation? checkbox with the most recent Effective Date listed within the Election Details of the retirement enrollment record and click Update. Based on the number of records you have selected, a confirmation message stating, Auto Escalation Enrollments will be updated. Are you sure? is displayed. - Click Yes to update the selected records. - Click No to remain on the form.

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
WSP-2910 Changes to the Employee Details Form On the Employee Details form, under the Other tab, under the Miscellaneous section, the following two new fields have been introduced: - Qualified OT Exempt - As of [Image: screenshot] Field Name — Description Qualified OT Exempt — This field is optional. This field is a check box. This field currently has no functionality, but it can be leveraged to determine which employees should not be included in future qualified OT imports for 2025. In 2026 and beyond, this field will be used to exclude employees from any future development to automate or recalculate these amounts. As of — This field only displays once the Qualified OT Exempt field is selected. If you have selected the Qualified OT Exempt field, this field is required. Provide the date from when you want to block the system from accumulating qualified OT for any employee. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRHuman Resources User Guide.

WSP-2923 Changes to the Pay Codes Form On the Pay Codes form, under the Processing Options section, the following two new fields have been introduced: - Qualified OT Factor - Pay Code is used to pay daily OT [Image: screenshot] Field Name — Description Qualified OT Factor — This field is optional. Define the percentage of overtime pay that should be included in qualified overtime calculations by selecting the appropriate factor from the following options to ensure only eligible overtime amounts are reported in compliance with OBBBA’s rules. - – Select– (default) - 100% : Half time - Calculates at the standard 0.5 of the employee’s hourly rate. - 50% : Double Time (1x) - Calculates at the standard employee’s standard full hourly rate. - 33% : Time & A Half - Calculates at 1.5x of the employees standard hourly rate. - 25% : Double time (2x) - Calculates at 2x of the employees standard hourly rate. Pay Code is used to pay daily OT — This field is optional. This is an informational setting that will be used in future reports to flag employees who may be receiving daily OT and require additional review for FG overtime. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration and Processing User Guide.
Field Name Description

WSP-2718, WSP-2724 Changes to the Print Service Global Check Parameters Form On the Print Service Global Check Parameters form, under the Global Check Configuration section, a new field named Exclude suppressed Pay Codes in Gross Pay on Checks? has been introduced. [Image: screenshot] When on the Pay Codes form, the Print on Paystub field is set to NO, Suppress Printing on Pay Stub, the following grid illustrates the functionality of this field: [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR System Administration User Guide.
WSP-2723, WSP-2724 Changes to the Print Service Options Form On the Print Service Options form, a new field named Exclude suppressed Pay Codes in Gross Pay on Checks? has been introduced. [Image: screenshot] When on the Pay Codes form, the Print on Paystub field is set to NO, Suppress Printing on Pay Stub, the following grid illustrates the functionality of this field: [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Client Administration User Guide.
CMP-336 Changes to the State Garnishment Rules Form On the State Garnishment Rules form, under the Rules for Calculating Withholding for Child-Support Payments section, a new field named Include Charged Tips In Base Pay? has been introduced. [Image: screenshot] This field indicates whether charged tips are included in base pay when calculating the maximum amount to garnish for child support for the selected state. This field is a drop-down. Select of the following options: - Yes (Default) - Charged tips (a pay code with class of earnings flagged for used to pay for charged tips) will be included in the base pay. This option retains the existing functionality to calculate the child support garnishment. - No - Charged tips will not be included in the base pay. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration and Processing User Guide.
CMP-6793 CMP-6795 Changes to the State Rules Form On the State Rules form, only for the state of Oregon, a new field named SIT Combined Reporting is introduced. This field does not appear for any other state. This field will be used during payroll processing to force the tax basis for specific state taxes to be assigned the same tax entity (PEO or Client) as is assigned for SUTA. [Image: screenshot] Oregon is a combined reporting state that has historically always been PEO report only. To support Oregon HB 2236(Permits professional employer organizations (PEOs) to report payroll information in aggregate on behalf of their clients) this new option has been added. For combined reporting, all state taxes must report on the same level including SIT. While we support this today for SUTA and SUTA Components, SIT could previously only be set to an override on the employer level. With this option, for pay dates starting 1/1/2026, Oregon employers now can change the PEO/Client reporting designation for additional Oregon state taxes that do not naturally follow the client reporting dates within the client detail tax tab. - This is not a required field. - Unchecked - This field is unchecked by default. When this field is not set on Oregon, AND for all client types other than PEO, AND for all states other than Oregon, there will be no change in tax basis. - Checked - When this field is checked for OREGON PEO CLIENT TYPES, all of the following taxes will report using the same tax basis P or C for PEO Clients: - 38-23 (WBF) - Employee - 38-24 (SUTA) - Employer - 38-26 (WBF) - Employer - 38-27 (State transit) - Employee - 38-28 (SUTA offset) - Employer - 38-20 (SIT) - Employee - 38-40 (PFML) - Employee - 38-41 (PFML) - Employer - 38-51 (Lane Transit) - Employer - 38-52 (TRI COUNTY TRANSIT) - Employer - When you select this field, you will receive a warning stating Warning, payroll processing will use the SUTA tax entity for other state taxes with the tax IDs 20,23,26,27,28,40,41,51,52. Are you sure? You can click Yes or No. - The existing tax basis designation hierarchy Tax Deduction → State Rule → Employer Detail → Client Detail is extended to the State Tax Deduction codes that are currently excluded such that: - If SUTA is configured to be PEO or Client, all of the above tax codes follow the SUTA Reporting designation. - Not all Oregon tax codes will follow the new SIT setting. For example, the following state and local tax codes are excluded from this logic: - 38-46 (Portland Metro SHS). - Any County or Local tax codes. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration and Processing User Guide.
WSP-2310, WSP-2313, WSP-2369, WSP-2708 Client Global PTO Maintenance form (NEW) Use this new form to view and configure client specific Global PTO parameters. [Image: screenshot] To access this form, click Client. Under Client\ Change, click Client Global PTO Maintenance. To configure client specific Global PTO parameters: - 1. Complete the following fields: Field Name — Description Excluded Plans by State — This field is optional. This form provides the ability to exclude full states from the Global PTO enrollment and accrual process. This option is intended for clients who may be required to provide State Sick Leave in certain states but not all. If you want to, you can now exclude certain Global PTO Benefit Plans from the enrollment and accrual once the client is enabled for Global PTO. - State - You can enter the two digit state codes manually or you can click the State hyperlink and select them from the Select States (permitted list of States Code records configured on the State Rules form) dialog box. You cannot select a state here that is already listed in the Global PTO Plan Overrides section below. - Description - This field automatically populates the state name once the State field is populated. Excluded Plans by ID — This field is optional. If multiple Global PTO Benefit plans exist on the State Rules form for a state, and you need to prevent enrollment and accrual in one or more plans for that state for the client, you can enter the specific Global PTO Benefit Plan IDs here. If client has Global PTO Benefit Plan IDs configured under this field, then creation and/or accrual of any Global PTO plan(s) identified in this field will be ignored. - Exclude Plans by ID - You can enter the Global PTO Benefit Plan IDs manually or you can click the Exclude Plans by ID hyperlink and select them from the Select Global PTO Benefit Plans dialog box. You cannot select a state here that has already listed having Global PTO Plan Overrides. - Description - This field automatically populates the Global PTO Benefit Plan description once the Exclude Plans by ID field is populated. Global PTO Plan Overrides — When Global PTO Plan Override rules are configured, this section will display all existing Global PTO override rules for the client. You can click on the number hyperlink under the “Line #” column to open the Global PTO Client Override form to view the override rules for that state. You can make changes to the override rules on that form and save the changes which will reflect here upon editing. The following columns display for this section: - Line # - State - Plan ID - I/E - Employee Type - I/E - Pay Method - Override Plan ID Sort By — This field is drop-down. You can select the sort order for the list above by any one of the following options: - Order Applied (Default) - State - Plan ID - Employee Type - Pay Method - Override Plan ID 2. Click Save to save the changes. 3. Click Delete to delete all records of Global PTO exclusions for this client. 4. Click New Rule to open the Global PTO Client Override. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration and Processing User Guide.
Field Name Description
Excluded Plans by State This field is optional. This form provides the ability to exclude full states from the Global PTO enrollment and accrual process. This option is intended for clients who may be required to provide State Sick Leave in certain states but not all. If you want to, you can now exclude certain Global PTO Benefit Plans from the enrollment and accrual once the client is enabled for Global PTO. - State - You can enter the two digit state codes manually or you can click the State hyperlink and select them from the Select States (permitted list of States Code records configured on the State Rules form) dialog box. You cannot select a state here that is already listed in the Global PTO Plan Overrides section below. - Description - This field automatically populates the state name once the State field is populated.
Excluded Plans by ID This field is optional. If multiple Global PTO Benefit plans exist on the State Rules form for a state, and you need to prevent enrollment and accrual in one or more plans for that state for the client, you can enter the specific Global PTO Benefit Plan IDs here. If client has Global PTO Benefit Plan IDs configured under this field, then creation and/or accrual of any Global PTO plan(s) identified in this field will be ignored. - Exclude Plans by ID - You can enter the Global PTO Benefit Plan IDs manually or you can click the Exclude Plans by ID hyperlink and select them from the Select Global PTO Benefit Plans dialog box. You cannot select a state here that has already listed having Global PTO Plan Overrides. - Description - This field automatically populates the Global PTO Benefit Plan description once the Exclude Plans by ID field is populated.
Global PTO Plan Overrides When Global PTO Plan Override rules are configured, this section will display all existing Global PTO override rules for the client. You can make changes to the override rules on that form and save the changes which will reflect here upon editing. The following columns display for this section: - Line # - State - Plan ID - I/E - Employee Type - I/E - Pay Method - Override Plan ID

WSP-2311, WSP-2370, WSP-2877 Global PTO Client Override Form (NEW) Use this new form to view and configure client specific Global PTO override rules. [Image: screenshot] You can only access form using the Client Global PTO Maintenance form. Click the New Rule button on this form to open the Global PTO Client Override form. You will not find this form from the search bar. To configure client specific Global PTO override rules: - 1. Complete the following fields: Field Name — Description Employee Type — Select groups of employees based on their Employee Type to override the existing global pto enroll and accrual logic. Select either Include or Exclude from the drop-down for one more Employee Type. You can manually enter them here. Click the Employee Type hyperlink and select them from the Select Employee Type Codes dialog box. Pay Method — Select groups of employees based on their pay method to override the existing global pto enroll and accrual logic. Select either Include or Exclude from the drop-down for one or more of the following pay methods: - Hourly - Salary - Variable Salary - Commission - Driver State Code — Enter the state for which the override rule applies. Enter a two-digit State code that has NOT already been added to the Excluded Plans By State grid on the Client Global PTO Maintenance form. PTO Benefit Plan — Select the PTO Benefit Plan that the override rule applies to. Select a Global PTO Benefit Plan ID available for the selected state from the drop-down. Override PTO Plan ID — Select an existing Global PTO Benefit Plan to replace the Global PTO Benefit Plan set in the PTO Benefit Plan field. This is a required field unless the Exempt employees from accruals in this PTO Benefit Plan field is checked. Exempt employees from accruals in this PTO Benefit Plan — Check this field to exempt employees from accruals in this PTO Benefit Plan for the client. Note: When you check this field, the Override PTO Plan ID field will be cleared. 2. Click Save to save the changes for the client-specific Global PTO override rule. You cannot save this form if: - both the Employee Type and Pay Method fields and blank for a Global PTO override rule, OR, - for a specified state, the Override PTO Plan ID field is blank and also the Exempt employees from accruals in this PTO Benefit Plan field is not checked. 3. Click Delete to delete the override PTO plan for the state. 4. Click Cancel to clear this form. 5. Click Close to close this form and return to the Client Global PTO Maintenance form. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration and Processing User Guide.
