CMP-6811 Validation of SOC to TTOC relationship On the Positions form, from now on, the system will validate when you enter a TTO Code against the SOC Code during the creation of or updating a Position. [Image: screenshot] - Invalid TTO/SOC combinations result in an error message: TTO code [] and SOC code [] are not related. - Invalid TTO code results in an error message: TTO Code [] does not exist. - Invalid entries cannot be saved. - Valid TTO code entry is allowed when the SOC code is blank. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Client Administration User Guide.
CMP-6821 W-2 Delaware PFML update Beginning Tax Year 2025, for the state of Delaware, the YTD Employee PFML contribution (tax Code 08-40) will be added to the Form W-2 build for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients to report on the employee’s Form W-2 and Form W-2c in Box 14 with the description DEPFML. The amount reported is the total employee PFML contributions withheld for the year.
CMP-6820 W-2 Maine PFML update Beginning Tax Year 2025, for the state of Maine, the YTD Employee PFML contribution (tax Code 20-40) will be added to the Form W-2 build for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients to report on the employee’s Form W-2 and Form W-2c in Box 14 with the description MEPFML. The amount reported is the total employee PFML contributions withheld for the year.
CMP-6590 W-2 Oregon PFML update Beginning Tax Year 2025, for the state of Oregon, the YTD Employee PFML contribution (tax Code 38-40) will be added to the Form W-2 build for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients to report on the employee’s Form W-2 and Form W-2c in Box 14 with the description PFMLI. The amount reported is the total employee PFML contributions withheld for the year.
CMP-6837 Employer Tax for Paid Family and Medical Leave To support the new Minnesota PFML tax deductions, significant changes will be effective 1.1.26; State Misc 3 ER (-41), which has historically also been used to support the employer PFML portion, but is currently being used for the Minnesota Additional Assessment Fee. To support the separation of the Minnesota Admin Assessment fee from the employer PFML tax logic, we have introduced a new State Misc 4 Employer Tax Identifier, -54. For pay dates on or after 1.1.26, tax code 24-41will be used for employer contributions to Minnesota PFML. The Minnesota Additional Assessment tax will be reassigned to tax code 24-54. To prepare for this transition, the following updates will be required: - 1. Tax Code & Report Settings - Update the description of the existing tax code 24-41 and add the description to tax code 26-54. - Tax Code 24-41 : Minnesota Paid Family Medical Leave (Employer) - Tax Code 24-54 : Minnesota Admin Assessment Fee - Ensure the tax code 26-41 PEO\ Client report setting is configured to Client before 1/1/2026 payrolls. 2. PrismHR Tax & MasterTax Mapping - Update the tax code mapping for PrismHR Tax & MasterTax imports to reflect the new identifier. 3. Rate Overrides - Migrate any existing rate overrides for the Minnesota Admin Assessment fee to State Misc4. - Use State Misc3 for Minnesota Employer PFML rate overrides. 4. Tax Suppression Review - Remove any suppressions that may interfere with the new tax code functionality.
CMP-6840 New State Misc4 Rate field introduced For each of the following forms, a new field named State Misc4 Rate has been introduced. Enter the state miscellaneous 4 rate here, for example for tax code 24-54 (Minnesota). Employer Tax Rate (SUTA) [Image: screenshot] State Tax Rates (SUTA) [Image: screenshot] State Tax Bill Rates (SUTA) [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Employer Administration User Guide or PrismHR Billing User Guide

Employee Portal (EP) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
EP-9410 Universal Employee ID on Employee Details The Employee Details form in Manager Portal now displays an employee’s Universal Employee ID for the PrismONE application. Managers can use this information to verify that employees have connected their accounts to the PrismONE Mobile App or other PrismONE ID integrations. For more information, see the in-product help.
EP-9571 Retirement Plan Setup Option to Prohibit 401k Deductions Clients can now prohibit employees from editing or enrolling in retirement plans that include deduction types marked as Prohibited. If this option is selected, when an employee views the Employee Contributions form, the following rules apply: - If the employee does not have an Employee Contributions amount toward the Prohibited deduction type, the deduction type is hidden. - If the employee does have an amount on the Prohibited deduction type, the employee must enter a null value for that deduction type to save their updates. With this configuration option, clients can restrict employees from making updates to deductions that are prohibited by their employer or plan administrator. For more information, see the in-product help.
EP-9631, EP-9632, EP-9633, EP-9634, EP-9635, EP-9636, EP-9639, EP-9640, EP-9641, EP-9642 Enhanced Employee Details Enhanced Employee Details The Employee Details form in Employee Portal has been enhanced with an updated user interface designed to provide more visibility and ease of navigation while retaining all current functionality. The new form design has more available space, making it easier to view more of the employee’s information at once. For example: [Image: screenshot] Menu options are now arranged as a horizontal bar, providing more screen space for employee information below. Information is now arranged in columns which are sized to the current screen, providing full support for mobile devices and desktop displays of various sizes. HR Actions are now accessed via a menu on the right. Select HR Actions to display a menu with all available options. When a HR Action is selected, the HR Action options remain displayed as a menu, allowing managers to quickly navigate through and perform several actions. To return to the employee information, simply select one of the menu tabs. For example: [Image: screenshot] Using this new configuration, managers can view employee information more easily by viewing more details at a time and navigating quickly through menu tabs and HR Actions. For more information, see the in-product help.
EP-9668 Taxable Wages on Payroll Inquiry Form Employees can now view taxable wage information on the Taxes Withheld tab on the Payroll Inquiry form. This form displays a breakdown of all taxes withheld from their pay, such as Medicare and Social Security. Employees can use this form to verify that their taxes are being withheld correctly based on their pre-tax savings. For more information, see the in-product help.

Onboarding / Benefits Enrollment (OBE) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
OBE-6813 Warning Message for Same Effective Date as Posting If the system detects that an existing Benefit Coverage Detail record has the same effective date as the Benefit Enrollment posting process, a warning message now informs the service provider conducting the process. This warning displays the company, employee ID, employee name, and offer type of the posting to make it easier to determine the discrepancy. The batch can still be posted successfully by disregarding this warning message, if necessary. For more information, see the in-product help.
OBE-9711 Enhancement to Decision Recommendation Tool Wording Plans suggested by a Decision Recommendation Tool during Benefits Enrollment now display the Save plan button, which is used to save the plan details as the recommended plan for later steps. The previous wording, Select plan, implied that only the recommended plans could be selected, and has been changed. When a user saves a recommended plan, the plan displays with a label indicating that it was saved on that recommendation tool. In addition, users can select the menu item for their decision recommendation tool to compare saved plans. For more information, see the in-product help.
WSP-2740 Enhancement to Unarchive Benefits Web Enrollment To improve visibility, the Unarchive Benefits Web Enrollment form no longer displays the Batch Number, Batch Status, and Completed Batch fields. These fields almost never displayed relevant information for this form, and thus have been removed. For more information, see the in-product help.

Prism (PD) Enhancements

Ticket Category Description Summary Help Content
PD-20003 Billing Enhancement to Billing Rules (Unbundled) Form The Select Billing Rules list, which is accessible by selecting Billing Rule on the Billing Rules (Unbundled) form, now displays values for the following fields: - Rule Number - Rule Description - Rate - Rule Based On - Rule End Date - Voucher Type - Batch Type - Obsolete - Obsolete Date - Billing Code - Benefit Plan For example: [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Billing User Guide.
PD-19722 and PD-19749 Client Enhancement to PTO Benefit Plans and Time Off Setup Workflow Forms In association with the Nebraska Healthy Families and Workplaces Act in effect as of October 1, 2025, which allows employees to begin accruing leave after they have worked 80 hours, a new field, Begin accruing hours AFTER ___ hours worked, now displays in the Flat Amount per Hours Worked panel on the legacyPTO Benefit Plans form and the Time Off Setup Workflow form. For example: PTO Benefit Plans form [Image: screenshot] Time Off Setup Workflow form [Image: screenshot] > Note: Note the following: - You must select the Flat Amount by Hours Worked option in the following fields to display the Begin accruing hours AFTER ___ hours worked field: - Calculation Basis field on the PTO Benefit Plans form - Accrual Method field in the Plans panel on the Time Off Setup Workflow form - Employees do not begin accruing hours until they reach the number of hours worked as entered in the Begin accruing hours AFTER ___ hours worked field. - Accruals differ depending on whether you enable If the actual hours worked are not an even multiple of the hours worked then accrue a fraction of the accrual hours. For more information, see the in-product help, PrismHR Client Administration Guide, or PrismHR PTO User Guide.
RRT-6601 Client Enhancement to PTO Register Types Form The warning that displays when you select End of Quarter in the Trigger Method field on the PTO Register Types form was updated to provide more clarity when using this setting. For example: [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Client Administration Guide.
WSP-2628 Client Enhancement to Client Details Form The Classifications panel in the Client Details form now provides the following: - A truncated version of the SIC Code and NAICS Code names using ellipses (…) now displays. (Cursor over the SIC Code and NAICS Code descriptions to display their full name.) For example: [Image: screenshot] - The first three multi-entity groups associated with a client now display in alphabetical order, which replaced the original Multi-Entity Group field. (You can scroll down to view other multi-entity groups.) For example: [Image: screenshot] In addition, you can select a multi-entity group to display its details in the Multi-Entity Group Details form. > Note: Note the following: - Users whose user role is set to FULL or INQUIRY for the Multi-Entity Group Details form have enabled access to the links that display in the Multi-Entity Group column. - Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Multi-Entity Group Details form can only view the client details (no links display in the Multi-Entity Group column). For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Client Administration Guide.
WSP-2780 Client Enhancement to Compute Commissions Form The system now computes the Commission Basis Amount for PTG Commission Base in the Compute Commissions form using the calculation logic of the Target Amount divided by the number of invoices. For example, if there are four invoices in the commission period, the Target amount (10000) would be divided by the four invoices in the period, which would set the Commission Basis Amount = 2500. (This is logically consistent with Net commission = Commission Basis Amount * Percent rate; 2500 * 30% = 750.) For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Client Administration Guide.
API-7687, PD-19029, PD-20208, and PD-20210 Human Resources Enhancements to Employee Details Form The following enhancements are now available on the Employee Details form: - The system now updates an employee’s mailing address across clients for employees who have the same Employee ID for multiple clients. - Information for the following fields no longer displays after an employee is deidentified using the Inactive Data Deletion form: - Work Email - Work Phone - The audit entry for deidentified employees that displays on the File Audit form now displays the user ID and the IP address of the user who ran the deidentification process. (Previously, the User ID field displayed “Background Process” and the Client IP Address field displayed “N/A.”) For example: [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Human Resources User Guide.
PD-19191 Human Resources Enhancement to Approvals Pending Form Previously, the PTO amounts in the Approvals Pending form did not match the amounts in Employee Portal (EP). To resolve this issue, leave approvals now display the hours from the employee’s PTO register in the Detail Description column in the Approval Summary section: - Register YTD Accrued - Register YTD Taken - Register YTD Available For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Human Resources User Guide.
PD-19952 Human Resources Enhancement to Employee Fields Import Form Four new WH347 fields now display on the Select Field list in the Employee Fields Import form when you select Field Code in the Fields to Update panel. For example: [Image: screenshot] > Note: Note the following: - These fields reside in the WH347 Skilled Trade Classification panel on the Skills & Education tab in the Employee Details form. - All WH347 fields are required as part of the import, but fields other than the Journeyworker/Apprentice field can have a blank value for the data. - The WH347 Apprentice Program Approval and WH347 Level of Progression fields are only allowed if you enter Apprentice (RA) in the Journeyworker/Apprentice field. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRHuman Resources User Guide.
PD-20206 Human Resources Enhancement to Employee Dependents Form The system now removes the following field information in the Employee Dependents form from employee records when an employee is deidentified: Dependent Details panel: - Last Name - First Name - Social Security Number Address Details panel: - Address - Address Line 2 - ZIP Code - City - State - Primary Phone - Work Phone - Email Note: To deidentify employees, select Employees in the Data Type field on the Inactive Data Deletion form. (For more information, refer to the “Removing Inactive Customer Data” topic in the PrismHR Client Administration Guide, which displays when you select the help ( [Image: screenshot] ) icon in the Inactive Data Deletion form.) For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Human Resources User Guide.
WSP-1731 and WSP-1732 Human Resources Enhancement to Mass Employee H/R Actions Form A new field, Employee Selection Method, now displays on the Mass Employee H/R Actions form. For example: [Image: screenshot] You can use the Employee Selection Method field to select employees from a generated list or import a list of employees for a mass H/R action using the following options: - Generate List: Selecting this option and completing the required fields generates a list of employees who meet the selected criteria. - Import List: Selecting this option and completing the required fields displays the Upload Employees button, which you can select to import your list of employees who meet the selected criteria. > Note: Note the following when working with Import List: - The system only accepts uploaded files as a single-column list of employee IDs in either .txt or .csv format. - Employees listed in the import file who do not exist in the selected client are automatically excluded from the import. - The system validates the contents of the imported employee list and if any employee does not pass validation, they are not included in the on-screen report. In addition, if “Fail” displays in the Import Status column in the report, this indicates that the employee does not match the selected criteria. (You can access this report by selecting Download Report.) - If no employees pass validation a message displays, “There were no employees with selected.” > Note: Note the following: - Users whose user role is set to FULL for the Mass Employee H/R Actions form have enabled access to the fields on this form. - Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Mass Employee H/R Actions form only have view access to the fields on this form. - A message displays when you select one of the options listed above. (This message originally displayed when making a selection from the H/R Action field.) For example: [Image: screenshot] Click OK to continue. - You cannot edit the H/R Action or Employee Selection Method after making a selection in these fields. (Click Cancel to clear the form.) For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Human Resources User Guide.
WSP-2836, WSP-2837, and WSP-2838 New Employee Import Enhancement to New Employee Import Dashboard Three new options, Division, Department, and Project Codes, are now available in the Table field on the Employee Import Code Translation Tables form, which you can access by selecting Code Translation Tables on the New Employee Import dashboard. For example: [Image: screenshot] You can use the Division, Department, and Project Codes options to set up a translation table for division, department, and project codes, so you can use this translation table to change the import file code to an accepted PrismHR code. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR New Employee Import User Guide.
PD-19174 Payroll Enhancement to Employee PTO Accruals Report A new column, Current Balance, now displays in the Employee PTO Accruals Report. For example: [Image: screenshot] The Current Balance column displays the YTD hours available for each employee from the Employee PTO Register for each register type. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Reports guide.
PD-19549 Payroll Enhancement to Eligible PTO Report Form The system did not display the correct column headers in the XLS report output of the Eligible PTO Hours Report that you can generate using the Eligible PTO Report form. All columns now display the correct header in the XLS report output. In addition, the following columns now display in the XLS output of the Eligible PTO Hours Report: - Calc Hours: The weekly average of the hours the employee worked. - Balance: Subtracts the hours used from the eligibility hours. - 5+: Indicates if the employee was hired more than five years ago. For example: [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Reports guide.
PD-19968 Payroll Enhancement to Summary Time Sheet Entry Form A new column, Status Type, now displays on the Summary Time Sheet Entry form. For example: [Image: screenshot] The Status Type column displays the employee’s classification status (first part of status type) and employee type (second part of status type, separated by a dash (-); for example, A-FT): - Classification status: A for active, L for on leave, or T for terminated. - Employee Type: FT for full-time and PT for part-time. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Processing Guide.
PD-20035 Payroll Enhancement to Batch Payments Form A new column, Edit Employee Details, now displays when you select Yes in the Suppress Allocation column in the Batch Payments form. For example: [Image: screenshot] Selecting the Edit Employee Details ( [Image: screenshot] ) icon in this column displays the Time Sheet Allocation form, where you can assign the Department, Division, Location, Shift, Position, Project, and Phase allocations. For example: [Image: screenshot] After entering the allocation types, click Accept to apply the values to the batch payment. Note: If you override the home data fields in the Time Sheet Allocation form, a checkmark displays in the Edit Employee Details column in the Batch Payments form. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Overrides Guide.
PD-20141, PD-20142, PD-20143, and PD-20144 Payroll Enhancements to Payments Pending Form The following enhancements now reside on the Payments Pending form: - You now have better visibility into the wire processing status when a payroll is in WT.PEND status, so you can stay informed about the progress and status of this process. The payroll still resides in WT.PEND status, but it will have a secondary status to help you understand whether the file has been created for the bank. As part of this updated process, the secondary status changes to “Created” after users create a file during ACH processing. - Four new fields, File Status, Transfer Type, Client ID, and Cost Center, now display. For example: [Image: screenshot] These new fields display the following information: - File Status: Displays the wire processing status, which is either Created or Pending. (Only wire transfers display Pending.) - Transfer Type: The transfer method for ACH information as configured on the Billing tab in the Client Details form, which is either Wire Transfer or Reverse Wire. - Client ID: The ID for the client that displays in the Client Name field. - Cost Center: The description for the cost center created in the Client Details form. - The Display Invoice button no longer displays because now you can simply select a Payroll number and the invoice displays. - You can now select multiple payments to process and mark as received by selecting each Payroll line item or select all payments by clicking the new checkbox next to the Payroll column and then click Mark Received. (Previously, you could only select one payment at a time to mark as received.) - Note: After making the selection and clicking Mark Received a message displays, “Are you sure you want to mark these payments as received?” Click Yes to continue. (This updates the batch Status so the payroll processor can continue to process the payroll batch.) For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Processing Guide.
PD-20146 Payroll Enhancement to SuperBatch Form A new icon, [Image: screenshot] , now displays in the SuperBatch form when you create a wire file. For more information, see the in-product help, PrismHR Payroll Processing Guide, or Understanding the SuperBatch Status Icons task sheet.
PD-20148 and PD-20153 Payroll Enhancement to Scheduled Payments Form A new field, Phase, is now available on the Time Sheet Allocation form, which you can access by selecting the Edit Employee Details icon on the Scheduled Payments form. For example: [Image: screenshot] Note: You must enable the SCHEDULED-PAYMENTS-CHANGE-DEFAULTS custom feature code to display the Edit Employee Details icon. You can enter or select a Phase that is valid for the current client, which is applied during payroll processing to any payments made to the specified employee. Note: The Phase field does not display if the Project with phase option is not set up as a Detail Time Sheet Field on the Time Sheet tab in the Client Details form. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Overrides Guide.
PD-20149 Payroll Enhancement to Employee Scheduled Payments Report Two new columns, Proj and Phase, now display in the output after running the Employee Scheduled Payments Report. For example: [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHRPayroll Reports guide.
PD-20150 and PD-20151 Payroll Enhancement to Payroll Allocation Report Parameters and Payroll Allocation Report Forms You can now sort by phases using the new Allocate/Sort by Phase option in the Primary Sort, Secondary Sort, and Tertiary Sort fields on the Payroll Allocation Report Parameters and Payroll Allocation Report forms. For example: [Image: screenshot] [Image: screenshot] You can use the Allocate/Sort by Phase option to adjust the sort criteria by the project phase. Note: If you do not enable the Sort On Allocation Codes Instead of Descriptions parameter, the system will sort fields by description. In addition, if you enable the Phase option, the system will sort Phase by code (there is no description for phases). For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Reports guide.
PD-20205 Payroll Enhancement to Employee Garnishments Form Information for the following fields on the Employee Garnishments form no longer displays after an employee is deidentified using the Inactive Data Deletion form: - Docket Number - Annotation - Case Identifier For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration Guide.
PD-20174, WSP-2825, WSP-2826, WSP-2827, and WSP-2828 Payroll Enhancements to Data Import Tool The following enhancements now reside in the Data Import Tool, which is available on the Operations\ Import Processing menu. New TTO Code Field in Position Codes Import Template You can now import valid TTO codes (Tipped Taxable Occupation Code that applies to an eligible tipped position) while importing positions using the Position Codes import template. For example: [Image: screenshot] Note: The system displays an error during the import process if the TTO Code is invalid, “<TTO Code> is not a valid TTO Code.” New Client Details (Special Delivery) Import Template You can use this import template to import special delivery instructions for the client to reduce the amount of manual work required. For example: [Image: screenshot] The following fields that display on the Client Details (Special Delivery) import template allow you to update existing records or add new records without including the entire list of data: - Replace existing data: Replaces existing data with data included in the file but does not remove data that is not included in the file. For example: - If the system already has a delivery method for location 1 and location 1 is included in the file with changes, the system confirms the changes. - If the system already has a delivery method for location 2 and location 2 is not in the file, then the system keeps the location 2 delivery method data. - Remove existing data (default): Removes existing data that is not included in the file for that client. For example: - If the system already has a delivery method for location 1 and location 1 is included in the file with changes, the system confirms the changes. - If the system already has a delivery method for location 2 and location 2 is not in the file, then the system removes the location 2 delivery method data. - Keep existing data: Prioritizes keeping existing data and adds new data included in the file. (That is, if data exists and is included in the file, the upload skips the value in the file and keeps the existing system values.) For example: - If the system already has a delivery method for location 1 and location 1 is included in the file with changes, the system keeps the existing data, not the data included in the file. - If the system already has a delivery method for location 2 and location 2 is not in the file, then the location 2 delivery method data remains the same in the system. > Note: Note the following: - Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Client Details form cannot import data using the Client Details (Special Delivery) import template and subsequently, the Data Import Tool icon will not display on this form. - Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Client Details form can view the Client Details (Special Delivery) import template, but cannot import data. - Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data. - Users who do not have access to a particular company through client access groups are unable to import data into that company. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration Guide.
RRT-6601 PTO Enhancement to Time Off Setup Workflow Form The warning that displays when you select End of Quarter in the Accrual Frequency field on the Accrual Schedule panel in the Time Off Setup Workflow form was updated to provide more clarity when using this setting. For example: [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR PTO User Guide.
PD-19883 System Enhancement to ACH Files Effective March 20, 2026, regardless of ACH volume, all Prearranged Payment and Deposit Entry (PPD) Credits for wages and similar compensation now includes the description “PAYROLL” in Position 54-63 in the Company Entry Description field in the ACH file. Note: This standardization helps RDFIs better identify payroll-related transactions and prevent fraud associated with payroll redirections. (The ACH files now reflect this information.) Important! If you are using a Third Party Format in the ACH Originators form for the ACH file this update will not affect those files. For information about ACH files, see the in-product help or PrismHR ACH User Guide.
PP-1986 System UEX Update for Prism Header and Menus The Prism UEX has received a stylistic update to the main header bar, the breadcrumb trail, and the menus. The icons, coloration, and spacing of the UI has been restyled. For example: [Image: screenshot] In addition, the Prism menus now display the category headers on their own lines, with the categories organized into individual sections. In addition, the menus can now display three or four columns based on the available space in the browser window. For example: [Image: screenshot] This enhancement updates the user interface throughout Prism to improve the experience navigating menus and breadcrumb trails. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR System Administration Guide.
PP-2036 System Style Updates for Sign In Screens The Sign In form and the Reset Password form have been updated to the current UX standards and maintain consistency across the platform. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR System Administration Guide.
PP-2074 System Enhancement to the Employee Portal Configuration Size To support the new drag-and-drop interface for resizing widgets in Employee Portal Configuration Templates and Client Overrides, the Dashboard Configuration form now supports a wider and taller viewport size. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR System Administration Guide.
WSP-2789 System Enhancement to User Roles Form You can now obsolete a user role that is no longer in use by enabling Obsolete on the User Roles form. For example: [Image: screenshot] In addition, selecting Role ID displays the User Role Search list, where the new Obsolete column indicates whether the user role is obsolete (Y) or not obsolete (N). For example: [Image: screenshot] > Note: Note the following: - You cannot assign an obsoleted role to a user or obsolete a user role that is currently assigned to users. If this occurs an error message displays, “This role must be removed from all users before it can be obsoleted!” - Once a user role is obsolete, you cannot manually enter an obsoleted role for a user. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR System Administration Guide.

Fixes

Benefits Administration (BA) Fixes

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
WSP-2733 Previously, on the Retirement Register Adjustment form, when you created a new transaction and saved the form without providing any input in the Adjustment Date field, an error with a message stating, Adjustment Date is mandatory was displayed. Upon clicking Ok, the Adjustment Date field was disabled and you could not enter the any value in the required field, which was incorrect. Now, this is fixed. While saving the form for a new transaction, if you miss to fill any required fields, and when you close the warning message, you can now enter the missing required fields and save the form.
WSP-2752 Previously, on the Benefits Eligibility Report form, when you ran a report, in the Benefits Eligibility Summary Report that was displayed, all the applicable benefit rules for a Benefit Group were not displayed. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2795 Previously, on the Employee Retirement Loans form, when you selected the Loan Number, the Employee ID displayed but the Employee Name did not display automatically. Additionally, when you opened the Employee Retirement Loans form in a modal view, the Close button did not work properly. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2796 Previously, on different Group Benefit forms, while using the Employee selector, when you searched for an employee in the Employee ID or Name search field, the results displayed the search term which was not within the Employee ID or Name criteria. This was an incorrect behavior. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2810 Previously, on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form, the warning message validation that appeared when you changed a value in any fields worked for only the elective amount fields. Now, this is fixed. The warning message validation that appeared when you changed a value in any fields now works for all the election fields.
WSP-2835 Previously, on the Employee Dependents form, when a dependent of an employee had a Social Security Number and if the SSN Mask Override field on the Report Print Options form was set to Show Employee ID, then the Social Security Number field for that dependent displayed blank values. Now, this is fixed. When you set SSN Mask Override as Show Employee ID, then on the Employee Dependents form, if an employee has a dependent, the Employee ID is displayed as a read-only text in the Social Security Number field.
WSP-2855 Previously, on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form, after you select an active enrolled Employee, and then under the Retirement Register Adjustments section, when you click the hyperlink value under the Transaction No. column, then on the Retirement Register Adjustment modal form that is displayed, the Cancel button appears on the form, which was not an expected behavior. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2856 Previously, on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form, the system allowed invalid setups in the Elective Amount field that did not work with the Auto Escalation? field, which lead to potential configuration errors. Now, this is fixed. The Auto Escalation? checkbox can be selected only when: - Elective Type has a value in the Amount field which is greater than 0 and Percent is selected. - Elective Type has a value in the Amount field which is greater than 0 with Percent selected and additional values exist in the Employee Contributions table.
  • Elective Type has a value in the Amount field which is greater than 0 and Percent is selected.
  • Elective Type has a value in the Amount field which is greater than 0 with Percent selected and additional values exist in the Employee Contributions table. | WSP-2892 | Previously, on the Retirement Plans form, under the Eligibility Requirements section, the values in the Employment Type drop-down list were not displayed. | Now, this is fixed. | | WSP-2965 | Previously, on the Benefit Summary Statement form, when you generate a Benefit Summary Report, then on the Benefit Confirmation Statement report that is displayed, the dependents with SSNs did not display accurate Employee ID. | Now, this is fixed. | | WSP-2987 | Previously, we had fixed an issue that caused the system to calculate a Non-Elective Match for the payroll even after the employee had attained or crossed the Compensation Limit under the Plan Year Deferral Limits section on the Retirement Plans form when the Non-Elective Match field on the Retirement Match Rules form is blank for the corresponding retirement plan. | Now, this is fixed. With this release, we are reverting the changes made so that the system can calculate a Non-Elective Match for the payroll even after the employee has attained or crossed the Compensation Limit under the Plan Year Deferral Limits section on the Retirement Plans form when the Non-Elective Match field on the Retirement Match Rules form is blank for the corresponding retirement plan. | | WSP-3019 | Previously, on the Benefit Plan Setup form, after selecting Plan Class as Retirement, when you select the Plan ID whose Auto Escalation is not flagged, and then try to save the form by making any changes under the Eligibility Criteria section, then an error message is displayed stating, Auto escalator cannot be unchecked even for employees who are not enrolled in the selected plan, which is an incorrect validation. | Now, this is fixed. The records are now saved without any error unless the employee shown in the error message has a valid enrollment in the plan being saved. | ### Compliance (CMP) Fixes
Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-6930 Previously, on the Positions form, after clicking the Benefit Group hyperlink, you received different errors. Now, this is resolved. On the Positions form, after clicking the Benefit Group hyperlink, you are presented with the benefit groups set up for that client.
CMP-6849 Previously, when the Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers process was run, and an employee had taxable wages with overlimit wages to the SUTA state being processed that had been backed out via tax adjustment before running the utility, the did not recognize the tax adjustments. Now, when the Recalculate Taxes on Vouchers process is run, and an employee has taxable wages with overlimit wages to the SUTA state being processed that have been backed out via tax adjustment before running the utility, the adjustment will continue to occur. Each occurrence will be reported in the processing reports, on-screen process log report, and the Job Control Status report, including the PDF and XLS versions, with the following message stating Employee XXXXXX in company XXXXX has 0.00 Gross Taxable with an Overlimit amount >0.00, resulting in a negative tax amount. Additional adjustment may be required.
CMP-6839 Previously, for the state of Delaware, the system used to report incorrect figures for PFML (DE0000-014) on the MasterTax RTS file. Now, this is resolved. Delaware PFML records on the RTS will be updated to report: - 500 records, DE0000-014 positions 95 - 108 QTD Net Taxable Wages, Gross - Sheltered up to the wage limit (currently correct) - 500 records, DE0000-014 positions 109 - 122 YTD Net Taxable Wages, Gross - Sheltered up to the wage limit (currently correct) - 500 records, DE0000-014 positions 137 - 150 YTD Gross Taxable wages, Gross Wages - Sheltered wages NOT excluding overlimit wages 601 record, DE0000-014, positions 72 - 85 QTD Gross Taxable wages, Gross Wages - Sheltered wages NOT excluding overlimit wages - 500 records, DE0000-014 positions 123 - 136 QTD Gross Taxable wages, Gross Wages - Sheltered wages NOT excluding overlimit wages > Note: Note: This is true with SBEA and NONSBEA versions and w/wo account ID.
CMP-6787 Previously, the 500F records in the MasterTax RTS Schedule R dis not correctly report the YTD values for Q4 for the 00-12TIPs and 00-16TIPS. Now, this is resolved. 00-12TIPS and 00-16TIPS correctly report in the QTD wage amounts (positions 95-108 and 123-136) and YTD wage amounts (positions 109-122 and 137-150) in the 500F records on the Mastertax RTS, Schedule R.
CMP-6747 Previously, when an employee was assigned to a Remote Worksite Location, the FUTA bill rate was getting calculated based upon the FUTA rate applicable to the resident state, like the FUTA accrual. Now, when an employee is assigned to a Remote Worksite Location, the FUTA bill rate will be calculated based upon the FUTA rate applicable to the resident state, like the FUTA accrual.
CMP-6734 Previously, the option to exempt an employee from state withholding was not available for all states on the New Hire Entry form. Now, this is resolved.
CMP-6452 Previously, the Local EFW2 export for the Local EFW2 Code ‘Tax Services PA’ (Jordan Tax Services) was missing the required RT (Total) record. This was causing file upload errors. Now, this is resolved. Local EFW2 export for ‘Tax Services PA’ includes an RT record (total record) for each RE record (Employer record). The RW record is also present, since it is necessary for the RT record.
CMP-6450 Previously, the Local EFW2 Code ‘Tax Services Admin’ (BERKHEIMER) was missing the required employer 6-digit PSD code on the RE record position 222-227. This was causing file upload errors. Now, this is resolved. The Local EFW2 export ‘Tax Services Admin’ (BERKHEIMER) RE record position 222-227 will be zero-filled.

EERT-2911 When a 1099 contractor employee was employed by multiple companies but had the same Employee ID across all organizations, the 1099 form in Employee Portal did not display all pages of their form. Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
EERT-3023 When a user updated a Handbook document type for Onboarding in Document Management, the document displayed the updated version for that user, but displayed the outdated document version name for employees in their Saved Documents. This is fixed.

EERT-3061 When a user displayed the View/Compare Benefits form during Benefits Enrollment, Spanish language options did not display properly. This is fixed.

Prism (PD) Fixes

Jira # Category Issue Summary Resolution
PD-20001 General An error message that a direct deposit update failed sometimes displayed when users entered a direct deposit on the Deposit tab in the Employee Details form for employees who transferred between clients or were rehired. This is fixed.
PD-20406 General There were times when the Payment Pending form had a slow response time. This is fixed. To improve the performance on the form, Multi-Entity Groups have been removed. In the upcoming release, the indexing will be improved, and the Multi-Entity Groups will be reinstated.
PP-1933 General When a user added a new row in the Local Tax Identifiers subsection of the Employer Details form, the user could add duplicate tax codes. This is fixed.
PP-2016 General When a user made changes to individual records on the Timesheet Detail form, pressing the Enter key did not save the changes. This is fixed.
RRT-6590 General When users exported reports to Excel with a column that contained only a percent sign (%), the export failed and the system displayed an error message. This is fixed.
PD-19033 Payroll The system disregarded tax exemptions at the pay code level in the Check History Import form when users entered a value for a non-taxable payment. The system now honors Pay Code Tax Overrides when non-taxable amounts are imported.
PD-19330 Payroll The system sent a Payroll Finalization email to the Payroll Approver before the payroll was posted/finalized each time a payroll was approved. Worksite managers who are Payroll Approvers now only receive a Payroll Finalization email one time when they approve the same payroll more than once.
RRT-6577 Payroll The system did not include the employee’s ID in the error message, “There is insufficient funds to pay taxes on voucher,” in the warnings and errors when the payroll was calculated even though the issue was related to a particular employee. The system now displays the employee’s ID in the error message, so users can easily determine which employee has insufficient funds.
RRT-6672 Payroll CMP-6747 was generating payroll processing stoppages for some employees stating “Cannot read SUTA accrual rate” due to missing SUI rates. This occurred when that employee had an Override Geocode with an Override End Date set on the Address tab of the Employee Details form. This is fixed.
WSP-2782 Payroll When users imported client commissions using the Client Commissions import template and enabled the Keep existing data and update duplicate field in the Data Import Tool, the system did not honor null values as equivalent in the Salesperson, Based On, Based On Item, and Based On Plan fields and created duplicate entries on the Commissions form. This is fixed.

Welcome

PrismHR software is specifically designed to help Professional Employer Organizations (PEOs) and Administrative Services Organizations (ASOs) reduce risk, be more efficient, expand business, and be more profitable.

When you choose PrismHR, you are choosing more than just a software platform. You are partnering with a team of professionals who are deeply invested in the PEO and ASO industry and dedicated to providing the best technology and services possible. You are also partnering with other professionals in the industry in the sense that we all learn from each other.

WSP-2800, WSP-2801 Changes to the Benefit Utilities form Under the Benefit Utilities section, after selecting the Auto Escalation utility, when you click Search, a new button named Report has been added in the Results section which allows to generate a report of the search results. To update the records displayed in the search results, select the record(s) and click Update. Once the records are updated, you can view the report. For more information, see Benefit Utilities help topic.
WSP-3086 Changes to the Retirement Plan Enrollment form On the Retirement Plan Enrollment form, when you select a plan and provide an effective date, then under the Election Details section, the earlier read-only Retirement HPE Status table has been renamed to Mandatory Roth Catch-up Participant. [Image: screenshot] For more information, see Election Details help topic.
WSP-3111 Temporary logic for Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit selection On the following forms, - Retirement Plans - Benefit Plan Setup when you select the Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit option for the Deemed ROTH field, the system uses the same logic that is used for the No (Default) option. When you select Deemed ROTH as No (Default), then the Pre-tax Catchup contributions is taken as pre-tax until total pre-tax contributions equals the 402G limit. Once the 402G limit is reached, no further Pre-tax or Pre-tax Catchup is taken for contributions. For more information, see Setting Up Basic Information for a Retirement Plan and Setting Up a Benefit Plan help topics.
WSP-2914, WSP-2915. WSP-2916 Functionality of options under the Deemed ROTH field The Secure 2.0 Act includes a mandatory Roth catch-up requirement for Highly Paid Employees (HPE) participating in a 401(k), 403(b), or 457 retirement plan. For the 2026 tax year, employees with $150,000 in prior year, Social Security wages must contribute catch-up on a Roth basis, to the extent they have not previously made Roth contributions during the year. To comply with this Act, we introduced the following options for the Deemed ROTH field on the Retirement Plans form: - No (default) - Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit - Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup before 402(g) limit - Pre-tax to ROTH and Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit Determining a Highly Paid Employee - An employee is considered to be an HPE only if the corresponding Retirement Year is defined and the HPE Prior Year field is set to Yes on the Mandatory Roth Catch-up Participant table under the Other tab on the Employee Details form. The functionality of the drop-down options for the Deemed ROTH field are listed below: - No (default) - This option is selected by default. Selecting this option signifies that a plan does not have a Deemed ROTH feature. Additionally, this option does not force any amounts to ROTH or ROTH Catchup. However, any elected ROTH and ROTH Catchup contributions will continue until limits are reached. For example, if an employee is an HPE for prior year and the plan offers a ROTH catchup component, then Pretax catchup is taken until the 402G limit is met. Once the Pre-tax and the Pre-tax Catchup contribution hits the 402G limit ($23,500), then the Pre-tax contributions stops, and any elected ROTH and ROTH Catchup contributions can continue up to the limits ($23,500/$7,500). - Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit - This option will be available with the January release. Currently, this selection this option uses the logic of No (default) option. - Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup before 402(g) limit - This option automatically treats all subject employee Pre-tax catch-up elections as Roth elections regardless of whether the total pre-tax contributions equal the 402(g) limit. It limits the Pretax contributions to $23,500 for HPEs. Note: Please note the following: - This option will not be available when Prohibit Deductions is checked for either of the following on the Retirement Plans form: - Roth Post-Tax Deduction Code - Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code - If an HPE has a retirement Catchup deductions taken as Roth Catchup, the deduction is taken using the Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code assigned under the Deduction/Bill Code Overrides section on the Retirement Plans form. When there is no code on the Retirement Plans form, then the Roth Catch-up Deduction Code assigned at the system level is used as default. - When the deduction is taken using the Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code, the deduction displays as a ROTH catchup on voucher and on the Employee Retirement Plan Register form. - Pre-tax to ROTH and Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit - This option automatically treats subject employee pre-tax elections as Roth elections only after pre-tax contributions reach the standard contribution limit. This means that the Pre-tax elections are limited to $23,500 and if there are any remaining Pre-tax elections, they are taken as Roth elections. Note: Please note the following: - This option will not be available when Prohibit Deductions is checked for either of the following on the Retirement Plans form: - Roth Post-Tax Deduction Code - Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code - If an HPE has a retirement pre-tax or Catchup deductions taken as Roth or Roth Catchup, the deduction is taken using the Roth and Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code assigned under the Deduction/Bill Code Overrides section on the Retirement Plans form. When there is no code on the Retirement Plans form, then the Roth or Roth Catch-up Deduction Code assigned at the system level is used as default. - When the deduction is taken using the Roth or Roth Catch-Up Deduction Code, the deduction displays as a Roth or Roth catchup on voucher and on the Employee Retirement Plan Register form. For more information, see, Setting Up Basic Information for a Retirement Plan and Setting Up a Benefit Plan help topics.

CMP-6892 Use Employer SUI Rate as Company SUI Bill Rate When the Use ER SUI rate as Bill rate setting is applied, you can use the Client State Tax Bill Rate for PFML State Misc3 ER (-41) codes when a Client State Tax Bill rate record exists. On the Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, if the Use Employer SUI Rate as Company SUI Bill Rate field is checked: - If no Client Bill rate record is set up on the client, Tax Bill rates will use the ER Tax Rate form (or vertex default if missing) - If Client Bill rate record is set up on the client, Tax Bill rates will use the ER Tax Rate form for all taxes (or vertex default if missing) except for tax code XX-41 (Employer PFML Bill Rate) When the Use ER SUI rate as Bill rate setting is applied, to use the client bill rate for State Misc 3 Employer (Paid Family Medical Leave), you must set a 0.00 Client SUI Bill rate. All Client Bill rates will be ignored except for the State Misc 3 for PFML. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR System Administration User Guide.

CMP-6329 Updates to Form W-2 build The State Income Tax Account Number on the employee Form W-2 will now be pulled from the Client Details form or the Employer Details form based on the tax deduction code, unless an override exists on the Employer Details form on the SIT Rpt Entity field for that state under the State Tax section. The State Income Tax Account Number on the employee Form W-2 will be: - Client State Tax ID when: - Tax deduction code set to report at Client Level and ER Details, State is set to -select- or Client - Tax deduction code NOT set to report at Client Level, but ER Details, State is set to Client - Employer State Tax ID: - Tax deduction code NOT set to report at Client Level and ER Details, State is set to -select- or Employer - Tax deduction code set to report at Client Level, but ER Details, State is set to Employer > Note: Note: If the State Tax ID is not available on the corresponding reporting entity, the Form W-2 will not build, and an error will appear on the W2 Error Report stating State Employer ID not found for Client # for State XX OR State Employer ID not found for Employer for State XX For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Employer Administration User Guide.

CMP-6825 Changes to the EFW2 and EFW2C Download file The Address tab on the Employee Details form auto-populates the State field once you enter the ZIP Code field. However, you can change it manually. In case, the lower case is used for the State field, the EFW2 Download file used to pick up that lower case which resulted in filing failures. The same applies to the use of tilde in the employee’s name, etc. From now on, to avoid filing failures, the EFW2 and EFW2C Download file will: Will only accept any of the following; all other characters will be excluded: - - Uppercase letters (A-Z) (If the state is in proper case, the export will translate it to upper case) - Numbers (0-9) - Space - Hyphen (-) - Period (.) For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Employer Administration User Guide.
CMP-6856, CMP-6822 Qualified Tips & Overtime (New Form) Use the Qualified Tips and Overtime form to update the annual data for qualified overtime and qualified tips to report them in the employee Form W-2 for the tax year This option is provided to support federal reporting and compliance requirements supporting the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA). For more information, please visit the article named OBBBA No Tax Setup Guide on the Customer Resource Center. If an employee works for multiple clients in a tax year, this form will report information for the activeclient only. If an employee works for multiple clients in the same employer, then Box 14 will have combined amounts when built on the employer. W2 data will be aggregated by employer if applicable. If an employee works between multiple positions, you should determine a single TTO Code for reporting purposes. Box 14 of the employee Form W-2 reports the qualified tips and overtime dollar amounts against the following applicable designations for SBEA and employer builds: - Approx Qualified OT - TTOC <TTO Code1>; Cash Tips If an employee works for multiple clients in the same employer, then Box 14 will have combined amounts when built on the employer. CMP-6837, CMP-6924, CMP-6946 Minnesota Employer Tax for Paid Family and Medical Leave To support the new Minnesota PFML tax deductions, significant changes will be effective 1.1.26; State Misc 3 ER (-41), which has historically also been used to support the employer PFML portion, but is currently being used for the Minnesota Additional Assessment Fee. To support the separation of the Minnesota Admin Assessment fee from the employer PFML tax logic, we have introduced a new State Misc 4 Employer Tax Identifier, -54. For pay dates on or after 1.1.26, tax code 24-41will be used for employer contributions to Minnesota PFML. The Minnesota Additional Assessment tax will be reassigned to tax code 24-54. To prepare for this transition, the following updates will be required: 1. Tax Code & Report Settings - Update the description of the existing tax code 24-41 and add the description to tax code 26-54. - Tax Code 24-41 : Minnesota Paid Family Medical Leave (Employer). - Tax Code 24-54: Minnesota Additional Assessment or Minnesota Admin Assessment. 2. PrismHR Tax & MasterTax Mapping - Update the tax code mapping for PrismHR Tax & MasterTax imports to reflect the new identifier. 3. Rate Overrides - Migrate any existing rate overrides for the Minnesota Admin Assessment fee to State Misc4. - Use State Misc3 for Minnesota Employer PFML rate overrides. 4. Tax Suppression Review - Remove any suppression that may interfere with the new tax code functionality. - For the state of Minnesota, the employer portion for Paid Family and Medical Leave tax amounts for tax code 24-41 will appear on check stubs in the Employer Contribution section as MN PFML, showing accurate current and year-to-date tax amounts for pay dates on or after January 1, 2026. [Image: screenshot] - When tax code 24-41 is redirected to an alternate tax deduction code, for the state of Minnesota, the employer portion for Paid Family and Medical Leave tax amounts will appear on check stubs in the Employer Contribution section as MN PFML Private, displaying accurate current and year-to-date tax amounts for pay dates on or after January 1, 2026. [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Employer Administration User Guide.
1. Tax Code & Report Settings
- Update the description of the existing tax code 24-41 and add the description to tax code 26-54.
- Tax Code 24-41 : Minnesota Paid Family Medical Leave (Employer).
- Tax Code 24-54: Minnesota Additional Assessment or Minnesota Admin Assessment.
2. PrismHR Tax & MasterTax Mapping
- Update the tax code mapping for PrismHR Tax & MasterTax imports to reflect the new identifier.
3. Rate Overrides
- Migrate any existing rate overrides for the Minnesota Admin Assessment fee to State Misc4.
- Use State Misc3 for Minnesota Employer PFML rate overrides.
4. Tax Suppression Review

- When tax code 24-41 is redirected to an alternate tax deduction code, for the state of Minnesota, the employer portion for Paid Family and Medical Leave tax amounts will appear on check stubs in the Employer Contribution section as MN PFML Private, displaying accurate current and year-to-date tax amounts for pay dates on or after January 1, 2026.
CMP-6791, CMP-6845, CMP-6846 Changes to the Tax Deductions form The Tax Deductions form has a new field named Form W2 Box 14 Override. [Image: screenshot] \ Field Name \
Field Name Description
Form W2 Box 14 Override Select one of the following options: - – Select – : There is no override for the specified tax code. - Suppress from Box 14 : The specified tax code will not be included in the Form W-2 though the tax will be withheld. - Include in Box 14 : The specified tax code will be included in the Form W-2. > Note: Note: The Tax Deduction code W2 override is intended to support W2 reporting requirements for Private State PFML Plans when the standard tax deduction is redirected to a unique tax code. While this can be extended to other tax codes, there are a few limitations when the overrides do not apply. Following are some examples: - NYC borough which is translated to a single NYC Code. - Colorado Occupational Privilege Tax codes - Oregon Transit tax codes
- – Select – : There is no override for the specified tax code.
- Suppress from Box 14 : The specified tax code will not be included in the Form W-2 though the tax will be withheld.
- Include in Box 14 : The specified tax code will be included in the Form W-2.
- NYC borough which is translated to a single NYC Code.
- Colorado Occupational Privilege Tax codes
- Oregon Transit tax codes
Box 14 Description Override This field only displays if Include in Box 14 is selected above. Enter the description of the specified tax code that you want to display on the Form W-2.
CMP-6900 Changes to the EFW2 Download for Maine The 2025 Maine EFW2 download will contain the required updates: - RS record: - EE PFML contribution amounts as reported in Box 14 of the W-2 in positions 308 - 317 - Blank filled in positions 318 - 512 - RT record: - Positions 10 - 24 report the Total of State taxable wages from the RS records (positions 276-286) for the ER, right-justify, and zero-fill. - Positions 25 - 39 report the Total of State income tax withheld from the RS records (positions 287-297) for ER, right-justify, and zero-fill. - Fill positions 40 - 512 with blanks For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Employer Administration User Guide.
- RS record:
- EE PFML contribution amounts as reported in Box 14 of the W-2 in positions 308 - 317
- Blank filled in positions 318 - 512
- RT record:
- Positions 10 - 24 report the Total of State taxable wages from the RS records (positions 276-286) for the ER, right-justify, and zero-fill.
- Positions 25 - 39 report the Total of State income tax withheld from the RS records (positions 287-297) for ER, right-justify, and zero-fill.
- Fill positions 40 - 512 with blanks
CMP-6831, CMP-6959, API-8438 ACA Transmission File update for 2025 For the year 2025, the SoftwareId on the manifest will be 25A0023083 when the file is run for original, replacement, correction, additional clients, etc. For the year 2024, the SoftwareId it will continue to display 24A0019620. Note: This does not apply to the California e-file. This update will be available following the 2025 December release on Monday 12/22/2025. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR ACA User Guide.

Employee Portal (EP) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
EP-9580, EP-9581, EP-9582, EP-9583 Year-End Tax Forms Now Available Year-end tax forms are now available to view in Employee Portal. These include the W-2, W-2C, 1099, and 1095C forms. For more information, see the in-app help.
EP-9705, EP-9776, EP-9777 ROTH Banner for Highly Paid Employees Employees who are flagged as Highly Paid Employees (HPE) on the Other tab of the Employee Details form will now see a banner regarding their eligibility for catch-up deductions on retirement plans. Clients can customize this banner using a new option on the Configuration Template and Client Override forms. Select the Custom HPE Roth Banner option to display custom text boxes for both English and Spanish versions of the banner. Clients can use this feature to comply with the new SECURE 2.0 regulations regarding highly paid employees at their organizations. For more information, see the in-app help.

Prism (PD) Enhancements

Ticket Category Description Summary Help Content
PD-20315 and WSP-2941 Human Resources Enhancements to Employee Fields Import Form - Two new fields, Qualified OT Exempt and Qualified OT Exempt As Of, now display on the Select Field list when you select Field Code in the Fields to Update panel. For example: [Image: screenshot] > Note: Note the following: - These fields reside in the Miscellaneous panel on the Other tab in the Employee Details form. - The Qualified OT Exempt As Of field is required if the Qualified OT Exempt field is set to Yes, Y, or y. - You can now import the HPE Retirement Year and HPE Prior Year fields in the following scenarios: - The client does not have a retirement plan. - The client has a retirement plan, but it is not set up for the year being imported. - The employee is not enrolled in a retirement plan. For more information, see Performing Employee Fields Import.
PD-20316 Payroll Enhancement to Data Import Tool A new import template, Tip OT Register, is now available in the Data Import Tool. For example: [Image: screenshot] You can use the Tip OT Register import template to import employee tips and overtime data. Note: This import template is associated with the new Qualified Tips & Overtime form, which generates the annual and quarterly data for Qualified Overtime and Qualified Tips for reporting them on the employee Form W-2 for the tax year for the client. (To access this form, select the employee in the Employee Details form, then select Qualified Tips & Overtime on the Actions menu. You cannot access this form using the search bar.) For more information, see Importing Tips and Overtime Data.

Fixes

Benefits Administration (BA) Fixes

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
WSP-3167 Previously, on the Retirement Plans form, when a Highly Paid Employee (HPE) was enrolled in a retirement plan setup with Deemed ROTH option as Pre-tax to ROTH and Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit, then while calculating the payroll, the employee’s Roth Catchup election did not stop even after meeting the catchup limit (while not meeting contribution or pretax threshold). Now, this is fixed.
WSP-3170 Previously, on the Retirement Plans form, when the Deemed ROTH option was set to No (Default) for an HPE with Catch-Up Starts At Limit flagged on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form, then the employee was unable to contribute Pre-Tax Catchup until Elective and Pre-Tax Catchup contribution reached 402g limit, or catchup limit even if they did not reach the 402g limit. This issue was primarily dependent on the wages paid to the employee. If the employee was paid higher gross wages, then the Catch-up contribution amount reflected in the system. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-3171 Previously, in some scenarios, when an HPE was enrolled in a retirement plan setup with Deemed ROTH option as Pre-tax to ROTH and Pre-tax Catchup to ROTH Catchup after 402(g) limit, then after calculating the payroll, on the Employee Voucher form, negative Roth Catch-Up amount was displayed for deductions, which was incorrect. Now, this is fixed.

Compliance (CMP) Fixes

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-4587 Previously, both on the Global ACA Parameters form and the Client ACA Parameters (Overrides) form, the Starts First the Month field for both new and ongoing employees were placed incorrectly. Now, this is resolved. On the Global ACA Parameters form and the Client ACA Parameters (Overrides) form, the Starts First the Month field for both new and ongoing employees now relates to the Stability Period.
CMP-6412 Previously, for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients, for the same tax year, if an employee was paid by two employers or two client federal entities, both having the same numerical values for their Employer IDs except one ad a leading zero, then on the Form W-2 of the employee, Box 12 retirement codes were overstated by the second employer. Now, this is resolved. Now, for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients, for the same tax year, if an employee was paid by two employers or two client federal entities, both having the same numerical values for their Employer IDs except one ad a leading zero, then on the Form W-2 of the employee, Box 12 retirement codes will accurately break out the data by the correct employer.
CMP-6594 Previously, when an employee was paid in more than one client under the same employer for the NY Metro Commuter tax, the P (PEO EMPLOYER) level record was overstated by the Client level information that was pulling in the wages for the employee from both clients. Now, on the P Record - the total reported is the combined total of all underlying C records.
CMP-6654 Previously, for an employee who lived in the state of Maryland, but was assigned to any other work state, and the Suppress Work State Tax field was checked on the Positions form for the employee’s position, then the State Income Tax for Maryland was not withheld correctly by the system. Now, for an employee who lives in the state of Maryland, but is assigned to any other work state, and the Suppress Work State Tax field is checked on the Positions form for the employee’s position, then the State Income Tax for Maryland is withheld correctly by the system.
CMP-6887 Previously, if employees from the state of Wisconsin updated their tax forms while filling up their Form WT-4 or Form WT-4A in the Employee Portal, it did not display in PrismHR as an unhandled tax. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-6889 Previously, for the state of Colorado, the Employer Quarterly SUTA Tax Export was missing the 12th of the month indicator in positions 212, 213, and 214 of the S records in MasterTax RTS. This caused fatal errors when uploading to the state, as these positions must contain a 0 or 1 per the ICESA File Format. Now, the Employer Quarterly SUTA Tax Export file for Colorado will report a 0 or 1 in the S records, positions 212, 213, and 214 indicating if the employee worked in a pay period that included the 12th of the applicable month during the quarter.
CMP-6932 Previously, if an employee had filed a Form W-8 BEN and was paid using a Supplemental Pay Code, and the custom feature code VSUPPLEMENTAL was not enabled in the System Parameters form, then the taxable earnings for Federal Income Tax displayed as $0.00 on the employee payroll voucher. Now, when an employee has an employee type for example W8 where the Tax Exemption field is set to Suppress All But Federal Income Tax on the Employee Types form, and is paid using a Supplemental Pay Code, the taxable earnings will report correctly on the employee payroll voucher with or without the custom feature code VSUPPLEMENTAL enabled in System Parameters form.

Employee Portal (EP) Fixes

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
EP-9872 When some users accessed Document Management, a message banner displayed indicating an error fetching the ruleset for a client. This is fixed.

Prism (PD) Fixes

Jira # Category Issue Summary Resolution
PP-2112 General When a user viewed the Retirement Exports form, the names of the Client ID field and the Employer field did not display properly. This is fixed.
PD-20341 Payroll The system incorrectly calculated the Pay Schedule and Pay Group setup for the Period Start date when users processed a semi-monthly payroll, which caused the payroll to fail and displayed an error when they ran the Pay Schedule Report. This is fixed.
PD-20449 Payroll The system displayed an incorrect Pay Date for Monthly pay schedules with the Pay Day “1” day of the Month with the Pay Period End set to EOM after the Pay Date. When a Pay Schedule is set up Monthly with the Pay Day “1” day of the Month with the Pay Period End set to EOM after the Pay Date, the system creates payrolls for the Pay Group that are paid on the first of the month, where the period starts on the pay date and ends on the last day of that same month.
PD-20452 Payroll The system displayed an error message during a Position Codes import when an import contained related TTO and SOC Codes. This is fixed.

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/Release-Notes/2025/12/whatsnew-R_202512.htm Path: Release-Notes/2025/12/whatsnew-R_202512.htm

Welcome

PrismHR software is specifically designed to help Professional Employer Organizations (PEOs) and Administrative Services Organizations (ASOs) reduce risk, be more efficient, expand business, and be more profitable.

When you choose PrismHR, you are choosing more than just a software platform. You are partnering with a team of professionals who are deeply invested in the PEO and ASO industry and dedicated to providing the best technology and services possible. You are also partnering with other professionals in the industry in the sense that we all learn from each other.

To view release notes for PrismHR, click any of the links in the Table of Contents. Each release is represented with a book that features the month and year. Click these books to expand product names and version numbers for the release. The most recent documents are at the top of the list. Use the Search feature to look for a specific keyword or phrase. Open any PDFs for Download book to view and print release notes documents from the past year.

Release Notes: Enhancements and Fixes

You can view release notes in a variety of formats. You can:

  • View the detailed release notes. See: Release Notes
  • Download a PDF containing the detailed release notes. See Release Notes PDF
  • Download an Excel spreadsheet containing the detailed release notes. See: Release Notes Excel Note: The Excel export of release note does not include images. View the Detailed release notes in HTML format to see images.
