Compliance (CMP) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
CMP-3152 FSA Support Non-Standard calendar year plan For plan years beginning in 2025, a cafeteria plan may not allow salary reduction contributions for a health Flexible Spending Account in excess of $3,300. PrismHR now supports non-standard calendar years plans for a health Flexible Spending Account. Taxable billing with shelters will follow the FSA mid-plan year and match the employer’s tax-accrual sheltered amounts. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Benefits Administration User Guide.
CMP-4099 & CMP-7025 Changes to the State Rules form PrismHR payroll system now supports state-specific annual exempt salary minimums to accurately record and maintain state-specific annual exempt salary minimums in compliance with regulatory requirements. On the State Rules form, in the Minimum Wage Rates grid, an additional column named Minimum Exempt Salary Amount has been added. This field is not mandatory. Enter the annualized rate only for Minimum Exempt Salary Amount. You can only enter numeric values up to 2 decimal places. Note: On the New Hire form, for an FLSA exempt new hire, if the annual salary (entered or calculated) in the Pay Rate field under the Pay Details section, is lower than the Minimum Exempt Salary Amount on the State Rules form for that state for the latest entered year, and you try to save the form, then you will receive a warning stating The employee has been assigned a pay rate that is below the [State Abbreviation] Minimum Exempt Salary Rate of [Amount]. This is a warning only. Continue? - Click Yes to save the change. - Click No to return to the Pay Rate field. Note: Additional logic to support pay rate changes & payroll calculation warnings to follow in upcoming release. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR System Administration User Guide.
- Click Yes to save the change.
- Click No to return to the Pay Rate field.
CMP-7048 State Specific Fields added to the PrismHR Tax Quarterly JSON The PrismHR Tax Quarterly JSON file has been updated to include additional State Specific Fields. These fields will appear in the Employee Wage Details section of the Quarterly JSON for SUTA tax codes as required. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Employer Administration User Guide.
CMP-6326 & CMP-6854 Changes to the Update Employee W-2 Forms form As a service provider, you can now review the associated client wage data when Form W-2s are built on the PEO Employer level. This will not be applied to W2 records built on the Client Federal Entity Register (SBEA build). A new Client Inquiry section has been added to this form. This section will only populate for tax year 2025 and onwards. When the Form W-2 data is built on the Employer and the associated client information is added to the build, the Client ID, Company Name, and Federal Taxable Wages will appear as read only on this new form. This information cannot be edited by the user. If an employee is associated with multiple clients, each client appears as a separate row with an accurate federal taxable wage allocation. Only users with permission to view/update employee Form W-2s can access the Client Inquiry section. This data will only display on 2025 + W-2s built after the January release. The data will optionally be available to print on the Employee W-2 as a later enhancement in 2026. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Employer Administration User Guide.
CMP-7089 MasterTax RTS is updated to V49 On the MasterTax Interface Parameters form, the Mastertax RTS Import File Version has been updated to V49 in PrismHR. If the MasterTax RTS Import File Version field is set to Version 48 or earlier, you will receive the following error message when you are running the RTS: You are running an older version of the mastertax RTS file download []. You must be on version 49 in order to generate the RTS file out of Prism. Your current version can be edited on the Mastertax Interface Parameters. The header on the MasterTax RTS file now also reflects 49 in Line 1 in the 000 record in positions 57-58, with or without the Schedule R Breakout field selected. Note: Support for MN SUI exempt reporting in RTS V49 to follow in a future release. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Employer Administration User Guide.
CMP-6925 GTL Pay Code exemption added to MN Admin Assessment For Minnesota Admin Assessment, beginning in 2026, Group Term Life (GTL) earnings are now treated as exempt for the employer tax calculation. What changed? - The payroll tax calculation has been updated so that: - The MN Admin Assessment tax is exempt on GTL earnings. - The exemption is applied to the system-assigned GTL pay code configured in System Parameters. - The exemption applies to both billing and accrual calculations. - This change is implemented as an earnings-based exemption, not via a pay code level tax exemption entry. Why this matters? Previously, MN Admin Assessment could not be correctly exempted for GTL because the pay code itself could not be exempted for this tax. This update ensures that GTL is excluded from the MN Admin Assessment tax base, aligning with Minnesota requirements and preventing over‑taxation on GTL amounts. Setup / Usage notes - Ensure your GTL pay code is correctly assigned on the System Parameters form. - Once configured, GTL amounts will automatically be treated as exempt for the MN Admin Assessment tax during payroll processing; no separate Tax Exemptions pay code setup is required. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration and Processing User Guide.

CMP-6998, CMP-6999, CMP-7000, CMP-7001 & CMP-7110 CA Pay Data - Tax Year 2025 reporting updates The updated export including the newly added data points and MENA classification will be released shortly after the standard 2026 February release. For tax year 2025 and later, the California Pay Data Reporting specifications have changed. To align with the updated state requirements, we have updated the EEO-1 Build, Import and CSV templates. The California Pay Data CSV export ( EEO Processing / EEO-1 Processing / Client EEO-1 & Pay Data Files (CA Payroll Employee Report) ) updates remain in development for Tax Year 2025. Note: These changes affect only tax year 2025 and forward; tax year 2024 and prior remain unchanged. Here is the California Pay Data Reporting link. - CSV template modified for CA Pay Data employees & Labor Contractor reporting - New data points added to CA Pay Data Build - To support 2025 California Pay Data Reporting requirements, we’ve enhanced the standard EEO-1 build and Export to include additional data points for California employees. These changes make it easier to classify employees correctly and to calculate weeks worked for the reporting year. ### What’s New ##### 1. Exemption Status For California employees, based on the FLSA status on the employee’s home position as of the voucher “as of” date, the EEO‑1 build now includes an Exemption Status field that indicates whether the employee is: - Exempt (Y) - Non‑exempt (N) The exemption status is included in the EEO‑1 Build and the EEO‑1 Export file. ##### 2. Employment Type Based on the employee’s type from the voucher “as of” date, the EEO‑1 build now classifies each California employee into one of three Employment Types: - F=Full‑time (derived from internal employee type codes and type classification) - P=Part‑time (derived from internal employee type codes and type classification) - S=Intermittent (assigned when the employee’s type is flagged as Seasonal = Y) This employment type is included in the EEO‑1 Build and the EEO‑1 Export file. ##### 3. Weeks Worked in Reporting Year The EEO‑1 build now calculates the total number of weeks worked for each California employee during the reporting year, summing all vouchers within the selected date range (the reporting tax year). This will be indicated as a whole number greater than zero without decimal places. The calculated Weeks Worked is included in the EEO‑1 Build and the EEO‑1 Export file. ##### 4. MENA Ethnicity For employees belonging to the MENA (Middle Eastern or North African) ethnic type: - For the Import EEO-1 Data form, the import file can now contain M for the Race/Ethnicity field. - When you generate the EEO‑1 Export file using the Client EEO-1 & Pay Data Files form, these employees will be further subdivided into the following categories under the Race/Ethnicity/Sex column: - B70 = Non-Hispanic/Non-Latino - Male - Middle Eastern or North African - C70 = Non-Hispanic/Non-Latino - Female - Middle Eastern or North African - D70 = Non-Hispanic/Non-Latino - Non-Binary - Middle Eastern or North African For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR System Administration User Guide.

CMP-7121 Weighted Average using Flat Sum OT calculation Enhancement to weighted average overtime rate calculations when employee pay includes flat sum bonus pay items (for example, CA meal premiums and CA sick pay). What Changed When the weighted average pay code parameters are: - Method = Work Week and - No Lookback Period is defined, the system now: 1. Calculates the regular rate excluding pay codes with a flat sum condition. 2. Calculates the regular rate for flat sum pay codes (using the same approach already used for flat sum OT: flat sum pay divided by regular hours only). 3. Adds the results of steps 1 and 2 to determine the final weighted average pay rate. This logic applies to both Legacy and Restartable payrolls. Why This Matters Previously, when flat sum pay items (such as CAHOUSING and CARENT) were included, the weighted average overtime base rate could be understated because the flat sum component was not properly blended into the weighted average rate. Now: - Flat sum bonuses are divided only by regular hours to get their regular rate. - That flat sum regular rate is added to the regular rate from all other applicable pay codes. - The resulting combined rate is used as the overtime base rate for weighted average pay codes. - This provides a more accurate and compliant overtime rate when flat sum bonus pay is present. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Payroll Administration and Processing User Guide.

Employee Portal (EP) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
EP-1095 Print Multiple Pay Stubs Employees can now print multiple pay vouchers at one time on the Pay History form in Employee Portal. Up to thirty payroll vouchers can now be printed at a time by selecting vouchers individually or using the Select All checkbox. Employees can download the vouchers as a single pdf. Employees can use this feature to quickly print multiple vouchers when they need several months of payroll stubs, such as for financial applications or loans. For more information, see the in-app help.
EP-9679, EP-9683, EP-9684 ZayZoon Support for the My Pay Widget Companies that use ZayZoon integrations can now include those features in Employee Portal more easily. Clients can add the standard ZayZoon widget or menu item on a Configuration Template or Client Override, and can also add the Get Paid Early feature from ZayZoon to the My Pay widget using its configuration options. For more information, see the in-app help.
EP-1837, EP-1838, EP-1872, EP-9154, EP-9923 View Employee Pay Details Managers can now view detailed information about an employee’s pay data on the Pay tab on the Employee Details form in Employee Portal. This tab contains multiple forms detailing aspects of your employee’s paystubs, payroll history, and total compensation. Information that displays on the Pay tab is secured based on the manager’s role and permissions. The Pay History tab displays information for individual paystubs. Managers can search for specific paystubs or filter by year. A column selector is also available to display additional information. Select View Paystub to display the Pay History: Paystub form, which displays information about the net pay, earnings, taxes withheld, and deductions. Select View Check on this form to display a pdf of the paycheck, which can then be downloaded or printed. The Payroll Inquiry tab displays general information for a selected year. Select the Earnings, Taxes Withheld, or Deductions tabs to display the information of that tab for the selected year. In addition, select the Pay History tab on the inquiry to display information regarding changes in the employee’s pay rates. The Total Compensation tab displays information about the employee’s salary, benefits, and taxes. The Overview tab displays a breakdown of the employee’s net pay and tax withholdings, plus a graph of their compensation breakdown. The Pay tab displays their pay information and breaks down their payment into hours and entitlements. The Benefits tab shows the amount of their paycheck allocated to benefits, and the Taxes tab displays the employee and company contributions to taxes. Using this new form, managers with the appropriate permissions can review detailed information regarding employee pay directly from Employee Portal. This data can be used to review paychecks, monitor past changes in pay rates, and verify compensation, benefits, and tax breakdowns for employee paychecks. For more information, see the in-app help.

Identity and Access Management (IAM) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
IAM-2044 Enhancement to My Login Settings Form When a user with multiple accounts exits the My Login Settings form, the user is now directed back to PrismHR. Previously, users were directed to a form that requested they reselect which account to log in with. For more information, see the in-app help.
IAM-2546 Enhancement to PrismONE ID Settings When a client is configured to access PrismONE ID via an external identity provider with its own Multifactor Authentication and passwords, MFA and password information are now hidden on the PrismONE ID Settings form. In addition, a banner message informs users that their accounts are using a third-party authentication source to sign in. For more information, see the in-app help.

Onboarding (OB) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
OBE-7361 HSA Employer Match on Benefit Confirmation Statement The Benefit Confirmation Statement now displays the HSA Employer Match amount and annual contribution limits. A disclaimer also displays to inform the employee that this is a projected match which may change based on circumstances such as pay periods, eligibility, and plan details. For more information, see the in-app help.
OBE-9656, OBE-9825 Override Offer Type Rules by Payee ID A new configuration option is now available on the Life Event Maintenance form to allow Service Providers to override the offer type rules for a life event by Payee ID. This option becomes available when Use Benefit Rule is selected in the Source of Effective Date field. When the option is selected, eligibility is overridden from benefit rules or group benefit plans at the Offer Type level for selected Payees. Select which date is used in the Eligibility Date Used From Override field. > Note: Note: When this option is selected, initial eligibility still takes priority. Using this option, Service Providers can ensure that certain payees override the normal benefit rules or group benefit plans for their offer types. For more information, see the in-app help.
OBE-9780 Enhancement to Primary Care Physician Form Employees can now mark the Current Patient field on the Primary Care Physician form to indicate that they are currently seeing this physician. This information is synchronized with the corresponding field on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form in Prism. For more information, see the in-app help.
OBE-9835 Set Decision Support Access for Specific Clients Service Providers can now disable decision support tools for specific clients. On the Client Controls tab of the Client Details form, select an option in the Decision Support field in the Enrollment/Onboarding Controls section to enable or disable decision support tools. With this enhancement, Service Providers can provide decision support capabilities to their clients more selectively. For more information, see the in-app help.

Prism (PD) Enhancements

Ticket Category Description Summary Help Content
PD-20066 and PD-20067 ACH Enhancement to ACH Originators Form A new option, ISO, is now available in the Bank Name field on the ACH Originators form. Important! You must test this new file format with your banking institutions before processing a live file. Not all banks may accept this format, so you must complete testing before payroll runs using the ISO format. For example: [Image: screenshot] When you select the ISO XML file format, the system creates a payroll payment in ISO file format for clients set up for reverse wire transfers. For more information, see Using ACH Originators.
PD-20505 Client Enhancement to Inactive Data Deletion Form The system now recognizes an employee’s last termination status month, day, and year and the current month, day, and year, so employees now display in the Inactive Data Deletion list when their last termination status date is more than the selected number of Years Terminated from the current date. For more information, see Removing Inactive Customer Data.
WSP-3220 Client Enhancement to Client Details and Payments Pending Forms A new option, Real Time Payment, now displays in the Transfer Type field on the Client Details and Payments Pending forms. For example [Image: screenshot] [Image: screenshot] Use the Real Time Payment option as follows: - You can set the Real Time Payment option on the Billing tab in the Client Details form to categorize and track a client’s billing setup for Real Time Payments (RTP). - You can set the Real Time Payment option on the Payments Pending form to filter pending payment results for Real Time Payments (RTP). For more information, see Specifying Client Billing Options and Listing Pending Payments.
WSP-3164 New Employee Import Enhancement to New Employee Import Dashboard A new option, 3rd Form I-9 ID Document, is now available in the Table field on the Employee Import Code Translation Tables form, which you can access by selecting Code Translation Tables on the New Employee Import dashboard. For example: [Image: screenshot] You can use the 3rd Form I-9 ID Document option to set up a translation table for 3rd form I-9 ID document codes, so you can use this translation table to change the import file code to an accepted PrismHR code. For more information, see Managing Code Translations and Import Field Mappings.
PD-19202, PD-20419, and PD-20519 Payroll Enhancements to Data Import Tool The following enhancements now reside on the Data Import Tool form: - A new import template, Position Classification, is now available. For example: [Image: screenshot] Note: The Position Classification import template is only available for service providers. You can use the Position Classification import template to import state and workers compensation classes for existing position classifications. > Note: Note the following: - Users whose user role is set to DENY for the Position Classifications form cannot import data using the Position Classification import template and subsequently, the Data Import Tool icon will not display on this form. - Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Position Classifications form can view the Position Classification import template, but cannot import data. - Users whose user role is set to INQUIRY for the Data Import Tool can view the form and import template options, but cannot import data. - The State must be a valid state code. Otherwise, an error message displays. - If your template lists the same state twice, the system uses the first instance but ignores the second instance. - Worksite managers and worksite trusted advisors can now access the Tip OT Register import template in the Data Import Tool when they have FULL access to the Qualified Tips and Overtime form. (Previously, the system wasn’t allowing these users to access the Tip OT Register import template even when they had FULL access.) Note: To access the Qualified Tips and Overtime form for an employee, select the employee in the Employee Details form. From the Actions menu, select the Qualified Tips and Overtime option. - A new field, Payee, is now available on the Employee Loans import template. For example: [Image: screenshot] The Payee field indicates the payee associated with the employee loan. > Note: Note the following: - The payee must be an existing payee and have a Payee Type set to Loans on the Payees form. - You can only use payees whose Third Party Format for the Processor ID associated with the Payroll Check Account is set to Cachet or –Select– on the ACH Originators form. - An error message displays if the Deduction Code does not have the Deduction Type set to Employee Loan Payment on the Deduction Codes form or if the Deduction Code is obsolete. For more information, see Importing Position Classifications, Importing Tips and Overtime Data, and Importing Employee Loan Data.
PD-20037 and PD-20038 Payroll Enhancement to Deduction Codes Form A new option, % of Earnings with Included Pay Codes, now displays in the Calculation Method field on the Deduction Codes form. For example: [Image: screenshot] You can use the % of Earnings with Included Pay Codes option to associate a non-qualified deferred compensation (NQDC) plan that the client set up with another company, where a percentage of the commissions is deferred, reducing taxable earnings. (This deduction code functions similar to a pre-tax deduction.) > Note: Note the following: - You must set the Deduction Type to either Voluntary or Pre-Tax Retirement Contribution to use the % of Earnings with Included Pay Codes option. (If you select another option an error message displays.) - Setting a deduction code with a calculation method of % of Earnings with Included Pay Codes and enabling the Voluntary deduction type deducts the amount applied to the pay code and treats the deduction as pre-tax when you enable 409(a) Retirement in the Voluntary Classification panel. - Setting a deduction code with a calculation method of % of Earnings with Included Pay Codes and enabling the Voluntary deduction type deducts the amount applied to the pay code and treats the deduction as post-tax when you do not enable when you enable 409(a) Retirement in the Voluntary Classification panel. - The onlyVoluntary Classification you can enable with the % of Earnings with Included Pay Codes option is 409(a) Retirement. (If you select another option, an error message displays.) When you select the % of Earnings with Included Pay Codes option, a new Pay Codes panel displays. For example: [Image: screenshot] > Note: Note: You must enter or select at least one pay code or an error message will display when you click Save. For more information, see Maintaining Global Deduction Codes.
PD-20414 and PD-20415 Payroll Enhancement to Payees Form A new option, Loans, is now available in the Payee Type field on the Payees form. For example [Image: screenshot] You can use the Loans option to designate payees specifically for employee loans. In association with the Loans option, a new panel, Loan EFT Parameters, now displays in the Payees form when you select Loans as the Payee Type. For example: [Image: screenshot] You can enter EFT details specific to loan payees in the Loan EFT Parameters panel: - Transit Number: The financial institution where the state disbursement unit maintains the account. - Bank Account Number: The account number of the receiving financial institution. Note: You can enter numeric characters 0-9, the dash (-) character, and alphabetic characters in this field, which can be combined. For example, CSP-98765 is an allowed Bank Account Number. For more information, see Setting Up Vendors to Receive Payments.
PD-20417, PD-20507, and PD-20508 Payroll Enhancements to Employee Loans Form - A new field, Payee, is now available on the Employee Loans form. For example [Image: screenshot] You can use the Payee field to enter or select the payee for an employee loan. Note: Only payees who have the Loans payee type on the Payees form display in the Select Payee list. Also, you can only enter or select a Payee whose Third Party Format for the Processor ID associated with the Payroll Check Account is set to Cachet or –Select– on the ACH Originators form. - A new column, ACH Reference, now displays in the Payments panel. For example: [Image: screenshot] The system displays the following information: - ACH information in the ACH Reference column, such as garnishments. - The employee loan deduction amount in the ACH file, which includes the routing and account number, client ID, and employee ID. For more information, see Setting Up and Tracking Employee Loans.
PD-20491 and WSP-3243 Payroll Enhancements to Bank Accounts Form The following enhancements now reside on the Bank Accounts form: - A new field, Account Type, now resides on the Bank Account form. For example [Image: screenshot] You can use the Account Type field to categorize new and existing bank accounts by the type of ownership, PEO Master, Client Owned, or Demo. - If a bank Account ID has already been used to process a transaction, you cannot delete it when one or more of the following conditions exist: - The system created an ACH file with the bank Account ID. - The system processed cash receipts using the bank Account ID. For more information, see Maintaining Bank Accounts.
WSP-3280 Payroll Enhancement to Void and Reissue Checks Form The system now prevents you from voiding and reissuing escheated checks on the Void and Reissue Checks form. If you try to void and reissue an escheated check, an error message displays. > Note: Note the following: - You cannot enter or select a check with a status code of E (escheated). - You cannot enter a voucher number for a voucher that contains a check with a status code of E (escheated). For more information, see Voiding Payroll Batch or Voucher.
PD-20454 System Enhancement to Pay Schedules Form A new option, On this Day of the Following Month, is now available in the second Pay Period Ends field on the Pay Schedules form. For example: [Image: screenshot] Important! The following options in these fields must be set to display the On this Day of the Following Month option: - Pay Period field: Select Monthly. - Pay Day field: Select End Of Month. - Pay Period Ends field: Enter EOM. Note: If you try to select On this Day of the Following Month without setting the fields listed above, the following error message displays: [Image: screenshot] When you apply a pay schedule to a pay group for monthly payrolls with the On this Day of the Following Month option enabled, the system calculates the period end date as the last day of the following month. For example, if the pay date is 7/31/2025 and the pay period start date is 8/1/2025, then the period end date would equal 8/31/2025. For more information, see Establishing Pay Schedules.

PP-1948 System Enhancement to Payroll Reversal Form Users can now sort results on the Payroll Reversal form by name. In addition, users can click Select All and Deselect All to quickly select or deselect all results. For more information, see the in-app help.
PP-2134 System Change to URL Endpoint Dependency The .asp section of the URL is no longer necessary for clients running an SSO configuration. For example, “htpps://your.website.com/site/dweb.asp?a=SSOIN&dbcgm=1” no longer requires the .asp section to be compatible with the SSO configuration, and could be shortened to “https://your.website.com/sit/a=SSOIN”. For more information, see the in-app help.
PP-2143 System Enhancement to Help Documentation The URL for help documentation on the PrismHR platform has been changed. Clients who link to the help directly will need to update their bookmarks. For more information, see the in-app help.
PP-2157 System Enhancement to Pendo Name and ID For clients who integrate Pendo into their system, the peoName and peoID fields have been updated to provide the user’s PEO name and PEO ID to Pendo when they access Prism. For more information, see the in-app help.

Fixes

Benefits Administration (BA) Fixes

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
WSP-2889 Previously, for a client set up with Departments Restrict Eligibility option selected for Eligible Benefits Determinant field on the Benefits tab of the Client Details form, the Benefits Eligibility Report displayed blank results even if Departments were set up with eligible benefits. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2934, WSP-3330 Previously, on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, COBRA Fee under the Coverage Details section were displayed only when you set the Status to COBRA and then saved the form. Now, this is fixed. COBRA Premiums and COBRA Fee are now populated immediately after you set the participant’s Status to COBRA. Additionally, the system recalculates the Total Premium contribution to 100% Participant Contribution of Premium (with COBRA fee, if applicable) and the Employer Contribution is displayed as net $0.00.
WSP-2935 Previously, during a payroll calculation process, if a Coverage Detail Effective Date is automatically created, then the system did not create audit log on the Benefit Detail Audit screen for that Effective Date. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2969 Previously, on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, under the Coverage Details section, when you selected a new Existing Effective Date, then the Updated Carrier field was automatically checked, which was an incorrect behavior. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-2970 Previously, on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form, Worksite Managers were able to manually enter an Employee ID and create an Employee Benefit Rule Override even for employees whose access were restricted for the Worksite Managers. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-3194 Previously, on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, saving an employee benefits enrollment record required you to click the Save button twice. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-3225 Previously, on the Group Benefit Plans form, when you set a plan for Do Not Allow EE Contribution and then when you add Plan Type for that plan on the Benefit Rules form, then the informational text under the Contribution Rules section displayed twice. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-3242 Previously, on the Employee Details form, under the Work tab, the Benefit Group selector included Retirement Only benefit group, which was an incorrect behavior. Now, this is fixed. The Benefit Group selector has been updated to use the new selector and benefit groups defined as Benefit or Both are now only displayed.
WSP-3291 Previously, in certain circumstances, the system displayed blank Premium and Contribution amounts on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-3315 Previously, on the Client Assigned To form, when you selected a client from the client list, the system displayed incorrect client name on the Benefit Plan Setup modal form. Now, this is fixed.

Compliance (CMP) Fixes

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-5923 Previously, after a Global PTO Benefit Plan was deleted and the corresponding the Global PTO Register is archived, even if there is no state plan associated, the subsequent payroll incorrectly reflected the PTO accrual if the timesheet location matched the deleted Global PTO Benefit Plan. Now, this is fixed.
CMP-6751 Previously, when an employer had a tax basis set for California State Income Tax (CA SIT), the S-Corp Benefit Tax Adjustments did not report the correct tax basis. Now, when an employer sets State Income Tax reporting to ‘Client,’ the S-Corp Benefit Tax Adjustments will have a tax basis of ‘C’ for the SIT. Conversely, if the employer sets the reporting to ‘Employer,’ the tax basis will be ‘P.’
CMP-6886 Previously, for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients, with and without Mastertax account id, when OR PFML tax code 38-40 was redirected on the Client Details form, RTS 501 record, statistic 1 (positions 67-80) and statistic 2 (positions 81-94) were not zero filled. Now, for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients, with and without Mastertax account id, when OR PFML tax code 38-40 is redirected on the Client Details form, RTS 501 record, statistic 1 (positions 67-80) and statistic 2 (positions 81-94) are be zero filled.
CMP-6904 Previously, the MasterTax RTS file C records did not correctly report the PA Work State flag on the Client file when the locality was Client Report, C tax basis. Now, this is resolved.
CMP-7038 Previously, for California employees with a Health Savings Account (HSA) match, the system incorrectly did not include the HSA employer match to calculate the taxable wages for California Employment Training Tax (tax code 05-26). This resulted in the CA SUTA (tax code 05-24) wages being different from the CA ETT (tax code 05-26) wages. Now, this is resolved. For California employees with a Health Savings Account (HSA) match, the CA SUTA wages are the same as the CA ETT.
CMP-7047 Previously, the WH347 report (both January 2025 and December 2008 versions) did not generate a zero report for certified projects that lacked payroll data for the specified week ending date. Now, the WH347 report (both January 2025 and December 2008 versions) generates a zero report for certified projects that lack payroll data for the specified week ending date.
CMP-7066 Previously, when processing a tax adjustment using the Tax Adjustments form, when the Adjust Client Tax Register field was selected, the employer reported tax code 24-54 (MN - Additional Assessment) was reporting a Tax Basis P instead of C on the employee payroll voucher. Now, when processing a tax adjustment using the Tax Adjustments form, when the Adjust Client Tax Register field was selected, any employer reported tax code will report a Tax Basis of C on the employee payroll voucher.
CMP-7077 Previously, while building the Quarterly Tax JSON Export, the job progress window incorrectly stated Building MasterTax Reconciliation Reports. Now, this is resolved.
CMP-7080 Previously, for the state of Minnesota, when payroll included Additional Assessment tax, the employer contribution billing amount (tax code 24-54) was not reported under the Employer Contribution on the Payroll Check Journal Report. Now, for the state of Minnesota, when payroll includes Additional Assessment tax, the employer contribution billing amount (tax code 24-54) will be reported in the Employer Contribution on the Payroll Check Journal Report.
CMP-7130 Previously, when an employee was assigned to a Worksite Location in Minnesota, and was paid in a timesheet in a worksite location other than Minnesota, the system incorrectly withheld STATE MISC4 EMPLOYER tax for that work state (non-existing tax code XX-54) creating errors. Now, when an employee with an assigned worksite location in the state of Minnesota is paid in a timesheet in a worksite location other than Minnesota, the system correctly withholds tax code 24-54 (MN - Additional Assessment) and no other XX-54 tax codes will be present.
CMP-7156 Previously, when an employee was assigned to a remote location in a state that was different from their resident state, and the employee went over the SUTA wage base limit, the billing portion did not correctly recognize the over-limit wages. Now, when an employee is assigned to a Remote Location in a state that is different than their resident state, the wage basis is accurate from payroll to payroll, with or without a wage base override, and the bill amount is also correct.

Prism (PD) Fixes

Jira # Category Issue Summary Resolution
RRT-6718 General The system allowed users to archive PTO registers in the Employee PTO Register form that had outstanding future leave requests. This is fixed.
WSP-3057 General The Field Name on the File Audit form, which is accessed by selecting Audit on the Actions menu in the Payroll Control form, incorrectly displayed as “Testing Field” instead of “Payroll Status.” This is fixed.
WSP-3193 General Users were able to enter duplicate codes in the Imported Code column in the Employee Import Code Translation Tables form. (The system translated the first entry listed in the table for duplicate imported codes, which caused confusion and unexpected results.) When creating or updating an existing code set, the system now validates whether duplicates exist in the Import Code column when users click Save.
PD-19939 Payroll The system did not count all terminated employees within the beginning and ending dates range in the Turnover Dashboard. This is fixed.
PD-20358 Payroll Users were able to access Payroll Approval Reports for posted payrolls in the Payroll Reports form. This is fixed.
PD-20442 Payroll The system incorrectly displayed a warning message in the Payroll Validation Report when an employee was paid below minimum wage because the calculation was based on Hours Paid instead of on Hours Worked. The system now calculates Gross Pay divided by Hours Worked to determine if an employee was paid minimum wage.
PD-20541 Payroll Users were able to enter an obsolete pay code in a timesheet (that is, it had an obsolete date in the past). This is fixed.
RRT-6620 Payroll The system included pay codes that used units and had Include Amount Paid Only in Overtime Calculation field enabled on the Pay Codes form in the hours paid calculation that determines the overtime due when overtime was calculated. The system now does the following: - When no fields are enabled, the system uses the default Hours/Units Paid. - When the Include Hours/Amount Paid in Overtime Calculation field is enabled, the system uses Hours Worked. - When the Use Hours Paid Instead of Hours Worked in Overtime Calculation field is enabled, the system uses Hours/Units Paid. - When the Include Amount Paid Only in Overtime Calculation field is enabled, the system uses Hours Worked.
- When no fields are enabled, the system uses the default Hours/Units Paid.
- When the Include Hours/Amount Paid in Overtime Calculation field is enabled, the system uses Hours Worked.
- When the Use Hours Paid Instead of Hours Worked in Overtime Calculation field is enabled, the system uses Hours/Units Paid.
- When the Include Amount Paid Only in Overtime Calculation field is enabled, the system uses Hours Worked.
PP-2151 System When the Geocode lookup for an address did not match the entered value in the City field, the employee’s entry in the City field was overridden automatically. This is fixed. The employee’s entry in the City field now takes priority when the Geocode doesn’t precisely match.
PP-2154 System Web extensions added on the Web Extensions form were not working properly for certain customers. This is fixed.

Welcome

PrismHR software is specifically designed to help Professional Employer Organizations (PEOs) and Administrative Services Organizations (ASOs) reduce risk, be more efficient, expand business, and be more profitable.

When you choose PrismHR, you are choosing more than just a software platform. You are partnering with a team of professionals who are deeply invested in the PEO and ASO industry and dedicated to providing the best technology and services possible. You are also partnering with other professionals in the industry in the sense that we all learn from each other.

To view release notes for PrismHR, click any of the links in the Table of Contents. Each release is represented with a book that features the month and year. Click these books to expand product names and version numbers for the release. The most recent documents are at the top of the list. Use the Search feature to look for a specific keyword or phrase. Open any PDFs for Download book to view and print release notes documents from the past year.

Documentation Enhancements

Click a link to read about the documentation enhancements included in this release.

Task Sheets

To provide a better customer experience, new or improved task sheets are available in the in-product Help. In the table of contents, you can select the Task Sheets topic (located just below User Guide PDFs) to display a list of the most current task sheets. For example:

[Image: screenshot]

  • Importing Employee Loan Data: This article documents how to import employee loan data in PrismHR using the Data Import Tool.
  • Maintaining Global Deduction Codes: This article outlines how to create a new deduction code, along with how to view and edit deduction code information on the Deduction Codes form.

Release Notes: Enhancements and Fixes

You can view release notes in a variety of formats. You can:

  • View the detailed release notes. See: Release Notes
  • Download a PDF containing the detailed release notes. See Release Notes PDF
  • Download an Excel spreadsheet containing the detailed release notes. See: Release Notes Excel Note: The Excel export of release note does not include images. View the Detailed release notes in HTML format to see images.

Benefits Administration (BA) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
WSP-2832 Changes to the Max Days Back Dating Validation The Max Days Back Dating field validations are now triggered for the following scenarios: - When auto populating a Coverage Starts date on a new record. - When manually updating the Coverage Starts date on an existing record on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form. - When changing the Status of a record to Active on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form. For more information, see the in-app help.
WSP-3318 Changes to the Benefits Eligibility Report form The Benefits Eligibility Report now correctly displays eligibility for Group Benefits when using Departments, Divisions, or Worksite Locations as Eligible Benefits Determinants. Additionally, when a determinant value has no associated eligible benefits, the report now shows NA instead of All, which was displayed earlier. [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the in-app help.
WSP-3325 Changes to the Group Benefit Plans form Under the Group Benefit Plans section, a new checkbox field, 3rd Party COBRA, has been added. [Image: screenshot] This field allows plans to be flagged when COBRA administration is handled by third party, supporting downstream API and reporting use while leaving existing COBRA functionality unchanged. For more information, See Establishing Basic Parameters for Group Benefit Plans help topic.
WSP-3339, WSP-3342, WSP-3344, WSP-3345, WSP-3346, WSP-3357, WSP-3361, WSP-3362 Changes to the Client Benefits Overview form - On the Client Benefits Overview form, the system now displays all the Primary Plan IDs in Bold format. Additionally, the system displays the Secondary Plan IDs in normal text format along with all the data for that Plan ID even when you click on a header to sort the data. Note: The system displays the same format of Primary Plans in Bold and the Secondary Plans in normal text after you select the View plans past end date and the View rules that are not found checkboxes. - The column order on this form have now been updated and is displayed in the following order: - Plan ID - Plan Description - HDHP Plan - Rate Group - Group/Rules - Template - Start Date - End Date Note: There is no change in the existing functionality with the Plan ID and Group/Rules hyperlinks. - On this form, the four new columns have now been added: - Section 125 Eligible - Deduction Code - If Section 125 Eligible column is flagged with Y value, then the Deduction Code for that record will be displayed as 125 Deduction Code. However, if Section 125 Eligible column is flagged with N value, then the normal Deduction Code for that record will be displayed. - Rebate Bill Code - The value displayed in the Rebate Bill Code column is based on the value displayed for 125 Deduction Code or Deduction Code. If Rebate Bill Code is not assigned for a record, then the system displays N/A. - Bill Code - On this form, when you sort data and then open a modal form by clicking any of the hyperlink from the Plan ID or Group/Rules column, the system now preserves your existing sort selections after you close the Plan ID or Group/Rules modal. - On this form, two new checkbox fields have been added. - Include retirement only benefit groups - This field allows you to filter Benefit Groups data that are flagged as Retirement only. - View benefit groups past stop all use on date - This field allows you to filter and view the data of Benefit Groups past the Stop All Use On date. - A new button named, Report has also been added towards the bottom of the form. Click this button to run a report on the Client Benefits Overview form and export the data. [Image: screenshot] For more information, See Displaying the Client Benefits Overview help topic.
WSP-3343 Changes to the Benefit Plan Setup form On the Benefit Plan Setup form, when you select Plan Class as Group Benefit and choose a Plan ID, then after clicking the View Deduction/Bill Codes hyperlink, following changes have been made to the earlier Plan Deduction and Billing Codes modal form that was displayed: - Section 125 Eligible field is now displayed as a checkbox. - The Deduction and Billing Codes are now displayed in a grid format. - The column headers now include Code, Description, Deduction Type, and Rebate Bill Code. [Image: screenshot] Note: All the information displayed on this modal form is in read-only format. For more information, See Setting Up a Benefit Plan help topic.
WSP-3359, WSP-3360 Changes to the Benefits Billing Detail Report The system now displays an Offer Type indicator to the right of the Plan ID while running a Benefits Billing Detail Report by clicking the Download Report button from the Billing History section on the following forms: - Employee Benefit Overview - Employee Benefits Enrollment [Image: screenshot] For more information, See Displaying an Employee’s Benefit Plans and See Manually Enrolling an Employee in a Benefit Plan help topic.

Compliance (CMP) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
CMP-7026 Validations added for Minimum Exempt Salary Amount To help you ensure exempt employees meet the state minimum exempt salary requirements, from now on during payroll processing (including Superbatch), the system now checks an exempt employees’ pay against the State Rules – Minimum Exempt Salary Amount for their work state. If an exempt employee’s earnings for the pay period are below the configured state minimum exempt salary, a soft warning message is displayed so you can review and adjust pay as needed. > Note: Note: Payroll can still be processed. Figure 4 - State Rules form [Image: screenshot] Figure 5 - Warning - Process Payroll Menu [Image: Warning in Process Payroll Menu] Figure 6 - Warning - Superbatch Menu [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR System Administration User Guide.
CMP-7001 CA Pay Data - Tax Year 2025 reporting updates For tax year 2025 and later, the California Pay Data Reporting specifications have changed. To align with the updated state requirements, we have updated the EEO-1 Build, Import and CSV templates. The California Pay Data CSV export (EEO Processing / EEO-1 Processing / Client EEO-1 & Pay Data Files (CA Payroll Employee Report)) updates are now complete for Tax Year 2025. The updated export including the newly added data points and MENA classification were released on March 12, 2026 via a hotfix. Note: These changes affect only tax year 2025 and forward; tax year 2024 and prior remain unchanged. Here is the California Pay Data Reporting link. - CSV template modified for CA Pay Data employees & Labor Contractor reporting - New data points added to CA Pay Data Build - To support 2025 California Pay Data Reporting requirements, we’ve enhanced the standard EEO-1 build and Export to include additional data points for California employees. These changes make it easier to classify employees correctly and to calculate weeks worked for the reporting year. ### What’s New ##### 1. Exemption Status For California employees, based on the FLSA status on the employee’s home position as of the voucher “as of” date, the EEO‑1 build now includes an Exemption Status field that indicates whether the employee is: - Exempt (Y) - Non‑exempt (N) The exemption status is included in the EEO‑1 Build and the EEO‑1 Export file. ##### 2. Employment Type Based on the employee’s type from the voucher “as of” date, the EEO‑1 build now classifies each California employee into one of three Employment Types: - F=Full‑time (derived from internal employee type codes and type classification) - P=Part‑time (derived from internal employee type codes and type classification) - S=Intermittent (assigned when the employee’s type is flagged as Seasonal = Y) This employment type is included in the EEO‑1 Build and the EEO‑1 Export file. ##### 3. Weeks Worked in Reporting Year The EEO‑1 build now calculates the total number of weeks worked for each California employee during the reporting year, summing all vouchers within the selected date range (the reporting tax year). This will be indicated as a whole number greater than zero without decimal places. The calculated Weeks Worked is included in the EEO‑1 Build and the EEO‑1 Export file. ##### 4. MENA Ethnicity For employees belonging to the MENA (Middle Eastern or North African) ethnic type: - For the Import EEO-1 Data form, the import file can now contain M for the Race/Ethnicity field. - When you generate the EEO‑1 Export file using the Client EEO-1 & Pay Data Files form, these employees will be further subdivided into the following categories under the Race/Ethnicity/Sex column: - B70 = Non-Hispanic/Non-Latino - Male - Middle Eastern or North African - C70 = Non-Hispanic/Non-Latino - Female - Middle Eastern or North African - D70 = Non-Hispanic/Non-Latino - Non-Binary - Middle Eastern or North African For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR System Administration User Guide.
- CSV template modified for CA Pay Data employees & Labor Contractor reporting
- New data points added to CA Pay Data Build - To support 2025 California Pay Data Reporting requirements, we’ve enhanced the standard EEO-1 build and Export to include additional data points for California employees. These changes make it easier to classify employees correctly and to calculate weeks worked for the reporting year.
- Exempt (Y)
- Non‑exempt (N)
- F=Full‑time (derived from internal employee type codes and type classification)
- P=Part‑time (derived from internal employee type codes and type classification)
- S=Intermittent (assigned when the employee’s type is flagged as Seasonal = Y)
- For the Import EEO-1 Data form, the import file can now contain M for the Race/Ethnicity field.
- When you generate the EEO‑1 Export file using the Client EEO-1 & Pay Data Files form, these employees will be further subdivided into the following categories under the Race/Ethnicity/Sex column:
- B70 = Non-Hispanic/Non-Latino - Male - Middle Eastern or North African
- C70 = Non-Hispanic/Non-Latino - Female - Middle Eastern or North African
- D70 = Non-Hispanic/Non-Latino - Non-Binary - Middle Eastern or North African
CMP-7169 Mastertax V49 file updates MN SUI Exempt PFML MasterTax v49 now reports Minnesota Paid Family and Medical Leave (MN PFML) for clients and employees who are MN SUTA (24‑24) exempt and therefore did not generate MN SUI 600 records earlier. For SUTA‑exempt scenarios, MasterTax v49 will now generate a separate MN PFML reporting record so that these wages are properly included even when no MN SUI record exists. For MN SUTA‑exempt employees in MasterTax v49: - A 600‑block RTS record will be created for tax code MN0000‑P27 when: - The employee has QTD or YTD wages under payroll code 24‑40 or 24‑41, and - The employee does not have a corresponding 24‑24 (MN SUTA) record in YTD. - The gross and taxable wages in the 600 block will report the higher of Payroll code 24‑40 in position 72-85 or Payroll code 24‑41 in position 86-99. This logic ensures MN PFML reporting is generated even when MN SUI 600 records are not created due to SUTA exemption. > Note: Note: For joint account employees (MN0000‑P27), only summarized totals are required. MasterTax will accept 500‑record level reporting, and 601 records are not required for these employees. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Employer Administration User Guide.
- A 600‑block RTS record will be created for tax code MN0000‑P27 when:
- The employee has QTD or YTD wages under payroll code 24‑40 or 24‑41, and
- The employee does not have a corresponding 24‑24 (MN SUTA) record in YTD.
- The gross and taxable wages in the 600 block will report the higher of Payroll code 24‑40 in position 72-85 or Payroll code 24‑41 in position 86-99.
CMP-7163 CMP-7164 Change to the Employee Details form Previously, for employees having creditor garnishment (and potential other garnishments excluding child support) who were paid on a daily basis, for less than 5 pay periods per week, the system could not accurately calculate the daily minimum net pay cap for garnishment amount correctly. As a result, garnishments were being blocked when they should partially apply. To mitigate this, on the Employee Details form, on the Pay tab, under the Compensation section, only for employees with a daily pay period, a new optional field named Pay Periods Per Week has been introduced. [Image: screenshot] - The field appears only when the employee’s pay period is daily. - Values can be entered as a whole number from 1 to 7 or left blank. This field lets you define how many times per week a daily employee is expected to be paid (1–7), which supports more accurate daily garnishment minimum net pay calculations when employees are paid fewer than five times per week. - Changing from a daily to a non-daily pay period requires this field to be cleared; you’ll be prompted to remove the value before completing the change. - Updating this field affects garnishment minimum net pay calculations on a go‑forward basis; existing garnishment amounts are not automatically recalculated. For more information, see the in-product help or PrismHR Human Resources User Guide.
- The field appears only when the employee’s pay period is daily.
