Compliance (CMP) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
CMP-6799 Enhanced Additional Medicare Reporting in RTS for U.S. Territories Previously, when a US territory employee’s Medicare wages exceeded $200,000, the Additional Medicare amounts were included within the standard US territory Medicare record rather than being broken out into a separate line — requiring manual adjustments in MasterTax. Now, when processing payroll for employees in Guam, the Virgin Islands, or with AG/W8 classifications, you will no longer need to manually adjust Additional Medicare amounts in MasterTax. The Reconciliation Tax Summary (RTS) file in MasterTax is now fully compliant for high-income US territory employees. ### What changed? - Territory-specific Additional Medicare records — The system now generates dedicated Additional Medicare records for applicable US territories and worker classifications: - 00-11GUADD — Guam - 00-11VIADD — Virgin Islands - 00-01AGADD — Agricultural workers (American Samoa) - 00-11W8ADD — W8 employees - Consistent with federal reporting — US Territory Additional Medicare reporting now mirrors the standard federal Medicare / Additional Medicare structure (codes 00-11 and 00-11ADD), ensuring a uniform approach across all employee classifications.
- Territory-specific Additional Medicare records — The system now generates dedicated Additional Medicare records for applicable US territories and worker classifications:
- 00-11GUADD — Guam
- 00-11VIADD — Virgin Islands
- 00-01AGADD — Agricultural workers (American Samoa)
- 00-11W8ADD — W8 employees
- Consistent with federal reporting — US Territory Additional Medicare reporting now mirrors the standard federal Medicare / Additional Medicare structure (codes 00-11 and 00-11ADD), ensuring a uniform approach across all employee classifications.
CMP-7176 MA PFML Employee State Specific Fields Added to Quarterly Tax JSON Export The Quarterly Tax JSON Export now includes State Specific Information within the Employee Wage Details for the Massachusetts Paid Family & Medical Leave (MA PFML tax code 22-40), as required by the APTM V5.1 file specification. When a quarterly unemployment filing includes the MA PFML Employee tax code, the JSON export will now populate a StateSpecificInformation object under the EmployeeWageDetails array containing: - Family Leave Contribution Rate — A 3-character numeric string (left zero-filled, range 0–100) representing the employee’s percentage share of the total Family contribution rate of 0.18%. For example, if the employee contributes the full 0.18%, the value is 100; if split equally with the employer, the value is 050. - Medical Leave Contribution Rate — A 2-character numeric string (left zero-filled, range 0–40) representing the employee’s percentage share of the total medical contribution rate of 0.70%. For example, if the employee contributes the maximum 40% (0.28%), the value is 40; if the employer covers the full amount, the value is 00. These rates are calculated per employee based on actual withholdings relative to the applicable state rule form rates for the quarter and apply to both SBEA and Non-SBEA clients.
- Family Leave Contribution Rate — A 3-character numeric string (left zero-filled, range 0–100) representing the employee’s percentage share of the total Family contribution rate of 0.18%. For example, if the employee contributes the full 0.18%, the value is 100; if split equally with the employer, the value is 050.
- Medical Leave Contribution Rate — A 2-character numeric string (left zero-filled, range 0–40) representing the employee’s percentage share of the total medical contribution rate of 0.70%. For example, if the employee contributes the maximum 40% (0.28%), the value is 40; if the employer covers the full amount, the value is 00.
CMP-7793 & CMP-7794 Changes to the Employee Tax Form The system now supports dedicated fields for capturing employee visa classifications and their associated pay date ranges, ensuring tax rules are applied accurately based on an employee’s eligibility period. On the Employee Details form, on the Tax tab, under the Federal Tax Filing section, three new fields have been added. See from the screenshot below. [Image: screenshot] - Eligible Visa Category - Select one of the applicable eligible visa categories from the following drop-down. If you select any option other than –Select–, you will have to enter a Visa Starting Pay Date and a Visa Ending Pay Date. - –Select– - Select this option if there is no eligible visa category to be applied - F-1 Student - J-1 Student - J-1 Scholar - H-2A Agricultural Worker - Visa Starting Pay Date - Enter the visa starting pay date for the selected eligible visa category above. This date cannot be later than the Visa Ending Pay Date. You cannot enter this date unless you have selected an eligible visa category above. If you have selected an eligible visa category above, you must enter this field. - Visa Ending Pay Date - Enter the visa ending pay date for the selected eligible visa category above. This date cannot be earlier than the Visa Starting Pay Date. You cannot enter this date unless you have selected an eligible visa category above. If you have selected an eligible visa category above, you must enter this field. ### Automated FICA and FUTA Tax Suppression for Eligible Visa Holders The payroll system now automatically suppresses FICA and FUTA taxes for employees with eligible visa types when the pay date falls within their defined eligibility period. This enhancement ensures tax compliance by automating exemptions that previously required manual oversight or were limited to FICA only. #### Key Details - Automated Tax Suppression: When an employee has an eligible visa type and the payroll check date falls on or between the visa’s start and end dates, the system will fully suppress FICA (Employee and Employer) and FUTA taxes. - Full Suppression vs. Blocking: Unlike “blocked” taxes, this logic entirely suppresses the tax codes and taxable wages, meaning they will not appear on the payroll voucher. - Standard Processing: If the payroll check date falls outside the eligibility range, or if a visa type is selected without defined dates, FICA and FUTA taxes will be withheld as usual. - Broad Compatibility: This logic applies to various payroll processes, including backdated or future-dated payrolls and different batch types, for both certified and non-certified employers. > Note: Note: - This feature is currently supported by the restartable payroll engine. - Retroactive adjustments are not automated; if a visa flag or eligibility dates are updated after a payroll is finalized, manual adjustments may be required for previous pay periods.
- Eligible Visa Category - Select one of the applicable eligible visa categories from the following drop-down. If you select any option other than –Select–, you will have to enter a Visa Starting Pay Date and a Visa Ending Pay Date.
- –Select– - Select this option if there is no eligible visa category to be applied
- F-1 Student
- J-1 Student
- J-1 Scholar
- H-2A Agricultural Worker
- Visa Starting Pay Date - Enter the visa starting pay date for the selected eligible visa category above. This date cannot be later than the Visa Ending Pay Date. You cannot enter this date unless you have selected an eligible visa category above. If you have selected an eligible visa category above, you must enter this field.
- Visa Ending Pay Date - Enter the visa ending pay date for the selected eligible visa category above. This date cannot be earlier than the Visa Starting Pay Date. You cannot enter this date unless you have selected an eligible visa category above. If you have selected an eligible visa category above, you must enter this field.
- Automated Tax Suppression: When an employee has an eligible visa type and the payroll check date falls on or between the visa’s start and end dates, the system will fully suppress FICA (Employee and Employer) and FUTA taxes.
- Full Suppression vs. Blocking: Unlike “blocked” taxes, this logic entirely suppresses the tax codes and taxable wages, meaning they will not appear on the payroll voucher.
- Standard Processing: If the payroll check date falls outside the eligibility range, or if a visa type is selected without defined dates, FICA and FUTA taxes will be withheld as usual.
- Broad Compatibility: This logic applies to various payroll processes, including backdated or future-dated payrolls and different batch types, for both certified and non-certified employers.
- This feature is currently supported by the restartable payroll engine.
- Retroactive adjustments are not automated; if a visa flag or eligibility dates are updated after a payroll is finalized, manual adjustments may be required for previous pay periods.
CMP-7814 Changes to Resident PSD code reporting for Pennsylvania employees Previously, when an employee worked in the state of Pennsylvania but lived in another state, we used to leave the Resident PSD code field blank in the Periodic Tax JSON Export and the Quarterly Tax JSON Export. We had to manually enter 880000 for the ResidentPSDCode field in the json file for these during the quarter end processes. Now, when an employee works in the state of Pennsylvania but lives in another state, in both the Periodic Tax JSON Export and the Quarterly Tax JSON Export, the ResidentPSDCode field in the JSON file will report 880000. No manual intervention will be required.
CMP-7865 Changes to the Client Quarterly SUTA Tax Export - Kentucky Kentucky’s Unemployment Insurance Portal (KUIP) requires quarterly wage and tax files to be submitted in ICESA fixed-length format. Accordingly, we have updated our Client Quarterly SUTA Tax Export for Kentucky so that the produced file meets KUIP’s ICESA requirements, including record length, field positioning, padding/justification rules, and validation expectations. KUIP processes only: - E-Record – Employer Header Record - S-Record – Employee Detail Record Any other record types (A, B, T, F, etc.) are disregarded by KUIP. File Specification (from “Kentucky Unemployment Insurance Portal (KUIP) ICESA File Format Reference Guide”) General File Specifications - File Extension: .txt only. - Record Length: Each record (line) must be exactly 275 characters (including trailing spaces). - Format: Fixed-length ICESA. - Only E and S records are produced for the KUIP ICESA export - KEIN = Client Details, KY - State Unemployment Insurance ID - Use Worksite Location, Worksite ID from employee’s assigned Worksite Location - Population rule: All fields must be populated to their exact length using spaces and/or zero-fill as specified. - Left-justify where specified; pad with spaces. - Right-justify where specified; pad with spaces or zeroes per specification.
- E-Record – Employer Header Record
- S-Record – Employee Detail Record
- File Extension: .txt only.
- Record Length: Each record (line) must be exactly 275 characters (including trailing spaces).
- Format: Fixed-length ICESA.
- Only E and S records are produced for the KUIP ICESA export
- KEIN = Client Details, KY - State Unemployment Insurance ID
- Use Worksite Location, Worksite ID from employee’s assigned Worksite Location
- Population rule: All fields must be populated to their exact length using spaces and/or zero-fill as specified.
- Left-justify where specified; pad with spaces.
- Right-justify where specified; pad with spaces or zeroes per specification.

- Record Length: Each record (line) must be exactly 275 characters (including trailing spaces).
- Format: Fixed-length ICESA.
- Only E and S records are produced for the KUIP ICESA export
- KEIN = Employer Details, KY - State Unemployment Insurance ID
- Use Worksite Location, Worksite ID from employee’s assigned Worksite Location
- Population rule: All fields must be populated to their exact length using spaces and/or zero-fill as specified.
- Left-justify where specified; pad with spaces.
- Right-justify where specified; pad with spaces or zeroes per specification.
CMP-7876 Changes to the Periodic Tax JSON Export form On the Periodic Tax JSON Export form, a new subsection named Periodic JSON Export History has been added beneath the build controls as you can see from the screenshot below. This feature helps customers and Support teams quickly locate and re-download previously generated Periodic Tax JSON/PTS export files, reducing the likelihood that processed files are lost. Previously, you had to navigate to Transfer Downloads to PC to retrieve periodic JSON exports. The export history is now available directly on the Periodic Tax JSON Export form. If no historical exports exist, the Periodic JSON Export History subsection displays an empty state message stating No export history found. [Image: screenshot] This subsection renders a table with the following columns (left to right) : - Date/Time - The date and time the file was generated. - Created By - The username of the user who initiated the build. - File Name - The JSON file name is displayed as a hyperlink. Please note that the PTS files are deleted after 60 days. - Audit Report - Click the View hyperlink to access the audit report associated with the export history entry.
- Date/Time - The date and time the file was generated.
- Created By - The username of the user who initiated the build.
- File Name - The JSON file name is displayed as a hyperlink. Please note that the PTS files are deleted after 60 days.
- Audit Report - Click the View hyperlink to access the audit report associated with the export history entry.
WSP-4024 Changes to the W/C Classification Rates form On the W/C Classification Rates form, only for the State of Washington, a new field named Time sheet based WC tax calculations will appear. This field is a checkbox which is unchecked by default. [Image: screenshot] > Note: Note: This is a currently a UI change only. The functional logic is expected to be implemented in an upcoming release.
WSP-4180 Check message enhancement with substitution variables As a service provider user managing client check configuration, you can now use substitution variables in client check messages, so that paychecks can display contextual employee and work-assignment information in the check message on a client-by-client basis. [Image: screenshot] You can enter the following substitution variables either in the Message Text section on the Check Massages form or in the Memo section on the Payroll Control form: - Worksite Location - {{HOME.LOCATION}} - Position - {{HOME.POSITION}} - Division - {{HOME.DIVISION}} - Department - {{HOME.DEPARTMENT}} - Work Shift - {{HOME.WORK.SHIFT}} - Project - {{HOME.PROJECT}} - Work Group - {{HOME.WORK.GROUP}} - Client Name - {{CLIENT.LEGAL.NAME}} > Note: Note: The Client Name comes from the Client Details form, while the other variables come from the Employee Details form.
- Worksite Location - {{HOME.LOCATION}}
- Position - {{HOME.POSITION}}
- Division - {{HOME.DIVISION}}
- Department - {{HOME.DEPARTMENT}}
- Work Shift - {{HOME.WORK.SHIFT}}
- Project - {{HOME.PROJECT}}
- Work Group - {{HOME.WORK.GROUP}}
- Client Name - {{CLIENT.LEGAL.NAME}}

Document Management (DM) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
DM-1574 Update to Bulk Import File Conventions The file format for bulk imports have been improved for convenience. The file name has only one requirement for the Client ID, and uses the following conventions. - Ignore the first grouping (before the 1st dash) - Ignore the numbers before the C/E in the middle grouping - The numbers following the C or E WILL BE THE CLIENT ID - Ignore the underscore and everything after it For example, if the file ID was “C12-34E4567_890”, the system would read this file as belonging to Client ID 4567. For more information, see the in-app help.

Employee Portal (EP) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
EP-3449 Additional Document Permissions Service Providers can now set more specific document permissions on Configuration Templates and Client Overrides. The document permissions now display as a multi-select field, allowing service providers to select or deselect separate options for Delete, Edit, Move, Rename, and Upload. By using these additional permission options, Service Providers can control document permissions more precisely across templates and client overrides. For more information, See Managing Configuration Templates.
EP-10915 Portal Rebranding Throughout the System The system for employee and manager logins has been rebranded to Portal. Instances where it previously displayed Employee Portal have been changed to simply display Portal.

Identity and Access Management (IAM) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
IAM-2985 Federated User Authentication Federated Users can now link an external user ID to their current account. This allows these users to link their legacy accounts to their current PrismONE ID. During the linking process, the user is redirected to their external identity provider to authenticate for the linking process. For more information, see the in-app help.
IAM-3028 Privacy Policy Branding from Portal When a user accesses the PrismONE login and the Portal form is configured with a custom privacy policy for the client’s configuration template, the custom privacy policy now displays on the PrismONE forms. For more information, see the in-app help.

Onboarding (OB) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
OBE-9376 Enhancement to I-9 Supporting Documents Explanation The instructions for the I-9 Supporting Documents section has been improved for remote employees. When the Remote Verification option is enabled for the employee’s Worksite Location, the explanation of the opt-out flag has been updated to read “I will present documentation to my employer or authorized representative in person.” When the Remote Verification option is not enabled for the employee’s Worksite Location, the system now displays the following message: “You can upload supporting documents using the form below. In person, physical documentation verification may still be required.” In addition, the opt-out flag has been updated to read “I will be presenting documentation in person only.” For more information, see the in-app help.
WSP-4247 Hover Over Description in Client Workflow Grid When the Workflow Description on the Client Workflow grid is too long to display in a single cell, employees can now hover over the field to display the text of the full name. For more information, see See Assigning Workflows at the Client Level.

Prism (PD) Enhancements

Ticket Category Description Summary Help Content
PD-23966, PD-23985, and PD-23987 Client Administration Enhancements to User Defined Fields Import Form The following enhancements now reside on the User Defined Fields Import form: - The text that displays in the Import Data panel on the User Defined Fields Import form now displays as follows: [Image: screenshot] - If your user role does not have access to the form/file listed in the import file, the import fails. - You must upload the most-recent version of the import file before performing an import so the field column headers match the field’s current type and required status. (If a field is duplicated, the system uploads the last value.) Otherwise, an error message displays, “INVALID COLUMN HEADER: download the latest import file.” For more information, see Importing User-Defined Fields.
PD-17422 Human Resources Enhancement to Employee Types Form You can now quickly perform a global search for “Employment Type,” which opens the Employee Types form where you can establish employee types that are used to define employee employment type. (Searching for “Employee Type” also displays the Employee Types form.) For more information, see Establishing Employee Types.
WSP-3980, WSP-3982, and WSP-4043 Human Resources Enhancement to Employee Details Form A new field, International Employee, now displays on the Address tab in the Employee Details form. For example: [Image: screenshot] Note: This feature is only available for service providers. To use this feature, you must enable the system-level INTLEMPLOYEE custom feature code on the System Parameters form. To waive requiring a US-based resident address for an international employee, select International Employee. > Note: Note the following: - After clicking Save a warning displays if the employee was paid in the past (that is, the Last Pay Date contains a date), “Warning: Employee records with pay data cannot be saved as International Employees.” - After clicking Save a warning displays if the employee was not paid in the past (that is, the Last Pay Date is blank), “Warning: International Employees cannot be processed in a payroll batch, as they do not have a resident address. Would you like to proceed?” Click Yes to proceed. The record saves without requiring Resident Address information. (If appropriate, select International Address and enter the employee’s international address in the Mailing Address panel.) - After selecting International Employee, data in the Address, ZIP Code, City, State, County, and Geocode fields clear. - International employees cannot process payrolls and should be placed in a placeholder Pay Group to avoid work stoppage issues during payroll. - When the following occurs during payroll processing: - An employee has hours on a calculated payroll - The employee record is then updated to an International Employee - The calculated payroll is finalized without recalculation The system displays a payroll error message and stops payroll finalization, then one of the following scenarios occurs: - If you disable the International Employee field from the employee record and attempt finalizing the payroll again, the system allows the payroll finalization process to complete successfully. - If you remove the International Employee pay from the timesheet, the system allows you to recalculate and refinalize the payroll successfully (assuming there are no other errors). - If you recalculate the payroll with the International Employee field enabled, the system displays a calculation error because there is no resident address for the International Employee and payroll finalization is no longer an available option in the payroll process. For more information, see Establishing and Maintaining Employee Address Information.
- An employee has hours on a calculated payroll
- The employee record is then updated to an International Employee
- The calculated payroll is finalized without recalculation
- If you disable the International Employee field from the employee record and attempt finalizing the payroll again, the system allows the payroll finalization process to complete successfully.
- If you remove the International Employee pay from the timesheet, the system allows you to recalculate and refinalize the payroll successfully (assuming there are no other errors).
- If you recalculate the payroll with the International Employee field enabled, the system displays a calculation error because there is no resident address for the International Employee and payroll finalization is no longer an available option in the payroll process.
PD-23636, PD-23679, and PD-23792 Import Processing Enhancements to Data Import Tool The following enhancements now reside in the Data Import Tool: - A new import template, Project (Certified Pay Rates), is now available in the Data Import Tool. You can use this import template to import certified pay rates (that is, position code, position title, base rate, fringe rate, and prevailing wage rate) for projects to reduce the amount of manual work required. - Several new categories, rows 13 through 42, are now available for import using the Projects/Cost Codes import template in the Data Import Tool. (These new categories represent the rest of the fields not originally included that reside on the Projects form, where you can set project information.) Note: You can use the Projects/Cost Codes import template to import changes to projects and cost codes to reduce the amount of manual work required. - Request: Update the Worksite Locations import template in the Data Import Tool to include additional fields that are critical for tax filings and E-Verify compliance. New fields being added (columns 37–41, all optional, appended to the end of the existing template): - 37: Worksite Federal EIN. - 38: Worksite ID - 39: Federal Entity ID - 40: Exclude this location from E-Verification - 41: Enable Remote Verification for this Location Fields are located under Client → Change → Worksite Locations (Other Parameters section). The template lives at Operations → Import Processing → Data Import Tool. The Sample Header File also needs updating. No security changes are required. In short, this is a template enhancement to allow bulk import of tax-related identifiers and E-Verify settings for worksite locations. For more information, seeImporting Certified Pay Rates for Projects Importing Project and Cost Codes, and Importing Worksite Locations.
- 37: Worksite Federal EIN.
- 38: Worksite ID
- 39: Federal Entity ID
- 40: Exclude this location from E-Verification
- 41: Enable Remote Verification for this Location
PD-20492 Payroll Enhancement to Net to Gross Calculator Form The Net to Gross Calculator form now accurately includes garnishment deductions when you enable the Supplemental pay voucher type. This enhancement ensures net pay estimates provided by the calculator align with actual payroll batch results. In addition, the following now occurs: - Accurate Supplemental Pay Estimates: The calculator now identifies and includes active garnishment deductions for Supplemental pay vouchers, provided no suppressions are active. - Arrears Handling: For Supplemental pay voucher types, the calculator specifically includes applicable arrears amounts to match standard payroll processing behavior. - Improved Visibility: Garnishment deduction line items now display in the NTG results table when you enable the Supplemental pay voucher type, maintaining consistency with Regular and Vacation voucher types. - Enhanced Calculation Logic: These updates ensure the final Net Pay result reflects all applicable deductions, providing you with a more reliable estimate for Supplemental payroll processing. For more information, see Net-to-Gross Calculator.
PD-23738 and PD-23739 Payroll Enhancement to Client Allocation Formats Form A new button, Copy, now displays on the Client Allocation Formats form. For example: [Image: screenshot] You can click the Copy button to duplicate an existing format code. (The Copy button is disabled until you enter or select a format code.) The Copy Client Allocation Format form displays, where you can save a new format code. Note: If you enter an existing format code in the Copy Client Allocation Format form an error message displays, “Format code already exists. Please choose a different code.” For more information, see Setting Client Allocation Formats.
PD-23743 and PD-23744 Payroll Enhancement to Payroll Allocation Report Add “Exclude Non-Cash Pay Codes from Allocation Base” checkbox to Payroll Allocation Report Parameters UI What it does: The Payroll Allocation Report currently has an “Include Non-Cash Pay Codes” toggle, but clients who want non-cash pay lines to appear on the report while keeping them out of the tax allocation base have no way to do that. Note: The new functionality only activates when both “Exclude Non-Cash from Alloc Base” and “Include Non-Cash Pay Codes” are checked. All other combinations behave the same as today. This story adds a new “Exclude Non-Cash Pay Codes from Allocation Base” checkbox to two forms: - Client / Change / Payroll Allocation Report Parameters (saved parameters) - Payroll / Report / Payroll Allocation Report (on-the-fly parameters) Key requirements: - Checkbox defaults to unchecked - Should be placed below the existing “Include Non-Cash Pay Codes” toggle - When checked on the Parameters form, the Report form reflects the same value - Existing saved parameter sets must not be affected — the new field defaults to off For more information, see Payroll Allocation Report.
PD-23785, PD-23786, and PD-23977 Payroll Enhancement to Deduction Codes Form A new Calculation Method, % of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types), is now available on the Deduction Codes form. Note: When using the % of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types) option, you can enable the 403(b) Retirement option and select multiple voluntary classifications in the Voluntary Classifications panel. However, observe the following when making these selections: - You cannot enable more than one “retirement” voluntary classification. - You cannot enable bothSection 125 and Section 132. After you select % of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types), the Exclude Ded. Type Code panel displays where you can exclude pre-tax benefit deduction types for plans that require contributions to be calculated as a percentage of gross earnings, such as COPERA. For more information, see Maintaining Global Deduction Codes.
PP-1395 Payroll California Data for Certified Payroll XML Download Report California certified pay data can now be downloaded directly from Prism using the Certified Payroll XML Download Report. To include California data, the fields for California must be configured in the Certified Payroll Details section of the Projects form. Data from timesheets that include California employees can then be accessed by running the Certified Payroll XML Download report. For more information, see Certified Payroll XML Download Report.
PP-2602 Payroll Enhancement to Export Email Information Notification emails for the Periodic Tax JSON Export form now include information about export details such as selected reports and build status, consistent with the existing Quarterly Tax JSON Export email. For more information, see Periodic Tax JSON Export.
WSP-3858 Payroll Enhancement to SuperBatch Form SuperBatch Filter Updates — New Delivery Method and Delivery Date Filters The SuperBatch filter modal now includes two new filter options: Delivery Method and Delivery Date. These filters appear beneath the existing Pay Date filter. With these additions, you can narrow your SuperBatch results to show only payrolls that match a specific delivery method or delivery date, making it easier to group and process like delivery activities together. For payrolls with multiple delivery methods — such as those with location-based special delivery settings — the batch will appear in the filter results for each applicable method. For more information, see Using SuperBatch.
WSP-3981 New Employee Import Enhancement to Import Field Mapping Form A new field, INTERNATIONAL.EMPLOYEE, now displays on the Import Field Mapping form that allows you to import a new International Employee in the New Employee Import form. For example: [Image: screenshot] You can include the International Employee column in the import file (with valid values as Y/Yes, N/No, or blank). Additionally, employees flagged as international can be imported without US-based resident address information. Note: When the INTLEMPLOYEE CFC is not enabled, the field is unavailable for import and resident address remains required. For more information, see Creating and Editing Import Mappings.
RRT-6871 Payroll Enhancement to Client Allocation Formats Form To ensure the system now displays 401k non-elective match amounts with no bill code in the Client Allocation Report for clients who have their own 401k plans, a new Allocation Code, 401KALL, is now available. You can use 401KALL to combine amounts for the following contributions: - Matching Contribution - PEO Matching Contribution - Safe Harbor Type One Match - Safe Harbor Type Two Match For more information, see Setting Client Allocation Formats.
WSP-3983 Payroll Enhancement to Payroll Control Form In association with the new field, International Employee (see WSP-3980, WSP-3982, and WSP-4043), you cannot enter or select any International Employees in the Employee panel on the Payroll Control form, which ensures that these employees are not included in the payroll batch. (If you enter an International Employee an error message displays, “International Employees cannot be added to a payroll batch.”) For more information, see Establishing Information for Processing Payrolls.
PD-23759, PD-23760, and PD-23824 Time Off Enhancement to Time Off Plans Form A new field, Linked Accruals Maximum Balance, now displays in the Time Off Plans form. For example: [Image: screenshot] You can use the Linked Accruals Maximum Balance field to define the maximum number of hours the plan is allowed to hold, which the system will use to limit how many hours are transferred from the linked Accrual Register each year based on the Balance Plan’s Annual Carryover. (Leaving the Linked Accruals Maximum Balance field blank indicates that any amount can be transferred.) > Note: Note the following: - If you Copy from another plan that contains a Linked Accruals Maximum Balance amount, the system populates that field in the duplicated plan. - If you configure a Balance Time Off Plan with a Linked Accruals Maximum Balance limit and the employee’s current balance is below that limit, when the system processes a Linked Accrual transfer only the hours needed to bring the balance up to (but not exceeding) the stop balance are transferred. - If you configure the Balance Time Off Plan with a Linked Accruals Maximum Balance limit and the employee’s current balance is already at or above that limit, when the system processes a Linked Accrual transfer no hours are transferred to the Balance Time Off Plan. - If you configure a Balance Time Off plan with no Linked Accruals Maximum Balance limit, when the system processes a Linked Accrual transfer the system applies the full transfer amount with no change to current behavior. For more information, see Defining Time Off Plans.

Fixes

Benefits Administration (BA) Fixes

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
WSP-3879 Previously, on the Benefits Billing Detail Report form, when you run a report with Primary Sort set as Benefit Plan under the Sort Parameters section, the XLS export missed the Selection Criteria column in the Column C. This issue affected both the Summary and Detail Report Types. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-3916 Previously, on the Benefit Rules form, when you selected a Benefit Plan or an existing Effective Date, then the Total Contribution columns displayed incorrect values. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-4030 Previously, on the Retirement Plan Enrollment form, under the Election Details section, when you entered a value in the Not to Exceed % of Pay field, then the percentage values entered in the field were not stored correctly, which lead to incorrect payroll deductions. For example, when you entered a value of 10 (intended as 10%), then the system stored this value in a way that caused payroll to interpret it as a much smaller percentage (10% was processed as 0.10%). Now, this is fixed. The input and display for this field now correctly handles percentage values. All new entries are now stored and interpreted accurately by payroll as the intended percentage. All the existing records that were affected by this issue (entries made between January 2025 and the June 2026 release) will not be automatically updated. The form will now display these values in a way that reflects how payroll has been processing them.
WSP-4162 Previously on the Group Benefit Plans form, fields under the Guaranteed Issue (GI) Limits section were required across all sections (Employee, Spouse, Dependent) when data was entered in any one section, which was incorrect. Now, this is fixed. GI Limits fields are now only required for sections that have corresponding Coverage Amounts data. For example, a Spouse-only Life Insurance plan no longer triggers a validation error when Employee and Dependent GI Limits fields are left blank.
WSP-4200 Previously, on the Employee Flexible Spending Accounts form, when you clicked the Plan Year hyperlink, the system displayed incorrect plan year. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-4258 Previously, when you ran a Slavic Import with the SEQSLAVICIMPORT custom feature code enabled, then the system cleared an employee’s Retirement Benefit Group when Column H was left blank in the import file. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-4262 On the Client Benefits Overview form, when you viewed the Client Benefits Overview Report, the plans with Network based Benefit Rules displayed special characters. Now, this is fixed.

Compliance (CMP) Fixes

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-7813 Previously, the payroll warning for an employee whose salary is below the state minimum exempt salary amount did not display when the Worksite Location Code was not the State Abbreviation. Now, this is resolved. For an employee whose salary is below the state minimum exempt salary amount, the payroll warning will display when the Worksite Location is in the applicable state, regardless of the Worksite Location Code.
CMP-7076 Previously, for both SBEA and non-SBEA clients, for employees in Guam, the system did not correctly report their federal income tax withholding for tax code 66-10 on the MasterTax RTS 601 record, if any for the quarter. Now, this is resolved.
WSP-4227 Previously, when processing a State Tax Levy configured for “Subsequent Gross Pay,” the garnishment calculation was not correctly enforcing the Federal Poverty Guideline (FPG) limit. In certain cases, the Garnishment Check Amount would exceed the allowable threshold of Gross Pay minus the Federal Poverty Guideline Amount, resulting in an incorrect deduction. Now, this is resolved. The garnishment calculation logic has been corrected so that State Tax Levy amounts based on Subsequent Gross Pay now properly cap at the Gross Pay – Federal Poverty Guideline Amount. State Tax Rules continue to take priority where applicable. The FPG enforcement is now accurately reflected in the Garnishment detail record.
RRT-6894 Previously, when calculating retirement contributions for an employee in the state of Massachusetts, the system incorrectly included the Employer 401(k) match contributions in the MA PFML taxable wages when not safe harbor. Now, this is resolved. - Employer 401(k) match contributions (including non‑safe harbor / non‑elective matches) are now correctly excluded from MA PFML taxable wages. - Employee 401(k) elective deferrals (the amount an employee chooses to defer from salary) continue to be correctly included in MA PFML taxable wages.
  • Employer 401(k) match contributions (including non‑safe harbor / non‑elective matches) are now correctly excluded from MA PFML taxable wages.
  • Employee 401(k) elective deferrals (the amount an employee chooses to defer from salary) continue to be correctly included in MA PFML taxable wages. ### Employee Portal (EP) Fixes

EERT-3804 The W4 form displayed the Original Hire Date instead of the Last Hire Date for Rehired employees. This is fixed.
EERT-3823 When a manager terminated an employee, the Termination Explanation field was not set as a required field. This is fixed.
EERT-3826 When Employee Statuses and Employee Types were configured on the Client Details form, the types were properly restricted on the New Hire Dashboard in Portal, but the statuses were not properly restricted. This is fixed.
EERT-3829 When an employee made changes to their personal information on the Address form, the banner reminding the employee that these changes might have tax implications did not display. This is fixed.
EERT-3832 Employees who were registered through PrismOne did not receive active alerts upon logging in. This is fixed.
EERT-3838 When an employee edited the custom Privacy Policy and clicked the View HTML icon, the changes to the policy did not save properly. This is fixed.

EP-11118 When an employee was part of two or more SMBs and attempted to access Portal using a client-specific URL, if that client was not one of the employee’s SMBs, the session would stall and prevent the employee from accessing the client selector. This is fixed.

IAM-2331 When a user with a registration code did not complete registration and tried again using the same code, a generic error message appeared. This is fixed. A message now displays indicating that the code has expired and that the employee must request a new registration link and PIN from the employer.
IAM-2424 When employees viewed their Account Settings form, and those employees had multiple linked accounts for a single organization, the My Linked Accounts section displayed the organization name multiple times as separate headers. This is fixed.

Onboarding (OB) Fixes

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
EERT-3827 When employees who were terminated tried logging in to the enrollment app were not alerted with a warning message that indicated that there were no active workflow available. This is fixed. If a terminated employee now tries to navigate from the portal to BE, then they would be unable to continue their enrollment process.
EERT-3828 Previously, on the Group Benefit Plans form, fields under the Guaranteed Issue (GI) Limits section were required across all sections (Employee, Spouse, Dependent) when data was entered in any one section, which was incorrect. EERT-3830 During the enrollment workflow, the Total Plan Premium displayed on the Life Benefit Plan tile was incorrectly calculated for Voluntary Life and Voluntary AD&D plans. This is fixed.
EERT-3833 When the tax forms page was configured to hide the navigation header, the My Progress sidebar did not display properly and had text cut off. This is fixed.

EERT-3857 Certain benefits import programs did not release EMPLOYEE.DED and EMPLOYEE.FLEX.ACCOUNTS record locks when no changes were made. This caused records to remain locked in production, preventing subsequent updates. This is fixed.
OBE-9803 When an employee enrolled in an FSA that was set to allow enrollment, but the Allow Coverage Amount Change field was set to No, the employee could not submit the workflow. This is fixed.

Prism (PD) Fixes

Jira # Category Issue Summary Resolution
PD-23849 General When a future termination date was entered for a Worksite Manager (WSM) who had access to multiple clients, the system immediately revoked access to all non-home clients — even though the termination date had not yet been reached. This caused affected managers to lose the ability to log in and work across their assigned clients before their actual last day. The system now correctly maintains a Worksite Manager’s full access to all assigned clients until the specified termination date. Entering a future-dated termination record no longer triggers an immediate change to security permissions. Access is restricted only once the system date reaches the recorded termination date, ensuring uninterrupted workflow through the manager’s final day.
PP-1944 General When managers tried approving New Hire approval, the system consistently displayed error message. This is fixed.
PP-2037 General When a user viewed the Time Sheets header on the Time Sheet Entry form, it remained fixed at its minimum width. This is fixed. The Time Sheets header is now expanded and dynamically resizes to fill the available screen real estate.
PP-2524 General When users searched for clients by name in Prism’s global search, the system displayed only the first 20 matches, which caused clients to appear missing. This is fixed.
PP-2614 General Users experienced significant slowdowns during login and while navigating for clients with large employee counts. This is fixed.
PP-2633 General When employees accessed the Users form, a literal “{1}” placeholder in the password and MFA status messages displayed instead of the configured identity product name. This is fixed.
RRT-6885 General The system stopped running payroll after users updated the default Deduction Code used for all Retirement Plans on the System Parameters form due to multiple type K records that were created in the Recurring Deduction form for all employees with a Retirement Enrollment record, which uses the corresponding default Deduction Code setting. In this scenario, a message now displays acknowledging the change and updates all associated records and provides a list of affected employee enrollments. After updating, the corresponding Deduction Code displays on the Recurring Deductions form for each associated employee, which is pulled into the payroll. If a user selects No in the initial message that displays or in the on-screen updated records that display, the system returns to the main form where the original values are automatically populated. Any Retirement Plans that have a Deduction Code Override for the corresponding Deduction Code being updated remains unchanged. When updating the Deduction Code on the System Parameters form, the Deduction Code only affects enrollments which are using the default Deduction Code assigned within the System Parameters form. > Note: Note the following: - If a user updates the System Parameters Deduction Code for ‘Loan’ and the Retirement Plan has no Deduction Code Override defined for ‘Loan,’ then the system updates all associated Retirement Enrollment records. - If a user updates the System Parameters Deduction Code for ‘Employee Deferral’ and the Retirement Plan has a Deduction/Bill Code Override defined for ‘Employee Deferral,’ then the system does not update the associated Retirement Enrollment records.
- If a user updates the System Parameters Deduction Code for ‘Loan’ and the Retirement Plan has no Deduction Code Override defined for ‘Loan,’ then the system updates all associated Retirement Enrollment records.
- If a user updates the System Parameters Deduction Code for ‘Employee Deferral’ and the Retirement Plan has a Deduction/Bill Code Override defined for ‘Employee Deferral,’ then the system does not update the associated Retirement Enrollment records.
RRT-6935 General When the system routed an HR-action approval (such as a Leave Request, Pay Rate Change, or Termination) to an assigned approver (Manager/PTO Approver) and that approver is later teminated and the pending approval was not reassigned, the approval became “orphaned.” (A nightly batch auto-processed it and, on failure, emailed a notification to an arbitrary, cross-client user who had no access to that employee.) The system no longer sends orphaned-approval “failure/resubmit” emails and now processes orphaned approvals.
WSP-4418 General Users encountered an error stating “There are no Import Field Map Definitions that match your spreadsheet” when attempting to import new employees using the Prism-Expanded field mapping, even when using the correct template and file formats. The New Employee Import has been updated to correctly match import mappings without requiring the “INTERNATIONAL.EMPLOYEE” header in the import file when the “INTLEMPLOYEE” Client Functional Constant (CFC) is not enabled. If the “INTLEMPLOYEE” CFC is enabled, the system now properly validates the mapping to include the “INTERNATIONAL.EMPLOYEE” field.
WSP-4070 Payroll When users created a new payroll batch using the Clone Last Batch option in the Payroll Control form, the system did not clone the information in the Delivery Method Override field on the Payroll Options form. This is fixed.
WSP-4336 Payroll The system did not post the deduction import amounts in the Time Sheet Deduction Import form for all employees in the import. In addition, the payroll vouchers posted these values as a lesser amount, with the decimal point over-adjusted two places to the left. This is fixed.
WSP-4406 Payroll Customers reported that delivery sheets were being automatically generated and printed with payroll reports (such as checks), even when the system was configured not to include them. This occurred specifically when the Paperless Delivery option was set to “all payroll output.” The payroll reporting process has been updated to correctly respect the Paperless Delivery configuration. Delivery sheets will no longer be generated or included in consolidated payroll reports when they are not required by the client’s setup.

June (R_202606)

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/Release-Notes/2026/06/whatsnew-R_202606.htm Path: Release-Notes/2026/06/whatsnew-R_202606.htm

Welcome

PrismHR software is specifically designed to help Professional Employer Organizations (PEOs) and Administrative Services Organizations (ASOs) reduce risk, be more efficient, expand business, and be more profitable.

When you choose PrismHR, you are choosing more than just a software platform. You are partnering with a team of professionals who are deeply invested in the PEO and ASO industry and dedicated to providing the best technology and services possible. You are also partnering with other professionals in the industry in the sense that we all learn from each other.

To view release notes for PrismHR, click any of the links in the Table of Contents. Each release is represented with a book that features the month and year. Click these books to expand product names and version numbers for the release. The most recent documents are at the top of the list. Use the Search feature to look for a specific keyword or phrase. Open any PDFs for Download book to view and print release notes documents from the past year.

New Features

We would like to bring your attention to the following list of new features for PrismHR.

List of New Features

Click a link to display the detailed release notes for the new feature

  • Commission Period Look-back: You can use the Commission Period Look-back form to administer Percent Target Amount (PTG) commission types. This form streamlines the process of identifying active clients who had payrolls processed during a specified look-back period but have no corresponding invoice data in a target period and automatically generates the invoice records needed to accurately apply PTG commissions. (See Administering PTG Commission Types.) JIRA # WSP-4233 and WSP-4234
  • Payroll Voucher Report: You can use the Payroll Voucher Report form to generate the Payroll Voucher Report for a selected client or pay date, so you can review voucher details before posting and reconciling against source data. (See Payroll Voucher Report.) JIRA # PD-23838
  • AI Assistant: The Prisma AI Assistant is now available for service providers. This AI assistant can provide help viewing release notes, answering common questions, troubleshooting problems, and configuring aspects of the Prism system. To access the AI assistant, simply click the icon in the lower right: [Image: screenshot]The AI assistant overlays on top of the current screen, allowing you to continue working while asking questions. > Note: Note the following:
  • A new permission item, HRPY.WORK*AI.ASSIST, has been added to grant access to the AI Assistant for user roles. These permissions can be changed on the User Roles form.
  • The AI assistant accesses PrismHR documentation to help answer questions and clarify procedures.
  • The AI assistant does not have direct access to customer data or personal identifiable information.
  • Using this new AI assistant, service providers can quickly query the assistant with any questions regarding forms and procedures in the Prism system to conduct their work more efficiently.JIRA # AIPR-1

Documentation Enhancements

Click a link to read about the documentation enhancements included in this release.

Benefits Administration (BA) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
WSP-2607 Enhancements to the Data Import Tool Form On the Data Import Tool form, when you import employee dependents, you can now identify employees using their SSN, Employee ID, or Clock Number. This enhancement ensures consistency across import types and provides more flexibility for managing dependent data. [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the Importing Employee Dependents help topic.
WSP-2611 Enhancements to the Benefit Import Maintenance Form While importing data on the Benefit Import Maintenance form, you can now identify employees by Employee ID, SSN, or Clock Number. This enhancement provides greater flexibility and aligns the tool with other import processes. [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the Setting Benefit Import Parameters help topic.
WSP-3018, WSP-4232, WSP-4264 Enhancements to the Cobra Participant Record Form - The COBRA Participant Record form now includes enhanced Social Security Number (SSN) validation for dependents. You will receive specific error messages for invalid formats or restricted number sequences to ensure data accuracy. - The system now prevents the deletion of COBRA Qualifying Event codes that are currently assigned to participant records on the COBRA Participant Record form. When a deletion is attempted, a validation message displays the number of affected records and provides a detailed report of the impacted participants. - With this enhancement, we have fixed the issue in the COBRA Participant Record where the Qualifying Event field failed to update when switching between participants. Additionally, a new ‘Open in new window (print or save)’ hyperlink is now available on HTML messages for improved accessibility and reporting. For more information, see the Maintaining COBRA Participant Records help topic.
WSP-3929, WSP-4419 Enhancements to the Benefit Rules Form The Benefit Rules form now prevents data entry and hides detail sections until the mandatory Benefit Group, Benefit Plan, and Effective Date fields are assigned. This update ensures data integrity and reduces confusion by gating access to contribution, coverage, and eligibility rules until the record is properly identified. [Image: screenshot] Additionally, the Benefit Rules form displays the Benefit Plan description next to the plan code. This restoration helps users quickly verify they are working on the correct plan when making rule adjustments. For more information, see the Setting Up Employee Enrollment Conditions help topic.
WSP-3979 Enhancement to the Purge COBRA Enrollees Form The Purge COBRA Enrollees form now features an enhanced Participant ID multi-selector with new filters for Enrollee Type, Client ID, COBRA Status, and Qualifying Event. This update also resolves an issue where the selector previously failed to display applicable participants. [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the Purge COBRA Enrollees help topic.
WSP-4228, WSP-4423, WSP-4249, WSP-4425 New Column Selector A new header toggle icon is available on the following forms that allows users to customize the on-form report by showing or hiding specific columns: - Employee Benefit Overview - Client Benefits Overview Additionally, a new option, Enable All is available in the column selector. This option appears when one or more columns are deselected, allowing users to quickly restore the full view. [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the Displaying an Employee’s Benefit Plans and the Displaying the Client Benefits Overview help topics.
WSP-4250, WSP-4478 Enhancements to the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides Form The Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form now hides all entry fields, links, and dropdowns until the mandatory Employee, Benefit Plan ID, and Effective Date fields are assigned. This update prevents potential data entry errors and ensures a clearer workflow for administrators. [Image: screenshot] Additionally, the form now displays the Benefit Plan description next to the plan ID. This restoration ensures users can quickly verify they have selected the correct plan when making rule adjustments. For more information, see the Overriding a Client’s Eligibility Rules help topic.
WSP-4409, WSP-4411, WSP-4412, WSP-4413, WSP-4415, WSP-4416, WSP-4417 New Next Pay Date Field A new field, Next Pay Date has now been added on the following forms that helps administrators quickly identify the next regularly scheduled payroll batch date during the enrollment process: - Retirement Plan Enrollment - Employee Benefits Enrollment - Recurring Deductions - Recurring Deduction Overrides - Scheduled Deductions - Scheduled Payments - Employee Deduction Arrears [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the in-app help.
WSP-4316 Enhancement to the Client Workflow Grid Form On the Client Workflow Grid form, you can now hover over a Client ID to view the corresponding Client Name. This enhancement improves visibility and makes it easier to audit enrollment workflows. [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the in-app help.
WSP-4329, WSP-4333 Enhancement to the Post Benefit Enrollments Form On the Post Benefit Enrollments form, you can now filter by Status Class (Active, On Leave, Terminated). Additionally, new columns for Status Class and Status Date have been added to the data table to provide better visibility into employee status. [Image: screenshot] You can also select multiple Client IDs using the new selection modal. [Image: screenshot] For more information, see the in-app help.

Compliance (CMP) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
2026 OBBBA Product Updates To prepare for 2026 reporting required under the OBBBA, multiple product enhancements will be added to the system in upcoming releases. These include: - The ability to recalculate overtime processed using the Straight FLSA Ruleset (which supports CA Daily overtime requirements) to the federal standard. - Automatic qualified tip and overtime calculations and W2 data buiilds. - Updated 2026 Form W-2 and Form 1099 formats.
- The ability to recalculate overtime processed using the Straight FLSA Ruleset (which supports CA Daily overtime requirements) to the federal standard.
- Automatic qualified tip and overtime calculations and W2 data buiilds.
- Updated 2026 Form W-2 and Form 1099 formats.
WSP-4033 Changes to the Washington Workers’ Compensation Classification Rates for Payroll Payroll programs have been updated to calculate Washington State Workers’ Compensation (WC) tax based on the timesheet level WC position. When the “Timesheet based WC tax calculations” flag is enabled on the WA Rate Template, Workers’ Compensation tax is now calculated using timesheet position-level Workers’ Compensation Classification Rates. The Employee Payroll Voucher (EPV) has been enhanced to store Workers’ Compensation hours by position Workers’ Compensation class, Employee Charged Workers’ Compensation Tax Rate, and Employer Charged Workers’ Compensation Tax Rate. For exempt/salaried employees, Workers’ Compensation hours continue to cap at 160 hours per month. When multiple Workers’ Compensation class codes apply on a given charge date, the highest applicable rate is used. Standard WA W/C processing continues when the flag is not enabled. For more information, see W/C Classification Rates
CMP-7792 New Form - Recalculate FLSA Qualified Overtime for OBBBA Payroll administrators can use this form to accurately recalculate and report the Overtime Premium amount on the Form W-2 using federal FLSA guidelines. You can validate the results of the recalculation before finalizing the process. You cannot recalculate payroll data that was entered using Overtime 1.5 or Doubletime 2X calculations at this time. Various filters are provided to specify the scope of the overtime recalculation process. > Note: Note: Client Access Group security is not enabled on this form To access this form, click Back Office. Under the Operations \ Action section, click Recalculate FLSA Qualified Overtime for OBBBA. To Recalculate FLSA Qualified Overtime for OBBBA for employees: Complete the following fields: - Client ID - Enter one or more client IDs for whom you want to recalculate FLSA Qualified Overtime for OBBBA or you can click the Client ID hyperlink and select them from the Select Clients dialog box. - Employer ID - Enter one or more employer IDs for whom you want to recalculate FLSA Qualified Overtime for OBBBA or you can click the Employer ID hyperlink and select them from the Select Employer dialog box. - FLSA Ruleset - Enter FLSA Rulesets with STRAIGHT (S) Reporting method only. - Location Group - This field is optional. Enter one or more location codes. - Pay Group - This field is optional. Enter one or more pay groups. - Year - Select the year from the drop-down. Years prior to 2026 will not be available. - Quarter - This field defaults to the immediate prior quarter. Select the appropriate prior quarter from the drop-down. - Suppress vouchers with FLSA hours = 0 - By default this box is unchecked. Check this box if you do not want to list employee payroll vouchers for the selected quarter which had zero FLSA hours. 1. Click Preview to view the list of recalculated payroll vouchers for employees based on the selections made above. No updates will be made to the actual payroll vouchers at this time. 2. Click Cancel to clear this form at any time. 3. Click the Download hyperlink: 1. after Preview to download the list of payroll vouchers without any updates in a .csv format. 2. after Update to download the updated payroll voucher list in a .csv format. 4. Click Update to update the employee payroll vouchers.

RRT-7024 CMP-7946 CMP-7945 CMP-7941 Changes to the Print W-2 Forms On the Print W-2 Forms form, the following two new form types have been added: - SPDF - Simplex, Four-Up, Not Self-Mailer PDF - LBPDF - Legal Size, Simplex, Four-Up, Self-Mailer with address panel on bottom When selected, W-2 forms are generated as fillable PDFs and made available for download from W-2 Processing > W-2 Reporting > W-2 Reports. Existing electronic W-2 suppression logic continues to apply. The W2 batch download process has been enhanced to support larger data sets. Starting in 2025 you have the ability to suppress the instruction page when generating the W2 batch. Customers who print and mail Form W-2s in-house will have an enhanced process for 2026 tax year reporting. To reduce challenges reported by alignment and printer settings, PrismHR will now print the complete 4 quadrant Form W-2 which should be used on Blank W2 stock to replace the prior 4-Quad W2 stock. This blank W2 stock produces the IRS instructions and has 4 blank perforated sections that will print directly from PrismHR. Customers who will be printing Form W-2 in house in 2026 are encouraged to review the enhanced 2025 Form W-2 formats for alignment, data formatting, and functionality prior to printing 2026 Form W-2s at year end. This new functionality currently has the following known issues which will be resolved in an upcoming release prior to Q4. - Printing Form W-2 should ignore electronic Form W-2 employees unless using the reprint - include electronic option – this currently does not work. - Box 14 does not adjust the font size when words fit outside the box and instead cuts off at the box line - this will be fixed. - Control number prints but does not start at 1 and instead starts at 2, this also affects the sort which does not work. - Reprint - Reissued statement does not appear. - When sorting by any option other than name, the generated zip file references the alpha range for names. Please note the following process change if testing the 2025 W2 PDF forms: - Do not rebuild Form W-2 data as this will reset already processed Form W-2 data - Print W-2 Forms: - Print W2 Form Type S or LB (previously supported format) before printing new PDF form type - Print W2 Form Type SPDF or LBPDF When printing the new PDF form type, if previously supported format is not printed first an error will appear “No W2 Forms selected”. CMP-7934 Changes to the PrismHR Quarterly Tax JSON export To support BLS (Bureau of Labor Statistics) reporting in PrismHR Tax, the BLS 3020 Multiple Worksite Report for PEO and ASO clients requires specific quarterly reporting. To support this, the PrismHR Quarterly Tax JSON export now populates the WorksiteCode field under the EmployeeWageDetails array for all SUI tax codes ending in -24.
