CMP-7944 Changes to the Miscellaneous Global Parameters On this Miscellaneous Global Parameters form, the Do Not Repeat Data on W-2 PDFs Beginning in field will be auto-applied to 2025 and beyond, so that data will not repeat on subsequent employee W-2 pages unless that information did not fit on the previous page of the form. For more information, see Miscellaneous Global Parameters

Employee Portal (EP) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
EP-11013 Support for International Employee Flag Portal now supports the International Employee flag on the Address tab of the Employee Details form. When this option is enabled via the system-level Custom Feature Code for the client and the employee is flagged as an International Employee, Portal now clears the address and geocode for the displayed employee record and disables editing these fields. The record can still be saved normally when other fields are changed. For more information, see the in-app help.
EP-11056 Spanish Translation Support for W-2 Election Configuration The W-2 Election Configuration form (System Parameters > Actions > W-2 Election Text) now includes Spanish translation fields in the Screen Text section. For each existing text field, a corresponding Spanish field has been added: – W2 Elect Intro (Spanish) – W2 Elect Terms (Spanish) – W2 Elect Disabled Message (Spanish) – W2 Elected Message (Spanish) – W2 Elect Accept (Spanish) When an employee views Portal in Spanish, the system displays the configured Spanish translation for the W-2 election introduction, terms and conditions, disabled and elected status messages, and acceptance text. This enhancement enables organizations to provide a fully localized W-2 election experience for their Spanish-speaking employees. For more information, see the in-app help.
EP-11154 Reports in Portal Managers can now view certain system reports directly through Portal using the new Reports menu item. This menu item can be added using the Configuration Templates form or the Client Override form. The first set of reports available in Portal include the following items: - Employee Time Off Accruals Report - Payroll Employer Tax Report - Payroll Summary Report - Payroll Billing Summary Report - Pay Code Summary Report With this enhancement, managers can view these reports while working in Portal to verify important information more quickly and efficiently. > Note: Note: Managers must have Full access on their user role to view the report. Inquiry access does not grant the ability to view the report. > Note: Note: For payroll-related reports, Managers must have access to all employees within a payroll to view the batch as an option on the report. If managers are restricted from accessing records for one or more employees in a batch, they cannot view that batch. Known Issue: On the Payroll Summary report, the Break Out Expense Reimbursement as Separate Column check box does not function properly, and should not be used. This issue will be fixed in an upcoming release. For more information, see the in-app help.

Identity and Access Management (IAM) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
IAM-2985 Federated User Authentication Federated Users can now link an external user ID to their current account. This allows these users to link their legacy accounts to their current PrismONE ID. During the linking process, the user is redirected to their external identity provider to authenticate for the linking process. For more information, see the in-app help.
IAM-3001 Enhancement to Error Messages When an error message displays from the Identity and Access Management system, the error message now displays the correlation ID from their system request. Users who encounter error messages can include this correlation ID on their support request to help identify the exact cause of their issue. For more information, see the in-app help.
IAM-3017 Support for SSO with SAML 2.0 Identity Providers The Identity and Access Management system can now act as an Identity Provider for Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) 2.0, allowing Service Providers to SSO into PrismHR products using the SAML workflow. Administrators can register SAML SSO clients using the SSO Services form found in the Actions menu on the System Parameters form. For more information, see the in-app help.

Onboarding (OB) Enhancements

Ticket Description Summary Help Content
OBE-9246 Automatically Archive Benefit Workflows Clients now have the option to automatically archive Benefit Workflows after a certain amount of time has passed. The new Archive unsubmitted enrollment workflows checkbox can be accessed by navigating to the System Parameters form in Prism and selecting Enrollment Options from the Action bar menu. Selecting this option and specifying a number of days enables the automatic archival of enrollment workflows after the designated time period. When this option is enabled, records from employees in all employment statuses are archived automatically. Records can be unarchived if necessary by navigating to Benefit Utilities and selecting the Unarchive Enrollments form. With this enhancement, clients can maintain enrollment workflow records more efficiently through an organized, automated system. For more information, See Setting Enrollment Options.
OBE-10401 Enhancement to Benefit Plan Offerings During Benefits Enrollment, employees now only see plan offerings that are available for their eligibility date. Plan offerings that are only available outside of the date no longer display as options. With this enhancement, employees can now decide on benefit plans without accidentally selecting plans that would result in a gap in coverage. For more information, See Defining Enrollment Plans.

Prism (PD) Enhancements

Ticket Category Description Summary Help Content
PD-23737 ACH Enhancement to ACH Journal Edit/Entry Form ACH Journal Entry Validation Enhancement To ensure data integrity and prevent processing failures, the system now validates transaction amounts during ACH Journal entries. This update prevents negative values from being included in ACH files, which previously caused errors during the Build Review Report process. - Negative Amount Prevention: The ACH Journal Edit/Entry form no longer accepts values less than zero. - Real-time Error Messaging: If a negative amount is entered, the system will display the error message: “Transaction amount cannot be less than zero.” - Data Integrity: Users are prevented from saving the form until a valid, non-negative amount is provided, ensuring that ACH files remain compliant with processing requirements. For more information, see Creating or Modifying an ACH Journal.
WSP-4280 ACH Enhancement to ACH Originators Form PrismHR now supports the use of a custom Header Trace Number in ACH files. This enhancement allows you to meet the specific formatting requirements of certain financial institutions, such as credit unions, by providing greater control over the NACHA file header and batch control records. What’s New - Custom Trace Number Field: A new, optional Header Trace Number field is available on the ACH Originators form (System > Change > ACH Originators). - Specific Formatting: This field accepts numeric values exactly 8 characters in length. - Automated File Integration: When populated, the custom number is automatically included in positions 80-87 of both the Company/Batch Header and Company/Batch Control records within the NACHA file. - Standardized Support: This feature applies to standard NACHA formats, ensuring compatibility where it’s needed most without affecting third-party formats or reverse wires. Customer Benefit This update provides the flexibility needed to comply with diverse banking requirements. By allowing for a custom Header Trace Number, you can ensure your ACH files are accepted by all participating financial institutions, reducing the risk of file rejections and streamlining your electronic payment processes. For more information, see Using ACH Originators.
RRT-7008 Benefits Administration Enhancement to the Client Benefit Overview Form Improved performance when loading Benefit Plan Setup from the Client Benefit Overview form. For more information, see Displaying the Client Benefits Overview.
WSP-4211 Benefits Enrollment Enhancement to Proxy Login Form PrismHR now allows authorized users to proxy into the Employee Portal for terminated employees. This enhancement ensures that you can provide better support to former staff and verify their portal experience directly. What’s New - Terminated Employee Proxy: The restriction that prevented proxying into the Employee Portal for employees with a “Terminated” status has been removed. - Seamless Support Access: You can now launch the portal proxy window for any terminated employee without encountering validation blocks. Customer Benefit This update improves your ability to assist former employees who still have access to the portal. By allowing you to proxy into their accounts, PrismHR enables you to quickly troubleshoot issues, confirm discrepancies, and ensure a smooth post-employment experience for your users. For more information, see Logging in as an Employee.
RRT-6953 Billing Enhancement to the Billing Events Form You can now configure custom comment templates for Third Party Sick Pay (TPSP) adjustments via a new field on the Billing Events form. These templates support dynamic placeholders for employee and billing details. If no template is defined, the system continues to use the standard default comment. For more information, see Establishing Billing Events.
PD-23997 Client Enhancement to Transfer Employee to New Client Form PrismHR now includes enhanced validation for benefit groups when transferring employees to a new client. This update ensures that only active and appropriate benefit groups can be selected or automatically populated during the transfer process, preventing the use of retired or restricted plans. What’s New - Restricted Plan Selection: When using the Transfer Employee to New Client form (Operations > Action > Transfer Employee to New Client), you can no longer select benefit groups that are designated only for retirement plans. - Active Status Enforcement: Benefit groups with a “Stop New Use” or “Stop All User” date that has already passed or occurs on the current date are now excluded from selection. - Improved Pre-population Logic: If an employee is being transferred to a client that has the same benefit group as their current one, the system will only automatically populate that group if it is still active. If the group has reached its stop date at the new client, it will not be pre-populated. - Manual Entry Validation: These same restrictions apply to manual data entry, ensuring consistency across all methods of assigning benefit groups during a transfer. Customer Benefit This enhancement improves data integrity and reduces administrative errors by ensuring employees are only assigned to valid, active benefit groups during a client transfer. By automatically filtering out retired and retirement-only plans, PrismHR helps you maintain accurate benefit enrollments and simplifies the employee transition process. For more information, see Transferring Employees to New Clients.
RRT-6956 Client Enhancement to the Carrier Plan Billing Report Form PrismHR has improved the performance of the Carrier Plan Billing Report form by reducing per-record overhead and optimizing security checks for service providers. These changes result in faster report generation, particularly when running the report for all clients, while maintaining identical output and data accuracy. For more information, see Carrier Plan Billing Report.
WSP-4183 Client Enhancement to Clone Client Form We have updated the Clone Client process to ensure that system-generated Client IDs are only consumed when a clone is successfully completed. What’s New? Previously, opening the Clone Client form would automatically increment the next available Client ID in the system, even if you didn’t finish the cloning process. This could lead to “gaps” in your Client ID numbering. With this update: - Smart Pre-population: The form still suggests the next available Client ID for your convenience. - Conditional Incrementing: The system now only officially “claims” and increments the Client ID once you click Clone and the process succeeds. - Duplicate Prevention: We’ve added a validation step that double-checks the availability of the Client ID at the moment of cloning. If the ID is already in use, you’ll receive a warning and the form will refresh with the latest available ID. Why It Matters This enhancement provides cleaner data management by preventing skipped Client IDs and ensuring your numbering remains sequential and accurate. It also adds a layer of protection against accidental overwrites, giving you more confidence when setting up new clients. How to Use Navigate to Client > Action > Clone Client. The system will handle the ID validation and incrementing automatically behind the scenes. For more information, see Cloning a Client.
WSP-4260 and WSP-4281 Client Enhancements to Client Details Form The following enhancements now reside on the Client Details form: Expanded Options for Tracking Client Payment Methods PrismHR now offers expanded options for tracking client payment methods within the Billing Setup. This enhancement allows for more granular categorization and improved reporting on how clients transfer funds. What’s New Expanded Transfer Type Options: The Transfer Type dropdown on the Client Detail / Billing panel now includes the following additional options: - Check Deposit - ACH Transfer - Cash Deposit - International Wire Customer Benefit These new options provide a more comprehensive way to categorize client billing preferences. By capturing these specific payment methods, you can easily generate detailed reports and gain better visibility into your billing operations. Support for International Banking Requirements We have enhanced the Client Detail and Billing sections to better support international banking requirements. What’s New? - International Client field: A new International Client checkbox is now available on the Detail tab (located directly below the NAICS code). - Dynamic Field Labeling: When a client is flagged as an “International Client,” the Routing Number field on the Billing tab automatically updates its label to Swift Code. - Flexible Data Entry: For international clients, the Swift Code field allows manual entry of up to 11 characters and bypasses standard ABA routing number validation. Why It Matters This update provides a clear way to identify international clients and ensures that their specific banking information is captured accurately. By dynamically relabeling the field and adjusting validation rules, we’ve made it easier to manage global client setups without compromising the data integrity of your domestic clients. How to Use 1. Navigate to the Client Detail tab and check the International Client box for the relevant client. 2. Go to the Billing tab to enter the Swift Code. 3. For domestic clients, leave the field unchecked to continue using standard ABA/Routing Number validation. For more information, see Specifying Client Billing Options and Maintaining Client Information.
RRT-6955 Employer Administration Enhancement to the W2 Batch Download Form The W2 Batch Download process has been updated to utilize a new fillable PDF service. This change improves the efficiency and reliability of generating W2 forms. For more information, see Setting Up Form W-2 Batch Download.
RRT-7083 Enhanced Dashboard Enhancement to Enhanced Dashboard Security PrismHR has enhanced the security and configuration logic for the Enhanced Dashboard to ensure that Service Provider access remains consistent and unaffected by restrictions intended for other user types. This update also clarifies the precedence of security settings for Worksite Managers (WSMs) and Trusted Advisors (WTAs). What’s New - Service Provider Access Integrity: The Dashboard Access form (Global Configuration > Access Dashboard) has been updated to ensure that settings chosen for WSMs and WTAs no longer inadvertently restrict access for Service Provider users. Service Providers will now maintain their full intended access regardless of these configurations. - Refined WSM/WTA Dashboard Logic: Dashboard access for WSMs and WTAs now correctly updates based on the options selected in the Access Dashboard panel. - Security Precedence: To ensure robust data protection, user role-level security now takes precedence over dashboard-specific settings. For example, the Employee Benefit Enrollment option will remain visible for WSMs and WTAs if their assigned user role permits access to the Employee Benefit Overview form, even if the option is unchecked on the Access Dashboard panel. Customer Benefit This enhancement provides more reliable and predictable dashboard behavior. By ensuring that Service Provider access is preserved and that role-based security remains the primary authority, PrismHR allows you to configure dashboard views for your clients with greater precision and confidence. For more information, see Using the Enhanced Dashboard.
PD-23946 Human Resources Enhancement to Employee Details Form We have expanded the Preferred Language options in the Employee Details section to better support diverse workforces. What’s New? You can now select the following languages from the Preferred Language dropdown (HR > Change > Employee Personal): - Mandarin (MAN) - Portuguese (POR) - Vietnamese (VIE) - Arabic (ARA) - Korean (KOR) - Russian (RUS) - Hindi (HIN) Why It Matters This update allows for more accurate employee record-keeping. Please note that these new options are currently for informational purposes only and do not change the supported languages for the Employee Portal, Onboarding, or automated system notifications. How to Use The new languages are available immediately in the UI dropdown and are supported via the Employee Import and Update APIs using their respective three-letter codes. For more information, see Maintaining an Employee’s Personal Information.
PD-24071 Human Resources Enhancement to Position Change Approval Form PrismHR now provides approvers with more comprehensive information when reviewing position change requests. By surfacing key classification fields directly in the approval workflow, this update ensures that decisions are made with full context and without the need to navigate away from the approval form. What’s New Enhanced Approval Details: The Detail panel of the Position Change approval form now includes three additional rows sourced from the new position record: - New Position Classification: Displays the classification assigned to the target position. - New FLSA Exempt: Indicates the exempt status of the new position as Yes or No. - New Remote Position Classification: Shows the remote classification for the new position (remains blank if no value is set). - Strategic Placement: These new fields appear immediately after the “New Position” row, maintaining a clear and logical layout for reviewers. Customer Benefit This enhancement streamlines the approval process and improves decision-making accuracy. Approvers no longer need to manually look up position details on separate screens, reducing friction and ensuring that critical factors like FLSA status and position classification are always visible during the review. For more information, see Changing an Employee’s Position.
PD-19994 and PD-19996 Payroll Enhancements to Redirect Direct Deposit Form The following enhancements now reside on the Redirect Direct Deposit form: Specifying Different Dates for Offset and Redirect Adjustment Vouchers PrismHR now allows you to specify different dates for offset and redirect adjustment vouchers when redirecting a direct deposit. This ensures that accounting and banking records accurately reflect when funds were returned and reissued. What’s New - New Offset Date Field: A new Offset Date field is now available on the Redirect Direct Deposit form. - Independent Date Control: You can now set a specific date for the offset voucher (which reverses the original transaction) that is different from the redirect voucher date (which reissues the payment). - Automated Posting: When an Offset Date is provided, the system automatically uses it for the offset voucher’s pay date and General Ledger (GL) posting date. The redirect voucher continues to use the Redirect Deposit Date. Customer Benefit This enhancement eliminates the need for manual journal adjustments to correct date discrepancies. By aligning adjustment vouchers with actual banking transaction dates, you can maintain more accurate financial records and streamline your reconciliation process. Capturing and Tracking the Reason for Redirecting a Direct Deposit PrismHR now allows you to capture and track the reason for redirecting a direct deposit. This enhancement ensures that adjustment vouchers include clear reference information, making it easier to match them with original transactions and understand the business cause for the change. What’s New - Redirect Reason Field: A new, optional Redirect Reason field has been added to the Redirect Direct Deposit form (Payroll > Change > Redirect Direct Deposit). This free-text field allows for approximately 60 characters. - Voucher Note Integration: When a reason is entered, it is automatically included in the notes of both the offset and redirect adjustment vouchers, prefixed with “Reason:”. - Enhanced Visibility: You can view the captured redirect reason on the Banking tab of the resulting vouchers. Customer Benefit This update improves auditability and simplifies payroll reconciliation. By providing a dedicated space to document why a direct deposit was redirected—such as a bank return or closed account—PrismHR eliminates the need for manual cross-referencing and ensures that your financial records are comprehensive and easy to navigate. For more information, see Redirecting Direct Deposit Amounts.
PD-23750 Payroll Enhancement to Payroll Control Form To help prevent scheduling conflicts and potential ACH or funding issues, the system now alerts payroll administrators when a manual or special payroll batch is assigned a pay date that falls on a recognized holiday. This enhancement ensures that users can verify the intended check date before committing the batch. - Automated Holiday Detection: When entering a pay date for a manual or special batch, the system automatically checks the date against the client’s specific holiday list and standard bank holidays. - Confirmation Prompt: If a conflict is detected, a warning dialog appears, allowing the administrator to either confirm the date and proceed or cancel to adjust the entry. - Streamlined Workflow: Once a holiday date is acknowledged and confirmed, the warning will not reappear on subsequent saves of that specific batch. - Non-Intrusive Validation: If the entered date does not fall on a holiday, the batch creation process continues without interruption. For more information, see Establishing Information for Processing Payrolls.
PD-23805 Payroll Enhancement to Pay Check Calculator Form The Pay Check Calculator has been streamlined to focus exclusively on Net Pay calculations. The Manual Check option has been removed from this form to ensure a more consistent and error-free user experience. What Changed? - Simplified Calculation Types: The dropdown menu for Calculation Type has been removed. - Net Pay Focus: The calculator now defaults to Net Pay as the sole calculation method. - Interface Cleanup: The field previously used to select between calculation types is now read-only or removed to prevent navigation to unsupported options. - Legacy Cleanup: Removed the legacy Manual Check option, so you can now access that functionality in the Payroll\ Action\ Manual Check Entry form. Why It Matters Previously, selecting the Manual Check option within the Pay Check Calculator could lead to errors. By focusing the tool on its primary purpose—calculating Net Pay—we have improved the reliability of the tool and simplified the workflow for payroll administrators. Customer Benefit Users can now perform pay calculations more quickly and with greater confidence, knowing that the tool is optimized for accurate Net Pay results without the risk of triggering legacy error messages. For more information, see Calculating Net Pay.
PD-23856 and PD-23857 Payroll Enhancement to PEO Client Accounting Form New Option to Exclude Non-Cash Pay Codes from Tax Allocation Base PrismHR has introduced a new configuration option in the PEO Client Accounting Template to provide greater control over tax allocation calculations. Users can now choose to exclude non-cash fringe benefit pay codes from the tax allocation base, ensuring that $0 allocation lines are not included in processing. Customer Benefit This enhancement provides greater control over how taxes are allocated across different pay types. By excluding non-cash items from the allocation base, you can ensure that your GL output more accurately reflects cash-based tax liabilities, leading to cleaner and more precise financial reporting. Key Benefits - Improved Accuracy: By excluding non-cash items from the allocation base, you can ensure that tax allocations more accurately reflect cash-based payroll costs. - Cleaner Reporting: Enabling this option prevents the generation of unnecessary $0 allocation lines, leading to more concise and relevant accounting data. - Flexible Configuration: This setting is managed at the template level, allowing you to apply different allocation logic to different clients as needed. How It Works A new checkbox, Exclude Non-Cash Pay Codes from Tax Allocation Base, has been added to the PEO Client Accounting Template screen (located at Client > Change > PEO Client Accounting). - Default Setting: The checkbox is unchecked by default for all new and existing templates. - Usage: When checked, the system will identify non-cash fringe benefit pay codes and exclude them from the tax allocation base during downstream processing. For more information, see Working with PEO Client Accounting.
WSP-3858 Payroll Enhancement to SuperBatch Form SuperBatch Filter Updates — New Delivery Method and Delivery Date Filters The SuperBatch filter modal now includes two new filter options: Delivery Method and Delivery Date. These filters appear beneath the existing Pay Date filter. With these additions, you can narrow your SuperBatch results to show only payrolls that match a specific delivery method or delivery date, making it easier to group and process like delivery activities together. For payrolls with multiple delivery methods — such as those with location-based special delivery settings — the batch will appear in the filter results for each applicable method. For more information, see Using SuperBatch.
WSP-3882 and WSP-3883 Payroll Enhancements to Payroll Options Form The following enhancements now reside on the Payroll Options form: Control Over Time Off Accruals PrismHR now provides more granular control over time off accruals for manual and special payroll batches. You can now select specific time off plans to include in these batches, ensuring accruals are only forced for the plans you choose. What’s New - Granular Accrual Control: When processing a manual or special batch, you can now select specific time off plans for accrual rather than applying it to all plans. - New Selection Field: A new “Time Off Plans” multi-value grid is available on the Payroll Options form (Payroll Control > Action > Options). This field appears when the “Force Time Off Accruals” checkbox is selected. - Updated Terminology: The “Force PTO Accruals” checkbox has been renamed to Force Time Off Accruals to align with current system conventions. Customer Benefit This enhancement offers greater flexibility for payroll processors, allowing for more precise management of time off accruals during non-standard payroll runs. By selecting only the necessary plans, you can avoid unnecessary accrual calculations and maintain more accurate time off records. Time Off Calculations During Off-cycle Runs Payroll administrators can now ensure Time Off is calculated during off-cycle runs using the new “Force Time Off Accruals” field in Payroll Control. What’s New? - Automated Accruals: Manual and special payroll batches can now trigger accruals automatically, treating them as scheduled runs. - Bypass Restrictions: Override standard “same period” checks for specific Time Off plans to ensure benefits are processed correctly. - Data Integrity: Includes safeguards to prevent forced accruals for previous years, protecting your rollover logic. How to Use: Enable the Force Time Off Accruals field and select the relevant plans in the Payroll Control/Options menu. This update applies to all calculation methods. For more information, see Setting Special Processing Options.
PD-23846 System Enhancement to W-2 Election Configuration Form Spanish Translation Support for W-2 Election Configuration The W-2 Election Configuration form (System Parameters > Actions > W-2 Election Text) now includes Spanish translation fields in the Screen Text section. For each existing text field, a corresponding Spanish field has been added: - W2 Elect Intro (Spanish) - W2 Elect Terms (Spanish) - W2 Elect Disabled Message (Spanish) - W2 Elected Message (Spanish) - W2 Elect Accept (Spanish) When an employee views the portal in Spanish, the system displays the configured Spanish translation for the W-2 election introduction, terms and conditions, disabled and elected status messages, and acceptance text. This enhancement enables organizations to provide a fully localized W-2 election experience for their Spanish-speaking employees. For more information, see Creating W-2 Election Text.
WSP-3807 and WSP-3808 System Enhancement to System Parameters Form A new Starting At field has been added to the System Parameters form (System > Change > System Parameters), allowing Service Provider users to define the starting number for auto-assigned client IDs. Previously, auto-assigned IDs followed an implied sequence; this enhancement gives administrators control over the starting value. Key details: - The Starting At field is available when Auto Assign Company ID is enabled. When Auto Assign Company ID is unchecked, the field is not editable. - Accepts integer values up to the maximum character length defined in your system configuration. - Validates that the entered value is not already in use. If a duplicate is detected, an error message displays the next available client ID. - Leading zeros are treated as insignificant (e.g., 002885 and 2885 are considered the same value). - The field is optional — the form can be saved with or without a Starting At value. For more information, see Setting General System Parameters.
WSP-4383 System Enhancement to User Roles Form PrismHR now offers more flexibility when retiring user roles by allowing you to obsolete roles that are no longer assigned to any active users. This update ensures that roles can be easily managed and retired without being blocked by inactive user assignments. What’s New - Refined Role Obsoletion Logic: The validation on the User Roles form (System > Change > User Roles) has been updated. You can now mark a user role as “obsolete” even if it is still assigned to inactive users. - Active User Protection: To maintain system integrity, the system still prevents you from obsoleting any role that is currently assigned to one or more active users. - Clearer Error Messaging: If you attempt to obsolete a role assigned to active users, a clear error message will now appear: “This role must be removed from all active users before it can be obsoleted!” Customer Benefit This enhancement simplifies user role management by removing unnecessary barriers to retiring old roles. By focusing only on active user assignments, PrismHR allows you to keep your role list clean and up-to-date while still providing a guardrail to prevent accidental disruption for active staff. For more information, see Defining User Roles.
WSP-4384 System Enhancement to Client Status Change Form PrismHR now includes a final confirmation guardrail when terminating a client record. This enhancement ensures that critical actions, such as deleting payroll batches and updating employee benefits, are double-confirmed to prevent accidental data loss. What’s New - Termination Confirmation Pop-up: When changing a client’s status to Terminated on the Client Status Change form (Client > Action > Client Status Change), a new warning message now appears after clicking Save. - Detailed Warning Message: The pop-up alerts you that terminating a client affects multiple records—including payroll batches, employee benefits, and deductions—and that these actions cannot be reversed. - Execution Control: You must explicitly click Yes on the warning message to proceed with the termination. Clicking No will return you to the form without making any changes. - Targeted Validation: This new confirmation step specifically applies to the “Terminated” status and does not affect other status changes. Customer Benefit This update provides an essential layer of protection for your data. By requiring a final confirmation, PrismHR helps prevent the accidental termination of client records, ensuring that such a significant and irreversible action is only taken when intended and after all necessary payroll processes are complete. For more information, see Changing the Client Status.

Fixes

Benefits Administration (BA) Fixes

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
WSP-3212 Previously, Dependent Care (DEP) deduction amounts on employee pay vouchers were not displaying as clickable blue hyperlinks. This occurred for midyear Dependent Care FSA plans when the account used a legacy offer type that was not recognized after the introduction of the new DEPFSA offer type. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-3799 Previously, there was no validation while copying a benefit plan on the Group Benefit Plans form. Now, this is fixed. We have now added a validation to the Copy Benefit Plan feature to prevent copying a plan to itself. This prevents billing rates from being inadvertently deleted when the source and destination IDs are identical.
WSP-4226 Previously, on the Employee Benefits Enrollment form, the eligible benefit enrollment records failed with a “CANNOT FIND PLAN TYPE” error when family-rated premiums were flagged alongside age-banded medical rates. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-4238 Previously, the Benefit Rules form did not collapse all subsections after saving or deleting a record. Now, this is fixed. The Benefit Rules form now correctly collapses all subsections after saving or deleting a record. This ensures the form returns to its default state, consistent with the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form.
WSP-4299 Previously, the Employee Retirement Plan Register form defaulted focus to the Plan ID field upon initial load. Now, this is fixed. The form now correctly defaults to the Employee ID field, as all other selections depend on the selected employee.
WSP-4321 Previously, on certain Benefit related forms, the system allowed to proceed when you provided a plan that was not assigned to the client. Now, this is fixed. We have now added validation to the Benefit Plan ID field to ensure only plans assigned to the client can be manually entered. This update affects Benefit Rules, Benefit Rule Overrides, Retirement Match Rules, and Benefit Adjustments forms.
WSP-4353 Previously, on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form, the Medical, Dental, and Vision plans with associated networks did not appear. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-4370 Previously, on the Benefit Rules form, the Existing Effective Date drop-down field did not clear after saving, deleting, or canceling a record. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-4371 Previously, on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form, the existing Effective Date drop-down field did not clear after deleting or canceling a record. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-4394 Previously, on the Client Workflow Grid form, the system displayed the client name even after clicking ‘Clear’ or ‘Cancel’. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-4459 Previously, on the Employee Benefit Rule Overrides form, the ‘Percent of Gross Wages’ field remained visible after saving, deleting, or canceling an override. Now, this is fixed.
WSP-4477 Previously, on the Benefit Billing Detail Report form, users could manually enter benefit plan IDs that were not assigned to the client. Now, this is fixed.

Compliance (CMP) Fixes

Jira Number Issue Summary Resolution
CMP-7039 Previously, the Common Pay Agent data from the latest year listed in Employer Details did not automatically populate in the EES Puerto Rico export file. You had to manually update the Common Pay Agent data for each year. Now, this is resolved. The Common Pay Agent data from the latest year listed in Employer Details now automatically populates in the EES Puerto Rico export file, without requiring to manually update the Common Pay Agent data for each year.
CMP-7861 Previously, the “Work Out of State” flag was missing from the MasterTax (MTS) 500 and 601 records for Pennsylvania (PA), even when the “Include Pennsylvania Work State Flag (Y/N)” field was selected on the MasterTax Interface Parameters form. Now, this is resolved.
CMP-7911 Previously, for employees in the state of Oregon, the Paid Family and Medical Leave (PFML) wages were not reported on the MasterTax 601 record positions 428-441 of the RTS file when PFML tax codes were redirected to alternate codes for example 38-40 to 38-22 and 38-41 to 38-35 for both Employer and Client reported tax basis. Now this is resolved.
CMP-7933 Previously, the system generated a garbled payroll error when calculating the KY County and School District Taxes and payed a larger amount of cash tips. Now, this is resolved.
CMP-7947 Previously, the non-Schedule R version of the Quarterly Tax JSON export incorrectly doubled Q1 tip amounts in the Year-to-Date calculation, resulting in inflated YTD wage and tax totals. Now, this is resolved.
CMP-7948 Previously, the non-schedule R version of the Quarterly JSON export was incorrectly reporting Subject YTD wages as taxable $7,000 for employees who had already exceeded the taxable wage limit but received no pay in the current quarter. The Schedule R version of the Quarterly JSON export was dropping the employees from the tax record block all together. Both versions were significantly under-reporting YTD Subject wage amounts. Now, Non-Schedule R exports now accurately include over-limit wages in the Subject wage calculation, and Schedule R exports no longer omit unpaid employees from the tax record block.
CMP-7950 Previously, the non-Schedule R version of the Quarterly Tax JSON export, incorrectly overstated tipped wages for 00-16TIPS by carrying forward prior-quarter tips on top of YTD totals, and for 00-12TIPS dropped employee records when no tipped wages existed in the current quarter even if they had tips in a prior quarter and should still appear in the YTD record for the tax year. Now, this is resolved. Both Non-Schedule R and Schedule R files now correctly report YTD and QTD tip wage amounts for all applicable employees.
RRT-6910 Previously, when an employee was employed in more than one client under the same employer in the state of Connecticut, the employee portion of CT PFML tax (tax code 07-40) incorrectly displayed an employer‑level tax record even when CT PFML was reported at the client level only. Now this is resolved. If you have employees paid under multiple clients and use client reported CT PFML, then: - CT PFML taxes reported with a tax basis of Client now display only at the client level on the Employee Tax Summary. - No employer‑level record is shown if the tax was never calculated at the employer level. - The display is now consistent and accurate for both employee (EE) and employer (ER) CT PFML taxes 07‑40 and 07‑41, including cases where an employee is paid under multiple clients for the same employer.
  • CT PFML taxes reported with a tax basis of Client now display only at the client level on the Employee Tax Summary.
  • No employer‑level record is shown if the tax was never calculated at the employer level.
  • The display is now consistent and accurate for both employee (EE) and employer (ER) CT PFML taxes 07‑40 and 07‑41, including cases where an employee is paid under multiple clients for the same employer. ### Employee Portal (EP) Fixes
Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
EERT-3846 When a worksite manager accessed the I-9 Approval form using a mobile device, the signature acknowledgement section did not wrap properly, preventing the manager from viewing the full acknowledgement. This is fixed.
EERT-3870 When a manager viewed the My Employees form in Portal, if there were more than 99 pages of employees assigned to the manager, page numbers with more than two digits were partially cut off. This is fixed.
EERT-3906 When a manager’s User Role was set to hide Emergency Contact fields, the manager could still see these fields in Portal. This is fixed.
EP-11144 When a timesheet in Portal included non-productive hours, opening the timesheet in Prism displayed those hours as productive. This is fixed.

Identity and Access Management (IAM) Fixes

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
IAM-3128 When some users attempted to remove the Authentication app using the My Login Settings form in Portal, an error occurred and the app was not removed. This is fixed.

Onboarding (OB) Fixes

Jira # Issue Summary Resolution
EERT-3840 When an employee viewed the Employee Confirmation Statement, English and Spanish text displayed properly based on the employee’s settings. However, when the employee downloaded the Enrollment Statement, the text did not correctly display in the employee’s selected language. This is fixed.
EERT-3851 When a user created or edited a business rule in the Business Rules Library, the rule could be saved even when no operator was selected a the Choose Operator field. This is fixed.
EERT-3862 When additional gender options beside the default Male and Female were enabled on the System Parameters form, these options did not display properly in the Personal Information section of the onboarding workflow. This is fixed.
EERT-3863 When an employee was currently enrolled in a High Deductible Health Plan (HDHP) medical plan and an HSA request message was attached to the plan, when the employee clicked Next the HSA message did not display. This is fixed.
OBE-10407 When an onboarding plan included a Zero Days From Start message, the email message was sent every day after the start day. This is fixed.

Prism (PD) Fixes

Jira # Category Issue Summary Resolution
RRT-7023 Billing Billing rules with invoice minimums did not calculate correctly when using a billing code other than ADMIN or blank. This is fixed. The system now ensures that minimum invoice amounts are properly applied to all specified billing codes.
PD-23822 General When a client record was removed using the Inactive Data Deletion Utility, historical COBRA records associated with that purged client remained in the system. For employees cross-hired with the purged company, these orphaned records triggered a warning during termination in their active client, stating that a new COBRA record would not be created and requiring manual intervention to proceed. The Inactive Data Deletion Utility was updated to ensure that all associated COBRA Participant Records (COBRA.ENROLLEE and COBRA.ENROLLEE.HISTORY) are fully purged when a client is deleted. This prevents orphaned records from interfering with termination processes for cross-hired employees in active clients.
PD-23969 General Worksite Managers (WSMs) and Worksite Trusted Advisors (WTAs) were unable to assign a WSM from a related company as a PTO Approver or Manager on the Employee Details form. Previously, the system allowed this assignment with a warning, but recent updates caused a hard error that prevented saving and reverted the field to the previous value. The validation logic for the PTO Approver and Manager fields on the Employee Details form was updated. WSMs and WTAs can now assign a WSM from a different company as a PTO Approver or Manager, provided the user has access to both the employee and the assigned WSM through Data Entity Security, and the assigned WSM also has access to the employee.
RRT-6925 General While using the Bulk Change Retirement Plan form to migrate employees to a plan using system-default deduction codes, recurring deduction records were not updated and deductions did not pull during payroll. This is fixed.
RRT-6927 General Users without full access to the Employee Benefit Overview form could still view and modify benefit enrollment workflows from the dashboard. This is fixed. The Benefit Enrollments by Status option now correctly requires full permissions for Service Providers, Worksite Managers, and Worksite Trusted Advisors on both the Enhanced and Legacy Dashboards.
RRT-6957 General Data Retriever reports generated special characters instead of numbers. This is fixed. The system now ensures that report data, including critical 401k information, is displayed accurately.
WSP-4054 General After importing a new Time Off Auto-Enrollment Rule, clicking the “New Rule” button incorrectly opened a form pre-populated with the data from the newly imported rule instead of a blank form. This occurred because the system’s in-memory counter for rule sequence numbers was not refreshed after the background import process completed. The Time Off Auto-Enrollment Rule Maintenance form has been updated to refresh the highest sequence number from the database before calculating the next rule number. This ensures that clicking “New Rule” always opens a blank form for rule creation, regardless of whether the previous rule was created manually or via import.
WSP-4418 General Users encountered an error stating “There are no Import Field Map Definitions that match your spreadsheet” when attempting to import new employees using the Prism-Expanded field mapping, even when using the correct template and file formats. The New Employee Import has been updated to correctly match import mappings without requiring the “INTERNATIONAL.EMPLOYEE” header in the import file when the “INTLEMPLOYEE” Client Functional Constant (CFC) is not enabled. If the “INTLEMPLOYEE” CFC is enabled, the system now properly validates the mapping to include the “INTERNATIONAL.EMPLOYEE” field.
PD-20360 Payroll Timesheet Detail Display Correction This update resolves a display issue in the Timesheet Detail screen that occurred when deleting specific pay entries. Previously, deleting a “Units” pay code (such as “Other”) would cause the system to incorrectly populate the “Hours Paid” field of the remaining entries with the pay rate value, leading to potential confusion during payroll review. - Improved Deletion Logic: Deleting a pay entry now correctly resets the entry form, ensuring that subsequent lines display accurate hours and pay rates. - Accurate Data Visualization: The review screen now maintains the correct “Hours Paid” values for remaining entries after a deletion, preventing misleading information from appearing before saving. - Enhanced Workflow Reliability: While the underlying payroll data remained secure, this fix ensures the visual interface consistently matches the stored records, reducing the need for manual verification. This is fixed.
PD-20628 Payroll The regenerated accounting file displayed the literal <> text instead of the expected DB/CR indicator value. The regenerated file now correctly resolves the token, matching the behavior of the original accounting file generation. We resolved an issue where the <> custom heading in PEO Client Accounting templates did not display correctly when using the Regenerate & Repost Accounting function.
PD-20737 Payroll Users encountered a payroll initialization error when a global voluntary deduction code was marked as obsolete, even if the employee’s recurring deduction record already had a stop date set before the obsolete date. The system was updated to recognize when an employee’s deduction is already stopped. If the employee’s recurring deduction has a stop date that occurs before the pay date, the system will no longer trigger a hard stop error during payroll calculation, even if the global deduction code has been obsoleted. This allows users to maintain historical records for voluntary employee recurring deductions without causing payroll processing issues.
PD-24079 Payroll The “% of Gross Earnings (less Deduction Types)” deduction method (PGDT) was not subtracting all qualifying excluded-type deductions from gross earnings if those deductions were positioned after the PGDT deduction in the employee’s deduction sequence. The payroll calculation logic was updated to ensure that all deductions of the excluded type are subtracted from gross earnings before the percentage is applied, regardless of their position in the employee’s deduction sequence. This ensures accurate calculation of the PGDT deduction base.
RRT-7002 Payroll Previously, on the Process Payroll and Time Sheet Entry forms, resizing the browser window caused the screen to go blank, requiring a manual page refresh to restore the data. Now, this is fixed. Additionally, the Time Sheet form requires a minimum browser form width. If the browser width is insufficient to render the time sheet correctly, an error message, “This process cannot be completed because the screen width is too small. Please increase the screen width and try again.” is displayed to inform the user.
WSP-4121 Payroll When a user role was set to Inquiry access for the Payroll History form, the system automatically protected all input fields, which incorrectly blocked the user from adjusting the year or using other filter options. The Payroll History form has been updated to allow interaction with the year selector, filters, and line chart dropdown even when the user role is set to Inquiry access. Access to individual payroll summaries continues to be governed by the user’s specific role security.
WSP-4160 Payroll Users processing multiple payroll batches in the superbatch encountered an issue where clicking the “Print all” button caused batches to automatically ship and disappear from the superbatch view, even when the Auto Mail field in System Parameters was empty. This prevented users from selecting the “Shipped” icon to run reports and print checks manually. The superbatch “Print all” functionality was updated to correctly respect the Auto Mail settings in System Parameters and the Paperless delivery settings in Client Details. The process now correctly determines whether to skip the “ship” step based on these configurations, ensuring that batches only auto-ship when intended and remain visible in the superbatch for manual shipping when required.
WSP-4252 Payroll The payroll process was not correctly respecting the FLSA exempt status for employees assigned to a remote position classification. When a position was configured with a remote position classification that was FLSA exempt, but the standard position classification was non-exempt, the payroll engine incorrectly applied non-exempt rules (such as half-pay calculations) to the remote employee. The payroll calculation logic was updated to ensure that the FLSA exempt status assigned to a remote position classification is appropriately respected during payroll processing, even if the standard position classification on the same position setup is non-exempt.
WSP-4336 Payroll The system did not post the deduction import amounts in the Time Sheet Deduction Import form for all employees in the import. In addition, the payroll vouchers posted these values as a lesser amount, with the decimal point over-adjusted two places to the left. This is fixed.
WSP-4406 Payroll Customers reported that delivery sheets were being automatically generated and printed with payroll reports (such as checks), even when the system was configured not to include them. This occurred specifically when the Paperless Delivery option was set to “all payroll output.” The payroll reporting process has been updated to correctly respect the Paperless Delivery configuration. Delivery sheets will no longer be generated or included in consolidated payroll reports when they are not required by the client’s setup.
RRT-7009 System Users with custom URLs intermittently encountered a “Nonce mismatch” error or were incorrectly redirected to the legacy login screen. This is fixed. The login process now correctly redirects to the PrismONE ID landing page by default.
WSP-4577 System When a client was terminated and the option to terminate active employees was selected as Yes, the system was not inactivating the employees as part of the client termination process. This issue occurred even after a warning message was displayed and confirmed by the user. The client termination process was updated to ensure that active employees are correctly terminated when the corresponding option is selected during the client termination workflow.

Welcome

PrismHR software is specifically designed to help Professional Employer Organizations (PEOs) and Administrative Services Organizations (ASOs) reduce risk, be more efficient, expand business, and be more profitable.

When you choose PrismHR, you are choosing more than just a software platform. You are partnering with a team of professionals who are deeply invested in the PEO and ASO industry and dedicated to providing the best technology and services possible. You are also partnering with other professionals in the industry in the sense that we all learn from each other.

To view release notes for PrismHR, click any of the links in the Table of Contents. Each release is represented with a book that features the month and year. Click these books to expand product names and version numbers for the release. The most recent documents are at the top of the list. Use the Search feature to look for a specific keyword or phrase. Open any PDFs for Download book to view and print release notes documents from the past year.

Before You Begin

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/Release-Notes/Shared-Files/Before_You_Begin.htm Path: Release-Notes/Shared-Files/Before_You_Begin.htm

Before You Begin

Note: Note: For the best experience, refresh your browser or clear your history to ensure that you see the latest features, styles, images, and in-product help in PrismHR.

Note: NOTE FOR USER ADMINISTRATORS

When there are new forms in this release, you must add the forms manually to user roles to grant users access to them. This ensures security because users do not get automatic access to new forms.

  1. Open User Roles (found in the Back Office menu [Image: screenshot] under System|Change).

  2. Open the user role.

  3. Click Add. The maintenance form opens, listing new forms and those that were previously removed from the role.

  4. Select only the forms that are appropriate for the role.

  5. Click Accept.

  6. Click Save.

See the Release Features for the newest forms and features in PrismHR.

For the best experience, clear your cache

Source: https://tech-docs.prismhr.com/SP_help/Content/Release-Notes/Shared-Files/Best_Experience_Refresh.htm Path: Release-Notes/Shared-Files/Best_Experience_Refresh.htm

Important! Always refresh your browser or clear your cache to ensure that you see the latest features, styles, images, and in-product help in PrismHR.

To clear your Chrome cache:

  • Open a Chrome browser window.

  • At the top right, click More (or the ellipses).

  • Click More tools, then select Clear browsing data.

  • At the top of the dialog, select a time range. For example, select All time to delete all browsing data.

  • Select the Cookies and other site data and Cached images and files boxes.

  • Click Clear Data.
